comment: So far has been my favorite professor ever, really funny guy and incorporates a bunch of memes in slideshows. 2 tests (fair if you study) a presentation (easy) and project (heavy research but easy grader).

Honestly the coolest professor I've had so far. This was the only class I had where I didn't feel crazy stressed out the entire time. He's very understanding and willing to help you out in any way he can. The class was slightly disorganized and it's mostly lectures but overall not difficult with 2 tests, a presentation and a paper. Highly recommend

Great guy. Presentations are easy to follow. He is a funny guy with lots of lenience. 2 exams, one paper and one presentation. a few discussion posts. He curved our test very well. easy class but you still learn a lot.

Pedro Moran-Palma is one of the nicest and most approachable professors I've had. I enjoyed the class although you have to be prepared to answer questions. His tests are easy compared to other professors I've had. Mr. Moran-Palma has a sense of humor and will help you however he can. Highly recommend.

Absolutely love this professor! I was really afraid to take Spanish 102 with him since I have not taken it in a few years. BUT, if you put in effort you will do just fine. Tests/quizzes are pretty similar to what i had in Spanish in high schoo. Definitely speak in class . He will purposely select the card w/your name on it . Participation is key!

He is a horrible teacher. His only qualification is that he is Mexican. Uses the Geneseo Spanish textbook. Small class size. He also teaches at another college so he only has one hour of office hours a week. Won't work around your schedule. If you prove him wrong he won't like you. Wouldn't recommend.
Easy A for anyone that know even a little bit about Spanish. Tests/ quizzes are very easy and he is a really nice guy. Definitely recommend taking 201 with him over the other professors.

Moran-Palma is a great professor.  He is ALWAYS ready to help.  Sometimes you can skip class but dont do it often because you will fall behind.  Do the hw in the book, and make sure you can talk out loud.  He will call on you in class, but dont worry if you mess up because he will help you through it.  He really wants you to get better at spanish!

Professor Moran-Palma was amazing, especially because I was positive I would do poorly in Spanish after not taking it in over 3 years. He was very precise about what he wanted us to know for the tests, and the final was not cumulative which is always nice. I think he's a pretty easy grader. I am so happy that I took my final Spanish class with him!

Professor Palma is a very nice guy but, not a teacher. He has trouble understanding why students are struggling in his class. If you ask for help he will just tell you to go to tutoring. If you take him just teach yourself everything and you'll be fine.

Van Cleve is an amazing professor. He is very caring, and does his best to make us laugh. He likes when students raise their hands to answer questions; mainly so he can see how well the class understands the topic. Attendance isn't mandatory but he gives a lot of extra credit during class that is used towards the final.
Ugh I love Cleve. Awesome man. Very smart.

Took both gen chem 1&2 with van cleve and really enjoyed him. Chem II I found that the lectures really complimented the textbook, but I needed both to get a really comprehensive understanding of the material (just textbook or just lecture slides were not enough). Plenty of extra credit opportunities as well.

I LOVE THIS MAN.  The sweetest old professor you'll ever meet, he's super funny and engaging for an 8am lecturer.  I wish I had him for gen chem 1, as long as you do the achieve assignments and so ok on the tests you'll be fine. He doesn't even need to teach anymore he's just in it for the love of the game, and that's what makes him so great.

I loved Professor Van Cleve. He really taught the material well and he was very helpful with reviewing for exams. He has office hours after every class which is really helpful as well. I always felt really prepared for the exams because the practice was very similar to the actual test. Highly recommend him.

Dr. Van Cleve was amazing and very accessible outside of class. He was very helpful in his office hours and very good at helping you understand. He gives lots of extra credit problems in his lectures so make sure you go to his classes. Very caring about his students and fun to work with. Loved Van Cleve so much he's such a sweet professor.

Prof Van Cleve was by far the best chem prof I have had. I never got chem but when I went to his office hours, he would help reteach everything and make practice problems!! So much extra credit and his practice tests reflected the real exams. If you study you will do great! So so so grateful for having him as my professor.

Dr. Van Cleve is a fantastic professor. He was always available for questions after class or during office hours. He is quick to respond to emails and is overall a funny professor. My only complaint is that he goes through lecture slides a little fast but he posts his lecture notes so you will be fine if you check back in.

Super interesting lectures, even for someone who used to not like chemistry too much. Grading, tests, and assignments were all very fair and easy to complete while still challenging your knowledge on the topic. As long as you do the 5 - 6 short (like 5 minute) assignments every other day you'll do fine.
Very good professor, always has office hours, provides extra credit in lectures, cares for students.
He gives extra credit for the final exam, he is very approachable and understanding. The tests are fair and nothing too crazy.
Very nice and good at explaining. Tests were fair and he gave extra credit. I would recommend taking him for 116 and 118.

Van Cleve gives lots of extra credit which will go on the final. He always sends out a practice exam before the exams. He makes 8:30 lectures manageable and he is helpful in office hours. Overall great guy, he explains topics in a way that is easy to understand, as someone who doesn't like chem, I ended up enjoying his class. Definitely recommend

For an 8:30 Chem class, this guy was great. Lectures were easy to understand and broken down into simple topics to help you know better. He is a great, super funny guy who truly cares and gives extra credit. Take him!

Van Cleve is a great guy and gives extra credit if you answer questions in class before an exam. He is straightforward with his assignments and test dates. His tests were all multiple choice which is a huge plus as well.

one of the worst professors here at SUNY Geneseo in the chem depart.  Even though I got an A I only have the textbook to thank not this prof. Please avoid this dude at all costs for Chem 1 and Chem 2. His slides are made by another person and he be mumbling in class. His concepts aren't clear and you will be suffering. Class was self-study.
very kind and understanding when it comes to grading. If you put in the effort for office hours he will give you extra credit.
Van Cleve is one of the best professors out there. He truly wants the best for his students if you seek him out. He provides great slides and lectures. He gives a lot of extra credit!

One of the best professors at Geneseo. He is incredibly kind and really wants you to understand the topics. His lectures and homework reflect the tests, so pay attention in class, take notes and actually do the practice problems. If you have and questions or concerns go to his office hours!!!! He will be very willing to help you.

Dr. Van Cleve always made sure to keep the course difficult enough for the class but not to the point where class averages were in the 40s/50s. His lectures constantly connect the the medical field and current studies so they are interesting. He also makes practice tests that strongly reflect the exam content.
He was very chill but did not teach the material very well. He always just expected us to know what he was talking about without explaining it

I really loved having Professor Van Cleve He was very accessible even outside of class hours and on weekends. He is very caring and understanding, he will take measures to make sure you understand what you are doing. His tests aren't terribly hard given the course and he gives a lot of extra credit. will be taking as many classes as I can with him!

Absolutely loved biochem with Van Cleve. He makes everything as easy as possible and will try to meet you halfway every time. He really loves to teach and I wish I could take more classes with him. Extra credit on all exams and optional extra credit essay. If you can take biochem with him, DO IT!!! Achieve homework 1x week and 4 exams.

I thought he was a great Professor, he really takes the time to go through things on the slides and do problems together in class. Lots of extra credit in class especially when attendance is low so just be sure to go to class.

Professor Van Cleve single-handedly kept me in my major. The class is difficult but he is willing to help you and genuinely wants to see you succeed. He explains concepts and doesn't just read off the slides.

I enjoyed Van Cleve's lectures. I decided to take his class next semester! You can tell he really cares about his students succeeding because of the effort he puts into making sure everyone understands the material in class. He does take attendance and you do receive a grade for attendance but his lectures are engaging and informational!
Amazing professor, he is very engaged during his lectures and actually sounds excited about the material that he is teaching. His tests are open book and reflect the homework.
Great professor, homework reflects quiz and test material, if their is a review session don't miss it.

He doesnt require attendance, as far as I can tell. He tries to engage everyone with the material, but will call on random names if no one answers. The tests were turned in online, so ik several people just stayed in their dorms to take it. There are opportunities for extra credit. Van Cleve is a good teacher for chemistry, would recommend.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework', 'Test heavy']

comment: Prof. Van Cleve is a nice guy, his lectures can be very dry at times but he tries to keep things moving. Homework consists of a 5 question assignment every other day and is fairly straightforward and has hints included. Tests are the majority of the grade but he does offer extra credit. Chem is typically difficult, he isn't a bad prof for it.

Chose to take him again for 118. Very easy going, knows this is a hard class, tries to lighten the mood with some jokes lol. Skipped classes but very easy to catch up with textbook. LOTS of extra credit. Wants students to do well. HW assignments are a 5 question quiz untimed and get 2 attempts, he also gives hints for the HW. Tests were reasonable

Professor Van Cleve is alright. He was terrible at teaching math-the SI explained how to do math better than Van Cleve did. He is a lot better at teaching concepts, but he doesn't fully explain himself a lot. If I had to take him again I would, but he's not my first choice.

Im gonna be honest, I didnt go to a single one of his lectures. I did everything online and Im gonna pass with flying colors, but thats just because I already took a class very similar to this, just without credit. The online homework/quizzes are easy if you pay attention to his slides/the textbook, and he does answer questions if you have any.

Van Cleve is a truly wonderful professor. He's very helpful if you have questions, and responds to emails almost immediately. You definitely have to attend class, otherwise you may get behind and be completely lost during lecture but that's with any science class. Overall would 100% recommend.

Chem 116 is a tough class but he is the most accessible prof outside of class I have this semester. He's kind and admits this stuff is tough and helps you work through it in office hours. Unless he has something going on he always responds to emails and is willing to work with you. The department offers curves on some tests. You have to go to class
tags: ['Accessible outside class', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Lecture heavy']

comment: Rushes through the lectures but ends classes early. Doesnt explain him self fully and you have to fill in the holes. Does not answer questions just confuses you more when you ask. Power points are very sloppy and formatted weirdly by him. Holds review classes that do help and review good material.

His lecture style allows students to be more engaged as he imbeds a lot of practice. He also provided A LOT of practice exams to make sure everyone had a more than fair chance. He also added 10 points on a few of our exams which helped! He is accessible outside of class. During class, he tries his best to explain multiple ways for everyone to grasp

Professor Van Cleve is a really great professor and all around guy. He's very accessible outside of class and is always willing to answer in class questions as well as meet you in office hours or make time outside of office hours to meet with you. The content can be difficult but he makes it understandable and provides extra credit opportunities.
Literally doesnt explain anything and expects everyone to be chem legends. Also hasnt responded to my emails but thats fine..

Really relaxed, down to earth professor. Had him for intro chem lab, he explained the lab in good enough detail way faster than other lab instructors do and we often got out significantly earlier than other lab classes. Can't say too much about grading because LA did most of the grading, but would highly recommend for any course.

The best chemistry professor in Suny Geneseo. Definitely take him, accessible outside class, fast email response and essy homework. He curves the test and puts his effort to make test easy. His powerpoints have notes which is great and shows how much he cares about students.

Van Cleve's lectures can sometimes be confusing and hard to follow. However, going to office hours and talking to him one on one was extremely helpful, he is very approachable and eager to help. The subject matter is difficult, but he curves his tests A LOT.

In this class we read primary documents from history and textbooks, and students lead class discussion through power points that we created. Each student in the class leads one discussion. 6 short response questions and one final paper, and the occasional quiz. Professor Adams was great. She is passionate about the material she teachers.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK']

comment: Do not take a class with Prof. Herold unless necessary! The class was purely her talking at you, with very few pauses for student engagement. It was very difficult to take notes. The worst part of Prof. Herold is that she hasn't graded a single thing all semester, even after a classmate called her out a week before spring break.

Herold was nice at first and I was excited about this class but she not a great professor. She talks the entire time about the reading that was due two classes ago and doesn't use brightspace. She doesn't grade anything until the last minute so it's hard to know what grade you even have. Shes caring but I would never take her class again.
tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things']

comment: We didn't get our grades back until after final grades were due. This gives no time for feedback or improvement or for us to challenge our grades. Extremely harsh grading, and there is a huge project worth only 10% but the final exam is 35%. We read so many books and then she would miss classes and we would get behind. Disorganized. Lecture heavy.

Professor Herold is a pretty solid professor. She is a fair grader and doesn't had out a lot of work. Every class is a lecture/discussion. Reading and paying attention in class is necessary. She takes a very long time to grade things and provide feedback. Doesn't respond promptly to emails. Nevertheless, she is super kind and I took a lot out.

The material itself wasn't the issue for this course, it was the fact she didn't put in grades until finals week, meaning there was no way to check your progress. She also never gave us back our final exam grades, only our grade in the class which was frustrating. Overall this course involves a lot of reading and lectures based on those.

Prof. Herold is extremely passionate about what she teaches, and that makes a class I wasn't sure I would like enjoyable. Some of her assignments threw me for a loop. she is an understanding grader on most assignments and extremely accommodating as long as you communicate.

She is easily the WORST professor I've ever had here at Geneseo. All she does is talk AT you, and she cancels class half the time. She didn't grade anything til after final grades were already due, and I didn't get my grade for her class until two weeks after final grades were due. She is very confusing, and is late to class every single day.

Herold is one of my favorite professors thus far. Her lectures are amazing and full of passion. Attendance may not be mandatory for a grade, but if you want to pass you NEED to go to class. The books we read can be super confusing, but she really explains them in lecture. Note taking is encouraged. Her tests are long and difficult, so study hard.

Test were not crazy hard, but the time she gives for how long the test are is crazy. Never finished a test in that class. She's a fine person but I kinda resent her for this class. FYI i never went to class, but if not for a friend who went without fail, i would have failed.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things', "Skip class? You won't pass."]

comment: Prof Herold is fine. Not the most interesting class you will ever take, but overall she's a pretty good.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Test heavy', 'Clear grading criteria']

comment: Very reading intensive. Although attendance wasn't mandatory as a grade, if you didn't go and take notes from the discussions, good luck. Had to read about 6 books and write 3-4 essays with 2 presentations. There aren't too many small things to grade so you really need to focus on your writing skills. She did provide really cool insight though.
tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass."]

comment: Dr. Carly Herold is BRILLIANT. She is funny, quirky, an exceptional lecturer, relatable, and very caring. She encourages students to participate and hears them out fully. Though political theory classes tend to be lecture heavy, Dr. Herold makes reading Plato and other philosophers fun and her passion for what she does shines through. Take her!

Professor Harold is one of those inbetweeners. You could love her class or hate it but most likely you'll think it's just "eh". She covers the material she needs to in class and is always open to questions and class discussion. She can be a little frazzled with schedules so your reading calendar will change but, trust me, you will be reading. a lot

You don't learn much from her at all and the amount of reading she expects is insane. Quizzes every Wednesday but they aren't hard. VERY discussion based class so you learn a lot about your classmates opinions, but nothing of what is on the tests.

It's clear she's passionate about philosophy, but as someone who isn't, I found it very hard to participate in mandatory discussions. She assigns a ton of reading for each class and is tough grader, but she also takes months to get papers back to you, which makes it hard to know where you stand or improve for later assignments.
tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass."]

comment: Herold is a very knowledgeable professor and loves what she does. Her lectures for humanities are long and can be boring. She takes forever to grade assignments. However, if you need help with anything in the class, she is quite helpful and understanding.
tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Tests? Not many']

comment: Super boring and her voice is the most annoying thing ever, but a smart lady none the less. Gives a ton of reading but if you keep up with them you'll do fine, otherwise don't bother with this class because you'll drown. Tests are pretty easy (if you read!) but grades essays tough. only 2 papers and 2 tests, but short quiz every class.
tags: ['LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES', 'LECTURE HEAVY']

comment: My least favorite professor ever. Takes the entire semester to grade 4 page papers, saying "I don't think you guys know how much I have to grade!" Maybe don't be a professor then? Made me come in for a quiz when I had the flu. Wound up 2 tenths of a point shy of an A- and she didn't round up, despite the high level of subjectivity in her grading
Takes forever to grade things, and most of the class does poorly. Doesn't curve tests, and gives weekly quizzes on the readings, which take hours to complete.

Shes a real nice lady and easy to work with. She facilitates quality class discussion as well. Honestly, the functionality of the class isnt too much different from a Hum course, so if you do the reading youre fine. Only downside is she takes her time grading things so good look ever seeing your quiz grades. 10/10 recommend though.
The amount of reading I'm required to do for a gen ed is ridiculous.

This class was fine, but was kinda boring. You have to study for the tests, and the in class quizzes are open note so not too challenging. The class is pretty boring, but I got credit for it so I guess it was worth it?!?!

Overall, he's a good professor. Tests were okay, but some questions were overly specific for a lower level class. The two critiques I have is that he reads directly off his lectures, sometimes not getting all the way through and tries to rush through them. He does read them with enthusiasm, though. It's clear he wants everyone to succeed.

He is a great guy, makes lectures fun and interesting. He did assign a textbook, but it wasn't required to read or take notes on. Participation is definitely important because most of the in-class activities show up on the tests. If you need help with something, he's really accessible outside of class and is very helpful overall. Would take again!
He has low self esteem and it shows. He literally bullies students when he feels threatened.
Awesome guy. Mainly lectures but he finds a way to make it fun and indulges the class correctly. Exams are straight from notes and good grades are easily attainable. 100% recommend.

Here's the deal - You've gotta go to class. He does quizzes every class based on what you learned from his lectures. It's a very applied class meaning you can't just take notes and be fine. You have to DO the lab applications and DO the in-class activities. there were only 2 tests that were EASY. He is an ok teacher but wouldn't take him again.

Graded based on 3 exams, a paper, a project, and participation. Exams aren't too bad but you need to study notes and images from the powerpoint. The paper is enjoyable because you get to choose your own topic. the project is simple so it is a good way to boost your grade. Go to class b/c he offers free and easy participation points often.
tags: ['Accessible outside class', 'Graded by few things', 'Lecture heavy']

comment: Great guy! Lectures were off a powerpoint which was posted online. Test were fair, you needed to know specifics in the powerpoint such as graphs. Really inspired me and amazing teacher, really knows his stuff. 10/10 would take class with him again

Definitely one of the best professors I've ever had. He lectures alot but makes them interesting so I dont mind. Very helpful in office hours and genuinely cares about his student and their opinion on the matters

Dr. Tulowiecki is probably one of the best professors I have ever taken. He interacts with his class, and you have to participate to receive a grade. Hes very flexible and his office hours are always helpful. Take this class!

No doubt Allen is one of the most caring professors I have had. He has been incredibly accommodating in the midst of the pandemic and is very accessible. He applies what he teaches in his own classroom and very clearly knows what he is talking about. The class is challenging but no absurdly difficult. Do yourself a favor, take this class!

I am taking PSYC 350 with him online synchronously and he is the only professor I have this semester who has said he "understands" the particular stressors of college during a pandemic, and other life factors that would impact school, and actually shows it. Genuinely the sweetest and very responsive.

Prof Allen is a great teacher and it's clear that he cares a lot about all of his students. Grades are based on 3 tests and 2 papers (he lets you bring a cheat sheet to the tests) as well as group work that is very easy. The class can get kind of boring and repetitive but that's a given in a research methods class.

Doctor Allen is one of the most caring, passionate, and motivating professors I have had at SUNY Geneseo. His expectations are clear and he is willing to help you. He really notices effort and participation. If you attend class, contribute to class discussion, and work hard you will do well. Everyone should take at least one class with Doctor Allen

Professor Williams gave a very well written syllabus that is self explanatory and as long as you read it and make yourself familiar with it you will know what to expect. There are weekly chapter outlines, discussions, and two essay tests from the required reading and as long as you do the work you will pass the class.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Clear grading criteria']

comment: Williams is honestly not that bad. He does go off topic a LOT, but I didn't mind. You have to do a LOT of reading in this class, but I enjoyed most of the books. There are weekly pop quizzes on the readings and lecture, but if you read and show up they're pretty easy. He did grade the essay pretty harshly, so read the book and run an outline by him
tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES']

comment: Professor Williams is a boring lecturer and goes off on tangents more often than he addresses class content. I wouldn't attend class if it weren't for the pop quizzes because I learn more from the insane amount of reading than I do from listening to his lectures. I think they might actually confuse me more than help clarify.
tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Get ready to read', 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK']

comment: 3 exams, 1 paper, weekly 10q Mult ch quizzes. Not great but not awful. Each Class is a long lecture that often goes off topic/feels irrelevant or lacks context but he is knowledgeable about his class and can answer any question you ask. An awful essay will still get you a 70. Participation is irrelevant. If you read youll pass but its a lot to read
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS']

comment: Worst professor I have ever had. Do not take a class with him. He lectures the whole class, thinks he is gods gift to the earth, very arrogant and thinks he knows everything. Tests are pretty hard, papers are confusing.

I'm serious when I say do not take him for anything. I did fine in this course, but I HATED it. He would take off points for essays because he didn't agree with your opinion. We had to read roughly 100 pages a night from the driest textbook in the world. He doesn't believe in PowerPoint and half the class was spent talking about his childhood.

Dr. Williams likes to talk...a lot. He lectures at you the entire class, so participation really doesn't matter. Generally pretty easy if you put in the time and energy on papers and tests. He gives weekly quizzes (10 multiple choice), usually every Wednesday. Spends way too much time on the Bible, not nearly enough time on other readings.
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES', 'LECTURE HEAVY']

comment: Easy teacher, useful class, actually learn something.

Williams is very knowledgeable on subjects he teaches, and is pretty much able to answer any questions you might have on the material.  He gives a quiz every week (usually Wednesdays), but they're pretty easy if you read.  Essays can be tough but as long as you stretch the work out it's manageable.
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass."]

comment: A genuinely good person who is very knowledgeable in his field.  Grades fairly easily on his papers and gives good feedback.  If you love history you will enjoy some of his talks that go off topic.

Williams lectures are extremely boring, but full of the exact information you will be tested on and expected to write about. Come to class having at least read a summary of what you were supposed  you read and you will do fine. He gives weekly pop quizzes, usually on Wednesdays.
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES']

comment: This was a cool class. Prof. Williams tells a lot of stories that would not be on the test. 1st test: Persian war, 2nd test: Peloponnesian war. There is a quiz every wednesday: 10 mult. choice questions on the readings. Start the Greek Tyrants paper early: there are like 10 scholars and the articles are all really long. No study guides were given.
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass."]

comment: I enjoyed this class. He gives out a simple 10 question, multiple choice quiz every week based on the reading, but they are almost always on Wednesday. As long as you take the quizzes, they will boost your grade. The tests aren't hard, nor are the two papers. If you pay attention in class, it will be easy. He gets sidetracked often.
tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES']

comment: "What can I say" about Dr. Williams and HUMN I?  When it comes to the Bible he is the most accurate.  Students may not want to hear it because they want to believe what they want to believe (or maybe afraid of what they think they will have to give up to believe any other way).  Dr. Williams does digress during lecture but does return to topic.

His lectures will often spiral into litanies of anecdotes (his record was 11 minutes straight before a lecture began) but if you do the reading, his lecturing will make the  material more understandable, and if you don't, it won't make much sense. He's also very approachable if you have questions. Papers are a cakewalk. Really chill guy, too. Read!

This class was about Greece which is Williams' specialty. He's brilliant as a scholar but he's boring in class. He still uses overhead projectors and transparencies for visuals. Papers are pretty easy if you do the reading. He spends about a quarter of each class talking about anecdotes which usually aren't related to class material.

Williams is a really nice guy, and he's incredibly knowledgeable. But as a professor, he's scatterbrained. His lectures, which feel 10 hours long, usually go off-topic for quite a while. He's never clear about what he wants for assignments. He gives reading quizzes that are hard even if you read. Don't take a class taught by him unless you have to.

Dr. Williams is brilliant and knows a lot about everything. Class is not terribly hard. Easier grader on tests than papers. Gives too many IDs to prepare for but still not a bad prof. The only issue is he gets REALLY far behind. We covered Hamlet in 20 minutes. Overall not bad as long as you actually interested in learning about humanities.

Couldn't have asked for a more knowledgeable professor.  I'm a history major but came into class not having study ancient Greece since high school. I was very intimidated at first, but he helped me pick it right up. Only downside (though his thoughts were always interesting) was he often got himself off topic while lecturing. Highly recommended.

Don't be too intimidated by the amount of reading he requires for his course.  Do the reading and there will be no surprises on the tests and quizzes. Always gives multiple choices for essay questions and provides ample study material. Only thing to be weary of is grammar on assigned essay, he will light you up for even the smallest grammatical err

Williams is brilliant. If you want to learn and be challenged, take his class. If you're looking for an easy grade, do not take his class. He knows absolutely everything about his subject which helps and gives bonus on the tests.

DO NOT TAKE DO NOT TAKE. Took hum with him and he made my semester horrible. He is arrogant and thinks he knows everything. He preaches to you, so you better believe what he does or you're screwed. His tests are absolutely nuts, he thinks we are machines. Spends over a month on the bible. I will never ever take a class with him again EVER!!!

Very smart and capable teacher. Truly passionate about his teaching. Well read on the material and very helpful. Go to office hours if you need help with the essay. Anecdotes in class are usually funny.

Williams only lectures for the whole time you're in class, so it might be a bit of a drag. Weekly quizzes are given but they're not too bad. He gives review sheets for tests but preparing them is a lot of work. Overall, he's an easier grader on tests than papers. Make sure you go to office hours cause he helps you out a lot there!

very knowledgeable historian. Has read all the texts in their original language so he understands the way things are translated to help you better understand the authors meaning. Easy grader. very enthusiastic about his class

Super enthusiastic, really loves teaching and loves the material. A little bit eccentric, and assigns a lot of reading, but as long as you do the reading and have a sense of humor, you should have problem doing well.

He is an arrogant professor who thinks he knows everything. You cannot challenge his beliefs at all. He is very religious and it comes out in his lectures. What he teaches is his own opinions and is not appropriate at all. If you want to discuss and understand humanities, DO NOT take him. He preaches to you.
grades essays based on your opinion not how your present it

Prof. Williams is an amazing professor! He is extremely knowledgeable about history and is always willing to explain something. There are weekly quizzes but as long as you do the readings you should be fine. The exams are essay based, but again you have to study... if you put in the effort it will definitely pay off and Williams is very enjoyable
Great professor, fairly easy class. All the material is straight forward. Weekly quizzes (easy) to make sure you are attending class. Would recommend!

comment: Awful, awful teacher.

Dr. Nicodemi is inspirational. She is extremely helpful and loves talking to aspiring students. Her classes are tough, but she does implement a hefty curve that will boost your grade. She grades based on how well the class does. Don't just pay attention to the number grades. Talk to her and build a relationship. She will help with anything you need
There is a lot of leeway on exams as long as there is conceptual understanding of the material. Just check your math grammar and enjoy professor Nicodemi's stories of Newtonian Calculus.

Nicodemi is a sweet lady who cares about her students. I would much prefer to have her as a grandma instead of a professor. This class allowed the bright students to excel and those who struggled with math were left in the dirt. She is willing to help, but there isn't much you can do to perform well on tests without natural mathematics ability.
I love Professor Nicodemi; she's so sweet and genuine and always wants to help her students succeed in her class.

You would learn a fundamental, mathematical proof skill in the class. She gave us  the ebook she published, so I didn't buy any textbook for the class. If you preview the chapter before she talk about it in the class, you must catch up the material easily. No Effort No Gain!! I got 80 something in all exams, and it ended up with A-. Easy Grader''

She very much is "that professor" that high schools tell you about; no spoon-feeding whatsoever. Her tests and quizzes could be easy, only if you actually do the hw (which is never turned in, so no one bothers). The only time class made sense is when the TA taught.
She was often extremely confusing and scatterbrained. She is an intelligent woman, but she has trouble teaching clearly and effectively.

Decided to write after reading review below. Future possible students, the info given below is not true. If you go to class, and do the homework, you will learn. Her lectures are great, you learn a lot. The quizzes and test are of homework and class work. Also for tests she gives a review sheet that will be similar to what is on the test.

Extremely bright professor.  Loves math.  Does an inadequate job of actually teaching anything.  Sample problems done in class are nothing like the things done on quizzes, and tests are a whole separate world.  Take her class and you basically have to teach yourself the material, and that in itself is difficult with this textbook.
The best and sweetest professor I have had at Geneseo. Nicodemi requires a lot of work outside of class, but it pays off. I have learned so much from her. She has had a huge impact on my time here.

Nicodemi is a wonderful professor. She leaves the fresh baked pie of Calculus sitting on the windowsill, allowing the aroma to drift through the minds of all those who wish to indulge in it. Equipped in her multi-pocketed safari vest, she will lead you  through the treacherous plains of mathematics, teaching you to appreciate it on the way.

Best math professor I ever had. Keeps class interesting and moving. Gives all students fair chances to do well. Makes you work to learn doesn't just give you a formula sheet. I would recommend taking any calc with her.

Absolutely love Nicodems. She is sweet and really cares  about her students and their success. Gives everyone a fair chance to improve their grade. Get ready to go on a safari though Calc II bootcamp! Favorite teacher so far, I'm taking Calc III with her even though I don't need it for my major.

She is very unclear and confusing. She is very intelligent but it is a waste for her to be a teacher. Everything she's says makes sense if you're one of her math scholar colleagues. I'm not a math major but, I liked math. I LIKED it, due to her. I avoid it.
She is a very tough professor, but I learned so much. She is always willing to help and really cares about the success of her students. If you don't put in the effort you will do poorly.

I started out in community college with A's in all of my math classes. I thought I loved math, until I got to this class. Proofs is the worst class Geneseo offers. If you are a math major, I would avoid her for proofs unless you like feeling frustrated.
I changed majors because of her class. Proofs is already a hard/boring class, and she makes it 100x more boring/difficult than it has to be. Don't take a class with this woman ever!
I just don't like the woman. She turns proofs from something that may be doable, into something that is impossible. She is ridiculously hard, and I would never take her again.

She is the best professor I have had at Geneseo.  She made me work harder than any professor before, but if you put in the work and are up front when you don't understand things and ask for help, you'll learn so much from her.  I am so prepared in my upper level classes because of Calc 2 and Proofs that I took with her.  She's the greatest!

Very sweet and intelligent lady, but her tests are very challenging. Made us work on side projects on MATLAB in an ELA class which was another challenge for me.. I recommend ela with a different teacher.
Sweetest woman. Love her. Loved the class, will answer any question you have, will never make you feel bad for not understanding. Sit near the front would be my only advice

A very nice woman. Sometimes she is hard to follow in class and doesn't give the best notes but the tests aren't too hard and curves almost every test. The final was a little tough but overall she was okay. I would recommend taking the class.

Managed to destroy my GPA and my interest in math. The worst professor I've ever had at Geneseo. Not sure how anyone can like her. Class is boring and she is hard to follow. Less than useless in office hours and took off points for stupid things on tests. Good luck.
Great professor. Very helpful, and really knows what she's talking about.
Loved having her as a teacher. One of the best teachers at Geneseo.
One of the greatest professors I've ever met in Geneseo. Highly recommend her!

She is awesome and is always helpful outside of class! I would definetly reccommend her! Her tests are fair and are not extremely long, weekly quizzes that make you actually learn the material and a fair amount of homework! I loved going to her class!

This teacher is very unclear in her lessons in Math239. She has everything on "My Courses" and the book you use is one SHE wrote so forget teaching yourself from the book, it doesn't help. She is unorganized in her thoughts and when teaching. She jumps around and nothing seems to link together. I really don't know what Im suppose to learn from her.

AMAZING TEACHER. Love her. Absolutely knows what she's talking about and in my opinion is quite funny. She takes a lot of time to explain a problem rather than just telling you how to do it. Recommended for any of her courses =)
She is the best math teacher i have had at Geneseo yet

Olympia is possibly the sweetest woman I have ever met. She offers tons of extra credit and makes calc II as manageable as possible. It moves quickly and will be tough no matter who teaches it, but I definitely recommend her. Very helpful outside class and the weekly quizzes force you to keep up with the material so you dont fall behind. Great prof
Calc II was pretty straightforward. She knows her stuff very well. Weekly quizzes, fair tests. Loads of extra credit opportunities. Definitely recommend her for Calc II.

incredibly incredibly helpful. although calc 2 moves fast, i have never had a professor who was more interested in the academic progress of his/her students. reccommended for anyone looking to take calc 2.

It is important when taking this calc 2 with her, you must be very good at calc 1 already.  if you are behind she isn't great at helping outside of class. no extra credit, no retests. not a good teacher in my book.

Goes very fast, tests are free game on anything she says or assigns for homework even if they are not on any review she does, not very approachable outside of class, if you know what you're doing pretty well shes a decent teacher. but if you need help, avoid her class if possible.
best math teacher by far.  she definitely keeps your interest for the whole class too, i learned more in her class than i did in any other class at geneseo.
Awesome teacher. Extremely fair and approachable. (Gives extra credit way too much) If you go to class and do the homework, you're set for an A.
no good

She sometimes assigns an obnoxious amount of work, but grades generously.  She runs her class in a non-routine way, so it's never usually boring.  Her tests can be surprising, sometimes very easy and sometimes very hard.  She is interesting in that she allows group discussion on politics, etc.

She is pretty unclear during lectures.  Gives really hard problems that people in the math learning center can't even help you with.  My love for math is completely gone, but she is a pretty nice lady.
She is a really nice teacher, grades fairly and gives out lots of bonus points just for doing the work.  Tests are fair, and she's helpful in and out of class.

She is the best teacher I have ever had- she made me love math and want to be a math major.  She gives fair quizzes and tests and is a fair grader.  She truly loves teaching and wants you to understand the material.
She's not the most helpful and pretty unclear. you have to learn a lot from the book because things jump around like crazy.

Post Empire literary London, the most boring class ever. Everyone was confused and disengaged. Lectures and assignments didn't really make any sense. Lots of small assignments throughout the course. It was a very easy course and he is an easy grader, and understanding about absences and late work. Just obviously doesn't care.

Harrison was genuinely as useful as a rusty paperclip. His attempts at making jokes are difficult to watch and by the end of the semester began to do nothing but anger me. Lessons are painful to sit through. He's also incredibly arrogant and rude. He's blatantly dispassionate about teaching. No one is engaged or attends. Save yourself the pain.

Very nice and laid-back. It was difficult to grasp the point of what he was saying sometimes. My notes are 50% questions, 45% ideas, 5% answers. Many assignments are participation-based. There were 5 discussion posts and 2 papers. You have a lot of freedom in where your paper goes, as long as it stems from the course topic. Reasonable reading.

Literally my favorite professor, awesome class dynamics with banter, his lectures are as interesting as a lecture can be and he does acknowledge the blandness of his content with dry humor and theatrical pizzazz. Discussion forums are semi-frequent, but they're pretty simple and they are outlined in class.

Prof Harrison was an okay teacher. He was kinda confusing and you never really knew what he was talking about because he would start class as if he was in the middle of a conversation already. pretty chill, only two papers the entire semester, lots of reading. not that bad at all. takes attendance. not rude, but has dry humour.

The lectures can be very boring, and drag on. He also tries to make jokes about the book and the subject of the day too often. When we have group or class assignments there is no instruction. A somewhat nice person, but I wouldn't recommend.

I miss Bill. He's an administrator now and doesn't teach any classes. If you showed up, turned things in on time, and didn't fall asleep, then you got an A! He's a kind man who is just angry that the books are disappearing from the library. 12/10 as a person and professor.
Definitely the best professor to take HUMN 220 with. I wish he was teaching HUMN 221 as well! Would love to take it with him. He is very funny during lectures, but he does talk a little fast.

Best professor to take Humn with. Recognizes that student are there because they need the credit. Talks a mile a minute, but he's very fun to listen to and tries to make the material interesting. Barely used the textbooks, though they do come in handy with the group projects and paper.

Not an "easy" teacher, but is lenient with his grades. I did most of the readings but I think just skimming through would've been okay. I didn't do well on his final paper, though. If I had, I think I would have gotten a better grade. He is intelligent and seems like a nice person.

Harrison is probably one of the best professors to take HUMN with. He doesn't take himself very seriously. You have 6 quizzes which are extremely easy if you at least skim the books, a midterm, an 8 page paper, and a take-home final exam. It's a pretty easy class, and he tries to make HUMN interesting (although he seems to acknowledge it's not).

definitely not as bad as i thought it would be in the beginning of the semester. he's a fairly good professor although sometimes his ideas can be confusing. he can be really funny though! i did a lot better than i thought i would do in this class.

The content isn't complex and it's not tough to do well.  If you read the books you'll do well on all of the quizzes.  There's 6 quizzes, 2 presentations and 2 papers.  The class is interesting if you enjoy looking at literature and critiquing it.  It's a pretty easy class, and Harrison is very entertaining and intelligent.. slightly awkward though

Quizzes worth 20%, if u do the readings, it’ll be easy, but he goes through them afterwards, so the rest of the class time is boring-participation is worth 20% so u have to be there. Harrison is amazing. He's a bit scatterbrained and sometimes hard to follow but he is a great guy and knows a LOT about his subject area.

he's easy... yes... but don't bother going to lectures if you're looking for an intellectual discussion... Unless chicken sex or "chair-ness" is your thing. I did next to nothing for this class and got a B+ but i thought it was the biggest waste of time in my life. I would've preferred a prof who would actually TEACH something!

I enjoyed this class. Professor harrison def. has a very unique style and is crazy at times...but in a completely entertaining way. I enjoyed the class and learned a lot. He is a little confusing at times when it comes to explaining his critque on essays...you really have to pay attention to get what he is telling you.
Well, it's definitely an easy class, but a boring one too. He's okay, not the greatest class or professor, but I guess it's good if you want an easy A...and who doesn't???

Great guy, real helpful and just plain genuine. Funny as hell, too. Pretty easy grader, A few essays made up the whole class grade, got B's on all of them effortlessly. Lecture content can be dull sometimes but he does his best to make it enjoyable and for the most part, it is. Definatly take him for any class possible.

He is funny and very unique.  He is in no way a hard grader, unless you sleep the whole semester (but then who isnt a hard grader?).  No pop quizes, no suprises.  He's a great teacher, good for HUM if you like philosophy.
he's funny, very intelligent, but somehow the class just isn't that interesteng. sort of a hard grader, also

i would 100% recommend adabra to anyone taking french for the language requirement! he is very funny and while he likes to “scare you” and make things seem difficult, he truly wants every student to succeed. very kindhearted person and you can tell he is passionate about what he does. best professor i've had at geneseo!

This is my fourth class with Dr. Adabra and it has been my favorite. He is funny and knows what he is talking about. He makes a lot of jokes about making his students cry but actually wants us all to succeed. Helpful at office hours and a good person to talk to about anything. Lectures are engaging, and the content is interesting.

He is intimidating at first but is actually super nice and hilarious, he constantly makes us laugh as a class and really knows what he is talking about. We had 1-2 homework(s) every week, 2 compositions, midterm, final, and oral exam but what do you expect, its a language. you absolutely cannot skip class or you wont pass, participation is required

Prof. Adabra can be intimidating at first but once you get to know him, he is one of the funniest and most genuine professors on campus. His class is engaging but will be difficult if you're not willing to work. Tests and homework are fair if you study for them and he provides good feedback. Overall, an amazing person and professor!

Professor Adabra is extremely knowlegeable, professional, respectful, and funny. Although he assigns a lot of reading, all of it is fun as it allow one to fully dive into the different narratives that exist within the French and Francophone worlds. He will never hesitate to help you. Very understanding, wise, and interesting. Definitely recommend.

He's a great prof and will teach you if you want to learn, that being said you have to work for it. Because of covid, attendance wasn't mandatory, but it still essentially was for this class. Biggest downside is that he does not accept late work, with no exceptions, and he only accepts work as a physical copy.

comment: Unless you do not pay attention in class, you would grow as a thinker. It was such a great experience for me being exposed to narratives of voices often ignored in Western media. My experience was made only greater given how unique this type of course is at Geneseo. No doubt I will be taking the knowledge I have gained in his class into the future.

A truly funny, understanding, and easy-going guy. The entire class is very hard to mess up as long as you show up, he isn't out to fail anyone. If I had any complaint it was just that he really pushes class participation, which isn't great for us shy people. The movies he shows are all great, the tests are easy enough, il est fantastique!
Class really made 0 sense. He made us feel stupid pretty often and I never understood what he wanted. Whole class is based on articles we find ourselves and present. I didn't really learn a thing.

Adabra is an intimidating guy but I have a lot of respect for him. He wants his students to do well and the class really wasn't bad in terms of the amount of work. It was by far my favorite class this semester. Only advice - go to every class, he notices!!

kodjo is awesome. a great guy and a good teacher. he makes class fun and i feel like even though we just goofed off half the time that i still learned a lot from him. also ask him about leaving togo... he's BA

comment: best professor ever.

Honestly one of the best professors I've ever had. I found his accent hard to understand in the beginning but it gets a lot easier. He's always willing to take or crack a joke and you can tell he genuinely enjoys what he does. It's a great atmosphere and a class I'm very glad I took.

By far my favorite professor in the language department. He really cares about his students. Very helpful, organized, enthusiastic, smart and fun. Wants you to meet deadlines and develop critical thinking. I would recommend him to EVERYONE!
Very Helpful. A great man and teacher. A welcome change.

Perhaps one of the most enthusiastic and helpful professors in the whole entire school. He truly wants his students to learn and is always willing to take the extra step to make sure you understand the content. Tests are pretty simple and easy; his final is pretty much the past three exams combined. Take for language requirement!
He was easy going in class but had helpful comments on papers and truly just a great guy to teach a class

Very interesting prof. Most importantly he knows what he is talking about and I love his personality and teaching style. Funny guy but also very serious at times; but classroom set is very relax and welcoming. Charismatic in many ways.
I love this man. Best. Prof. Ever. Enough said.

I take lessons with Dr. Stanley and I enjoy going to lessons because she really tries to understand what will help you progress. Honestly, she cares about you as a person too and you'll find you get in a lot of conversations about all different kinds of things.

She is such caring professor that will inspire you to love piano and sight-reading too!  She's a really sweet person who really knows her stuff, and she makes me actually WANT to practice :) This class was Piano A, so really basic piano and I learned SO MUCH in just one semester!!  5 quizzes ,1 final,  EASY just playing prepared material for her.

comment: I took Theory Skills 2 with Dr. Stanley and while I could tell she understood the material, I felt she was not helpful in class. She focused mainly on sight reading and rhythm and barely reviewed dictations, which was my weakness in the class. When I asked for help, I received none. I don't understand why she did not want to help me.

I do not recommend this class. I have a music background and this class confused me. He expects you to have perfect pitch just like him, and he doesn't explain things clearly at all. Doesn't reply to e-mails in a timely fasion-still waiting for a reply 5 days later.
Cutest old guy you'll meet at Geneseo. Take his class if you want to get to know this funny guy.

Textbook is used inclass. He doesn't take attendance but he'll know if you're not there cause he learns everyone's names. Funny in an old guy way. Classes are easier for people with musical experience. Study and go to class and you'll do well. Quizes in the beginning but die out towards the end. Exams are not hard. He's willing to help you.

Quality professor. Great class for fine arts requirement. Teaches basic music theory, if you have any experience with music you will be golden. Beginners are given special attention (he loves them!), so don't worry. A few written tests, and a piano exam (basic). Gives the class kazoos which he makes you play sometimes for fun. Highly recommended.

Nicest guy.  The class is pretty easy if you have any music background.  If not, he is still a pretty easy grader.  Go to class, listen, and practice the performance stuff before the exam.  Also, he is very willing to meet before or after class for anyone that wants extra help.  I would definitely recommend Basic Musicanship with him!

This man is so nice it's ridiculous. He's funny, intelligent, and amazing musician.  The material is difficult, especially for someone who has no idea about theory- so don't expect and easy ride.  He's very good about meeting before class for extra help. Definitely recommend him.

This man makes me laugh harder than any prof I've ever had. The class isn't necessarily easy, but he's willing to go over things as many times as it takes. He's very liberal on his grading, especially on performance exams. I would strongly recommend the class- I have little musical background, and received an A, as well as many laughs.

Richard is awesome! If you're interested in music and are willing to put forth the effort, this class is perfect for you.  He can be a little hard to understand if you haven't had any exposure to music, but he tries very hard to help everyone understand.

This class was not as easy as originally expected and I can not imagine taking it without previous musical background. With that said, Balkin is a cute old guy who REALLY wants you to be interested... although he has a tendency to jump around the book and rush to teach at the end of class

This class is VERY easy if you have ANY musical background... if you don't, he is very helpful at making you understand what is going on, so it is not hard in that respect either. Recommended either way if you want a fun and easy class. He is a little scatter-brained at times and it is pretty funny. I actually look forward to going to class.

Richard is such a sweet guy and likes to make class fun for people. You just want to hug him. People with no music background will find the class hard cause he's not too clear at times. Class almost always is let out early. Awesome guy and fun class!
Richard is the best, and possibly the nicest person I know!

I'm not sure if he even still is a professor here because I heard he was leaving at the end of last semester. HE IS BY FAR THE BEST OPTION FOR OB IF YOU WANT FAIR GRADING AND TO ACTUALLY LEARN. He is by far the better option it is literally not close. Exams are a story format where it's contextualized MCQs as you go with 2-3 SAQs at the end.

Everything was going well in this class, had an A average and was exempt from the final exam. However, I had a bad group project member who tanked my group's project. I reasonably went to Redlo to explain the issue, he said it wasn't his problem. My grade dropped from an A to a C and it was not my fault at all. Decent professor, not a great guy

Class is pretty easy, Online quiz answers can be found in the free online textbook he provides. The professor is nice, a little odd, blunt at times, but funny. Exams arent hard if you study. There is a group presentation at the end, and his grading is fairly easy. Assignments are helpful for school of business students.

I love Redlo. He has a pretty chill personality and can be super funny. The textbook he had us use was free and his grading made sense. Sometimes the quiz questions were weird, but you can look in the textbook for answer

Redlo was overall a great professor. He is clear about his expectations and his assignments are extremely doable. Hes good at explaining things if you need help or clarification. He can be funny. However he has a strong no BS attitude and is very blunt/direct. He will NOT baby you or make exceptions without a good reason.

Super interesting lady. This particular course relied heavily upon the students ability to speak and understand basic Spanish, but she was super helpful and very funny. Professor Brea is an angel. She is definitely a bit tough on grading sometimes, but she is hilarious, so sweet, and you genuinely learn so much in her class. This was a class I was actually excited to attend.
