comment: Pay attention in class, because something she mentions once will probably be on the final. Her lectures are really random, as are the projects. Make sure to really ace the conjugation quizzes to keep you grade high. She is a tough grader on homework, which can be time consuming, so don't procrastinate it.
Professor Brea is really, really good at teaching Spanish and she's really funny. There's a good amount of work to do but it's easy if you work decently hard.

Prof. Brea is the sweetest thing, she cares about her students education and is from Spain so is obviously very good at what she teaches. There's lots of homework but nothing that is unbearable. Her tests & quizzes are easy as long as you pay attention in class. I would 100% take a class w/ her again. She's so funny is available whenever you need.
Not bad to take for your Language requirement. Somewhat inconsistent with the syllabus, but she makes students aware when changes are made. She's fun and makes class enjoyable. I would recommend

Pretty easy professor who is really nice. Confusing at times and is fairly inconsistent with the syllabus.  Real fun however and makes a spanish surprisingly enjoyable.  Definitely one of the better professors out there and one whom I would recommend.
I like her as a person, and she is an OK teacher. If you go to class, and do the homework/diaries you will do well.

Fun teacher, but not especially clear. I always am unsure of when assignments are due and what to do on assignments. But if you know your spanish, her tests are really easy. haven't studied for one and get 95's. journal entries and essays are common. homework assignments take a while when using textbook. If you like fun classes I'd suggest this.

I really like brea. Shes really funny and very nice. Wasn't that difficult of a class but still a lot of work involved if u want a good grade. At the end of the year a lot of assignments were thrown at us and it got to be challenging and brought my grade down. Not a bad class but I wish it would have prepared me better for higher level SPN classes.

This must have been Brea's first time teaching Composition because she did not do a good job of it. I worked by butt off for a B-. No one went to class (I went everyday) and it didn't even matter because we did nothing substantial to help us with our writing. Our assignments were unclear and her feedback was useless. Learned nothing from her.

Brea is such a cute and funny lady, but I wasn't such a big fan of her teaching methods. She'll definitely go over new topics but there's going to be material that she won't cover, and you'll have to learn it on your own while studying. It's not too difficult or tedious though. She can be an easy A if you do study.

She was certainly a little loco and would reveal personal information about students to the class (things from e-mails, who dropped, etc.). Her teaching methods were frustrating and seemed pointless sometimes but the tests and hw were easy

Brea is great! She is really, really funny. She explains everything, including grammar, in Spanish, so be prepared to actually listen. Her requirements aren't bad. She makes class so entertaining, though!
shes really fun interesting a nice.. but not a great teacher per se.  i didnt learn much in her class. very unclear

This class was pretty much of a review for me, but helped me solidify a lot of things. She can sometimes be hard to follow, and if Spanish is really easy for you you might get bored. But she's nice, funny, and if you do your work you'll do well.
Although this was my lowest grade, it was my absolute favorite class to attend.  She is very funny and very helpful.  If you know anything about spanish you will have a much easier time then I did.
Nice professor, helpful, and knowledgeable of subject.
She's a very nice and funny lady who'll help you as much as she can. Her quizzes are mostly easy but her exams can be hard. I do think I could have put more effort in studying.

Entirely one of the sweetest professors I've had at Geneseo.  She genuinely cares about how you're doing, inside and out of the class, and is very understanding.  The hints during quizzes and tests don't hurt either. She once handed my quiz back to me seven times over to fix things on it. It was strange, but very nice of her to do.

Silly little lady and a good professor. Can grade hard on projects but an easy grader on tests and homework. Is very random and entertaining, gives lots of hints during quizzes and tests. Just don't forget to study your vocab and verbs!
She's very funny and sweet.  Her class can be a little confusing sometimes, but overall shes a good professor.
She's a sweet woman and she'll totally pass you if you act like you're really trying.
Buena, Buena, Buena

She's a little crazy but absolutely adorable.  If you struggle with spanish she'll try very hard to help you as long as you put forth the effort yourself.  She doesn't tend to assign too much work.  And if you fall behind she doesn't hold it against you.

Brea is the best.  She is the first spanish teacher that actually made the subject enjoyable.  She cares about how students do and helps in any way that she can.  It is an easy class as long as you look over the stuff real quick before class and do the homework.  Tests are sorta hard.

BEST TEACHER IN THE WORLD! She cares about you and your progress. She keeps class interesting, she is funny, organized and helpful. He tests can be on the hard side but she will help you in any way possible. HIGHLY HIGHLY RECOMENDED! YOU WANT THIS PROFESSOR!

was so helpful outside of class, very understanding and funny. She definitely made Spanish fun and if I had to take another semester of it, it would be with her. She works you hard, but if you go to class and pay attention, you'll do fine.  She really does care about how you do.

One of my favorite classes here so far!  She's a harder grader & she gives a lot of writing assignments.  On the other hand, however, you can retake conjugation tests as many times as you want.  A very funny woman and VERY helpful - HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!!!
I love Señora Brea!!!  She is hysterical and so cute.  She is a hard grader, but she lets you rewrite your papers and retake quizzes.  A lot of work outside of class.

Senora Brea is the BEST spannish teacher i have ever had!! She helps you in anyway possible and always make her class fun. She can be a hard grader, but you can re-take a quiz or test if you just plain messed up. Really I HIGHLY recommend her!! 10/10!
BEST SPANISH TEACHER EVA!!!!

She is a very fun teacher to have, and her quizzes are very easy, but her tests can be hard, but she will let you take them over so it doesn't really matter.  The only bad thing about her is that she doesn't really clarify what you are supposed to be doin

Easy tests and quizzes, very nice lady, occasionally her jokes aren't funny, but you have to laugh at her effort, at least she tries.  Highly recommended if you don't do well with foreign languages (at least for 102)
Crazy! Hard grader!
Awesome Professor!
If you really struggle with foreign languages this is the profesor to take.

I absolutely did not like this class. It was EXTREMELY repetitive, and he makes it VERY clear that he wants students to have this class be the main focus of their life. He loves theater, and is very passionate about it. He made me dislike theater completely, and want nothing to do with it. He reinforced why I love musical theater and not theater.

Professor Boucher is very passionate about his work. I really enjoyed the plays that we read in this class, they were very interesting. He is very angry if you do not show up to class, so make sure to attend all classes. He is an okay professor. Not someone I would want to take again. Sweet but a little over the top.

I took this online theater class thinking it would be an easy A. This class was fairly easy and manageable, but he is a harsh grader. I got points off for little things that I shouldn't have. I thought it was very unfair that he only gave us 30 minutes to complete a 30 question quiz that was not easy and very specific and detailed.

Ray is an amazing professor. Hes very laid back and doesnt require much effort; he does like to have class participation, but he doesnt force anyone to answer his questions. There is no final, just three module quizzes that were fairly easy if you did the previous assignments. Highly recommend him as a teacher, hes very fun to interact with.
tags: ['Amazing lectures', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Graded by few things']

comment: Great professor. Very passionate about what he does and always has a story to tell which makes the class interesting. Assignments are simple. Would highly recommend!

This class is an easy A. You can tell Boucher is very passionate about theater and from the lectures, I went to I did learn a lot from him! A test for each module and discussion posts based on plays we discussed. I highly recommend him, he is great!

Prof Boucher is a great teacher. Grades only on a few things but it's easy to get a 100. Most information is in the lecture notes (which are also posted on Canvas) and the textbook. Textbook material is dry but not difficult. He doesn't mind alternative ways to learning the material as long as you understand it.
Awesome guy, cannot recommend him enough. Just make sure you submit assignments on time and you're guaranteed an A. It's a super interesting class too.

txtbk used once for paper, borrow from friend. great acting advice, but strict grader. does not post assignment details on canvas, and forgets to explain them. a lot of emotional labor, but if you show up and meet with your partners outside class to rehearse you'll be fine. doesnt accept 'excuses', but cares about wellbeing

Without a doubt, Ray Boucher has been one of the best professors I've had so far. He takes the time to get to know each individual student, and really cares about your personal growth as an actor. He also gives AMAZING feedback. There is one book required for the class that there is a test on, but it's an easy read. HIGHLY recommend Ray's courses!
Amazing professor. Tests are basically vocab from the slides. Some plays to read from the textbook but not too bad. extremely easy class. Would recommend 100%

Drops the lowest test grade, tests really just come down to memorizing the lectures and plot of the readings we are assigned to read. You don't really even need to go to class to do well. This should be an easy A, I was just lazy and really didn't put any effort into this class. Ray is a great guy and makes his lectures rather interesting.

Ray is very kind. The material including the tests are pretty straightforward and easy. You have to pay attention and read in order to pass. The lectures are engaging because he talks to you and expects participation but doesnt force you. Hes passionate about theatre and teaching it. Even if you dont enjoy theatre you wont regret taking him.

Professor Boucher makes the course Introduction to the Theatre all the better. Not only do you learn a lot if you're taking this course for a GenEd credit or not, you actually become engaged with how rich the history of theatre is by the way he teaches. I definitely have a better appreciation for theatre now, all thanks to Professor Boucher.
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Graded by few things', 'Amazing lectures']

comment: He makes lectures enjoyable considering people take his class because it is a gen ed requirement. Attendance isn't necessary, but if you do want the A I suggest it because he explains things very well which helps for exams. Exams are straightforward, just make sure you READ THE PLAYS and study his slides. If you do you will most likely get the A.
Very good professor, he reads your work and gives good feedback, forgiving, easy going, easy grader, and I wish I could take another class with him!

class is easy as long as you do the basics. Show up to class and study a bit. Good to show up to class to know what is on the test specifically & class discussions are tested. do the extra credit. Lowest test gets dropped. You can skip the last test if you're happy with your grade. Highly recommend for fine arts gen ed, not a lot of work required

Easy and fairly interesting class. Very interesting and funny lectures. I enjoyed going to his class. A few plays and videos to watch outside of class but other than that lectures are online. Tests get harder as the class goes on but nothing too crazy. I enjoyed this class. Great teacher and very caring toward his students.

I didn't even like theater but he made class pretty enjoyable for me. Very fun and upbeat guy. Easy A class if you just study the slides and the gist of the plays. He gives you extra credit and drops the lowest test grade. I would take this class with him for an easy gen ed grade booster.

I took this class as a requirement - no interest in theatre whatsoever. He makes lectures interesting and posts the slideshow notes on canvas, so if you really wanted to, you could never go to class. Occasionally lets you out early. Only 4 exams, 1 quiz (on a play you have to see during the year). Very nice guy, easy class. Would recommend 100%

Lectures are a lot of fun. Attendance isn't mandatory but you'll do much better if you show up. You will have to read plays but he gives you a fair amount of time to do it, just make sure you keep track of what you need to read when because he doesn't remind you. Lecture is very interactive, but you don't have to participate if you don't want to.

Boucher is an amazing lecturer. I would definitely recommend him for your fine arts gen-ed. There are four exams and one required viewing of a play with a quiz the next class. All the powerpoints are posted online so it is possible to do well without attending class, although his lectures are great. Make sure you read the plays.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things', 'Amazing lectures']

comment: Tests are just memorization of terms and people. Need to read a few plays that aren't hard to read. Lectures can be boring. Easy fine arts credit. Extra credit assignment can give you 3 more % points to final grade.

It was an easy A over the winter session, there were a few things that were graded discussions were graded fairly easy as long as you were very well thought out the papers were not bad either although he is a little tougher about grammar. He also accessible through email pretty quickly so you can always reach out if you need help with anything.
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS', 'EXTRA CREDIT']

comment: Because Boucher is an actor he presents the material in an entertaining way-coming from someone who only took it for the credit. Easy A if you make flash cards for the tests. Sometimes it's helpful to show up to class because he'll emphasize information for the tests.

Take this class for an easy A for a fine arts credit. All of the notes are posted on a powerpoint so attendance isn't mandatory. The readings in the textbook are covered in the notes, but make sure you read the plays. Lots of easy extra credit, so take advantage of it.
tags: ['Clear grading criteria', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS', 'EXTRA CREDIT']

comment: 4 tests and 1 quiz. Posts notes online so you don't have to go but he makes everything super easy to understand if you do. Reading the textbook isn't necessary but reading the plays will help ensure you do good on the tests. Have to see one play. If you can memorize things easy and want an A for your fine arts credit this is the class for you.

He is really passionate about what he does but lets be honest, most people are looking for an easy A to get the fine arts credit over with. I would definetly take this class again but you do have to devote some time going over power points and plays if you want to do well
He is great and hilarious. test are medium hard, make sure to learn all slides and read plays. alot of extra cerdit to save your grade.

Boucher's lectures are mandatory if you want to pass but I always forget that because his classes are that good. He's hilarious, keeps everything upbeat, is honest and really shows that he's passionate about what he does and compassionate for his students. Super easy class, but not boring.

Boucher is one of the most interesting people I've met. His stories are so cool and his lectures are just all around fun. The tests are super easy if you take notes and listen in class. There are a few plays you need to read but they're great. If you do a worksheet with the play, you get bonus points.

Super chill, he'll tell you to call him Ray. Everything you do in class will be posted online in a powerpoint, so you don't really need to show up. However, discussion can actually be interesting and can certainly help you remember specific info. Graded based on four unit tests that are 40 multiple choice questions. Pretty much all memorization.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS', 'EXTRA CREDIT']

comment: Great professor who really cares about his students. Easy A IF you put in the work and read the plays he assigns. A lot of the questions on the tests are based off the plays you are assigned so read them. Also gives extra credit so take advantage and do it. Some questions on test are on what he says in class and not on slides.

He is a real homie, he takes boring lectures and somehow makes them hilarious and interesting. He expects a lot from you so all you need to pretty much is read the plays and go to class and pay attention. The lectures are actually funny and he sometimes gives you hints on the test. He's a real peach 10/10 recommend.

Not an easy A at all especially for a fine arts requirement. Could not get above a B- on any of the tests despite the fact that I felt like I was overstudying for theatre. However, lectures are always fun with Boucher. I never missed a class.

This class is NOT as easy A. It is way more work than what should be required for a 100 level theatre class. Even the theatre majors in my class didn't get an easy A. He makes the questions on the plays (which take hours to read) so specific. He also teaches each class as if it were theatrical performance and it gets old super quick.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria', 'TEST HEAVY']

comment: Ray was a great professor, he makes the topic interesting and you can see he really cares about theatre. His tests were easy, and he gives 10 points just for seeing a show. A fair professor, but you have to read the assigned plays or you won't pass the class.

Basically writing here to tell you not to buy the book if for class. There are readings from the book that are focused on the test, yes, but you can find all the readings online. Class if pretty easy if you do the readings and go to class. He also gave us an extra credit oppurtunity which was cool.

Only had 3n tests in the class. Had to go to one school production for easy 10pts to grade. Didn't have to show up to lectures only to tests. Couldn't pass class if you skipped tests. Lectures are fun and easy to follow along. Great class to get an easy A and to boost your GPA if needed. 10/10 would TOTALLY recommend

Super boring but you have to pay attention in lecture because he tests on the little things he says in class. Constantly goes on tangents. At least 10 VERY detailed questions on each play you read per exam. Decided he would offer one extra credit after people bombed the test, had to pay to go to the play and then write an essay on it.
tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'TEST HEAVY']

comment: I took Theater 100 in my first semester of freshman year and Boucher really made my very first semester memorable! He's a wonderful teacher who makes lectures interesting and easy to understand. There are only a few grades altogether but he offers extra credit and the tests are mostly definitions straight from his lectures. Would recommend!

Easiest class I have taken at SUNY Geneseo. Ray is super nice, and his lectures are very entertaining. If you pay attention in lecture you can pass the tests with minimal studying. He makes the class fun. Changes my concentration to Theater because I loved this class with him so much.

This was one of my FAVORITE classes, taken for Fine Arts GenEd credit.  Ray is AWESOME and he really tries to give you every opportunity to get an A. Tests are VERY fair and pretty easy if you know the material... just showing up will help you pass because the lectures are really helpful. He gives A LOT of extra credit, only 3 tests and 1 quiz
Easy class, but also fun. I didn't mind it at all.
tags: ['Clear grading criteria', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS', 'EXTRA CREDIT']

comment: Boucher was a pretty good professor.  It was a class i actually didnt mind getting up early for.  3 tests, and a quiz makes up the grade, but there is a lot of opportunity for extra credit.  I'm not a theatre person at all, i just took the class for my fine arts gen ed, but I definitely learned a lot in his class.

Boucher is amazing- makes lectures entertaining, provides examples of different theater styles in relatable ways (ex- a scene from Beauty and the Beast). Attendance isn't mandatory- powerpoints are online so you can catch up. Make sure you read the assigned plays or you'll fail the tests, but there are good extra credit opportunities just  in case.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria', 'EXTRA CREDIT']

comment: Makes an 8:30 not bad to go to! Attendance isn't mandatory but i'd go anyway because he gives really good lectures. Posts all the notes online and grades are only 3 tests and a quiz. Definitely a good fine arts credit class.

He's really passionate and has a really good way of explaining things so even boring topics seem interesting. He's very engaging, but participation isn't mandatory. The tests are super easy as long as you've paid attention (look over the textbook readings and listen in class), and he gives lots of opportunities for extra credit.
Thea100 is an easy a. That is if you put in the work, if you don't, get ready to be annoyed. he also gives an absurd amount of extra credit, so take advantage.

This class was supposed to be easy but it is my hardest class. He is really condescending and thinks he knows everything. Will ask really stupid questions and want to shoot yourself. Do not take, he is the worst. :(
Straight forward professor with semi-interesting lectures

Overall a wonderful teacher and experience. The class is fairly easy due to already having acting experience, but even if you don't he's quick to help, and will help you to personally grow. He is understanding and caring about disabilities. My only complaint is that he thinks he's really specific on what he wants for papers, but he really isn't.

As long as you read the plays, read the textbook, and attend class you will get an A. If you do one of those three things you will pass. The quizzes were all very easy. I got a 70 on the final and still got an A. He is very nice and interesting.

I did not expect to enjoy a 8am intro theater class, but he made lectures and discussion interesting enough that it was one of my favorite classes! He makes the class very discussion based, which makes it way more enjoyable. There's little to no textbook reading, but a lot of the test is from the lecture/discussions, so go to class and take notes.

He's super enthusiastic, and very well put-together. Always prepared for class, and enjoys class discussions ( you don't really need to participate, but pay attention!). Take advantage of his easy 10 ec points by volunteering in the theater because that saves your grade. Gives quizzes based on plays but you can take them at home. Take notes!!!
1010 would recommend. Boucher gives fantastic feedback and insight as long as you are willing to keep an open mind.

Boucher was a nice guy, and he used our semester as a guinea pig for doing online quizzes, which were pretty simple, definitely a grade booster. My main issue was he seemed unorganized, many quizzes had errors and we had to fight for answers. He changed things luckily, but it was frustrating. Also, asked very specific test questions.

I adored Dr. Boucher's lectures. Boredom is a rarity in his classes, and overall, it's a very nice way to earn your fine arts requirement. I am one that likes class discussion, and so this was the perfect class for me. I learned quite a bit over the semester, and would absolutely take another theater class with him. Read your textbook, folks!

Professor Boucher has a bad rep for being egotistical but I found him to be really funny and genuine! He clearly is well-educated in theatre and performance and is very understanding. He gives some great extra credit opportunities that barely anyone takes advantage of. If I was more interested in theatre, I would definitely take from him again!

For me, this class felt a lot harder than it was. If you show up for classes you will probably get a solid grade. If you do the readings and  take notes, an A is guaranteed. His extra credit is very helpful and fair. He is also gives generous curves on the mid-term and final exams. This is a good class to take for one fine art gen ed credit!

Get ready to read a ton of plays from your textbook because he gives 20 question quizzes on those plays almost every week. Not a lot of paper assignments but a ton of studying and you must go to class. Also, if you work behind the scenes on a show with Johnnie Farrell, you can get up to 10 extra credit points, which will really help.

I didn't like his personality at all, so I rarely attended class. However, it's easy as long as you use his website for notes and make sure to actually READ AND OUTLINE the text book because there can be questions on test from book  that aren't in the class notes. I found it helpful to read the plays then watch them on youtube. Do extra credit!!!!

Boucher has definitely made this class harder than before. The quizzes had confusing choices and sometimes asked really specific questions. You have to read the plays. GO TO CLASS because at least half of the test questions are class discussion based that cannot be found on his website. He can be kind of condescending but it's not too bad.

Nice guy. Easy to get an A -- if you go to class. A lot of test material is based on class discussion. So go! (I skipped a bunch of classes toward the end of the semester and the grade I got on my final reflected that). Quizzes are simple IF you do the readings, but you shouldn't expect to be able to just look at SparkNotes and get a great grade.
Read the plays and show up for classes and you'll get an A.

Overall pretty easy. Learned that he changed his quizzes to make them longer and slightly harder than past semesters, but otherwise, not too bad. His lectures are long and mostly him ranting about something unimportant. His notes are all on his website, so it's not completely necessary to come to class although tests are partly based on discussion.

Always complains about people skipping his class. Always complains when people leaves class after his quizzes. He's an easy A though. I had a perfect score throughout the class and just winged the final and still got an A. Really boring.

Take Acting with Ray Boucher! He is a real guru and will make you a much better actor. I was always impressed by the performances of my classmates after they received instruction from Boucher, and mine definitely improved over the course of the class. The class is almost all participation and effort with a paper or two. Best class, highly recommend

Great option for a fine arts requirement. The professor and information were easy to understand. He also makes it interesting. There's some general reading of plays required, but nothing unreasonable or that can't be handled. Overall, loved him and the class.

TAKE THIS CLASS. I AM TELLING YOU TO TAKE THIS CLASS. I missed half the classes, went in for the quizzes and the final exam and BOOM I got an A. I suggest you do go into class (even though it's 8:30) because though his quizzes can be sparknotes'd, his final is based on class material. Do the extra credit! It's an easy 5 point booster on your grade.
He's a good guy, but his ego is too much. His quizzes and tests are very easy, but he definitely carries a holier-than-thou attitude.
Very easy class but he tends to act out anything that he says which can be very annoying at 8:30 in the morning.

Easy A IF you read and GO TO CLASS! He helps attenders by telling what to study. He puts notes online. 2 exams (midterm and a final). A few small 10 question quizzes on the plays. Had to see one play on campus. As a Christian, I disliked the material because of its content. Also didn't enjoy his ego, but overall he was a "nice guy."
Great guy! learned so much from him and had a lot of fun doing it. Don't make him mad or he can be scary but for the most part he is always positive and fun. Take any class you can with him!

I would only recommend this class if you are looking for an easy A. However to have him as a professor, I would not recommend him at all. He is very cocky and even though he is extremely enthusiastic for 8 am, he ego is hard to listen to

Great professor! The class is an extremely easy was to get an A. Such a nice guy, but make sure you don't text during his lectures, because he WILL call you out on it in front of everyone. Highly recommend this class for a fine arts requirement!!!!

You can tell he really loves theather and really know a lot about it which is very refreshing. He makes class exciting and engages the students. I love his class it is really a great way to start off the day.
Lectures were straight from his notes online, tests were straight from the notes. Very easy class. Ray can be frustrating with his occasional rants but overall a decent experience.

As someone with no interest in theatre, Boucher made the class surprisingly enjoyable.  He loves theatre and his passion resonates in the class.  He got me interested in it, and for something that I never thought would happen, that's saying someting.
Fantastic guy. Engaging and fun. Made theatre a joy to go to 8:30 MWF

Professor Boucher is great! I was not looking forward to theatre, but he makes it so interesting and fun to learn about theatre. I actually enjoy theatre now and appreciate it more than I used to. He's a great guy and very clear in his expectations. Take him if you get the chance, you won't regret it!

such a pleasure to work with. Boucher is such an animated teacher who's enthusiasm is infectious. I appreciated his humbleness and willingness to work with his students regardless of their individual level of skill. Acting I is a fun and easy class for sure, but Boucher just makes it 10x better. Couldn't have asked for more

BOUCHER!!!! Such a great professor! Everything is pretty much class discussion with an easy paper every couple of weeks. Only complaint was how much out-of-class time was needed for the final project, which isn't hard anyway. Great sense of humor. I always looked forward to his class.

This class is by far the easiest way to fulfill a fine arts requirement. I attended the first class, the days papers were due, the midterm, and the final, and never looked at the textbook and still managed an easy B+.  If you go to class you're in for a definite A.

Got an A. I have no interest in theatre, but he is well-spoken and makes it somewhat interesting. I only took notes if the info wasn't on his website. Read through the notes 4 times or so before the exams and know the writers/works. Plenty of extra credit available if you need it. If you skip, make sure you watch the videos on your own.

Boucher's class was fun, sarcastic and easy. I didn't attend most of the classes, but I wish I had dragged myself out of bed and went. I ended up getting an A- but could have easily gotten an A had I gone to more classes. Highly suggest him.

By far one of the best teachers I have had at Geneseo, especially in the SOE! She is extremely helpful, accommodating, and knowledgeable, plus just an overall fun, happy person. TAKE A CLASS WITH HER!
A wonderful teacher who is extremely clear about expectations.  Everything she teaches is meaningful and valuable.  She is always willing to help and provides a lot of support.  Fabulous!

She is a nice lady who is knowledgeable about the subject. Sometimes she was difficult to understand, but not bad. She would often change her answers to questions about assignments. Class overall is not difficult. Tests are online. Not a bad teacher overall.

Dr. Jung is awesome. Even though sometimes you can't understand a word of what she says, she will continue to reexplain herself to help. There were a lot of handouts in this class but I think I really learned a lot.

Professor Becker was a great chemistry professor! I understood so much more of the material by having him as a teacher, and I did much better than I expected to do! He's very friendly and approachable, and funny in class! Would definitely recommend.

Prof. Becker was a great teacher, very clear on what he wanted you to know for exams, and his exams were concept based and fair. Pay attention in class, do practice/old exams, and do all the homeworks (not many of them) and you'll do well. I highly recommend taking chem with him! I learned more chem from him than any other geneseo teacher thus far!

Becker is a good professor but he isn't always on his game. While he will teach everything that you need to know he makes mistakes on his lecture slides and sometimes his test answer keys. He'll give you back the credit if you catch them thought. I'd recommend him as a professor.

Professor Becker is a great teacher. He makes the material easy to understand. And his lecture is always the first one to run out of space. Some times he cracks corny jokes to lighten up the mood. Super nice guy!
Very friendly and helpful! Pretty Easy grader, is willing to explain anything you don't understand. I really enjoyed having him as a teacher

He is a great professor and teaches the class in a fun manor and is very approachable. Walking through halls he knows who's in his class. He also has a lot of hw that greatly helps GPa. Tests are fair and he gives out reference tables to help with them. My favorite professor so far.
Very easy!! he has lots of homework to boost gpa. in class assignments for extra credit. He also drops the lowest test score out of 4 tests!

I can easily say she is by far the worst prof I've ever had. I learned next to nothing from her class; most of it was wasted as she focused on the format she wanted us to have for the final paper without actually teaching us anything. She cared abt format > content. The many assignments were just busy work that didn't benefit us. Avoid at all costs
Professor Heller is very knowledgeable in her field of work, she made my least favorite class very enjoyable. If you have the chance, take a class with her

Dr. Heller is my favorite professor at Geneseo by far. Her experience in the field (4 deployments overseas) and her genuine care for the subject matter and her students make her far superior to any other professor I've ever taken. Participation is 20% but she makes it SO easy to be involved in class discussion. Grades are based only on papers.

There are two midterms which are very specific and no amount of time studying will make you do well, but homework grades make up for this. ily
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Lots of homework', 'Accessible outside class']

comment: Professor Aimers has a lot of homework for each class. I never found the reading boring. The homework is typically a 10question vocab quiz and 14 short responses. They will be based off the reading or videos, all of which are very interesting. The midterms are VERY specific. Review EVERYTHING and do it well. Not too challenging :) he's very kind

Aimers made me loved going to anthro class every time. While attendance is not mandatory, you are graded on your overall participation. He does't exactly explain assignments in class but it is all on canvas with plenty of time to do them. His lectures where fun and interesting and he has a lot of experience. Good class to take!!

Amazing professor. He clearly knows his subject matter well but is willing to admit that he doesn't know everything about everything. I think people give him a lower score because participation is so heavily weighted but he makes it so easy to participate and he really wants you to so it's your own fault if you don't. He wants to help you succeed.

He is very passionate about his work, which you can clearly see. However, he seems to assume that everyone is majoring in anthropology when this isnt the case. I took it my first semester of freshman year, and it was challenging. His grading criteria is difficult as no one got a 100 this year on either of the 2 major written assignments.

comment: Extremely vague, subjective grading style. Poorly structured class. Expect long, dry readings for homework and a participation portion that ranks students based on how often they speak in relation to other students in the class.
tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass."]

comment: He is very passionate about his field and that is quite clear, but his attitude is frustrating. The questions on the test are either common sense or super detailed. Participation is really important, but the chances to participate are limited. The final includes an essay portion in which you write three essays and he only grades one of them.

Definitely wouldn't take his class again. Not even sure why my advisor placed me in it during my first semester. Lectures are very boring and so are the readings. He expects a lot which can be expected from a professor but he's vague about what he expects. You'll find out what he expects after the assignment is graded.

He is definitely very passionate about his field and although the material itself is not very difficult, he is a very harsh grader. He was also harsh in the participation grade despite the fact that I never missed a class. He provides very little feedback for his grades. If you read the text you can get a good grade.

You have to read the textbook to pass the course!!  for the most part the class isn't very hard but it is time consuming and you need to put in effort. about three short writing assignments that require some research, and three tests total (including the final). The tests are hard. His lectures can be interesting if you care about the subject.

He knows a lot about anthropology, but expects that out of his class. It's an intro class and he wants us to be anthropologist. Test are super hard and really specific and he grades essays insanely hard. Good Luck! I wouldn't recommend ANTH 100 with him.

Aimers is a great guy who is very passionate about his field. Participation is a big part of your grade so keep that in mind. There are tons of opportunities participate in class and there are interesting discussions to take part in. He manages to keep his class fresh and interesting. Definitely take this class. He is a great guy!

James Aimers is an incredibly knowledgable professor so if you are thinking about majoring in Anthropology, he is a very good professor to take. However, if you are just taking the class for credit, I would try and go with someone easier. I learned alot but didnt do very well. Also participation is graded on a curve, which makes it very competitive

Very experienced expert in his field, so if you're looking for a career in Anthropology, it might be a good idea to get to know him. And that's easy, given that he's so friendly.  But. His teaching style was nonexistent -- everything was taught to us by other students via group projects. Probably would've been very interesting if he taught it.

Be careful. He doesn't outline assignments well at all in class, can be quite pompous and somewhat rude, and apparently has no problem dropping your grade down an entire letter and a half despite perfect attendance that is supposedly worth only 10% of your grade.

Yes, he's hard. But if you do all the work, you can manage a B easily. He spreads his grades out on assignments such as the textbook material and posting onto the school's wikipedia page. He's also very helpful if you e-mail or go to him. I didn't really pay attention in his class but I did all the work. Test grades were average but managed an A-.

Very knowledgeable in the field, many published works, will poignantly spot mistakes, reads every line of every bibliography and then gives you a good grade with opportunity to revise.  As a general rule--just take my word for it: read all assigned material TWICE before the test, and hope you don't read slowly or have ADD definitely not High School

took cultural anthro, really fun class! He showed interesting clips and kept powerpoints interesting and helpful. Need to read the book for the quizzes but the nice part is that the quiz questions tend to show up on the exam. The writing assignments are challenging but fair. Tests aren't hard.

Thought this class would be a lot easier, esp since I had already taken a 200 level anth course. Well, I was wrong. I like Aimers a lot as a professor but he definitely expected a lot out of the students for an intro level class. Tests were harder than expected but bearable. The material was interesting but I just couldn't devote the time to it.

Highly enthusiastic teacher. Reading quizzes require you to do the reading but they are a big grade booster. The wiki assignments were relatively short and easy considering they were the bulk of the final grade, and he makes it clear what he wants from each assignment and gives constructive feedback which is useful in improving your writing.

Good teacher. He was clear on what he wanted from every assignment (detailed assignment documents are available online) and gave clear and sufficient feedback. Really interesting material and he's quirky, but engaging. The reading quizzes are really thorough. Tests are specific, but all multiple choice. Don't take for an easy A, but it's worth it.

Seems laid back in class, but he is a very hard professor. If you dont like reading or writing WIKI entries in 400 words or less on a chapter 170 pgs. long, then DO NOT TAKE! He is a stickler on citations, and grammar. He is not afraid to tear your paper apart. And his main form of testing is multiple choice...and not the easy kind either.
I have to agree with the two previous comments. The professor can be particular and critical with grading, yet scatterbrained when it comes to the lectures. I regret taking this class.

I like him, he has a fun, energetic vibe that made his classes somewhat interesting. I'm glad I took this class because you really realize that a lot of american ways of doing things aren't the only ways, there are many other equally valid ways of doing things. This class isn't an easy A though, so don't take it for that.

Weekly online quizzes, and article reading. Final paper on Material culture was kinda tough. Powerpoint posted after each lecture. Very Nice and helpful, and enthusiastic about subject matter. Will reference his Maya Archaeologist site alot. Recommend, not highly but he's a good guy.

An interesting class, though this could be largely related to the subject matter. Fairly substantial reading with weekly reading quizzes. You will find out what material culture is, and write, what I found to be, the most difficult essay I have written for a 100 level class. Very serious about plagiarism.

He is a very intelligent man who knows what he's talking about. He puts all slides from class online. A participation grade is required and is somewhat difficult to achieve since everything is clear. I wouldnt recommend this course as a core since there are easier courses offered. Extremely hard to get an A. Is very strict with plaigerism.
i liked this class a lot, it was very interesting. i would definitely recommended taking a course with him.

nice guy however I DON'T RECOMMEND THIS COURSE IF YOU WANT AN A his lectures are interesting and easy to understand however tests are specific and more difficult than necessary he also grades the paper too harshly. he is one of those professors who give As VERY SPARINGLY

He's undoubtedly an intelligent man with a great personality and great interest in what he teaches. He uses power point and many visual (and auditory) aides to support the material. However the level of his expectations for a 100 level class are significantly higher as are his standards in grading. The class is interesting but certainly a challenge

awesome guy, really helpful. he has easy online quizzes to boost your average. tests are fairly easy but he has some really specific questions that aren't really fair. only one paper, 1500 words. we all had to lead a debate on a controversy with 3 other people. again, nice guy but more work than some of the other 100 level courses
AWesome professor, he is real nice and love for people to ask question so he can answer them, very liberal and easy-going! I will recommend anyone to take his class!

Tests based on lectures. Plays music before class and shows videos. A very nice intro to anthropology. One text book is hard to comprehend (Woodward) but he does go over them in lectures and answers your questions on it. I would recommend this class
I've only had him a month and I've learned so much. I've always been interested in Anthropology and he has made my introduction into this field very enjoyable. He's really fun!
not a very hard class. very easy going and willing to answer any questions.
People who do poorly in Technical Theatre usually didn't do the readings. Pay attention and take notes, even on the readings, which you should do. Ask questions. Very kind and understanding.

johnnie is by far the best theatre professor/ the best professor in general at the entire school. such a sweetheart and cares so much about his students. He is so passionate about the stuff he does, if you have a chance to take a class with him do it! Always willing to walk things through with you, not much work, does take attendance.

Johnnie is an amazing professor. We met for only 50 minutes a week on Friday. The class was simple and was graded out of 10 points. Show up and participate in the class, and you get a 10/10 for the day. You get one grade dropped at the end of the semester. The activities are nothing hard, Johnnie will walk you through everything. Would recommend!!

comment: Really nice guy but a 94 in the class is a B+ so expect to get a lower grade even if you work really hard. Lectures are extremely boring and very long time-wise but exams are solely based on what he says in class. There arent a lot of assignments so it's easy to keep up with but I just wouldn't take this class unless you're a theatre major.

Open office hours, and very nice man. no pp presentations, lectures are all just him standing at the front and explaining terms. online tests are open note, use your textbook for those. tests are difficult mostly from a 'list everything in this category', which makes it easy to lose points. 40 mandatory hours of stage crew, most positions manual

comment: Johnnie Ferrell is a great guy, but I don't recommend this class if you don't intend on studying something similar. The Production Crew is a bit of time-consuming work outside of class. The class seems a little over the top for a Gen-Ed, but he's a very nice guy.

Very nice guy but his class is extremely boring and he seems to forget that not everyone in the class was a theatre major. I had a hard time paying attention because the lectures were extremely boring and tests were sometimes difficult because he named things in class differently than the textbook did. Was an extremely boring class and professor.

Definitely cares and deadline lenient but goes on and on about stuff that isn't really in the textbook or pertains to class. No slide presentation or notes to copy, talks too quickly and randomly to really take many good notes of your own. Texts are unnecessarily hard for the class, not all the information is in the textbook or talked about.

Johnnie is a literal gift from heaven. He is so accommodating and willing to help, you just have to keep communication open with him. He knows so much about lighting and tech theatre and is just such a great person. He's so easy to talk to and has some great stories. If you show up to class, you'll pass.

If you aren't interested in technical theatre the class is boring. His lectures are boring and he more often than not gives the wrong textbook pages. His exams are extremely hard and no matter how much studying/reading of the textbook you do, you will struggle. I will say he is lenient when it comes to the technical reviews and prop papers.

Johnnie has a heart of gold and is willing to help his students out, especially when theyre going through a rough time. Lectures can be dull, but Johnnie is so passionate and such a nice guy its worth it. Also sometimes treats class with food while doing stage crew work. Johnnie deeply cares about and recognizes students he sees are trying.
you definitely wont get an A if you dont study but the assisgnments are easy, makes you do outside work for criedt like go to plays and working stage crew for a week. lecture are SOOOO dry and boring

Johnnie is such a great guy! Class is a little dull if you aren't super into theatre, but that being said, I learned a lot from his class. He is such a sweet guy you wouldn't want to disappoint him. A bit of work just for gen-ed, but I'd say worth it for Johnnie.
Johnnie is so nice! His class may be a little boring when you have to watch videos. A large chunk of your grade is participation in a stage crew.

I found this class super boring, but definitely go to class, its only MW, and its way easier to learn the boring info from him than try to read it in a textbook.  You also have to do 45 hours of crew work, which sucks and takes up valuable evening/weekend time, but was super easy.  Johnnie is also a great guy and super willing to help anyone out

Class is easy, but the assignments can take awhile. There aren't a ton, but you'd definitely have less work taking thea 100 instead of Johnnie's class. If you do take this class, know that an A is a 97 (Johnnie is a SUPER easy grader, 9.8/10 on assignments is easy) and you'll spend 45 hours doing crew in lieu of Friday class. Johnnie is awesome.

Fantastic professor and great guy overall. Super nice and is willing to help you with anything. Really loves what he does and it shows. Has you go about the theatre space and learn by doing. If you are a theatre person, take his classes. You won't regret it. Being on a build/light crew with him is a lot of fun and highly recommended.
Super nice guy, easy class. tests are really straight foreword and there's a lot of partial credit opportunities.
Johnnie is great, he is very nice and loves what he does. His class is easy if you go and pay attention, and the tests are very straight forward.

Took Theatre Tech with Johnnie, and he is the nicest person I have ever met! He's my favorite professor by far. Easy tests. You get to build the sets for plays & musicals. Such a nice person to work with!!! I recommend this class for anyone.
Great class if your seriously interested in lighting design. Very abstract class, one exam but mostly based on class discussion and participation. Recommended for basically any class.

Johnnie is seriously one of the nicest people I know. If you show interest and talk to him he really knows his stuff. He's kinda disorganized with class lectures but I recommend going anyway as a lot of the exam material is lecture based. Crew hours count for 33% of the grade so make sure you get them done. This is not a passive learning class.
Great guy, fun and easy class. Enough Said.

Avoid this class, crew hours are the biggest load of it ever. Its ridicuolous out of class hours for a 3 credit class. Dont even go to class and tests are the most pathetic excuses ever. he as a person is as flaky as they get. BORING TERRIBLE CLASS

Johnnie is AWESOME.  Had two classes with him; he's also my boss at stage crew.  Really nice guy, rambles sometimes, but pretty funny and really does what he can to help you out.  Show up every day and you'll do fine.
as long as you come to class you get an automatic A+ = )

Of course this wasn't the most fun class in the world, but Johnny is seriously a gem. He tries his hardest to make it interesting, and you actually feel terrible when you don't go to class, simply because you don't want to let him down.

THEA 130: very nice man, but frikin BORING class. (though I suppose it's hard to make nails and screws interesting...) don't take it if you're looking for a FUN way to fulfill a fine arts. THEA 129: still a nice man, much more enjoyable class... we actually build and do stuff.
Johnnie is the most personable professor that I have ever had.

Best class ever

This is man has to be one of the kindest sweetest guys alive.  He is always busy but will always find time for you and he genuinely wants to help his students...  His classes are laid back and fun but educational
Very cool guy.  Always busy cause he's involved in everything, but he's willing to work with you.
one of the nicest, most easy-going professors you will ever meet.  he really cares about his students.  easy grader.

Fall semester 2022 was his first year teaching. Class is extremely disorganized. There are two textbooks required for the course, one of which we didn't use. His class is extremely lecture heavy and hard to pay attention to. Although he helps guide students with studying, we skipped multiple chapters due to disorganization.

It's pretty basic stuff. A lot of it is all in knowing your terms. I haven't read a single page of the book and still get high grades on HW and exams.
Exams are on paper.
Super nice guy overall. He does talk a lot, but he obviously is telling us everything from his business experience, which is awesome, because he's not a teacher but a businessman.

Professor Tang's class suffered from a significant lack of organization. Assignments/quizzes were frequently handed out with barely legible writing in both English and Chinese, and contained frequent errors. Additionally, students are required to provide their personal phone numbers for the class.

do not take her class if you don't really want to learn Chinese.

Professor Tang is a very sweet person. But she would frequently ramble during the class about unrelated topics. Use Taiwanese standards for a Mainland Chinese class. Had unrealistic expectations to speak Chinese at an almost fluent level. She was inconsistent on grading standards/expectations.

Professor Tang repeatedly overstepped personal boundaries, gave unsolicited advice, gossiped ab ppl, & exhibited narcissistic qualities. Students who defend her for having good intentions need to recognize that intentions don't matter as much as impact. So many ppl dropped the class when I took it. Class was disorganized & expectations inconsistent

Do not take this class! You will end up not learning or understanding anything. Professor's english isn't good and is incredibly hard to understand what she's saying. Long class, No canvas, or any technology allowed. Also just really unorganized and too close with students. She has called me on the phone several times for being late to class.

Professor Tang is one of the most caring professors. If you respect her, she will respect you. I took her for Chin 102, 201, 202 and she honestly cares for her students. ridiculous rules like no water, can't leave to go to the bathroom, must remind teacher to hand in homework or no credit is received. Can be very unclear with what's being asked. I definitely do not recommend taking this class. AVOID AT ALL COSTS. You will most likely not learn anything. I took the class wanting to learn chinese because I have always been interested but I did not learn anything.

Professor Tangs Chinese class is without a doubt one of my favorite classes here in Geneseo. She is an extremely caring teacher which forwards a lot of moral integrity. Very sweet woman who is very invested in her students' progress. If you do not do the work assigned, you will not do well. Do the best to avoid this teacher! she has no ethice and unprofessional, you will get confused in the class as she misrepresents the Chinese culture and she lack of knowledge about Chinese even though she came from China. Jasmine Tang is without a doubt the most helpful professor I have ever worked with. She will go far out of her way to help students genuinely interested in her course. One of the best people I have ever had the pleasure to meet.  Jasmine will go out of her way (and I mean farr East out of her way) to help her students She is caring and wants her students to learn! She's fabulous and hot! I just love her classes! She would provide us with everything which has to do with Chinese culture! Learn from her and you can know a big country! It's fun especially when you would like to go on a trip to China! Just kidding!

This professor is a superior! Great teacher! Fun to be in her class!

Excellent teacher. Although in earlier posts, people accuse her of "yelling", or "playing favorites", I believe she means well and wants us all to learn. Her dedication and desire for us to succeed is reflected in every class.

Pankratz is my favorite professor at Geneseo, and even though I haven't take her in a while, I will talk to her from time to time.

Professor Pankratz is a wonderful professor. She knows her material really well and she cares about her students.

AWESOME PROFESSOR. Stop what you're doing at this very moment and go register for her class. Incredibly helpful and approachable--TAKE HER CLASS.

Such a great professor. Makes everything easy to understand and wants you to do good. Very understanding and kind.
an absolute gem. makes lectures fun and always does activities to better understand the material. applies real world conflicts to what we're learning. 10/10 would take again.

She has been my favorite professor and class of all time. Her lectures are engaging and she shares stories and videos and is super funny. All her powerpoint on on canvas. Dr. Showers is a very go with the flow person. There's no set lecture schedule, grading scale or breakdown of assignments. Dr. Showers is reasonable but the grading criteria seems harsh given the amount of questions that are on the quizzes but not found in any of the readings. Your notes can only get you so far when some of the answers to questions aren't even able to be derived from them.

Quizzes were kind of hard but the class as a whole wasn't bad we didn't have a final or many assignments.

HPE was really easy to complete, but I often had to retake assignments due to how they crossed over from canvas. Hopefully these issues are straightened out for next semester because otherwise the course was straightforward and easy to complete.

THIS WAS SO BAD. THERE IS NO REASON WE SHOULD NOT BE ABLE TO SEE WHAT WE DID WRONG ON  QUIZZES, HOW ARE WE SUPPOSED TO LEARN MATERIAL IF WE CAN'T SEE WHAT WE ARE DOING RIGHT AND WRONG. I actually took WGST - 205. The class was interesting and Dr. Rutkowski was very nice and a good person. However, I took this thinking it would just be a fun extra class but it was a lot of work. ENGL 458: Louisa May Alcott. Rutkowskis the GOAT. Every English major should take one of her classes. The English program here is great, but we hit a lot of interesting concepts that were more interesting than the text may have been at face value.

You will never receive a 100 but always a 95 if you try so you still get an A. Don't take the class if you're not passionate about LGBTQ+ topics and issues as it's heavily based on that but if it is something you are passionate about 100% take it. Also Alice is amazing and funny

comment: I took ENGL467 with Rutkowski and LOVED IT! We have one quiz and one discussion post a week that go with readings, and one final paper for course work. She has all of her texts provided via link and Brightspace, so you also don't have to buy any books. She is a lovely, witty professor! Definitely consider taking her, she's now one of my faves

I actually took WGST 205 but that wasn't an option. I like Dr Rutkowski a lot as a person, but she is so so as a professor. We didnt have a syllabus for a few weeks which stressed me out, sometimes the class went totally off topic and she never redirected. Work load was really easy, until it wasn't and we had multiple things to do in the last week.

Best WGST professor. Hands Down. I assume that RAs or education majors would have to take this class, but if you just want an easy A or even a job opportunity in the future, take this class! Alice is such a nice person and genuinely cares for her students both inside and outside of class hours.

Safe Zone training program. amazing resource to meet other allies and members of the LGBTQ+ community educators on campus. grades very easily except on final reflective paper, where you should pay attention to grammar. has students pick textbooks and facilitate program. so supportive for tough circumstances

showstopping, incredible, amazing. great feedback, but harshest grader i've had. 12 page paper for final, but you'll be well prepared. uplifts student voices and perspectives. based on in class discussions, but easy to make up with special assignments

comment: She is a DOLL. So sweet, but make sure you participate- it is a participation/convo-based class. It was all online this semester, so things were a bit different but she was still a rockstar. Get all of the texts she asks you to get because they will be used for class. Her quizzes are easy and essays are fair and never too long or tedious.

Prof. Rutowski genuinely loves teaching, and it's plain to see. Her (online) classes were enjoyable and I genuinely felt regret if I missed any for a reason. The work she assigns is complimentary to each other and makes sense, though for this specific course, was pretty depressing at first. I recommend her if she continues teaching WGST classes

I am currently taking two classes with this professor and she is' awesome. She doesn't just ramble on and on like many other professors. She connects with her students and os very understanding. We also get a break during our hour and 45 min class which isn't required to have a break.

This Fem&Porn course contains A LOT of reading assignments, and the class only consists of discussions. She tends to interrupt while students are speaking to interject her viewpoints. The papers are comparable to a 300 level (challenging criteria, very conceptual). She is passionate and nice, but I wouldn't recommend. Too challenging to enjoy.

I had taken her for humn as a soph, and after all I heard about how hard HUMN is, I was delightfully surprised with her class. She is insanely caring, funny, and will help you if you need it. Beware, there are quizes every day but if you read and take some notes they are easy As each time. Only two papers and one final. I absolutely loved her!

Far too harsh of a grader, even after seeing her about one of the papers I still received a bad grade. There is a quiz EVERY DAY- if you skip class your grade will drop every day as you will receive a 0 on a quiz. Quizzes are so difficult that even after reading the books I didn't know the answers. No extra credit.A good person but not a good prof.

comment: Not an "easy A" for sure, but hands down the most influential professor and class I've ever taken. You read, you'll do fine. Tips: GO TO CLASS and take good notes and mark down page numbers when she says them to refer back to

An unreasonable amount of reading, even for an English class. The class was discussion based, but her questions didn't facilitate interesting discussions and she often rushed through people's explanations. She's helpful for the writing process, but her grading criteria is very unclear and seemed somewhat subjective

I'd say Professor Rutkowski is easily one of the best professors to take if you're new to the major (or just want a cool lens to look at 19th century literature through). Interested in queer/gender theory? You'll Iove any of the classes she teaches. Overall, a fun and laid back classroom experience. She wants you to get an A.

She's pretty fair but if class discussion isn't up to her standards, she gets really angry. She is a harsh but fair grader, and I didn't realize how hard the grading would be based on how easy everything else is. The readings are insane. 200+ pages sometimes between classes and forum postings have to be done way before class, which makes you rush.

Great teacher. She is very knowledgable and loves what she does. There are several readings throughout the course, but most of them are very interesting. It is a discussion class, so participation is graded. There are also weekly forum postings, but she lets you miss 2 of them. She is very helpful is asked and overall a great person.

She get's really into all the texts and she is a tough grader. Make sure you have someone check over your work before handing in anything. The class is very interesting but majority of the readings are really dry!!!

Professor Rutkowski's "Voices and Perspectives" class was a very interesting class to attend, being based exclusively on discussion, the best way to study Literature. Her grading was never clear though, and papers were tough to do very well on. Aside from that, she gave simple reading quizzes and one group project (also tough grading).
The class itself is wonderful- great discussion, and Prof. Rutkowski is so fun and interesting. It is hard to get As on her papers though, and she's never totally clear on what you did wrong

Do not take an Alice Rutowski class... shes one of those teachers who gives you a bad grade if your work doesnt reflect her thoughts/opinions on a topic. One of the worst classes I took at Geneseo in my four years. AVOID HER AT ALL COSTS

I love Alice Rutkowski. She always has an incredible amount of energy; sometimes it's even hard to keep up. Professor Rutkowski is very passionate about what she teaches and it come across in the way she teaches it. Class was entirely discussion based and you didn't have to talk but your grade would suffer if you didn't occasionally chip in. She makes the class fun and doesn't mind going off topic a bit. Prof. Rutkowski is extremely nice. Class went quick for an hour and a half and the readings very actually interesting. She treats the class as an equal discussion and interjects with her own points. Worth it.

Amazing I learned lots of stuff... The end of the class you view movies and her choices were awesome! if you can take a class with her do it!

ugghh... she is way too bent on "creative teaching" and class discussion.. but she is a nice lady. Her grading is a little too tough and she is unclear with what she wants.

I learned a lot through doing the research myself and he is encouraging,

Not every class is that rewarding.

comment: Dr. Brubaker is a great professor and a fun guy. Lectures and thorough and interesting. He is always happy to help and wants you to succeed but you do have to work. comment: Professor Brubaker does not give out easy As, but if you work hard it is 100% achievable! Barnabas is a great teacher for organic. He is the most helpful professor I have ever had at Geneseo. The subject matter isn't easy but he does a good job telling you what you should really know and focus on.

Hands down one of the best professors at Geneseo. Overall not a hard lab at all if you do your work and show up to lab. If youre confused he is more than happy to help. There is no reason that you should come out of this class without an A if you put the effort into it. DEFINITELY TAKE HIM FOR 119

Obviously he knows a lot about the material, but he struggles to covey all of that to students. Some tests were impossible and others were way too easy to make up for the hard ones. Just use the book to teach yourself and do practice problems and you'll be fine.

Really nice person. helpful. class is bases mostly on textbook, so if you read your textbook and do the hw problems you should be good. takes student opinions for test. Pretty Good teacher. Slightly easy grader.
Horrible. With the curve you'll probably get an okay grade but if you need orgo for the mcats or biochem, stay away. He is essentially a rambling idiot in class.

Whoever decided to let barnabas teach orgo must have been high. We didnt get to 4 chapters that all the other orgo classes got to, and the tests were totally random. Worst professor I have had at geneseo thus far.

Barnabas is the worst thing that has happened to the chem program at geneseo. i learned nothing, taught myself everything. He is incoherent, dumb and could not answer any questions during class. Great guy but grade depends on T.A. if you have someone whose name begins with a K quit, but Barnabas is one of the nicest guys, and always willing to help.
Barnabas made lab interesting and fun and always tried to make everyone happy.  Grades have a lot to do with who your TA is but for the most part the class is easy.

Always ready to help so long as you are an honest, hard-working student.  Constantly repeating his mantra "Stay happy" :) Easy to get along with and makes lab enjoyable even though it's still a lot of work.
Great guy, but the curve is unfair. An 88.9 is a B.

Barnabas is a nice guy. I'm not amazing at Chemistry, so I didn't do so well, but he really tries to help and he tells a lot of jokes. He genuinely cares about the students too.

I would highly recommend lab with Barnabas. He's always extremely helpful and happy.  Promotes "Planting for 100% Harvest" and "stay[ing] happy."  Such a great professor and human being!  (Note: there is a final exam for lab; save your pre-labs!)

Barnabas is one of the funniest and nicest professor i have met so far. Chemistry is his 2nd passion, right behind Golf (haha). He has office hours in which he is willing to help you solve problems and understand lab procedures. He also has TAs that have their own office hours to check your work.

Everyone at Geneseo should meet Barnabas.  Coolest, most down-to-earth guy ever.  Helpful with labs, and gives great life advice to boot.  Chem lab itself is very picky with grading, but he doesn't do the grading, LI's do.  My favorite prof here.

This class is very difficult.  Although I am not particularly apt in sciences, I don't feel like I get enough practice at the things he teaches.  He says things once and you never really hear about it again.  Tough office hours, but a very genuine approachable guy, the class and material are confusing but I'd like to think he does the best he can.

I must admit his attempts at cheerful wisdom were a bit annoying. However, he is a good, helpful lab instructor and his pre-lab advice can be invaluable (especially because the student instructors don't know how to answer your questions so often).

barnabas is the coolest person on the planet.  he is amazing, and he will help you with anything.  he is really the nicest guy ever.  he is willing to clear anything up and spend as much time with you as you need.  he is smart and just really awesome.  you definitely want him as a prof.  he rocks.

Absolutely the nicest guy ever.  He is so willing to help you...go to office hours if you need help.  I found chem lab was picky with grading...I followed each lab word for word and still only had a B+.  Keep a good notebook!  Highly recommend Barnabas!!

Nice, funny, and helpful, but sometimes he can try to trick you as to what assignments are due when. Do not skip pre-lab by any means. Make sure you know where he is during lab because there's no guarantee your ULI will be useful.
I loved Barnabas. He just wants everyone to be happy. I would recommend his class to anyone.

Barnabas is a great lab instructor!  He is always willing to help if you are having trouble, or just chat and make sure you are "staying happy and having fun!"  If you can take a lab with him, I highly recommend it.

Barnabas is a great guy. I've had him as a lab instructer for 2 semesters  and I recommend him to others. He'll help you stay happy in a frusterating course.

Very acecssible and helpful. He wants you to pass as much as you do. You have to do the work, but he will help you if you get stuck.

genuinely sweet and very enthusiastic about the subject matter. a great lab instructor - very patient and understanding and accessible.

Barnabas is the man!  He's very friendly and very helpful; he's easy to flag down in lab if you need help, and even if you don't need help he'll come up to you and give you suggestions or just see how you're doing.  If you can take a lab with him I highly recommend it.

Unorganized. Isn't spectacular about responding to emails. Constantly clears her throat when giving a lecture. Writing assignments are way too open-ended... just try your best and hope it's what she's looking for.   But a nice lady overall and the class isn't bad.

Really not that bad. Class can be boring and her opinions are a little crazy, but she will respect you if you state your own opinion. Not difficult to do well at all.

Dr. McLean is an overall decent professor to take General Physics with. Dr McLean is a super nice person. He was one of the better physics professors. His office hours were pretty good though and he explained the math well there.

Physics is gonna be hard no matter who you have. James is really smart. Hes a tough grader for labs. The homework is hard but if you go to the office hours he will help you get every answer. He also puts effort in on learning names. I wouldn't recommend the class... but I like him.

Professor McLean is alright. He is clearly very smart, but he gets side tracked easily and doesn't always explain things very thoroughly or well. comment: The weekly homeworks at some times were literally impossible. They are graded extremely harshly, and the tests were just as difficult. For a 100-level gen-ed class this was far too difficult.

He'll give you every possible resource you need to do well in this class. I was out for 2 weeks with pneumonia and he sat down with me outside of class to set me up for the test. His canvas page has a link to the study guide for each test as long as past exams (and solutions), old homeworks with explanations, textbook links and more.

he is very hard to listen to. he stutters on his words and teaches his lectures from a binder. lectures have nothing to do with the homework and you have to look it up yourself. exams are not hard but you need to self teach. the TA is your friend with him. the class wouldve been easier if he taught it better.

He really does his best to be engaging but the only person interested is him. His lectures don't make a single ounce of sense, the homework is hard, and you will spend hours working outside of class. Way harder than it should have been.
The lectures are seemingly random and have nothing to do with the homework assigned, which was extremely difficult. Do not take if you have no background in physics.

This class was way harder than it needed to be. Dr. McLean tries to get information across but it's not always clear to everyone and is seldom backed up by examples. The homework is never what you expect and as a result ends up being difficult but tests are easily passable by attending class, and taking practice quizzes he offers.

TBH, his class is totally different with his homework. He only teaches the background of the questions and you need to figure out by yourself about the homework. There's no point in taking this class. If you took AP Physics in high school and did well, you already have the credit and don't need this course. I dont recommend taking his class without a physics background. Very hard to understand the concepts hes teaching, since both he and the textbook he wrote are vague and difficult to follow. This is insanely hard when stated you do not need a physics background. I ended up dropping because I didn't want an F on my GPA. I did put in the work and effort, the textbook he created is useless. Well, the highlight of every class is that he plays musicvideos for the first 5 minutes. McLean is very good at teaching compared to other physics professors Ive had but with that being said, analyt 2 is still very difficult for a 100-level course and is very time-consuming. if you go to class, pay attention, do hw and study hard you can prob do well. If you have an interest in physics and basic knowledge, then you'll find this class very interesting. McLean's lectures are more consistent with the exams than the homework, so expect to use the textbook for outside work. Good professor. He is smart, approachable and has a great sense of humor. His examples and methods of explaining things aren't the best and he goes pretty fast, but he will help you if you need it and will always try to make the material fun and interesting. He always makes Ice Cream in his physics 3 class, and its the best thing ever!

Very nice professor. His class is very hard though and nearly impossible if you have not taken Physics before. He is helpful during office hours but isnt great at explaining things during his lectures. If you enjoy physics this class is for you. If you dont, its best to stay away.

You really need good phys and math skills going into the class. The topics are difficult to understand. He dosent explain them too well. The WebAssign hw is tough and the tests arent any easyer. You really need to read each chapter if you want to have any idea what you are doing in this class.  Study hard and you just might get out with a B!

Don't take any classes with him.  The exams are near impossible and very unfair.  He will ruin your GPA and find humor in it.  He's very smart but expects you to do the same work as an ivy league physics major.

Professor McLean was easily the best professor I had this semester. Extremely intelligent guy. You should have a background in physics before you take this course though. Homeworks can be difficult, so can labs. It was well worth it, though. Great guy.

McClean is a really good guy and  can be very helpful, but without a background in physics, a lot of studying, and a lot of effort on homeworks, it would have been very hard to do well in this class.  Not an ideal way to satisfy a core requirement.

extremely witty and tries to make physics interesting. tests are pretty difficult so attend all review sessions. Good class but you should have some background in physics first. confusing lectures, confusing testssssssss!

Dr. McLean is a funny guy.  He acts goofy on purpose, and he sort of waddles around the room.  ALso, he plays a music clip before every lecture.  This class was difficult though.  I would probably steer clear unless you've taken Physics before.  Lectures are confusing, but if you work with someone on the hw there shouldn't be a problem.

Prof Sugarman is AMAZING!!! She is such a sweet lady, really caring and accepting. Very friendly as well. Her class was very easy, however, it is still a lot of work for a one credit class. Dr. Sugarman makes the class as easy and painless as possible. She makes it interesting and does her best to keep it up to date with current events and student interests. Great at responding to emails too!

Dr.Sugarman is a professor that you wish you had more than half a semester to be in her classroom. The discussions are great, and she is easy going.
