I took Bechard for animal behavior. Bought the textbook that we never used. The papers asked for too much detail to be given in a small number of pages. The midterm was ridiculous. Going to class was pointless. Only positive aspect was the extra credit. Bechard gives okay feedback on assignments, but clearly is new to teaching.

So Bechard isn't terrible but she isn't wonderful either. Her demeanor and lack of understanding on how to properly teach a college course leads to a long difficult semester of trying to figure out exactly what she wants. If you don't write things exactly how she wants you to, expect to receive a failing grade. She's harsh with grading.

comment: I really recommend taking her class. She makes it clear from the start that the way to do well in her classes is by coming to class and paying attention. As long as you do that, she makes sure she is available to her students needs and is very nice. Easy A if you put in the effort.
tags: ['Gives good feedback', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Clear grading criteria']

comment: I have Bechard for both PSYC 251 and PSYC 233 and I love her! If you go to class (which isn't "mandatory")you will get a good grade. She offers loads of help especially for her research methods class and gives you a bunch of time to do your work IN CLASS and will sometimes even fix your paper for you. I would take her again for sure!

She has a very nice personality but her grades in the class are weird. This is based on 5 tests with an extra bonus and a writing assignment. Basically you need to pass the tests to pass the class and she's very vague in terms of her lecture slides. Take her class only at the risk of having unanswered questions
tags: ['Clear grading criteria', 'TEST HEAVY', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS']

comment: Bechard is new to Geneseo and it shows. She grades the class on five tests as well as an extra bonus assignment, although its hard to tell what is for credit and whats not because she is so horrible at explaining what she wants. Her class always left me with questions that she consistently answered in an unprofessional way. Do not take her class.

Yes, he's a sweet guy. Yes, he is helpful understanding and a fair grader. But holy cow his class is SO BORING. You can get by with reading little and not attending a lot of class but when you do go, its like being forced to watch paint dry. And beware, much of your class work will be passed around for other students to read and critique!

Professor Butterfield, although boring, is an extremely kind man.  As stated before, you are only graded on 5 essays, and he grades fairly too as long as you try to incorporate the writing techniques he teaches in class.  Overall I recommend him to people considering taking his INTD Ancient Myth class.

Although his INTD can be a bit of a bore, Butterfield really is a kind, generous man.  He grades very fairly and is always willing to help you when needed.  You are graded on a total of 5 essays and that's it.  (so the readings are more or less optional).

Class is comparable to watching paint dry, but you literally do not have to buy a single book, show up for class, or put in any effort what-so-ever. If you are able to produce four essays and a final paper, you will end up with an A-.
Kill me. this guy stands in front of the class and reads notes in a monotone voice for 2.5 hours. never ever take him.

Prof McCausland is who you should take DANC100 with for sure. You don't have to go to lectures, but you should to get an idea of what would be on the test and you HAVE to go to the participation classes because that's a big chunk of your grade

Such a nice lady. Go to her lectures and she lectures for 30 minutes, take notes from exactly what she says, then you watch movies the rest of the class. You have to go to the dance studio like once a week to "dance", but it's actually fun and that's 10% of your grade. For tests, find a quizlet and memorize everything and you're going to get an A.

super nice lady without a mean bone in her body. Lectures can be really dry but class is super easy. Participation classes are fun as long as you don't take yourself too seriously. Tests are annoyingly detailed but not too bad as long as you study.

A super sweet old lady who just wants you to appreciate dance. GO TO ALL HER CLASSES and you will be golden! Don't do any readings online, they're not necessary. Studio classes are a must and are super fun even if you can't dance. Review all lecture notes for her exams and you are good. Attend as many dance concerts as possible for ec!

Her class is really easy and everything on the test is whatever she teaches you in class. Don't skip her classes on her dance studio - you lose a lot of attendance points! The 1-page papers are really easy and her class is half-lecture, half-videos. It's really interesting! Would recommend for an arts gen-ed.
Jackie is a great down to earth person. Her class is easy and clear. Just make sure to participate and it will all be good.

Really nice professor. The class is beyond easy. You mostly just watch videos of dance. She gives a ton of reading but you don't actually have to read any of it. None of it is used on the tests. Class is espescially easy for dancers. Best classto take for an easy A

Great fine arts class to take, wonderful lady. Paying attention in class is a must, but other than that you don't have to do anything but study your notes from the test. Even though it's easy, studying is a must!

By far the most understanding, caring, and happy professor at geneseo. Shes verryyy passionate about dance to say the least. The studio is fun and she cares more about participation than test grades. It was nice to not have to sit in a lecture hall every class. She cares more for your participation than test grades. Highly recommended! loved her

Prof. McCausland is very nice and knowledgeable about many different types of dance. The studio classes were fun but the lectures were very boring. She uses many videos but they are old and can get boring too. Prof. is a bit annoying; she laughs at her own jokes but she means well. I would recommend this class to anyone looking for a fine arts cred

Lovely lady, very motherly - always smiling and happy to share her love of dance. She is very knowledgeable about what she does. The lecture classes are alright and there are lots of videos; the studio sessions are always fun. The class itself is extremely easy; you don't even have to buy a textbook! Really sweet lady, easy gened, HIGHLY RECOMMEND!
makes me hate dance even though dance was my life before this class. very boring and confusing tests

What a kind woman! Is always smiling and likes to get to know students' names. You need to study for tests. A portion of the grade comes from participation in the dance studio, which is fun. A few short essays are the only homework, plus attending performances. The class was mostly girls.
boring lectures, fun in the studio. you do have to study for tests, but you DO NOT have to read any of the assigned readings! tests are not hard though. very easy grader on papers!

She's really into the subject matter and makes dance out to be the end all be all of the universe. The lecture is boring but being in the studio is alot of fun. The only homework is a few readings, which are completely unnecessary. Tests are easy. Good class to take for your fine arts requirement.

Really easy way to get your fine arts out of the way. The class is really easy, you dont need to know how to dance. The class is kinda boring when you are in the lecture and she sometimes acts like everyone is there because they love dance but she is a great professor.
Absolutely the easiest class ever, she is so nice and funny. Take her.
I really like her.  She's really nice and the class is pretty easy.
so good.
Jackie Rocks! She is the best yoga teacher you could ever find!

she is a nice lady.  dance 100 is fun, tiring in the middle of the day though.  lectures are boring but videos are cool.  she sometimes gets a bit political which I didn't like, but she teaches dance well

Very easy and fun class.  Professor McCausland is more interested in getting students involved with dance than testing their knowledge.  She is a GREAT teacher, very sweet and fun.  I had a rough semester and she was extremely understanding through it all.

There are three tests in this class and if you study alittle you will do well. Most of the time you get to dance in the studio which is 30% of your grade! Pretty boring lectures but you watch alot of movies. Better then most fine arts classes!

She's an interesting lady to say the least. Her class was pretty boring but it didn't involve a lot of reading. She basically tells you everything you need to know for her tests and you get to spend time prancing around the dance studio.
Love this women!  She's stuck in the 60's but I wish more people were!

Great professor! Cook is extremely knowledgeable, and he is always willing to help. Great class for anyone majoring in political science or history. His papers are tough, but if you work hard and go to office hours, good grades are attainable

If you read the assigned quiz readings and take notes in class you will do great. His lectures can be wordy and lengthy but he keeps it interesting with jokes and he gives you every answer he is looking for in the essays. Overall my favorite teacher!

Professor Cook is a very interesting man. I took this class because of all of the amazing things I've heard about him. Although he is a great lecturer and extremely intelligent, he is a difficult grader and doesn't connect to the students. He is unhelpful during office hours and doesn't promote discussion in class. I learned a lot, but GPA suffered

I came to Geneseo with hopes of obtaining a quality education. While I learned to write well in this class, I realized the days of the romantic view "I'll take this class because I'll learn a lot from this professor" are long gone. Bill Cook is the reason why I realized I can only take "easy A" profs if I have any hopes of getting into med school.

Although he is both witty and wise, he tends to be a bit pretentious. Also, left school a week early & left lecture to a fellow professor and had trouble with the final exam because of this. In addition, he was late handing in our final grades and it has now been 3 weeks since the test and I am still waiting for my grade. Hope he is enjoying Italy.

I was looking for an easy A, and that is NOT what he offers. Take a class with him if you are looking for someone to challenge you and make you think. Very interesting, dynamic lecturer. (And his outfits are CRAZY!)
Shalom! This boychik schleps around giving kibitz like he's some kind of macher. Oy vey, he's just meshuga.

William R. Cook is the man. You have to put in the work to do well. For example, you should write your papers a week before they are due. He likes it when students challenge him. It is important to remember that these professors are not Gods. If you work hard for him, he will really care about how you perform in the class.
Good overall. . . tended to be an arbitrary grader. . . GO TO OFFICE HOURS IF YOU WANT TO DO WELL!
tough teacher... have to read a lot to really get a decent grade on your papers. and absolutely hit office hours to chat about exam essays, his thoughts..

He is a very funny man, but this class was just sooooo boring for me. I couldn't keep my eyes open (probably doesn't help that it was an 8:05 class though...). I found this class pretty difficult- he is a hard grader. But, he is one of the coolest professors at Geneseo.

He's the man, easily the most interesting professor I've had at school. Only if you're a crappy writer will you suffer.  Papers were challenging, but in a good way, they were actually kind of fun to do since his notes helped so much. In class tests could be tricky, and he's sort of a tough grader, but getting at least a B is not hard by any means.

By far the best professor I have had thus far at Geneseo. Knew just about everything about the subject matter.  He is fairly tough in his grading, and if you can't write well forget about taking anything with him.  He is very quirky which is a welcome departure from some teachers around here.

Great professor.  He has so much knowledge, I never found a question or a topic he did not know the answer too.  Almost made me wish I was a history major!  We went on a field trip and he had so much cool stuff to tell us.  Definitly worth it for anyone in the history field!

I took his Democracy in America INTD 105 last year, and it was AMAZING. It is definately the right class to take for kids who are going into Political Science or History. He is a VERY dedicated teacher, and really likes helping freshman adjust. His papers are tough, but he grades based on improvement. He may take you on a sweet field trip too!

This class really isn't that hard, I just seriously believe that people just really suck at writing.  If you're anything remotely solid of a writer you'll have no problem. The reading isn't that much, plus every lecture is interesting. Never once have I day dreamed because the discussions are great.  Recommended, interesting and not that hard.

he's not as personal with students as other professors I've had here, but I still like him. He's pretty damn smart and he does have a unique way of making you interested in otherwise boring crap like "the nuns of poitiers"... the papers suck. a lot. but the essays on the exams arent so bad.
I still speak with this incredible teacher 5  years after taking a course with him.  Most inspiring teacher I've ever had.  I plan to meet with him in October.
No Comments

I took The Age of Dante with him and Professor Herzman.  He is one of the most devoted professors I've ever encountered.  He has a genuine interest in the subject and is elated whenever students express an interest.  He's very quirky, but that just adds to
No Comments
Best lecturer you could ever have in college.  I never took a note and passed with a B+.

Don't waste your time taking this class, esp. if you are a girl. He's an incredibly hard grader with nothing to say but nasty comments. He may be one of the greatest profs here, but only take him if you're prepared to get a C. Def. prefers guys over girls.
Best teacher ever.  He's only hard if you aren't a good writer.  He is inspirational, passionate and a wonderful human being.  Thank you Dr. Cook!
I loved his campaigning stories! He ran for office (and lost :( ).
very funny, hard grader, always fair, makes class interesting and he makes you think about things u might have not thought abuot before

Had him for Early Christian History and History of the Bible. One of the most interesting and open-minded profs on campus. Critical thinker and teaches you to be one too. Loved the class and his teaching style.
The WORST professor ever. poor paper feedback, makes you feel like a failure. PLEASE!!! RE-THINK taking any of his classes. Way too involved with his campaign days-yea he lost. go figure??

mean, demoralizing, honest, smart, self-enthralled, prefers male students to female students, and horrible grader--poor feedback on papers and tests, wants you to think you are not as smart as you think you are, but generally someone you can learn from--good person to audit class from, for example

I'm an English major, so I'm used to lots of class discussion.  Bill Cook does not do enough to encourage this.  Other than that, he is a terrific lecturer, and very personable.  He's open for discussion of class material any time you see him, but don't expect to change his opinion anytime soon.
It's been a while since I had Dr. Cook, but he was awesome.  Anyone who says he was hard should probably consider community college or a job at McDonalds!
Tough grader, interesting lectures.
No Comments
Loved his class. he made uninteresting material very intresting and was very responcive to our needs. Good speaking voice and presence, he sounds like someone on NPR
Arrogant fool - run - don't walk - away from this guy - he is so full of himself and unresponsive to his students it's sad!
If you don't take this guy for humanities, you are totally missing out. He actually makes it interesting and relevant! I enjoyed this class tremendously

horrible grader, does not care about his students, pompous, arrogant.  just a stubborn old man who thinks he's God's gift to the world.  be prepared to agree with whatever he says - any personal opinions are not tolerated.  over-rated.

Every Geneseo student should take a class with Cook before graduating. Most interesting lecturer I've ever had and one of the most thoughtful and intellectually exciting professors around. Knows what matters in life and what teaching is all about.
Learned a lot, extremely hard grader.  His Covenant House dinners were awesome!  If you ever get a chance, try to go to one!
knows tons about his subject & great sense of subtle humor.  he's a superb teacher, but you have to go to his office hours- he's a tough grader. take him if you're interested & want a challenge :)
Extremely smart, but tough
Definitely leave your own ideas outside the door. Do not expect to get a good grade in this one. In fact, if you open your mouth at all, make sure it's to kiss his bottom.
Good lecturer - eccentric and enjoyable - but not open to any competing ideas - presents some questionable theories as established facts
Tough grader, eccentric but a good guy.  not a bad professor, pretty helpful.
good lecturer; good sense of humor; tough grader.  might be better in a smaller class where he actually learns your name
He lectures too much. Too restrictive on writing assignments and only gives you a good grade if you agree with what he has to say. If you have your own ideas, don't take him.
No Comments
Great lecturer, but tough paper grader
Amazing and knowledgable man!!
expectattions are too high
Seriously, get his old test. Projects are easy, test are hard if you don't have his old test.
Get his old exams. It's the only way to pass the class.

Professor Gu's lectures are of minimal value, but attendance is mandatory. You will need to read EVERYTHING in the textbook, and even then, his tests intentionally try to trip you up. He is obviously brilliant, but he is a dreadful teacher.

You must read all chapters (in their entirety) and do all assigned homework to do well on the exams.  You should learn about 20% of all material in lectures.  He takes attendance though, so go to class but realize you won't get much out of it.
He is impossible. It's impossible to pass without having his old tests or cheating a lot!

Worst teacher I have ever had at Geneseo.  Does not teach anything and they expects you to know everything for the test.  The only way to possibly pass the class is to get a hold of the test before hand.  DO NOT TAKE WITH HIM.

Gu may be my least favorite professor at Geneseo. I was excited to take another finance class, but this one was nearly impossible with him. Some of his stories were funny, but that didn't make up for his lack of clarity and helpfulness. Students would ask questions in class and he wouldn't understand them. It confused everyone in the class.

If i had a choice I wouldn't have taken Gu. I know that he is really smart and he's pretty funny but he just isn't good at teaching. If you want a good grade you either need to get a hold of the tests or teach yourself everything.

One of my favorite professors. A riot in class and will do a headstand in front of the class if you ask him to. Projects are long but easy A's. Tests are hard. Be sure to PARTICIPATE and pay attention in class and your grade will be fine.
No Comments
He's funny. Very easy on paper and projects. Tests are hard, but you won't do too bad as long as you study hard. Good luck!
Really nice guy but very hard class, allows u to bring in a cheat sheet for tests... final was optional

i have him as an advisor - he absolutely sucks hardcore at that. i've gone to him 3 times about 3 separate issues.. he never once helped me. his answers were always "i dont have that access" or "i dont know if this is possible.. but just try." and it WAS his fault, because i got perfectly clear answers from another professor i turned to.
Dr. Gu is good, explains everything very clear, and he is willing to help students. However, he is HARD! especially the exams

Really funny, nice guy, and a good teacher.  Class is a bit pointless to attend if you actually do the reading though.  A lot of the test questions are straight out of the end of the text book chapters.
Dr. Gu is the man. His course is straightforward, the tests are cake, and the hw isnt bad at all. To top it all off he's hilarious and his accent is definitely entertaining. Really nice guy too.
One of the funniest professors ive ever had
he's...  i thought he was cool and easy and funny at first.. but he's got some issues man.
what a wonderful man- so cute and great sense of humor! teaching style makes it easy to learn.

I LOVE David Robertson. He is caring for his students and wants them to succeed. Three tests each worth 20% of final grade so be prepared to study to pass the class. Does a fun assignment where you get to walk around the village. Lecture heavy but overall very nice and funny professor to have. Highly recommend taking a Robertson GEOG class.

comment: This class is very easy. Attendance is important since Top Hat questions are used to track it. Taking good notes is key to doing well on exams. The professor is very nice, though the class can be a bit boring. People who say the exams are hard either didn't go to class, didn't study, or didn't take good notes. No hw aside from two easy projects

Currently I'm in GEOG102 and I am also taking this for a Gen Ed, so it's not major related for me, however the class is literally a breeze. No homework besides 2 projects and you just really need to show up, pay attention, and take notes. Study your lecture notes and you'll easily pass his midterms, the questions are common sense. He is the goat fr

This class was very easy, straightforward, and I enjoyed the lectures. Dr. Robertson is great, but sometimes comes off a bit rude when handling situations and accommodations with students. Still, you can tell her cares and wants the best for his students.

Exams- 60% of your grade and are ridiculously hard.1st test average was a 78 and he said that was really good for his tests. Mandatory attendance-even if you show up everyday and do the Tophat you might not even get full credit attendance. You have to get every question right for full credit. Tests on what he says not ppts

Dr. Robertson made an otherwise somewhat difficult subject fairly easy to understand. He inspired me to potentially pick up a geography minor as a history major, which isn't something I'd considered at all before his class. I miss him and wish I could take more classes with him!
NOTE: he doesn't actually care if you don't read the textbook.
love dr. robertson!

I really enjoyed the class. There is a walk about assignment we had that I was dreading but it was actually easy and very enjoyable, took me around 1 hour. I found the material to be interesting but it may not be the case for everyone. Professor Robertson was amazing to have and I would absolutely take a class with him again in the future.
tags: ['Amazing lectures', 'Graded by few things', 'Accessible outside class']

comment: I loved GEOG 102 with Dr. Robertson! The workload is very manageable with minimal outside-of-class work. Make sure you attend the lectures! There will be an attendance question every day counting toward 20% of your final grade. I enjoyed this class and found it very interesting. Would recommend!

Dr. Robertson is a nice person, however his lectures are not very engaging. He reads off the power point for a majority of the class and then adds random information in once in a while that could be on the exam. Its hard to go to class because its so boring, but it is not a difficult class. The exams were pretty easy, you just have to go to class.

His exams are slightly annoying because there's 55 questions in 50 minutes which makes it stressful but definitely not a hard class. You do have to actually attend class because he uses tophat and sometimes a random fact that is not on the powerpoints will be on the exam. It was hard not to fall asleep though because it was rather boring.

When it comes to lecture material it is informative, but he leaves out key pieces so that you attend his class. His PowerPoint slides is mixed with important and unnecessary information for a multiple-choice exam that has random in class information that he skims over. He will often get off topic and you will fall behind.
tags: ['Participation matters', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Graded by few things']

comment: I liked human geo with him. He posts lecture slides so you could probably just use those and do fine on the tests but I'd go to class since he uses tophat. But the class isn't hard, and he's a nice guy
If you go to class and pay attention, you will do well. There is no homework or out of class work. The tests are straight from the lectures and he preps you well for them.

Robertson is an easy enough professor to follow, all you really have to do to well is show up to class, pay attention, and take notes. For some people in my class even these three criteria was too much apparently

Professor Robertson was an amazing professor. He is super kind, informative and reasonable. He expanded my knowledge on human geography and I did really well in the class. He is straight forward on what will be tested and he really wants his students to succeed. Highly recommend this professor. He really works with his students to insure success.

Dr. Robertson was overall a great professor! He really helped put me on the right track. I had him as a freshman and he helped improve my study skills and show me the importance of studying. Dr. Robertson likes to see his students succeed. Although you must go to lectures to pass the class, a lot of the information is not on the slide shows.
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Clear grading criteria', 'Lecture heavy']

comment: This professor was a great and knowledgeable one to be teaching this class, and I learned a lot from his class and was always interested and engaged. I loved the class overall and it was not very work heavy outside of class. However the professor lacks basic empathy for his students and is not the most kind person youll ever come across.

Loved him he was a very nice and understanding teacher. But he did complain about attendance in the class. His test was you remembering the lecture so I suggest to record them. His class was two parts the class itself and stuff for freshman to learn about the school. Highly recommend as a incoming freshman.
Had to email professor to get into a required course late. Responded with outright disrespect, just a generally mean person. Takes the course way too seriously for so little work.

One of my favorite professors at Geneseo. He's really caring and a great guy who really wants to see his students succeed. He'll always answer emails and be as helpful as he can be. His class is also extremely straightforward and easy to understand - 4 tests, 2 writing assignments and also attendance participation. 10/10 would recommend.

Grade is based on four exams (all mc) and a project. The exams are an easy A if you take good notes in class and take the time to study. Dave is very good about saying what will be on the test. Three opportunities to do the project which consists of mc, short answer questions, and an essay. Cares about his students' success! Take this class w him!
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class', 'Clear grading criteria']

comment: Dr. Robertson is probably my favorite professor at Geneseo. I've taken a few classes with him, and he really cares about his students. He gives great feedback on the writing assignments in this class (6 weekly short responses to readings and a 12 page final paper) and I truly feel like he made me a better writer. I'll miss him when I graduate!

This is by far the worst professor at Geneseo. Save yourself and don't take this class. He is not helpful to students who are not geology majors and will find random things on exams or papers to deduct points from. His lectures are horrible and make zero sense. His grading criteria for the final debate and report are non existant.
tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LECTURE HEAVY']

comment: Robertson is by far one of my favorite profs at Geneseo. You have to take notes in his classes to pass, but you should be doing that anyway. Hes coordinated, nice, and answers all your questions. If you put in the usual amount of effort, you'll get a good grade. Read, take notes, have fun - you'll do great.

This class was a waste of time. If I could go back I wouldn't take it again. This professor tests on statistics that he will mention once in class. Lazy as well. Hopes of skipping? Not likely. Only tests on lectures. If you have to miss skim the book or get the notes from someone else. Take GOOD notes. Pretty much have to write everything he says
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS', 'LECTURE HEAVY']

comment: I had him last semester, and he was great! such a cool dude, i honestly wish i was his friend. the tests are the material straight from class, so go and take good notes. Also, make sure you know the statistics because theres quite a few of those. the EOR 's are not hard, and are just a grade booster. really interesting class.

90% of grade is exams - 35%, 35% and 20% final. 10% is a 3 page paper on an envo related event. 2% extra credit for a 2 page paper. I advise against taking this class unless you're good with exams. Midterms are only 70 questions, so every question is .5% of your grade. Textbook is only used for 6-7 hw questions on each exam, so just borrow it.

I went to most of his classes, made 9 page review sheets, studied with others, yet I still struggled on his tests. Ridiculous. Very condescending to students and made asking for help unpleasant. He refused to take my extra credit assignment for no reason, saying " I don't have to waste my time helping you out". Are you kidding me?! You assigned it!

Robertson is the best professor in the Geneseo Geography department, I say that having taken at least one class with all of them. He is tough but fair, you will certainly pass if you do the work and go to class. Not only is he a great professor, but he is a great guy and helped me immensely as the geography chair. Two thumbs way up.

Great guy. Fairly easy grader with extra credit options available. Tests are super easy just go to class and get the notes. He will tell you in lecture everything that is on the test. You just have to go.

Helpful, funny guy you can have beer with. Homework & outreach reports totally doable. Instructs material clearly but not concisely. Reads off notes instead of presenting PPTs by memory --> dry lectures. Too many statistical Qs on exams, which should be more conceptual. Should break up lectures with videos so students are more interested in class

He is a great speaker and very knowledgeable about the environment. I feel like the only major thing he could improve is his grading scheme. Altogether, tests should not be worth 80%-90% of your grade. If he is going to make tests worth that much of your grade he should ask better questions on tests. Make sure you do all of the homework.

Cool dude but what a boring class. You can basically get all the notes from the powerpoint, don't even have to bother going to class. I wish I found the content more interesting because he seems awesome.
A good man and a very straight forward classs. Snoozed a lot though in class.

I loved Dr. Robertson. The class was really straightforward and the Google Earth assignments were fairly easy. He is really approachable in office hours and the help sessions and is willing to help you do well. I found the class really interesting. Highly recommend. Definitely do all 4 Google Earth assignments.

Do not need textbook. Take notes and you won't fall asleep cause lectures can get dry. Class goes by fairly fast. Grading is fair. Do all the GE assignments. Make sure not to copy off each other cause he reads through them all. Pretty simple to get an A. Work hard and go to class.

Two test and 4 GE assignments. 2 GEs are mandatory and 2 are optional. Do all 4 you get an extra 4 point boost on your grade at the very end and the exam:GE is 60:40. Do 2 and it's 80:20. Go to class esp for the final exam. He put a lot of inclass material that's not on pp on the final exam. Not hard to get an A. Sometimes boring. overall recommend

Easy class. Easy going guy, presents all the info you need to know on powerpoints (which are also posted online). Grades from 2 tests, a debate, a paper and attendance. An easy A- at least if you put the study time in for the tests, your grade can be lowered if you get a bad debate group (chosen at random).

Don't take this class if you're a good student looking for a good grade.  Regardless of how much work you put into the test he will still find points to take off.  Tests are out of 30 points and there are only 2 tests that count for 50% of your grade meaning that each point he takes off for the silliest of reasons really hurts your grade.

This was a very interesting class that taught me something new every day.  Prof. Robertson is a great teacher who doesn't only read off his slides.  Tests are easy and extra credit makes getting an A easy.

Good teacher, very clear power points. Material is fairly basic (I took a similar class last semester however). Attendance not mandatory, I often skip and still pull off good grades. Provides PLENTY of extra credit opportunities. Recommended

This class was awesome! Professor Robertson knows his stuff and really enjoys teaching. The class was really interesting and not hard at all. Do the HW. Its really easy and will help you with the test. You don't have to read any of the textbook material. Make sure you go to class to receive the necessary statistics that he reveals before the test.

I thought this class was extremely interesting so I never minded going to class or doing the work. Writing assignment was really easy. Second test was harder than some people expected, but still not that bad and all multiple choice. I would take this class again if I could

Boring. Boring. Boring. Dull. Man.  Only a few questions on the exams are from class, so read the textbook, do the homework and look over lecture slides and there's no reason to go to class.  And the writing assignment is a joke.  A painfully stupid one.

I loved this class.  It opened up my world to environmental issues which I had no idea ever existed.  Topics like rock mining, global warming, resource use and renewable energy were covered.  I love his teaching style because it gets the point across.  Tests were extremely fair and its easy to do good on them if you study for 2 hrs.  Great class!

I did not enjoy his teaching style.  I didn't like him as a person, I felt his tests were created soley make you do bad created only with shotty multiple choice questions.  He is condescending and arrogant, even though canadian professors are generally nice, he was not.

I am not a fan of his class/teaching style at all.  I found him soo repetitive.  HE SAYS "K?" AFTER EVERY SENTENCE.  This bothered me and I found myself getting distracted by it.  I started counting and once I got up to 25 I stopped.   I felt like this entire class could be summarized in half an hour, to be honest.

He is a very cool guy (duh, hes canadian!). The class can be very boring some days and very interesting other days. Your grade is based on a midterm and final exam and one or two projects. Make the effort to do good on the projects! You don't really have to read the textbook at all- he even says so. Just take good notes in lecture. Oh, he says "K" a lot, and it really bothers me lol.
Ok class. Could be really interesting some days and really boring the next.  One project was a real pain, tests are a challenge and you must study and go to class. Nice guy.

Very nice guy, and fair. Tests are pretty easy, and makes class interesting. Probably one of the best professors at geneseo. Only drawback, puts a lot of emphasis on class participation, go to class and do the work.
No Comments
Best teacher I have had at Geneseo. Likeable guy and funny. Oh, and by the way, "sulphur" is the British, and more widely used spelling for "sulfur." The guy's Canadian afterall.
Pretty easy professor, nice guy, and FUNNY.  Lectures sometimes a little boring but you can tell he cares about what he is teaching.
this class sucked, extremely boring, and an unfair grader, also not exactly an easy A

He's a moron, however his class is the easiest thing ever.  the man spelled sulfur like this: 'sulpher' in one of his sildes, which happens to be part of a book he is publishing.  need an easy class, take this, just try not to kill yourself from boredom.

He does know his stuff, but it's dry material and he makes it even drier. No enthusiasm; he simply repeats himself over and over, reading aloud his sentences so you can copy them word for word. Booooring.
You better buckle your seat belt with Robertson. Great instructor, he knows his material so don't try to fake it....he'll challenge you!
boring class, talks down to his students, often sarcastic when answering questions, making students feel uncomfortable. I would not recommend this class.
The class was really interesting. Robertson is a great professor - really is into the material, and that helps a lot, I think. Definitely would recommend this class. Not overly difficult.

Dr. Roberton's Issues class is awesome.  It has inspired me even more to puruse a career in the Environmental field. His tests are straight forward, but don't expect them to be too easy!  It is disturbing to find out the many ways in which we harm the environment, but i still recommend it!
Did not enjoy this class at all. Least favorite.

Great class, and great teacher.  Robertson knows what he's talking about and is passionate about it.  You'll like the class if you don't care much about the enviroment because of Robertson, and you'll love the class if you care about him.  Offers extra credit and only 3 tests with 1 other assignment
Really interesting class, and he knows his stuff. He's really into the material and it shows, and it makes his classes good. Tests are very fair. Highly recommend the class to others!

Dave's the man.  Took some pass/fail geog courses with him.  Not a big fan of geog, but he cares about it, and you have to respect that.  Pretty easygoing. Easy tests if you attend and take notes, I didn't and I still passed.

dave's classes are well thought out, and interesting. you can tell he really cares about the students, their interests and how they feel about the class. his classes are best when you get to know him.

Dr. R is a great teacher and a great person as well! The class was interesting, though sometimes a little depressing to learn what we are doing to our planet, but I admire that he wants to get the word out about Environmental issues. Plus, Love the hair!
Great guy loves his Canadians
He is one of the best professors!  A generally good guy.  Tests are pretty straightforward and fair. The class was easy.
He is THE MAN!! very interesting, funny, and clear. he actually wants you to learn, I also took Environmental issues with him... highly recommended
Robertson's a great guy and he teaches the class really well. Very interesting class in itself, would definitely reccomend it to anyone.
A great class, interesting, though provoking, some good reading, and the tests are reasonable and predictable.  A great teacher, very easy to get along with.
Graduated, and had to give Dr. R.  a good rating since he was one of my favorite teachers.  Thanks all of the help
Great guy, you take notes, you do well on the tests
Easy if you go to all his lectures. Can be a little boring, but it is an intro geography course so i didn't expect anything special. Very clear in explanations
No Comments

Most classes average around 60s on both tests but with all of the online assignments which aren't too hard, people still end up with A's and B's. Gives a lot of extra credit opportunities for participating in class. Tough class but caring professor that understands how hard it is. Wont allow anyone to fail.

comment: Great guy who cares a lot. Everyone who takes his class should pass his curves are crazy, and doesn't want anyone to fail. Go to class if you want to get those random extra credit points he throws out, but otherwise you don't need to go. I got a 69 and a 64 on the midterm and final and still got a B somehow.

Gifford is a real funny guy who tries to make all his lectures interesting, despite it being all about accounting. He is always accessible outside of the classroom and will set up individual appointments if you need assistance. The material is somewhat challenging depending on the chapter, but the midterm and final are VERY difficult so be prepared

Gifford is a nice guy but his lectures are boring and honestly pointless. Graded assignments are 100x harder than lecture problems. Go to his office hours as much as possible. Class is hard but he gives tons of curve. Points for attendance so go to class. As long as you try, you will pass. ACCT majors: I would avoid if possible, won't learn much.

comment: Great guy and ok professor. His lectures were average and the assessments were very difficult but if you put in the time and effort he will not give you a poor grade. Highly encourage you to go to as many office hours as humanly possible as he will help you and your effort will reflect your grade. Don't be discouraged on assessment grades.

Super difficult class. Pretty different than any other classes I've ever taken. The average on our first assessment was in the 30's, so try to get past the assessments. Most people can easily end with a B- or B after the extra credit points and 5.5% participation grade boost. Gifford is a really nice and helpful guy, though. Go to review sessions!

Professor Gifford is a very nice person. He gives 2 online assignments for each chapter, which you can get high grades if you put effort. Drop lowest scores. He's available for help outside of class. Midterm and Final are difficult, so you must work hard to get high grades. Gives extra credit for participation and going to class.
Giffords class is so difficult but he does what he can to make it interesting. He also makes it mathematically impossible to fail as long as you go to every class and hand in every assessment.

Go to class everyday. Insane amounts of extra credit for just showing up. Can get out of final and get automatic A if you go to class and have over 90% assessment average. In class assessments are tough but gives many out of class in Excel which are easy to do well on. Take advantage of all extra credit opportunities and get to know him personally.

He has a hilariously weird sense of humor. His assessments and tests are REALLY TOUGH. I failed at least half my assessments. HOWEVER, if you go to every class and look like you put in effort he will give you a MASSIVE curve, I had a 62 as my final grade but he gave me a C+, my only complaint is that he uses excel to teach which was hard to follow.

Amazingly dedicated to his student! Tough class, but work your hardest and the curve will save you. First few exams can be rough, but he drops the lowest. I ended up with an A because of his generous extra credit and curve. He lets his students call him for help and is always extending his office hours and review sessions to accommodate students.

He is just too cool. He has a lot of review sessions to help you until late at night, gives many extra credits, and saves students who make an effort. Go to the class every class because he will give a huge extra credits for it.

Terrible Professor, not clear in the way he derives your final grade. Classes are unnecessary because his tests (all online) are 10 times harder than lecture problems. Stay clear from this class at all costs possible!

Dr. Gifford is a great professor.  He is more dedicated than most teachers at Geneseo.  He is constantly making longer and new office hour times to meet the demands of his students and loves to help you.  Assessments are difficult & require lots of reading/practice.  Attend all classes though & he will offer some extra credit at the end

Super nice, dorky accounting teacher who makes it very hard to fail his class, while simultaneously making it hard to get an A. If you read the text book and do the homework you'll be fine. Also, he gives a lot of extra credit to those who attend class!

Boring class but pretty easy.  Consists of online quizzes and homework and a midterm and a final.  Make a good group for the online portion and you should be fine there. lets you bring cheat sheet for midterm/final and helps you a lot with curve and extra credit.  Go to class and you can easily get an A

Grade consists of 10 online quizzes, 10 online homeworks, a midterm and final, both you can bring a single sheet of paper with whatever you want on it. His lectures are a little tough to follow b/c he doesn't explain step by step. Decent prof though, helps you out with grade at the end.  Also go to every class b/c he gives mad attendance extra cred
Great Teacher, knows his stuff, very clear and helpful whenever you have a question. One of my favorite teachers at this school
Great professor. Really easy class, especially over the summer. He does seem stressed out of class but in class he's very enthusiastic and humorous.
great professor with tons of real world experience that he uses in teaching

He teaches entirely on excel, which makes it extremely confusing to follow his train of thought. However if you attend class every day it will pay off in the end, because he takes attendance and it helps your final grade.
his tests are fair (def. not easy, but use his review sheets-they're a godsend).  witty man-keeps class interesting and offers a fair amount of extra credit.  loved him!
The best prof this school has to offer.

Extremely intelligent, relates to material extremely well, the material itself is thought provoking and interesting. He might seem a little "fake", but get to know him more than just for office hours, and he's an awesome guy. Tests are fair enough, grading is easy (make sure you write SOMETHING), lots of extra credit. Highly recommended.
No Comments
In class he's an excellent, funny little man, but in his office hours he seems so stressed out or something.  Overall though, it's an easy way to take an accounting class

Cappon has no idea what is going on half of the time. his tests are related to the old text book, and he has yet to convert to the new texts style of teaching. this makes it impossible to learn what he wants you to know, considering all his slides are PREMADE from the new text. not an easy A, but confusing and you have to teach it ALL to yourself.

Interesting professor, he crashes out hard when someone is on their phone during class. But he's a caring professor and gives a lot of feedback when you need it. His lectures are soooo boring but the class is so easy for a good grade. Good guy and decent professor overall.

I have mixed feelings. You never know how he'll react to a question. The environment was a little strange at times, but he's also funny. Very harsh grader and will pick apart everything you say, but only because he knows so much. Very reactive to phones and technology, DO NOT take your phone out. will say to your face if he doesn't like you

Super goofy guy, did a handstand during class 1 time. NO BRIGHTSPACE. Doesn't check email often, but is lenient in excusing absences. Don't need to do all the reading, just take note of the page #'s he cites during class for the papers. 4 3-paragraph assignments total, very easy. Lectures can feel disorganized, random storytelling, but he's funny.

comment:
If you've taken one Derne class you've taken them all. This guy has lost his mind. Lectures are completely unorganized and he makes up what he's going to teach on the spot. "We are boldly going nowhere". 4 short writing assignments and mandatory attendance but you can just tell him you are sick, he's surprisingly understanding. 
Honestly, love him.

This class was super easy. He doesn't use bright space so nothing was online. Attendance was mandatory but there were no tests. Not a heavy workload at all. Overall, just a funky and funny guy who will probably randomly start singing and dancing.

Super attendance heavy class, lectures can get really boring. However, a very kind and understanding professor. Class is very group focused, and there are only a few assignments to be graded on, but he goes over all of the assignments in class so you are guaranteed to pass as long as you attend the classes.

he is what you make of it. he wants to connect with you, he wants you to ask questions and be present. if you skim the reading you will be fine, he talks about it all in lecture anyway. attendance is mandatory and his final is 3 things you learned in the class. he has three assignments for the course and its impossible to fail them.

comment: very funny guy. kinda weird, but kept a boring class interesting. He gets side tracked kinda easily so try your best to pay attention. Also doesn't have the best handwriting. But he makes it almost impossible to fail,

weird guy, makes you dance in class. 4 short assignments with 3 paragraphs each. thinks hes clear on what he wants from you but focuses more on trying to have you practice the assignments than actually teaching you anything. have to read a lot of articles in a reader he makes.

comment: All of "presence" so don't expect to be able to use any type of technology during class. And hey if you need to pee, you better hold it. I did badly on the first essay but he made it so that you won't fail because of it. Overall, it was fine. Wouldnt do it again

Professor Derne really takes the time to grade and give good feedback on assignments. He's also very clear about what it takes to get a good grade. His feedback is always helpful. Some of the readings aren't very interesting, but they do make you think.

Professor Derne is definitely one my most favorite teachers that I've had whether in high school or college. He makes for a friendly environment in the classroom and makes it easy to get to know your classmates. Definitely one of the most enjoyable classes which I never dreaded going too.

Professer Derné is such a nice man. He is specific in how papers are written, but he spends a lot of time going over how to write them and gives great feedback on them. All he wants is for people to be engaged and participate. Say anything, really! He'll probably give you a high-five. This class is worth it for the high-fives.

TONS of reading, sometimes you need to do them but occasionally you can get away with not doing them. A little quirky but positive and lots of energy. VERY serious about attendance -- do not think you can show up late or leave in the middle of his class. Participation is mandatory but if you make an intelligent he will take it from there.
tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'So many papers']

comment: Derne by far is the strangest man I've ever met. He definitely made 8:30s worth it. His classes are big on discussion. We discuss the readings that we were assigned but I never read them because he would go over most of them first 3 papers and 1 final term paper. Which seems like a lot but it wasn't bad and he hold office hours to go over in detail
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class', 'So many papers']

comment: As long as you show up and actively participate you will do fine. His essays are not as hard as you think, you just need to follow his guidelines exactly and meet with him before they are due to get his insight. In the first weeks you might think he is a tad bit insane (the jury's out on that one), but I liked his class and his many quirks.

comment: Very enthusiastic professor, but a really tough grader. Uses his own textbook in class which is kind of annoying. You can't ever be late, and you can only miss two classes before he deducts points. Very very very tough grader. Makes you work in groups every class and talk out loud a lot in class too. and in case you missed it VERY tough grader
tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'SO MANY PAPERS']

comment: Super eccentric but definitely one of my favorite professors I've ever had. Derne is a more 'real' than most other professors, meaning he doesn't put on airs and really tries to connect with his students.

Derne is by far my favorite teacher at Geneseo. Along with SOCL 358, I took SOCL 240 and INTD 105 with him. Received an A in both of those. He is the strangest guy and an extremely helpful professor. He acts very weirdly but it just makes the dry readings of the class actual bearable. Everyone should take his classes! He makes 8:30s worth it.

I could not get through the readings because they were so boring. Thankfully you don't actually have to do them to do well. Participation is easy; just connect ideas in class to life experiences. Don't get discouraged by grading. Reiterate ideas a lot in papers. Professor Derne is very approachable and will give you feedback to get better grades!

Steve Derne at heart really is not a bad guy, he's funny and enjoyable. As a professor he is terrible, he goes terribly fast with no hope of reading what the hell he wrote on the board. He assigns thousands of pages of reading which are terribly boring. As a history major i believe I am a very capable writer and didn't receive over a 50 on a paper.

I love Derne! One of my favorite professors. Super quirky and tangential but lots of fun and very informative. Uses his own experiences to teach and explain. Not very available but helpful when tracked down. In my experience, the students who did badly were the ones who didn't understand college essay writing to begin with. Rules were pretty basic.

So far the worst professor I've had at Geneseo. He's confusing, since he goes off on random tangents and brings in things from his personal life that have nothing to do with the class. When he tells you do the same, your example is always wrong in some way. His essay grading system is complicated, and when you ask for help, he's rude .  F- Rating.
Very sporadic when grading essays, very unhelpful when asking for help on essays, but if you just do what he says in class (which is not always clear) you will be good

Dr. Derne is amazing! I'm surprised as a Berkley guy he decided to teach at Geneseo. He is very eccentric and corky! His teaching style makes what is a tough subject easier and more understandable. He is very precise in his notes however. He's also very clear about expectations. Participation grading makes attendance mandatory. I loved this class!

Probably one of the worst instructors I've ever had in college, even though he is very smart. It seemed as though he always came to class unprepared and just jumps around from topic to topic. Also can be very rude: I tried to ask him a question after class and he told me he couldn't talk to me because he had to speak to another student.

Professor Derne may be eccentric and somewhat weird, but he's a good guy and loves the material he teaches. Class attendance is pretty mandatory- he grades participation (easy if you come to class) and the notes from him make the class fairly easy. Put in the effort and you will do well.

Two years out of Geneseo, and Derne's classes and the material taught in them is some of the only information i retained. His bizarre teaching style really engrains information in your head, and his personality makes it fun! don't take yourself too seriously, and youll do wonderful in these classes.

Makes the classical theorists very easy to understand. Yes he is eccentric but after you get use to it it helps you stay focused in class. I had a big class so take home midterms were easy. Go to his office for help on the paper or you will get a bad grade. Just pay attention and take notes! He reviews everything before tests that you need to know

When I came to Derne for help during his office hours, he told me that I'd never been taught how to write because I have a strong personality. That's rude, and it's garbage; I earned two fives on my AP English exams. The worst part was that I really was willing to take direction from him...he didn't seem to be willing to give it, though.

Okay, so he does really random things--but I guess he just really likes hula and horseback riding. He actually is really nice, but you do have to write what he wants you to write. The thing is, I always had a fun time in his class and I legitimately LEARNED a lot.

His antics are sometimes entertaining...but often annoying. If you enjoy writing papers that regurgitate verbatim what he already told you in class you'll be fine. Not much room for your own ideas and his grading is unpredictable and unclear.

I learned nothing from this class.  When people describe him as "out there" they are not lying.  If you try to go to him for help, he will rewrite your paper the way HE thinks it should be...if you agree with everything he says in class you will be ok.  He is the most demeaning professor I have ever had in my college experience.  Avoid at all cost.

His classes are easy as long as you attend, participate, and write papers early. If you go to him with a finished paper, he literally rips it apart and prints you out a sheet to help re-write it. I went from getting a 78 on my first paper to a 98 and 100. He also repeats everything to make sure you understand. Participation required but  not hard

Derne will go on record as one of my worst teachers. He was unprepared and we went over stuff more than once because he obviously couldn't remember we'd already done it. He will fail you if you don't write exactly what he wants to hear. At some points he called students stupid. He can't have spent any time outside of class preparing. Unprofessional

Derne Rocks! He definitely is a little out there, Sometimes takes breaks from material to do the hula or tai chi. The Book was very dense and hard reading but for each paper Derne went over what needed to be in them several times. He's a pretty cool guy, I'd definitely recommend him to anyone wanting to take a sociology course.

Classes are BORING to say the least. To get a good grade you need to parrot back everything he says in your 3 papers and have him read them over before they're due. Keep track of the quotes he mentions in class bc they're helpful for papers also. I really didn't learn anything until I went to study for the final

He is a very strange professor. His papers are complicated and to get a good grade you must follow his directions exactly and say what he wants to hear. He can be hard to follow and there is a lot of material. Participation and group work are important and can boost your grade.  Overall, he isn't the worst professor but certainly not the best!

He doesn't fit into the stereotypical professor role. He's out there, yes. He can ramble, yes. But I think it is his experiences and his wisdom that make him that way. Derne knows that "we're never gonna survive unless we get a little crazy" If you want a stereotype, don't take him. If you want something real - then do take him.

weird but nice guy. gives high fives. but impossible. analyzing history through psychoanalysis could sound fun, but i swear it's not. only four papers but they're dreadful. he is helpful at office hours but he rambles and so it's hard to really understand waht he's trying to say.  i hated this class. it was hard and dull. the book is HORRIBLE.

Condescending and pompous. First of all, does not understand the basic mechanics of college paper writing and thinks someone asked him to recite his lecture 100 times fast. Difficult to follow. Avoid.

He's pretty crazy, but not necessarily in a bad way. There's a lot of discussions that tend to go off topic. He's helpful with the papers and gives you a lot of topics to choose from. Just go to class and you should be fine.
I'm pretty sure that anyone who deprecates Dr. Derne is just upset about a low grade. I thought he was awesome.

Derne is hilarious. I had no interest in this class but now I like going b/c of his quirks and the material is actually pretty interesting. Just highlight the quotes he gives you in class b/c they will be very helpful later!

Ugh where do I begin. If you miss class he subtracts points from your grade for missing "group work." The group work is complete bull and really an excuse to make attendance mandatory. His papers are hard to write on your own but if you go in and talk to him he will really help you out. Avoid taking this class early because you have to go!!
Boring class.  Very helpful with papers.  Kind of weird.

Well, its really hard to describe Dr. Derne in 350 characters. I would most definitely say he's a bit out there, but he's also really funny. not too tough of a grader, though he's really subjective and tends to like certain people over others. Take 'um if you want an interesting class.

Dr. Derne is hilarious and I never want to miss a class because I can't wait to see what crazy thing he's going to do next. Yes he rambles and talks about wierd things but he's really passionate and if you go in for office hours or really listen to him, you'll do great.
I'm not a fan of Steve Derne. He's a wackjob- the kind that can be hard to learn from. He talks like a surfer dude. He high fives you if you make a comment he likes in class. Wierdo...
Boring lectures. Attendance and class participation is mandatory if you want a decent grade. Make sure you understand everything before you write one of his papers.
The worst ever ! .. I think his classes are the worst .. boring long .. Doesent grade papers fairly..

dont let him know if youre a psych major/socl minor, he'll automatically dislike you and will periodically tell the class he doesnt like those students. his grading is ambiguous and subjective; write only and exactly what he wants to hear. class is entertaining though, you'll never fall asleep.  not horrible, but not the best.

this man is absolutely useless ! worst INTD ever possibly the most boring class I've ever enrolled in and completely irrelevant to probably EVERY major available at geneseo. take his class if you have NO OTHER OPTIONS.

Derne is a silly man. He loves originality for your papers. if you show him that you are actually thinking about what he is saying, he'll love you for it. i agree with the person who said to bring your papers to him the day before; it DEFINITELY helps. plus, he breaks into random hula dancing/singing. i highly recommend this class for INTD 105.

He is definetly an interesting man but thats what makes the class interesting. If you want to do well, finish your essay the day before its due, and bring it to him to check it. He is so helpful with what he wants and will tell you exactly what to do so there is no reason a good grade is not accessable.

hes a weird guy for sure but once u get to knwo him, hes not bad. an acquired taste but if u go to office hours and understand wheres hes coming from, your fineee. he does do random things like take off his shoes n socks in the middle of the class

This guy is awful.  His formula for papers involved an utterly ridiculous/restrictive format where the student must come up with some bizzare thesis that contradicts itself.  He can't teach for 10 minutes without interupting himself to make a mindless criticism of President Bush.  He hates America, and is blatantly proud of it.  Avoid Steve Derne!!

As an alumnus, looking back Prof Derne was really top knotch.   I loved the soc of emothions class, it gave a great opportumity to think outside the box.   THe assignments were very interesting, and I feel, 10 years later, that I really got a lot out of it

TOO much work for a 100 level class, but Derne really helps you learn the material and tries to make it interesting.  He's a fun professor, and has very high expectations.  See him during office hours and make sure you are on the right page with his numerous assignments for this course.

Once you get the formula for the papers down, you can succeed in this class. Keep it simple and you'll do better. Great guy and makes the most of what could be insanely boring material. I loved him, despite some reservations.
grading is weird and very specific if you get the papers down you're fine. for the class, its very entertaining. he's crazy and a fast teacher. loveable guy but the final is hard as hell

Sometimes dry because of the subject of the class but he tries to make it interesting by using a current topic and also just being generally crazy. The grading was fair, just make sure you study your notes for the test and don't miss too many classes because then you miss group participation grades.
No Comments

Amazing, wonderful, fun teacher!  I loved this course and I'm not even a sociology major.  He's difficult, but the class makes you think so much that it was the one class I was depressed about finishing!

Professor Derne is a great teacher. He takes time to explain the material and stresses group work and participation in his class. From Hulla dancing to  the funny noise-clap thing he does, there's hardly a dull moment in his class.

This guy is great!  Very interesting guy, good thinker, a bit of an odd ball.  He'll entertain you.  He likes to hullah dance.  His intd is easy as hell, he explains everything extremely well.  I think he's a socialist.  Fun times.

The classes are discussion led, which proved to be hard to learn in. There are student groups assigned to lead the discussions, which was hard to pay attention during because the same things are repeated, and Eddy never interjects in the discussions to clarify or to elaborate. If she does contribute, she tends to go off on tangents.

Lectures are open discussions about whatever book was read. She is thorough in explaining the material and makes sure you actually understand. Class is not boring, and if it is she lets you out early. If you actually read and pay attention in class you will do just fine. Tests are mostly essay format.

comment: Nice guy, terrible professor. Lectures are impossible to take notes to. Gives no direction for outside of class work. Doesn't prepare you for tests.

comment: Drake is a great man; this class is just very difficult if you don't have a lot of extra time. One day a week, 3 hours long. Reading multiple books (that you purchase) has no meaning to your career. LOTS of books to buy, and you have a 90-minute presentation to complete over the course of class. Don't actually need to do the readings, but get books

There is an extreme amount of reading that I always found it impossible to finish, despite being a fast reader and a great English student in high school. The professor didn't respect my academic accommodation. There is a lot of extra credit, but I never had time to do it since there was so much work.

comment: hes a little confused but hes got the spirit. theres a lot of reading but its really not that hard. the canadian trivia contest was a bit nerve wracking but the losing team gets a 90/100 and the winning team gets a 95/100 no matter what. he does come into class with his pants falling down so thats pretty funny

He is old, and oldschool with the way he does things, but this class is very easy if you just do the work nessacary. There are about 4 essasys that you need to complete throughtout the course of the class. He gives lots of feedback and there is a 5% insentive to get it in early. Online days save you, as you can do whatever. Just do the work!

comment: DO NOT take Canadian Lit if it is not required for your major. It is so hard for no reason. There is a ton of extra credit which is nice but there is an excessive amount of reading each week. Many of his classes end up being online even though it is an "in-person" class. Overall it is not a class I would take again.

Canadian Literature with Dr. Drake is an excellent introduction to the English major. There is a lot of reading, but Drake is so passionate about them that it motivated me to stay on top of things. He gave thorough feedback, and even if you don't do well on the easy essays, there is enough extra credit to get a good grade. But trivia contest blows.

The lectures were painful to get through. He just talked about nonsense the whole time that had nothing to do in class. He explained things very difficultly making concepts hard to understand. The assignments were annoying and unnecessarily time consuming.

ENG361- History of the English Language. Lectures are long, boring, and lack meaningful purpose.  His directions are usually very unclear and overcomplicated to a point that none of it makes sense.  For example the syllabus is 27 page long, yet no one in class ever has any idea about what's happening or what the expectations are.
Participation and attendance matter.

*DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS UNLESS YOU ARE PURSUING AN ENGLISH CAREER (for example, do not take this if you are simply just a an education major, psych etc.) The project Dr. Drake assigned was to memorize a 2 page poem from Middle English, and he expected us to spend 2 hours a day memorizing, on top of the hours of readings a week. Very difficult.
tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework']

comment: Taking English 203 with Dr. Drake was definitely doable. He assigns hours of reading a week, however, his weekly assignments he bases the readings on are up to you on which reading you decide to analyze. He has a very manageable amount of papers that are very spread out, and he gives a lot of extra credit opportunities.
Never take a class with this man. Impossible directions to follow and will make you read a lot. He is also a super harsh grader. I do not recommend.

Dr. Drake grades tough on the essays but he gives enough extra credit opportunities and his participation is worth so much that this class should become an easy B+. Lots of reading throughout the week but they're used for extra credit quizzes.

i'm sorry but this guy kinda sucks. extremely boring lectures. he's nice and occasionally tells a funny anecdote, but that can't make up for mediocre teaching. he does really care about the subject matter but i didn't so maybe that's why. everything he send you will be unnecessarily long and complicated which really really irked me

First he was intimidating and scared me. However as the semester continued, he is actually a pretty nice guy and understanding! He is very passionate about what he teaches, so it can be over bearing. He does give a lot of readings and a weekly discussion post, however it is bearable. Honestly would recommend if you have a passion for literature.

Dr. Drake's class is definitely reading-heavy, but he is pretty accessible outside of class for help. He offers lots of extra credit opportunities, which is good for grades. His attendance policy is definitely tough, but if you explain to him a circumstance of your absence, he's pretty understanding. He's passionate about what he teaches.

I am currently taking him for Canadian Literature and I would recommend quite literally every other course. You are only allowed one absence, you cannot be late (It is an 8:30 class), you are not supposed to get up during class, and he assigns way too much reading every week. If you can, take any other English professor besides him.

comment: Wouldn't suggest his class. Good Luck.

I liked Dr. Drake as a person. However, his lectures were 2+ hours. That being said, as long as you kept up with the reading (there's a lot of reading) and turned in the essays on time, you were fine. He assigns your grade based on a few essays, though, so make sure your essays are good.

comment: Drake is a great choice for Hum, so much extra credit, you can get an A without really reading a whole lot or being a great writer
tags: ['Gives good feedback', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'EXTRA CREDIT']

comment: Professor Drake is really smart and is strict on participation. This class is challenging, you must read a lot, however, there is no reason to not get an A+ with all of the extra credit opportunities he provides. Hard work will get you far, he is truly a fair grader and wants you to do well.

Dr. Drake's Canadian Literature class was one of the most awful classes I've ever taken. He would often lead unbearable rants and every single reading was provocative or phallic in some way, or interpreted to be so by Dr. Drake. He offers a lot of opportunities for extra credit, which is fine, but the actual course was awful.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass."]

comment: Dr. Drake is a very interesting guy. He is quite passionate and knowledgeable about all things humanities. Class was often dull, but participation is important. A surplus of extra credit opportunities.
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', 'LECTURE HEAVY']

comment: I took a class with him abroad and he ruined the trip and the experience. He made most people uncomfortable and didn't care to make things interesting. If you see him as the professor for your abroad program do not go because you will be very disappointed with your experience. You spend so much time doing work for him you cannot enjoy the country.

Drake is an excellent instructor and teacher of material, though I worry that the sheer amount of material that he assigns will turn many off. He grades harshly and brutally, though it usually is fair; he has high standards. Probably would not recommend for majors outside of English. Delightfully awkward man who is extremely witty and intelligent.
