comment: Drake is a good professor and is very knowledgeable about what he teaches. He gives several opportunities for extra credit that should be taken advantage of. That being said, he is extremely nit picky and not clear on directions. One on the requirements is to memorize and present a 100 line poem so if in class, start working on memorization ASAP
tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass."]

comment: You'll learn a lot and it's a very interesting class, but if you want a good grade, you need to put work in. His assignments can be very complicated and specific and he's incredibly nitpicky, but he's a fairly easy grader and gives tons of extra credit. He's a good professor, but you need to stay on top of things to do well.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'EXTRA CREDIT']

comment: If you can ton of time to his class, go for it. He is knowledgable but nitpicky. HOWEVER, the reading is hard to get through with a lot of it. His syllabus is incredibly long, confusing, and overwhelming. He also sends long overwhelming emails full of study questions for every reading. Class is good ONLY if you have a LOT of time and energy for it.
tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK']

comment: Students who don't like Graham Drake are the students who are too lazy to put in the work, it's as simple as that. This class was very discussion-based which is much better than your standard talking head lecture class. He's a tough but reasonable grader, and he offers so much extra credit that there's no reason NOT to get an A.

Lectures were interesting.  Participation is a large part of the grade and I participated once and still got an A.  Never once read the books or spark notes and did fairly well on the papershe is a tough grader though.  Did one extra credit paper out of the 2,000+ that are available throughout the semester. Highly recommend.
tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'EXTRA CREDIT']

comment: Would highly recommend. He's kind of a nut, but extremely well organized and clear on what he expects. He makes things fun and exciting even at 8AM. You don't need to know every detail on every book, I used SparkNotes a lot and was still able to get the A. NEVER skip class or come in late! Endless extra credit. Actually found it semi-interesting!
tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass."]

comment: I recommend Drake to EVERYONE I know. He is oddly funny & teaches in a way that really makes it easy to learn. He does grade attendance & partic. so make sure you show up to class and say at least 1-2 things. Only had 1 exam, other 4 grades were papers & partic. Gives an unreal amount of EC each week so take advantage of it. Really fantastic prof!!
tags: ['Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'EXTRA CREDIT']

comment: I was a physics major at Geneseo, and didn't know anything about any of the literature we read before coming into the class.  Never did I find the class overwhelming or unfair.  Maybe people aren't used to doing work?  Dr. Drake was really passionate, and I actually enjoyed sitting through his class every day.

I would not recommend. Very intelligent, and kind man. However, workload expectations were excessive: posts every week, long take-home quizzes (many of them), having to memorize and recite a 3+ page poem, over 100 lines, on top of 2 papers. His class is quite boring, also. If you can handle the workload, he grades quite fairly. SHOW UP TO CLASS.

flamboyant and odd in his teaching but actually makes the awful class at bearable sometimes takes attendance everyday and a sign grade off for everyday you miss, didnt read a single book spark notes and take decent notes and its easy, only 2 essays and 2 tests, class is a discussion but just say one thing and then play games and did other hw and

At first, I was put off by the large amount of reading, and Drake's "pet peeves," which are picky. But, now I really enjoy him. He's interesting, knowledgeable, passionate, and an extremely fair grader. Lots of extra credit was offered, and he gave great feedback on papers. Just go to class, speak up, and do as much of the readings as you can :)

Drake is a very tough grader and his lectures are somewhat incomprehensible.  Before this class I was very interested in the subject and open to discussing it, but his lectures completely negated that.  It was a chore and a punishment to simply attend class.  His class is more lecture style and this takes away from the topic.

MUST GO TO CLASS. A lot of reading but that's true of any humn class. The tests are really hard but considering there are only two and they count for so little it's not a big deal. Most of your grade comes from attendance and class discussion. The only time you need to memorize a specific date is for extra credit quizzes.

He's a really nice guy and yes, adorably awkward. He drops really great jokes. But it's true that he does expect an unreasonable about of reading and that he is very picky about some dumb things. Still, it's manageable. He gives lots of EC opportunities. I just wouldn't take it in conjunction with other stressful classes.

He's adorably awkward, with his bow ties and sweater vests and utter enthusiasm for the subject. Very interesting class. He drops some pretty hysterical jokes into the lectures. Pretty easy essay grader so long as you do the readings and can incorporate them, but its a *lot* of reading.

(I'm the last entry) ....your grade drops immensely if you miss more than one class. Stupid petty things are important to him, it's memorization he doens't want to hear what you think about anything just ridiculously difficult and unengaging and highly highly demanding. I can't say this enough really really HARD!

I'm an English major and cannot handle how much he assigns.  You have to remember 100s of dates and he expects you to know every one. Insanely tough grader, I had the wrong time period for a completely correct answser and he gave me a zero on that question. His syllabus alone is 18 pages of nonsense things that irk him and if you miss one class...

Drake presents the material very clearly. The class does lots of fun, interesting activities. He's VERY knowledgeable and helpful, if very (charmingly) awkward on a personal level.  He demands a lot of you with concern to reading, but it's worth it because you'll be learning so much. He also offers many opportunities for extra credit.

Drake's class is pretty tough but he is a great teacher. If you are not doing well he gives lots of chances for extra credit. He is extremely open and friendly to students, he makes it seem like he actually wants you to do well.

My first impression of him wasn't great but honestly, he grew on me and is one of my favorite professors.  He is incredibly knowledgeable and passionate about the subject matter, he's funny and makes class interesting.  He expects a lot of time and effort from his students, but not anymore than he puts in.Really cares about his students, great guy!

Very thought provoking class!  I learned a ton from the text and his lectures.  He is a very fair grader and is crystal clear about everything. The class focuses on the literature aspect of the bible and the koran, not religion though some comments lean towards atheism.

Took for Brit lit, couldn't remember #. This man is brilliant. He's shy, but he's very nice, his lectures can drag a bit, but he's funny and likeable. Had to memorize and recite poems for this class, really fun. Have to do work and study, but honestly, if you can't handle that then you shouldn't take his classes.

Oozing with arrogance, Professor Drake is a professor to avoid--in my opinion.  I  was inundated with pedantry and condescending scoffs.  When he feels the need to criticize his intellectual subordinates, he should remember that his undergrad college was not Harvard.  I feel that he felt threatened when his authority was questioned.  Rewritten.

Drake is an amazing professor. I think that he is one of those people you either like or you don't. I personally thought that he was very understanding and willing to work with the students. He offers you every possible way to contact him if you should have questions. He gives almost too many opportunities for extra credit. Read! Speak up in class!

Brit Lit I and Chaucer: Wonderful guy, helpful. Bark is worse than his bite. Seems to be a little shy, but is exceedingly, remarkably fair in every way. Gives ample opportunity for extra credit. Lectures are always interesting, he tries so hard to crack jokes, clearly passionate about subject. Refreshingly predictable, but not boring by any means.
Great professor, really committed to his work- asks a lot of his students but gives more than ample chances for extra credit. Drake is extremely knowledgeable about his subject matter.

Drake really is arrogant, not that smart. He knows a lot, but that doesn't make him any more intelligent than me. I got an A in his humn 1 and humn 2 classes, but I strongly dislike him anyway. He makes inappropriate comments about Jake Gyllenhall and other male actors. In addition, he lives all the way in Connecticut and rarely shows up for class.

I dunno what to think. I usually fear going to my class with him, but when I do my work its a pleasant experience because I feel smart. lol. I don't feel like he looks down on students, I just think he kinda needs to read less and play halo more or something

I have to admit that at the beginning of the semester I was terrified of him. He's a brilliant guy but he expects a lot from his students. If you put forth the effort, so will he! Don't expect to waltz into his class and do fine just because you showed up. You will learn A LOT, but be sure to do all the reading and don't slack off.

if you get him drop the course before it even starts! His midterm and final are insanely hard and no matter how much effort you put in you are still going to do horrible in the class.... I'm a A to B student and I'll be lucky to get a C-

Gives a slightly insane amount of work but if you're interested, it's fascinating.  Pretty fair grader.  He's brilliant, so if you get the idea that he thinks he's above you, it's because he is.  So he gets to be arrogant.  Very idiosynchratic but in a cute way.  Not exactly warm (in or out of class) but an excellent, engaging professor.
Drake is articulate, but gives too much work for the course.

Amazing class. Demanded and expected high results, but willing to work with students.  Set a high bar and pushed us to get there, discovered amazing concepts and a thirst for literature.  Agree with the others- take this class and be prepared for the work and work's rewards.  You cannot take this class if you expect to miss any due to a play, unfortunately.
Put me to sleep

If you are lazy you won't like this professor. I LOVED it! I learned more in this class than any other. Partly because it was my senior year and I was finally disciplined, but mostly because of the awesome professor.

This class was very interesting and he knows SOOOO much! If you asked questions he would most likely clarify. We asked what would be on the final and he told us to study and entire 300 page book for a 25 question multiple choice test! Be prepared to work hard!!!
Be prepared to work.  Very nice and worth taking, just don't fool yourself:  you're going to be doing a lot of work.
I learned a lot in his class.  He is a wonderful lecturer, and the exams were fair.  I think it helps if you know how to write, and if you're good at getting the gist of readings pretty quickly.

He demands a lot, so only take him if you want to concentrate in what he is teaching, because you will learn a lot but it will be difficult. He's some one I wanted to perform well for because he is so intelligent.
a horrible human being, endless amounts of work, pointless quizzes, makes you feel stupid when you participate in class.... don't ever take a class from him
Awful... really a bad teacher... thinks he is above students... mean guy
Tons of reading, always wants you to know specific dates of historical events exactly to the date...condecending to everyone including his co-professor.

A lot of pointless reading, massive amounts of work, and Drake hasn't a clue that we don't desire to become as learned as him in just one semester. Unbelievable for a 200-level course-- I had to drop it.

does lecture a lot, but is unbelievably intelligent.  he really knows his stuff!  he is very easy to contact and is great about answering email.  midterm is hard, but the final project at the end of class in place of a final is great.

Class gives a good background of Brit Lit but is painfully boring. The quizzes are tough because he expects you to regurgitate everything he had said. He's a fair teacher and very nice, but he needs to learn how to deliver a lecture.
he's very clear about what he expects from you and he's good about returning papers quickly, he's a little odd but very fair and he offers extra credit opportunities

Take him if #1--you want to do endless amounts of reading, and #2--if you want to feel like a fool when you offer answers to questions.  He's a very intense man...I dont suggest taking British Literature from him
Awful! Never take him for humn unless you want endless amounts of pointless work
very fast-paced, hard mid-term. easy to contact.  overall, very fun.
A little odd, alright teacher

Although some of the ratings may be daunting, I genuinely loved this class.  It was a very discussion heavy class, but as long as you input your opinion every once in a while you will be fine.  I would 110% recommend going to the writing center, it dramatically increased my essay grades.  Once you figure out what he likes he's super easy.

His participation standard is fairly high
u only read the leviathan (for hobbes) and it gets boring quick.

Participation is graded extremely harshly and his criteria is completely arbitrary. Perfect attendance is not enough, and you will be penalized if you're not the most talkative person in class. Lectures are dry, and the course as a whole is poorly organized.

Herold covers all the material you'll need for assignments (which are really just the tests) in class, but it's helpful to do the reading beforehand because participation is graded. Great about answering questions, before exams he will help you prep your essay if you go to office hours. Organized and respectful.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things', 'Accessible outside class']

comment: Herold is okay. He assigns a lot of reading and some of his lectures are confusing, but he encourages participation in class and seems to be passionate about the subject.

PLSC130: There is always assigned reading in this class! It was somewhat interesting as an elective but I could not keep up with the readings. I didn't have 2+ hours to devote to the class every day. If the subject truly interests you, take the class, but if you're looking for an easy A, this class is not it.

I took a few classes with Professor Herold but the moment that stuck with me the most was Constitutional Law when he entered and said "I am not a lawyer, and this is not a law class". What even is the point of him teaching the class then? Herold is a nice guy but a pretty terrible professor. Very dry lectures as well. Avoid at all costs.

Professor Herold is unclear about expectations for assignments. When you go to ask for help or clarification, he is incredibly unhelpful. His class is difficult for no reason. I studied and worked upwards of 7 hours a week for this class, and feel like I have learned nothing. His exams are ridiculous, they ask for information he only mentions once.

To be honest, he isn't my favorite. If you're not into philosophy this class isn't it. He is kind of a know it all and every time people raise their hands he told them they were wrong. He is really organized though and if you don't go to class you won't do good bc he lectures by word of mouth. He does give you a lot of time for assignments

Basics: requires you to buy the books (7 total), no technology in class, weekly quizzes, and 3 exams (take home long response). 
Not the most engaging professor and the material is heavy and hard to understand. If you disect the reading on your own, it isn't likely that you will reach the same conclusion. Attending class helps.

Professor Harold was knowledgeable and made his lectures entertaining. He challenged the class to view different opinions from the textbook. I would concur that he was a harsh grader, especially for the term paper. When he has criticisms, he's not afraid to tell you. He asked participants to read out loud at times which made it difficult to focus.
tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Participation matters', 'Graded by few things']

comment: Dr. Herold is okay as a person but grades extremely harshly. He is the professor who never gives a 100, and thinks it says something about his class not realizing it's actually a poor reflection on him. On the other hand, you can tell he really cares about the material he is teaching, though his lectures can be dry at times. Extra credit available!

Dr. Herold is a straight-up good guy. His lectures for Political Theory can get dry at times, but he cares deeply about what he is teaching and it shows. The level of reading can be hefty and very dense stuff, but he does what he can to help us understand what thinkers are saying. I would recommend him, as his passion for the content is admirable.

Awesome professor! He is very passionate about what he teaches in this course. Even though he assigns a lot of reading of cases, they are all super interesting. He gives a 4 question quiz every Wednesday on the readings, there is a midterm, a term paper and a final.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Graded by few things']

comment: Herold is one of brightest professors I've had, and one of the most passionate too! If you do the reading, participate and attend class regularly you'll get a good grade. He tells you exactly what to expect from the course. Lectures are actually interesting and explain the reading in depth. If you're struggling, he's approachable outside of class.
good guy tbh, lectures are boring and no slides, good news is tests are easy and he gives a couple extra credit assignments. just do the readings and you will get an A
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Graded by few things', 'Test heavy']

comment: Dr. Herold is a brilliant guy, and he really knows his stuff too. He's extremely passionate about what he teaches and it rubs off on you. His classes are challenging but rewarding. Show up to class, do the work and you will get a lot out of it. Can't recommend enough.
Not helpful at all. Graded harshly and by very few things. Midterm and final were almost impossible. Class was uninteresting and would never take another course with this instructor again.

Political Theory is dry. Prepare to be bored sitting in lectures hearing about a bunch of dead dudes. But Dr. Herold is great. He's a very smart person, and he clearly loves talking about what he teaches. One paper and/or a midterm and a final. Quiz on the reading on Wednesdays and attendance roulette on Mondays so go to class!
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Graded by few things']

comment: A lot of reading but if you're interested it's not bad and he goes through it all in class with well-facilitated discussion. Reading quizzes are easy, if you read. Exams are very hard because of all the material they cover. If you write a solid essay, he'll give you a good grade. Hard to get an A but he's worth the hard work/B grade. Learned a lot

I really enjoyed this class. Class isn't offered all the time. Books sometimes dry. A lot of reading, sometimes over 100 pages between classes. Every book asked to purchase was used. Prof. Herold keeps it interesting and is very available and willing to help outside of class.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS']

comment: Aaron Herold is a nice guy, but not a nice grader. The class was not interesting, very very reading heavy, and almost impossible to get an A in. Frustrating, would not take again.
tags: ['Tough Grader', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS', 'Tests are tough']

comment: He is an amazing professor. UTILIZE HIS OFFICE HOURS. If you go to his office hours and ask him questions he will lead you on the right path to get the grade you deserve. He is a tough grader but if you go to his office hours you will see your work pay off. I utilized it at every chance I could and my grade went up 2 letters. Its worth it.

Interesting person and seems nice. Grading is terribly tough. Offers extra credit but is worth extremely little- not worth your effort. I had my research paper finished in time to ask the prof for insight. He said he doesn't read papers twice, so you are on your own. My GPA came down considerably with this class.
Great guy and gives very good lectures. Material is interesting but there is a lot of reading and quizzes every Friday. I would take him again but he is a very tough grader.

He's such a nice guy. He assigns a lot of reading. I mean a lot of it. It's not terrible to get through, and he goes over it in class. Tests are pretty easy if you do the reading and pay attention in class. It was a discussion based class and he actually facilitated great discussions. Would 100% recommend. Great class, learned a lot.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'Amazing lectures']

comment: Lofkrantz is a really harsh grader but I think that's because she cares so much about her subject area. It's not the easiest class but there are no tests, just 5 papers and a rewrite and 2 map quizzes. If you like history and want to take a writing class then I recommend this one. Just know it's not an easy A but it's not too hard if you read.
horrible teacher. She has a Canadian accept and a stuttering problem. Unpredictable grader. My least favorite class.

Very harsh grader - I have only seen a few people receive A-'s the entire semester. An A is basically unheard of. She considers anything above a C+ to be 'good.' She has a stuttering problem. Not very helpful, although she does allow some in class writing days. No exams, but 6 papers. Lots of reading, and she gives map quizzes. Least favorite class
She is a good overall teacher. References her notes too much but is interested in the class material. Gives study guides for the tests which is nice and there is a 9 page research paper.
Good professor, class is 1 day a week and can be very long & dry at times, bring something to entertain yourself.  Nice guy overall.
Do what you are suppose to do and it won't be difficult to get a good grade. I got an A- is fairly ok amount of effort. His exams are tough but he curves.
Really awesome guy. One paper, one group presentation, and one final exam. The rest of your grade is showing up to class and participating. I would highly recommend taking any class he is teaching.

This teacher is great.  He goes straight from the text book and makes his own slides according to it.  You will get good grades as long as you read the text book each week because he only holds classes once a week.  Study from the book, listen to his lectures, and complete all the homework and you wont have a problem doing well in his class.

Fasoldt in my opinion was great this semester. For such a boring topic, he did his best to make it somewhat interesting. If you go to class, do the homework(minimal), and put a little effort in there's no reason why you shouldn't do well. His work experience is something I feel a lot of the other professors can't watch as well.

Does not teach well enough during class to cover all the material well enough.  Tests are extremely difficult but not terrible if you study well enough before.  Textbook is your best friend because you'll be teaching yourself.

He's an adjunct (accountant during the day and a professor at night). He knows what he's talking about but isn't a great teacher. Material directly from textbook. Grades relatively easily; believes in a curve on tests. Having him once a week is tough if you don't know what you're doing, recommend only if you've taken some sort of accounting before.

He tries. He's a really great guy, it's not his fault his subject is dry and boring. He lectures straight from the textbook, sometimes word for word, so note-wise it's okay to miss class, but he does randomly collect homework. He grades easily though, there isn't a ton of work.

Wylie was my first IR class at geneseo and as an IR major it was probably the best way to start it off. Shes very enthusiastic and approachable!I'd suggest her class to anyone and everyone but unfortunately she's here for only a year... :(

Looove Professor Wylie and this class. I didnt really know too much about the developing world and now I think i'm going to pursue IR on the developing world track. There's a lot of information but it's really interesting. She just wants to open up people what's going on around the world. She's such a cool professor and is super open to students.

A solid teacher but she gets off topic all of the time.  I'm decently interested in third world development which helped me along in the class, but it still is interesting material.  Not too many grades, but the grades she gives aren't too bad either.  I'd reccomend her.

I'm over a year out of college now, but the wound in me left by this class in 2022 is not one that time can heal. Seems to believe that her classes are your only classes.  Assigns way too much work, and the reading that she assigns usually doesn't wind up being all that relevant in the end.  I could not be paid enough to take another class with her.
Difficult grader w/equally difficult readings.  Although I was a huge fan of the topic, I was not a huge fan of the class!  If you like to read, take Emilye, if not, DON'T!

she gives a ridiculous amount of reading without feeling the need to explain what she wants us to know...she didn't help me at all when i aksed for it and seemed to be annoyed that i was asking for help.

comment: Lots of smaller writing assignments but fun to do. Expectations and rubrics were clear. Takes time to answer questions and make sure we're all good. Really learned so much from this guy.

Prof. Allgayer is the best professor I had. His door is always open. He made the materials interesting and relevant. if you know how to follow directions then you'll do fine in his class. if you don't then you'll struggle. some say he's a tough grader but he gives lots of helpful feedback and wants you to apply it on future work. he's also surprisingly caring and helpful.

I honestly do not know how allgayer is still teaching at Geneseo. I do not know how he got hired, he does absolutely nothing and has his TAs grade for him (which is not allowed) and they do not even know what is going in. He is sassy and rude to all of his students. Do not take him!!!

he has a good style of teaching where he includes not only lecture but powerpoint, videos, photos, etc. He barely gives the students any time to do the labs he assigns at the last 10 minutes of class. comment: Really enjoyed this professor. He managed to keep the class interesting and the course load light. This was my first time writing a 15 page paper, but his expectations were clear and concise.

comment: Anderson's class is not easy, if that is what you are looking for. However, his class is very interesting and teaches you a lot. His class was my favorite one I have taken this semester. As stated by other former students, she demonstrated clear bias in her treatment of students.  Most troubling was a highly condescending tone and language used toward students who asked for clarification or challenged her stance on issues.  I do not recommend her.
pretty unclear on expectations. some people she graded easily. others she really stuck it to them. would not recommend this prof.

Avoid if you can, ridiculous amount of written work. If you are unlucky to have her then do all assignments exactly like her stupid rubrics say. No more and no less. Many sleepless nights because of her assignments.

Conto is crazy!!!

He is not a good teacher, he meanders, digresses, and speaks in a boring tone of voice. I'm not sure why all the other negative comments got deleted, I didn't think that was allowed on this site. Dr. McPherson is a good professor. his tests are straightforward. If you ask for help he is happy to help

His intent to be helpful is clearly evident but he does go off on tangents at times. He's pretty laid-back and is a bit aloof with assignment deadlines sometimes. But overall, he's a great professor, caring and concerned in helping students learn.
I don't care how many great schools he went to, the man can not teach.

Very educated in his field; loves to talk about any questions you may have.  He can sometimes get off topic a little, but its only because he wants to let you know everything you had a question about!
some people are very smart, just not meant to teach

Its obvious he knows what he's talking about, but don't ask him a question or you'll never hear the end of it. He takes simple things and makes them as confusing as possible. He does however generally know what hes talking about
his love of science shows- not so clear during lectures- really cool guy.

Personally, I would say to avoid this professor at all costs. The tests are very unpredictable compared to the course material, but she wants you to succeed. If you want to know happiness do not take this course with this professor. she is so unorganized, all her slides are pictures. Her homeworks are nothing like the test which are all over the place. comment: Honestly, I have never had her for a class, but the few interactions I have had with her put such a bad taste in my mouth that I would never even bother taking a class with her. One of the easiest classes. Didnt have to come every day, just do the worksheet at some point. Class itself is discussion-based. AWFUL professor never take a class with her if you can help it. First day of lecture she decided to complain about students for 10 minutes instead of actually teaching us anything. Not very helpful either.

comment: Professor Muench is one of the most caring professors at Geneseo. She works with every student to make sure they will succeed in her classes! Her tests have multiple-choice, short response sections. She is willing to meet with you and explain what she is looking for when she grades exams and gives you tips for taking her exams.

Dr. Muench can be disorganized when grading and doing classroom activites. There are 5 tests, and you only take 3 (drop one, don't take one). There is a lot of forgiveness built into this course. This course was taken in Ghana and was a really amazing experience. There is quite a bit of writing but it's not difficult to do. Its 10+ reflections of your own experience and how it relates to the textbook. She was really flexible with due dates because it's a study abroad course

comment: When the assistant professor outshines the actual professor, you know its bad. Dr. Muench is incredibly bland and does not seem to really understand the material or how to relay it to the class. There are plenty of sections for BIO 117 & 119, and they are all graded and structured the same way- don't take hers unless you absolutely have to.
Don't base your opinion of this professor on the intro biology course. Get into upper level classes with her and you'll see how much of a gem she is.

Quite possibly the worst teacher I've ever had.

Muench is fantastic at the 300 level! She makes evolutionary both fun and insightful. She cannot teach at all and her lectures are just about big topic. She does't even go over much  in her power points. It's useless to go to class but you have to show up as she takes attendance.

Lots of reading in this class. Online quizzes are very easy and often the questions are already online. Tests are very fair. Lectures are pretty dry but you have to go for participation assignments.

Everything was discussion based, no actual lectures. You teach yourself and read the entire textbook. The only good thing about this class was that all exams were online so you can look everything up...until she changed the final to paper! Took all semester to return grades too. Last class I ever take with her.

Very disorganized. Takes all semester to get grades back. We didn't get them back until finals week. Unclear on what she wants. Everything was discussion based,barely any lectures.

Muench really is not suitable for a lecture hall setting. She reads from the slides and often questions herself before telling us to look it up. Honestly I feel like she would be better in a small classroom, just don't take her for intro to bio. Being a pre-bio major is hard enough. If you don't maintain that C+, you're out.

Reads straight from the powerpoint which consists of figures copied from the textbook. The only reason to come to class is daily group assignments which waste time and often don't relate to the material.

She can't give lectures to large classes. her slides are not relevant to the material on the test, which is mostly textbook material. Read and know the book, but going to lectures is pointless. She is much to eager to have you give up rather than actually learn the stuff.

Muench is extremely boring to listen to and not very knowledgeable in what she's teaching. Reads straight from slides also. If you're doing badly in the course and want to improve, her best advice is that you drop. Not helpful or a good teacher. She is the worst. Avoid.

Extremely dry lectures. Always has an issue with the PRS system. Gives reading quizzes for every chapter which aren't too bad as the answers are online. I thought she was great until Feissner taught and now that she is back... ugh... it's awful. Take another professor for general biology if you can. She's nice but just not a very good professor.
Try to avoid her if you can. She's a nice lady, just terribly boring and shy. I felt like she was afraid of the class! All the answers are online. Lots of textbook work!

This teacher is horrible!!! she is absolutely clueless on how to teach general biology! I had the unfortunate experience of having her 2 semesters in a row. she is rarely prepared for the class, completely rely's on the powerpoint, and does not answer your question clearly and properly. I would switch out of her class as soon as you can!

She seems clueless in a lecture class like this. Evolutionary is an easy class, mostly group discussion. She's a cool prof but that hour and fifteen minutes of STRAIGHT class discussion definitely gets old. Dr. Muench's class has been my favorite so far at Geneseo. Format is mostly group discussion with little lecture and there are a lot of group quizzes. You have to put in a lot of time to get a good grade, but she is definitely willing to help if you ask and very accommodating with the workload. Overall the exams were very fair.

Evolutionary biology was a great class. Class style is similar to her other classes in that they are largely group discussion. This is at times redundant, however they can be fun. Her tests require extra time so do not wait until the last minute! Put effort into the class and it will be worthwhile.

This class was absolutely miserable.  Every class is in the form of group discussion and there was little to no lecture on the part of the professor.  She was condescending and never willing to give extra help.  Even when she did, she was mean and unhelpful.

I really like Dr. Muench and this class was fun and easy enough. Each week we had a quiz from the textbook but we get to take it with a group that she assigns and our grades are always high..there are also some projects and essays due but she gives you plenty of time to do them. I find her friendly and will be taking other classes with her for sure

this is the second time i have had her here and she is a horrible teacher..gives NO direction/help, holds no interest during class, grading is unfair,material presented unclear,and is the most unapproachable, miserable person...anddd dont bother getting sympathy if a family emergency or death comes up because she doesn't have human feeling

We prepared for a project ALL SEMESTER, and it took me 30 mins to do.
Fought for my life to stay awake in class, which I've never had a problem with. Make sure to take really good notes.
Great professor, anthro is not my favorite subject but still kept me interested in the material. Very reasonable and made accomodations for me when I needed it.

His lectures are always very engaging, but quite dense. Tests are pretty easy, and the one essay has clear directions and prompts. Readings can be quite dense, but he doesn't put a huge emphasis on them.

Took his ANTH100 class for an outside major requirement and almost switched my entire major to ANTH. He keeps lectures very interesting and gives you helpful note guides to ease stress. Exams were super quick and reasonable. Was willing to help when I had absences with one quick email. Great guy!

He is a super funny guy and very passionate about his job, which I love, and it keeps the lectures interesting. I just had a hard time with the exams because they were so heavily focused on how well you took notes. Great guy

Pacheco is awesome. Attendance does matter if you want a good grade. But he is very very flexible if you just email him. His grading policies are SUPER FAIR. I would definitely take a class with him again.
Interesting class, assignments could be difficult at times.

Professor Pacheco is great! The course can be challenging though. There is a ton of information crammed into the slides and it can be hard to keep up. Tests can be difficult too but if you go to class, pay attention, and read the articles he provides, you should be okay. I would take another class with him in the future.

Pacheo is a nice guy but the exams are really difficult because his lectures are very hard to follow. He was very nice but not understanding. His tests are all written with short essay and long essay. I felt like I was taking an the AP Lit exam. It was absolutely impossible to pay attention in his class. He is an evil wizard who casts a spell on you to make sure you can't pay attention. Good luck on tests.

Pacheco is a very nice person, but I did not love him as a professor. Classes were all lecture based, with boring content (personally). Professor Pacheco makes the material engaging, but you'll need to stay on top of readings and attend lectures to do well. unstuck study was a lifesaver for prep!

This class was extremely difficult for a 100 level anthropology class. He is a super nice guy but personally the class was boring. But if you are taking it just for the credit I recommend, you can skip most the classes and it not effect you. For my class at least all the quizzes were take home so you can use notes, and the tests were also super easy as long as you skim the readings and watch the movies.

Exams in this class make NO sense. Quizzes are easy and open-note. Relatively accommodating of accessibility issues and included a slide based on a classmate's particular life experience to clarify a possible spot of tension, but tends to ramble while saying he won't ramble. 

Kind. Only major gripe is the nonsense exams.

comment: Professor Pacheco was amazing. He made sure his lectures were interesting and engaging, he would walk around in front of the classroom and would keep your attention on him. If you want to pass this class, make sure you attend the classes. This was a great course and he was a great professor.

Pacheco is such a kind man. Theres a decent amount of reading which is common for a 200 class. He respects his students and allows them participation points if absent and you email him for the zoom recording. He answers emails at basically lightning speed. It's evident he's passionate about the course and cares for his students.

comment: Prof. Pacheco is a really nice guy with passion for what he teaches and a genuine care for his students. The course consists of discussion posts and exams so performance on exams is important but you can use your notes and as long as you come to class you have everything you need to do well. He provides a lot of helpful feedback as well.

Keeped lectures interesting. Tests were all online, but wasn't a class you could cheat through as the questions were original. watched some interesting films. Seems to be a traditional family guy who holds traditional beliefs to a certain degree. Didn't bother me but I could see why it would bother others.

All quizzes online and a few short papers. Make sure you go to class when he's showing a film because it's going to appear on the quizzes and papers. He posts everything online so you don't have to go in but he gives very interesting lectures. Great guy!

Attendance is not required, but you will DEFINITELY do better if you go. Lots of weekly readings but you need to do them for quizzes and writing assignments. Lectures are easy to follow and understand.
Tests are hard and you wont be able to find the stuff on quizlet or anything, so it does require studying. He is extremely engaging and kind!!!

Class consisted of 5 quizzes and 3 writing assignments. Quizzes were online but they were timed. Go to lecture for the quizzes. For Kottak book, really only need to read chapter summaries. Whole essay on the Middleton book. He had a way of making his lectures interesting. You could tell he is very passionate about what he is doing!!
Awesome funny and just loveable. he noticed me when I didn't even try and that meant a lot.

Super easy class as long as you come to class on days where videos are being shown and do the readings. He is also a great person and makes the class so much more interesting to learn about than it is. He's GOATED.

Pacheco is very energetic and passionate about archaeology, which has made this class interesting. I enjoy going to class. He engages with his students and likes when you participate. I'm glad someone recommended this interesting class to me. This lecture is large enough that I didn't get to know Prof. Pacheco, but I'm sure if I went to office hours I would've. Professor Pacheco was an interesting man. His lecture slides are on canvas, so you don't have to be in class. We watched a couple of movies so we can write a paper, and he graded the papers harshly. Really sweet guy. He's really knowledgable and passionate about the topic which makes the class enjoyable. Make sure to read and study or else you won't do well.

Dr. Pacheco is a very sweet man and tries to make the lectures fun for everyone. Although attendance is not mandatory, you should go to all the lectures and make sure you read the assigned readings. Great Professor who is very passionate about anthropology. His class made me consider anthro as minor, and the lectures were always interesting. I love Mitschow! Compared to the majority of the other accounting profs at Geneseo he is 10x more interesting. You will not be bored in class and it will go by quickly and he will literally teach you exactly what you need to know for quizzes and exams.. no need to read the book unless you want extra info. i love this guy!!!

Mitschow is a hell of a man.  Very good at understanding/teaching accounting.  Don't have to read, just pay attention during lectures.  For tests, study the handouts/quizzes for 80% of the material.  Also, evey one of the 6 pop quizzes comes after a handout on the exact same material as the handout.  Good professor, take him if you can.

Great Teacher! If you need any help he is willing to do anything for you to understand it.  Class notes are extremely helpful.  Tests and quizzes are easy to prepare for. I went away with a great understanding of the material.
MITSCHOW IS THE MAN, if u get a chance to take any class with him do it, go to class and do the hw and u'll get a dam good grade, he'll answer any of ur questions, smart funny guy

Yeah he shouts and does annoying cartoon voices, but an A is definitely manageable in his class. The best way to get an A is to study the handouts, vocab, and old exams in his outbox. Mark is a very generous grader so don't sweat it if you make some mistakes along the way.
This class stressed me out a lot. Mitschow is unbearably loud and annoying. Hopefully a good professor will teach Acct 102 soon.
so animated-helpful for a super early class!  his quizzes and tests are fair (he gives you as many points as he can)...things you'll hear OVER AND OVER  'i digress' and 'shizam!'

Mitschow is awesome.  This class isn't too hard if you put in the time to do the non-mandatory homework and some of the reading.  Don't get caught behind because everything builds on the first few chapters.

This guy is crazy, but he's good to have in the morning, as he's always shouting.  I ended up hating this class though.  I only did well because I memorized how to do the problems, and didn't really learn them.  Lectures were not very well organized, didn't really learn anything in class.  Nice guy though.
Best accounting professor in Geneseo.

This class can be difficult. You have to try to follow what he says, which can sometimes be hard, as well as self-teach yourself. His tests can get frustrating because he asks for a lot of useless definitions. 2 exams and one final, as well as 5 quizzes and a group project. Quizzes aren't announced but you can see them coming. Oh yeah, I digress.
An amazing professor. He is so great at teaching and everyone should have him

I've had Mitschow twice and I honestly believe hes one of the best professors on campus. Great at dumbing down the material so that its easy to understand. Quizzes and Exams aren't hard if you listen to his hints. He pretty much tells you what is going to be on the exams.

Awful professor.  He could not care less about you as a student, soo frustrating to listen to, and he won't help you during office hours- there is no space in his office to even sit.  If u like to teach yourself and get screwed/tricked on tests,take him. otherwise,aviod at all costs.

This class was not easy, but I could not have asked for a better professor than Mitschow.  Generous grader on tests.  If you do the non-mandatory homeowrk assignments and ask questions when you don't understand, you'll do fine.  Very funny, nice and interesting.
No Comments

A great professor who loves to digress. He manages to make accounting semi-interesting for those of us that haven't chosen accounting as our major. Take this class in the morning, his shouting will keep you awake. He's very fair, and very helpful.

Great professor! His tests are long, but not very difficult at all if you study and understand the material. Also very willing to help you with anything during his office hours. He tends to shout, so you won't even fall asleep if you take his class early in the morning!

This guy is great. He's funny, yet stays on task, he's VERY approachable, knows what he's talking about, and is willing to take extra time to explain concepts. WILL NOT make you feel stupid. It's a tough course, but you can't get a better teacher for it. Put in effort, and you'll yield equivalent results. If you have to take ANY acct, get Mitchow!

Excellent professor who exemplifies what a true professor and mentor should be. Others can only learn from him.  Very fair grader and always accessible for help. Also, who else could make accounting fun, I digress.
Very good professor, will help, has pop quizzes but drops lowest grade, group project is helpful to real world examples... quirky and funny, a good prof.

Had him for 3 semesters. He presents material in a simple way, and if you do some extra work to see how it ties together with real world stuff you'll be golden. His tests really are hard though, but not un-takable. He tests on material covered only, and grades VERY easily. (think you failed? nope, you got a 78.) super funny...Highly recommended.

He's an overall great teacher.  He has assigned hw, but never collects it and the answer key is in the libs.  Try to do hw, and go to every class there are pop quizzes, usually on the stuff the day before.  Get old tests, they are the same but different numbers.  I highly recommend him.
If you don't share his politics you risk failing. If you are not a republican do not take this professor

Never has office hours that are not jammed with people.  Maybe that is a sign he should open more to help students.  Tests are HARD and no assigned homework makes the tests and quizzes harder.  People like him because he jokes around a lot, not because of his teaching.  Do not take him
Thanks to his teaching I am not in the super market buying "Catfood"
my favorite acct teacher...extremely inspiring to the profession.  he's the reason i've continued the path
Fair grader, tests can be a little hard, popup quizes. No homework. (graded).Awesome person, his class is enjoyable. Simplifies things soo much its damn easy. Oh, and Mitschow > Jay Leno
Helpful teacher ...cares about students "but I digress"
great teacher, really helpful and passionate about the work, "But I digress"
Awesome teacher, one of the best Geneseo has, really cares about all the students and wants to see everyone succeed, writes great recommendations as well

This guy is just great.  Presents boring information in a concise and interesting way.  Take this guy whenever possible and you will learn and have fun!
so much energy!! great person and wonderful teaching style
Always willing to help...Nice guy
so funny, wakes you up in the morning and drink tea in class

Way too much content to memorize for a normal human. Tests are very difficult. Office hours don't help unless you have already come up with questions. Gives practice tests but no extra credit. Only grades you on one presentation and 4 tests. Not a helpful prof.

Great elective to take if you can. Lectures are interesting . There is a lot of detailed info but if you can memorize it all you are good for the exams (there are 3). Be detailed in you responses. Part of the class is reading papers and presenting one. Paper findings are covered on tests but if you understand the presentations you will be fine.

He is a great professor. He cares about his students and makes sure everyone understands the material. He will break everything down so it is easy to understand, and he makes a lot of information seem like a smaller amount.

He is very clear about what is going to be on tests. He is extremely intelligent. He has lots of TopHat questions for a better understanding and easy points. His grading is great because your overall homework grade counts for your lowest test and the test grade is dropped. He has plenty of office hours and is very approachable. 10/10 take again!!!!

As a non Bio major the class was not too bad and he does explain everything as simple as possible, but he goes super fast. Don't write everything that you see on the board down only the important info. In class he just goes over whats on the slides in different words. Go to the TA sessions they really help. Do all the assigned hw online. STUDY

One of the most wonderful professor's I have ever had. Please take any and all classes you are able to with him and visit his office hours. Also, please take the time to come to class and study his powerpoints very well. If you know them, you will do well. Use Anki! It is ideal for his Immunology class.

ODonnell is so great. Hes kind and knowledgeable and he is the best prof Ive had so far. His tests are difficult but the practice test questions are all online. The class is challenging to keep up with. Definitely suggest bringing a laptop to type notes instead of write

O'Donnell was an amazing professor, he's adorable! I loved this class, he grades on 4 tests and online homework, and he drops the lowest test grade. He does TopHat for attendance, so you have to go to class if you want to pass. Reading the textbook will help a lot with tests.
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'TEST HEAVY', 'Amazing lectures']

comment: Bob is a great man. As a psych major, I was scared of Human Bio. BUT, he not only makes the class pretty simple, he's interesting as heck. If you don't go to lecture your grade will plummet (he does attendance and TopHat) but if you show up and take some time on the homework, you should breeze through.
O'Donnell is a true expert in the field of biology. If you have the option to take is class, most definitely do so! Especially if you enjoy human/animal biology.
If you can get ODonnell for anything, DO IT!

You need to be willing to put in work if you want to do well in his class. Tests can be difficult, but O'Donnell is very easy to get in touch with and always does his best to make sure his students understand the material -- as long as they are willing to come for help when needed. He truly cares about his students and enjoys teaching.

Lectures are a power point and then he adds notes off to the side. The power point is right out of the textbook just less in depth but his personal comments and off to the side notes are very helpful for exams as you see what he thinks is important and he explains things more clearly than the textbook does. He is a really nice guy as well.

Great prof for non-majors bio. Gives lots of opportunities to raise grade, like dropping the lowest test grade. Do well on the mastering (the avg counted as a test grade). Lectures are long but hell answer any questions. There's a lot of material but it's not hard to do well. Overall great class and great book!

Tests are a majority of the grade, but he is very willing to help you out. Very nice guy, just be sure you're ready for the tests. He's funny and makes the lectures interactive enough that you're not falling asleep. Formatted well and like I said you can always go to him with questions.

Tests are very specific. He's very knowledgeable professor, however hard to follow in lecture and information packed. Handwriting is impossible to read. He is interesting in class and I've never once fallen asleep in class. The work load and tests are a definite confidence destroyer. Just keep pushing though.

Just memorize slides and you'll get an A. I don't understand where these difficulty ratings come from. O'Donnell doesn't make his own test questions. You can find all of his questions online (because they come with the book) and just study those and get in the high 90's. C'mon now.  Overall he's great and probably one of Geneseo's  best profs.

Dr. O'Donnell is a great professor but this is a class you need to put a good amount of effort into to succeed.  Going to office hours will help a ton, he is a very approachable guy and will thoroughly explain things to you if you don't understand something.
tags: ['Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS']

comment: Cool guy. Read religiously and actively, not passively and a couple times. Follow PPs as guidline. Class lectures are passive because PPs are online, but you must go for TOP HAT credit.

Him and Spear make an interesting pair. O'Donnell knows his stuff and he is a nice reasonable guy. Has review sessions but come with questions, he won't spoon feed you. All the top hat questions are online. Study the quizzes.

Good professor but not experienced teaching non-major bio, so many things aren't explained. Lots of masteringbiology, very difficult tests and long/fast paced lectures. That being said, he really wants to his students to do well and love biology like he does. Also his first year teaching 103. He is really nice and helpful during office hours.
This class was living hell.

Bio is a hard class in general, but O'Donnell is an amazing professor. He explains the material very well in class and if you read the textbook and slides before class you'll be fine, but you have to study or you will fail the test.  O'Donnell makes class fun and if make use of his office hours!

Dr. O'Donnell is a great professor. Immunology is an excellent class and he really knows his stuff. He is super helpful in office hours and is just generally very understanding. The tests are tough but manageable.

This class was amazing, I felt like I learned more in this class then a few of  my other biology classes combined.  The material you learn and the thinking you learn to do to master the material I believe was essential for preparing to med/grad school.  The tests are difficult but he curves and the labs boost your grade.  A must take!!!

O'Donell is a great professor and in my opinion the best biology professor on campus. You can visit him whenever you want during his office hours to ask questions and he will make sure clarify whatever problems you have. His lectures are great and can keep you up, which can be hard 9:30 in morning. I plan on taking him again he's great !

O'Donnell's exams are centered in the higher tier of creative and informative thinking. During lectures he is often very active and manages a lot of material in a clear-cut and fast paced way. Reading expectations and chapter reviews assist in the extensive Campbell biology readings. Plus his Boston accent is great.

Dr. O'Donnell is really energetic and enthusiastic about the subject, which makes it a lot of fun.  The tests are tough but he is always willing to explain things and is very helpful.  Definitely take him if you can!

Such a clear and helpful professor. He is much better than Ray Spear, who often teaches classes in conjunction with O'Donnell--therefore, you need to prepare yourself for terribleness in one half of the semester in order to experience the godliness that is Dr. O'Donnell. There are four tests that count big time--with his teaching, I got 95+ on two!

This class was amazing! It is difficult and you need to put a lot of time into studying and the lab reports if you want an A  but Dr.O is fantastic and is always willing to help.  The material is so interesting and Dr.O teaches it really well. The only thing is sometimes it's unclear how specifically he wants you to know something, but just ask him

Dr. O'Donnell is the best professor I've had at Geneseo thus far. His lectures were extremely valuable, and I did very well on the exams as a result. He also offers weekly review sessions that everyone should take advantage of. You must read the textbook to do well, but that's not asking for too much. A+ 1010 would recommend.

Great guy, and he knows his stuff. All test are multiple choice, so unless you can prove him wrong on a question, you get no points for a wrong answer. Lectures are not that long, but bring a coffee... He does Top Hat questions that are graded, and attendance at random times during class, so stay awake.

Dr. O'Donnell just might be the best biology professor at SUNY Geneseo. He has so much experience in everything he does and is VERY knowledgable about what he teaches. He's always available for students who need help, I'd definitely take any class that he teaches!

Biology of Cancer is an awesome class that really breaks down the disease and you spend the entire semester on it! You learn so much and are able to tie in things you learn from Genetics, Biochem, Molec Bio, etc. so it is a great last course to take. O'Donnell is the best prof in the bio department and keeps you interested throughout the course!

Awesome! You learn so much and O'Donnell is by far the best professor in Geneseo. Lab was really interesting and you get to do a lot of cool experiments. Exams were challenging and require a lot of studying but if you put the effort in, you will do well. Definitely one of my favorite classes and will be very helpful for medical school.

Excellent teacher! Very detailed with material and is easy to understand.  Expects a lot from his students, and his tests reflect that.  However he is easy to talk to and ask questions and is eager to help his students.  Highly recommended!
very great teacher, clearly passionate about what he does. don't be afraid To ask for help when you need it. exams could be really complex though

Professor O'Donnell is one of the best at Geneseo. His slideshows are clear and he makes being in class exciting with his enthusiastic character. His homework assignments are a little bit tricky, but all you have to do is going to the tutors and they will help you out with everything. Definitely take Bio with O'Donnell!

Dr. O'Donnell is very energetic and passionate. It is extremely easy to stay focused and engaged while in class even in a lecture hall of 250 people. Challenges you, but if you put in the effort you will do very well. Incredible professor and would recommend him to anyone.

One of the best professors I've ever had. Explains everything extremely clearly and if you do the reading and take notes, it's not that hard to do well. His tests have notoriously low averages, but if you put in the effort and keep up, it'll show. He's also super eager to help and gives many opportunities for review and tutoring.

Going into Geneseo Bio, you know it'll be extremely hard. This being said, O'Donnell is the best person to take lecture with. You MUST do your own work, but he is clear and keeps you engaged during class. Very nice guy!

The class itself is very challenging, but Dr. Odonnell wants his students to do well. If you put the effort into learning, he will put the effort into helping you. One of the most dynamic and well rounded professors you'll ever take.

No doubt about it the class is hard, but he will the most helpful professor you've ever had.  Definitely do the optional homeworks he has and go to his office hours and you'll find a new love for biology.

This class is hard, no doubt about it. Do everything you can to get ahead, make sure to read before class, have all your hw's ready before quizzes, start studying early for tests, Take down all prs questions and answers, and go to his reviews and si. If this is your major, treat it like it.

O'Donnell is definitely the best biology professor I've had.  He is very friendly, clear, organized and willing to help you out. He makes cell biology very interesting and his excitement makes you actually want to go to class and read the text.  You need to read the text, go to class, and study hard if you want to do well.  You will learn a lot.

I cannot recommend O'Donnell highly enough. He explains everything very clearly using both powerpoints and his own on the spot drawings so that you understand everything the first time around. He also doesn't hesitate to answer any questions in class. However don't expect to do well unless you put in time and effort when going through the material.

O'Donnell is without a doubt the best bio teacher at Geneseo. He knows the material inside and out, conveys it well to his students, and is genuinely interested in helping everyone learn if they're willing to put in the time/effort. His classes are by no means easy, but you get out of them exactly what you put in, so an A is definitely attainable.

LOVE HIM!!! is easily one of the best bio professors at Geneseo hands down...so easy going, very approachable, and definitely knows what he is talking about...is always willing to help students out and really cares about how students are doing...even if you aren't a science major he makes biology AWESOME! DEFINITELY GET HIM & YOU WONT REGRET IT!!!

O'Donnell is one of the best bio professors i've ever had!  He explains everything so well you really don't need to read the text book. He makes class so enjoyable. Definitely recommend him, i absolutely loved him!!

O'Donnell is an amazing professor, he is extremely dedicated to his students and is very approachable during office hours.  It's a tough class no matter who the professor is, and even though you have to suffer half the semester with Spear it's worth it to have him.  Highly recommended!
GREATEST TEACHER IN GENESEO! he made me love biology. its a tough subject no matter who your teacher is. he makes it soo interesting and will do whatever he can to help you do well. LOVE HIMM!!!!

O'Donnell is an excellent professor.  His dedication to teaching and to the subject of biology is evident every class.  He wants you to learn and will do everything in his power to ensure that you are understanding the material.  The subject is difficult, and his tests are hard and complex, but he prepares you well.

Dr. O'Donnell is the greatest professor I've ever had. Lectures move quickly and tests can be challenging but are never unfair. He's very helpful in office hours and really made me love biology. Definitely take him if you get the chance.

O'Donnell is the greatest professor I've had this semester. Although he moves quickly, his lectures are crystal clear and he definitely knows what he's talking about. I would recommend skimming through the textbook as new material is being introduced.
He's very helpful and makes class interesting.  The class is hard but he keeps it on our level.

O'Donnell is the man. He loves biology and will make anyone else want to learn about it. I friggin' loved his class. His tests can be hard but not if you've come to his classes and studied. He's a great professor to have; very smart not boring at all.

Dr. O is the best prof I've ever had and Immunology was awesome. It's ABSOLUTELY necessary to attend class. If you think he went fast in Biol100 this doesn't even compare in my opinion... I heard lab was interesting as well, but the paper for the grad level class is nothing to stress over about- you get to pick your own topic.

Dr. O'Donnell is an excellent professor. Although he moves through the material rather quickly, his lectures are easy to understand, and he is always willing to help. I highly suggest taking BIOL 119 with him if you get the chance.

most organized professor i've ever had. he moves very fast but put his lectures online if you miss anything, make sure you do the readings. you get graded for PRS questions so you have to go to class. overall, awesome guy.

AWESOME! One of the best by far!! He is very thorough and his lectures make everything easy to understand. His tests are hard but he holds tons of review sessions which are helpful. Be really happy if you have him for bio.
As long as you go to class, pay attention, and read the readings assigned you'll do fine. Dr. O'Donnell is a great fast paced teacher.

Awesome teacher. Fun, easy, animated. Cares about the students. Literally will answer e-mails at 2am. Goes out of his way to help you. Gives a reasonably enjoyable lecture even with boring material at an 8:30 am class. Very fair in grading. Test are basically information directly from his slides which are online. Very friendly during office hours
Talks like hes at an auction, gives questions that you cant know the answer to even though you read the chapter 5 times. Take Briggs instead or Spear.

he's amazing. interesting, fast-paced but he'll stop and slow down if you need help. responds very fast in e-mails and is extremely helpful.  take his class!!! he'll keep you awake and help you learn the material

AMAZING TEACHER!  fast paced, usually go through one chapter in 50 minutes, but if read ahead then you should be fine.  tests consists of a lot of "all of the above" answers of questions with multiple answers. Group work is easy if all members participate
He is so great and so willing to help. One of my all time favorite professors.

He is amazing. General bio is not an easy class but he is available any time for help, very passionate about the class which makes it interesting. I was upset that he taught only one half of the course. you def have to work hard !

The tests are straight off the slides and notes so you don't even really need to buy the book (except maybe for Spear's half). He explains concepts very clearly and he's able to put them into terms that anyone can understand. His class is an easy A if you memorize his slides and can answer tricky, detailed test questions.
He is amazing! His class is interesting and he is so enthusiastic when he teaches. His slides are what is on the tests but the class is by no means easy. Awesome professor!!!
LOVE HIM. TAKE HIM IF POSSIBLE

Best bio teacher I have had. He keeps you entertained and teaches the material well. He is eager to help you out and tries to actually memorize your names and get to know his students. Definetly recomend him!!

O'Donnell is probably one of the best professors at Geneseo.  He is always willing to answer questions, and is especially helpful if you go to his office hours; he doesn't mind explaining things multiple times if that's what you need.  He goes pretty fast in class, but it definitely helps to keep people awake and on their toes.

LOVED this guy. He's so friendly and so approachable. Amazing teacher even though he flies through the material. Had him with Spear and you wouldn't believe the difference. Odonnell is a much better teacher.
Awasome teacher! knows his stuff! very nice and always clearifies any questions!Take him!

he is an amazing teacher. its nice to have a teacher that knows what hes doing and is so organized. he goes at a fast pace but its good if you want to stay up at 9:30 in the morning. he makes freshman so much more comfortable. and his tests arent even that bad either. great professor. take him!!
Although O'Donnell definietly has a fast pace, he is a GREAT teacher. He is very clear, and keeps his students engaged. He is also very approachable during his office hours. Take him!!
he flies through material but knows exactly what he is doing
Best teacher, and advisor I ever had
Odonnell is an awesome teacher! Very helpful and gives you tons of material and tons of notes.

People always complained, and still do over how tough he is.  In all honestly he isn't that tough.  His tests are challenging, but if you actually READ and STUDY and keep on top of things it isn't bad in the least. This is Bio, and every year there are 7000 freshman Bio majors that won't last as one, and those are the people that whine.
Dr. O'Donnell is amazing.  Teachers like him really make it easy for freshman to get adjusted to college life!

If you've made it this far as a bio major, you HAVE to take this class...  tough topic but Dr. O'Donnell really does an excellent job of teaching it.  I'd recommend taking the lab too.  I graduated back in 2001 and actually am doing my PhD in Immunology now, and trust me... I had a much better background than most of grad school classmates.
General bio isn't and easy course but O'donell does a good job of teacher the information and has a lot of energy when he teaches which helps.

Dr O'Donnell is the most caring nuturing man I know. He believes in all his students and loves his job to the fullest. He truly has not only inspired his students but he also has the same effect on his family.  You will not find a better person to learn from, and I am proud to call him my father.

Dr. Odonnell is awesome.  He is easily approachable and makes each lecture interesting.  The class is very structured toward the book so if you like that then your set.  Tests are details, but with all the practice tests, JITS, and review sessions they are not bad at all.
Tough tests (pay attention to details!), but you learn a lot and study hard beacause of them. SUPER approachable and just an overall caring guy. Dr O'Donnel is awesome!
I think Dr ODonnell is a great teacher, although watch out for his tests. He expects you to know all the details.
Really nice guy and very helpful but I felt the tests were really hard.
Well...any comments I could make about Dr. O'Donnell have already been made 1000 times over, so why dont we just stick with the old cliche, this guy is the best professor ever...
Great Professor!!-He is understandable and really nice.  You know I needed a ride to the airport, and he overheard--and then offered to take me himself! Can't get much better than that!

I had Dr. O'Donnell for Immuno, Bio. of Cancer & Gen'l Bio.  I graduated in 2000 but still remember his tough courses and awesome lectures.  He cares more for his students than any other prof. I've known.  I'm in med school now thanks to him.
Great Guy! Really cares about his students. Very willing to go out of his way to do something for you like a recommendation or just answer a question.  Best prof in Bailey for sure!

Dr. O'Donnell is a great guy all together. He's  receptive to students' needs and is always willing to help in an efficient and timely manner. Even though the classes I've taken with him have been hard, I really enjoyed having him as a professor.
This man is a teacher, not just a professor...great man
An outstanding professor across the board. You'd be at a loss not to experience a class taught by him.
i love this man..hes so great
ditto on all the good comments above, take any course you can with o'donnell, hes truly the best!
He would make an excellent teacher!

WOW this professor's a keeper! super duper enthusiastic attitude, and he's VERY nice. Very approachable, NOT arrogant at all like many profs may be. Hard course, but he's very good (wouldve done better if he taught the ENTIRE semester)

May be the nicest geneseo prof.  He is very approachable, so you can ask him interesting questions and get interesting answers back. Case studies in his class were also very interesting. Bio 1 was boring after taking AP bio in high school, though.

excellent professor
Amazing teacher, changed my life! Geneseo's best kept secret.
great prof and a great class.  made me want to do immunology in grad school, although grad school made me want study genetics and development

he is a super cool guy!  everyone loves him
Excellent professor. Bend over backwards for you.
Dynamic smart and approcable man, helpful and concerned for students.

While she is nice and knowledgable, she is an extremely tough grader. I'm fairly good at writing and was getting B's on almost every assignment, and was always told to "add more". The problem is there are barely any guidelines so I feel that it isn't fair to ask for more when there's no guide. Also heavily relies on TA grading which is not fair

Weekly quizzes, 30 minutes, open notes and online. Dont get discouraged by the first one! It gets easier and Dehart is very understanding. Weekly group assignments. NEED to watch lectures and do assigned reading (she posts them, no textbook). There was one individual project where you were required to write an essay. Put in effort & youll do good

comment: Dr. D really knows her stuff and is all around a great professor. If you're even remotely interested in child psychology I would recommend this class. There's a weekly online quiz, and the lowest one gets dropped. There's also a number of group assignments, which can be tedious but aren't too hard and there are a few short readings to do each week.

Dr. Dehart was one of my favorite professors at Geneseo. Her combination of passion, care, leadership, discipline, and comedy in the classroom made developmental psychology enjoyable. If you have the opportunity to take a class with her for your general education, minor, or major requirements, please do. You will not be disappointed.

Dr. D is super caring and I wished I took more classes with her before graduating. The class was easy. She can be a bit slow on grading and a bit disorganized but you learn so much in her class. One thing I didnt like was that group assignments were graded by the TAs, I feel like lots of the TAs graded well based on who you were/ if they knew you.

Professor Dehart was very sweet and helpful to anyone who needed it. I liked the individual projects and there were group assignments and quizzes every week. The lectures over zoom were not the most interesting and everything said you could read the book and learn. A fairly interesting class and remotely fair grader.

Literally the most kind professor this place has to offer. Gives essay test questions ahead of time so just get a head start on those and you will be fine. Take good notes and make friends in the class and exchange notes. Easy A my dudes. She is so nice and wants you to succeed. Take this class! Very knowledgeable from all of her years of research.

DeHart is pretty good, she is very knowledgeable in her area. She doesn't post notes so you need to go to class. Do the textbook readings they will be on the test. You have smaller group work as well as one group project but it helps boost your grade if you contribute.

comment: Dr.D is a great professor, she relies on group assignments, a group presentation, and your exams for your grade. She offers 2 extra credit assignments which are easy and really do boost your grade. You have to read the textbook, if you don't you wont pass the exams. make sure you read the boxes that are like mini case studies.

Mixed feelings on Dr. DeHart. Very kind lady, but the class is disorganized. Lots of reading! Exams are unique. Two projects that aren't difficult, but get started early. Interesting material but could be presented differently. Don't expect your grades til the end of the semester. Recommended if you're looking for a filler class/elective.

Dr. Dehart is a tough grader and her test questions sometimes are rather specific. She had two TAs who would sometimes teach lessons. Her teaching style itself was rather basic, but it was important to listen to whatever she said. The video lab was fun, and the group assignments were bearable.  Far from a bad teacher.
