comment: Dr. DeHart is one of my favorite professors at Geneseo. She's extremely approachable and is love by her students. She is very knowledgeable and her classes are straightforward with no tricks. Honestly, just go to class, do the readings (they are interesting), participate & you will get a good grade.
Definitely not a distinguished teaching professor- that must be a mistake - sarcastic, rude, mean

Dr. D is a great professor! She is quite sarcastic and depends on her TA's a little more than other professors, but she is really nice and incredibly supportive of both her students and the department. If you read the text (she did write it after all) and attend class you should get an A pretty easily. Loved the video labs too!

Out of 4 years of college, she is perhaps not only the worst professor, she is the most heartless, rude person I've ever encountered. Her reputation proceeds her. She is an embarrassment to the college.

Dr. D is a saint. Her class is so incredibly structured and it is really evident that she wants her students to do well. With that being said, she's not going to lower her standards so that people get higher grades. You must read the book, seeing as she wrote it! I feel like I am learning a lot from her; she's a really down-to-earth person.

Nice person. I wouldn't say the class is an easy A or anything...easy B if you read. Overall I didn't think she was that great of a professor like I read on here. She's not bad. I would say she is your average professor. She put most of the workload on the Teacher Assistants. Thankfully the TAs for our class were ok.
Very nice.  Gives excellent feedback.

Love this prof. She has a hilariously sarcastic sense of humor. Lectures are interesting, and the video labs are a nice change. Tests are straightforward, but you absolutely need to read the textbook.  Definitely recommend.

Dr. DeHart is VERY helpful. However, you MUST read the textbook. Lectures are fairly straightforward, and she shows a lot of videos. Very nice and clear. Helps you if you have any questions. I recommend her 100%.
Very helpful.  Tests are hard.  You have to read the book very carefully.  Interesting lectures.
Very fair grader, if you do the work you get the credit. Her tests are also very fair. She is very willing to help you out if you dont understand something.

This was a very ineresting class. Basically your grade depends a lot on the amount of work you put in, but it's not a hard class to pass.  The exams are great because you get the possible  questions and you can make outlines for your essays. Real easy to pass.
Good professor but is a hard grader, can do well if you study a lot.
Class can be boring and she doesn't let you out until at least 2 minutes over and she comes at least 5 minutes late. Nice lady outside of class, and will help you out.

Amazing class! So easy overall and SO many extra credit opportunities but at the same time you learn so much! She always has something interesting to say and prepetuates good class discussions. Also very nice and linient. It might be an easy A, but you definitely will learn a whoooole lot.
Easy class.  Fun topics.  Fair grading.  lots of useful application and discussion.  She's a pretty nice lady too.

Wonderful woman - fair, clear, enthuastic about the subject - couldn't ask for better.  Anyone who feels robbed after taking this class is a complete ass who needs to study and stay awake in class! (in response to the negative comment on the bottom)
Nice lady!! Fair grader. Not too much work. Interesting topics covered.
fair and VERY clear. The class is interesting and not very difficult. She teaches in a very organized way right along with the textbook. The tests are not bad if you have read.
Good Professor and nice lady! The topics are interesting and you are able to work directly with children in the lab. Her book is well written and easy to read and the study guide was a big help.
Good class, very easy. You don't have to go to class because group presentations aren't helpful, just read the book.

Interesting class.  Not a tremendous amount of work but it did require reading and the tests are not an "easy A".  Liked the lab work we did with children.    If you read and go to class you can at least pull a B or B+
I really loved her cross-cultural class- it was easy and interesting.  She is a tad forgetful at times, but very easy to talk to and a very nice person.
She's a fair professor. Not a lot of work. If you read the chapters and go to class, you'll do fine. Tests aren't too bad. Really enjoyed the class and liked DeHart a lot.
Very easy 300-level class.  Gives extra-credit and gives you the possible essay questions for the exams a week in advance and then lets you use your notes!

Whoever said that this class is hard "shouldn't be in college" as Dr. Dehart said. If you read, listen in class, and do the study guide you are sure to get an A. The project is easy if you put time into it, so there's another A. She's a nice lady and there's a lot of extra credit.

I think she is one of the worst teachers I have ever had. She is the most unclear and irresponsable professor and she is NEVER prepared for class. Her tests are ridiculous and you'll rarely pass them b/c she will never throw out any test questions like she says she will. She's horrible!!
Great lady. Very nice and will clarify anything you need help with. 1 group presentation and many additional group assignments. May rely too much on TA's and ours were awful.

Loves her job, is very willing to help at all times.  Very friendly and fun, makes class interesting.  Offers old tests to study from.  Lots of extra credit opportunity, but you won't need it if you do the reading and keep up to speed.  Highly recommended, she's also my advisor.  great lady :-)

A very easy A... she allows you up to 20 extra credit points and all her tests are open notes. She wants you to get a good grade. There is a group presentation but it's nothing too stressful... Take this class
shes awesome. the best teacher at geneseo.
lectures, has movies~keeps things interesting. offers lots of extra credit
shes awesome
No Comments
good teacher, friendly

Great Professor! He really wants you to learn the material and gives you ample opportunity to learn it before the exam. I really do not understand why people do not care for him all that much. Certainly the most useful course I have taken in college.
This is a self taught class. Almost worthless class time. The excel work is very time consuming. The Quizzes due the day before we talk about it in class, so there is no motivation to pay attention.

Yes, you will teach yourself this course. He doesn't. Excel homework takes HRS. However, very helpful & useful. The I.S quizzes are a joke & require no knowledge , but are more about finding a random word in a random sentence of a 30 pg ch. Oh & they're timed. Fun. -_- Horn is the type of prof who makes me angry I spend so much money on tuition.

Took this course online. He's not a bad guy, just making excels and taking quizzes. The excels are pretty long but manageable (cramming everything in a 6 week course), depending how good you are with them, and the quizzes are hard, so make sure you read. I would rather take him in the classroom than online. He also responds to email at a good time.

Do the practice exams, read in the books, go to lectures, don't be afraid to go to office hours. Horn is a great guy and really enthusiastic about his subject. Hands down the best course I've taken at Geneseo to date. These skills will be huge later on!
Homework takes up several hours per week but only counts for small portion of grade. Quiz material is not covered, let alone even mentioned in lecture.

Horn is a tough grader and does not give partial credit, he makes it nearly impossible to get an A. Online quizzes in lecture are impossible, and reading the online textbook barely helps. Homework does help for exams so make sure to do that! And also bonuses are not extra credit, they are part of your grade so do them.

I'm an A student, I never get B. But I got C from this course. I spent at least 4~7 hours a day to try to keep up with the course materials. But, you can't expect that what you learn from class will be on the test. Grading is arbitrary, he doesn't care about the type of problems for test, he just simply take them even it's not what we've learnt.

class test averages were in the 60s, literally impossible if you dont study and practice them. dont even bother with going to lectures. and his classes are so boring, suggest not taking this unless u absolutely need to

Got an A.  If you can do the practice exams within 1.5 hours you're good for the tests (and open notes if you need them).  He goes through stuff fast, but will answer any questions you have.  Even so, you'll be teaching yourself a lot of the time. People seem to be down on this guy, but I think he's decent.
Just review old exams. Everything is open notes. I was worried at first because he just told you do it all on your own, but ir is manageable. Just go over old exams before a test.
wow. good luck.
terrible teacher. i withdrew from his class but unfortuantely i'll have to take it again and he's the only professor who teaches the course! :0
here's the book-lemme know if you need any help aka the course in a nutshell (averages on tests were in the 60s)-however you WILL teach yourself this material and you WILL learn it because you did

Fairly straightforward class.  Don't really need to go to class as long as you know how to do examples on his practice tests.  If you know them, the real tests aren't bad at all.  I got 90s on them all.

Where do I even begin? I wanted to learn and maybe I did. But tests that compromise 90% of our final grade that are IMPOSSIBLE TO FINISH ON TIME are not representative of my skills as a student. Truly ridiculous. 10 % is devoted to a project which is a complete joke and a waste of time.

So the class seems easy, but the tests (which are 90% of the grade) are awful! Not only are they long but they're not like class information at all. Horn doesn't teach, and is more of a mentor. He is unhelpful and confusing. I really detest this class, even if some of it's useful information, it isn't presented as it should be. UGHHHHH

He's nice and an easygoing person but his lectures are hard to understand and not interesting. Go to his office hours a lot to go over your paper because he could grade it down if there's one thing you didn't cover because he didn't tell you to.

The class is pretty easy, but he is not the best at explaining things. You should definitely read the book because he will talk about things in lecture that you would not understand if you hadn't read the chapter. He is a very nice man and will pretty much write your programs for you if you ask him to help you.

Lectures are, well, boring. I struggled a lot with labs too. However, if you go to see him for office hours, it's better to get help from him; if you try to get attention during a lab you'll probably end up with your hand sticking up in the air for a while- too many people asking questions at once. Not bad, but not great either.
It's an easy class, but you really don't learn much.
Absolutely one of the worst professors i had to suffer through at Geneseo.  Stear clear, this man has no idea how to teach.

Good teacher.  a lot of interesting lab work with spreadsheets.  there is only 2 tests and they are very hard so study up.  I enjoyed the class because you learn a lot of information about using spreadsheets in business.  Good Luck!

Really sweet and a nice person, but kind of a space cadet. Really just takes lectures straight out of the books (images and all) but somehow is still hard to follow. Very soothing voice... made it hard to stay awake. I like her as a person but I struggled with her as a prof. Class wasn't that hard though anyway.

Not a good professor at all. She is nice, but doesn't know much about her subject material, and when questioned by students she rushes to sound like she knows what they're talking about when she doesn't. Very boring. Take the class when someone else is teaching it.

Interesting lectures, easy homeworks right from book that help grade, easy presentation, hard tests, but she grades other assignments easily enough that you should do well as long as you read the book.  Also, she's always willing to help during office hours or shortly after class.

This class was all over the place, and he honestly never seemed to know what was wrong with his code. Tests were more difficult than expected. He's super nice and available outside of class. He also grades your tests with you and gives you a chance to fix your work.

He's a very nice guy/person, but he is terrible as a professor. It's just tough to follow his lectures and curriculum, and I felt like I was teaching myself the entire semester. He also copies things straight from textbooks, which doesn't help. So I would not take another class with him.

Copies note straight from textbook that he told us we had no need to buy/rent. No calculators needed in class. Not good with elaborating on notes or explaining most things. Personally, my pre-calc from hs was not enough prep whatsoever, but also his expectations are high regarding what you should have for knowledge coming into class. Nice guy tho.
A pretty solid math professor at Geneseo, can be difficult to understand sometimes. Not my favorite but a very safe option

Took every class in the book with Ahmad. His use of formula sheets make it very possible to do well on every single test. Tests align with old tests/ study sheets, both accessible. Ahmad is such a genuine/ down to earth human being. I graduated, but if I could take a class with him now, I would. Would love to have a beer with him, awesome guy.
He's one of the best math professors I've ever had!

Dr. Almomani is an exceptional math professor. His ability to break down complex concepts into simple, understandable steps made learning enjoyable and engaging. His dedication, patience, and genuine passion for teaching created an inspiring and supportive learning environment, and I am deeply grateful for his impact on my education.

I had him for 230 and it was by far the worst class I've taken at Geneseo. Painfully disorganized - he showed up to each class without a plan and relied on students with prior coding knowledge to "teach" the class. Homework and exams were brutal and grading was very subjective. Weekly tutoring was needed to survive this class. Avoid at all costs!!!

Coming from some experience with calculus in high school, I had a slight advantage, but still found his tests to be very difficult. Homework and quizzes are easy, but tests are very difficult. Very nice guy and his lectures were really good. Review notes, and examples he posts because some test questions are exact.

Very nice guy, very fair grader. Tests are hard, but he gives a lot of points for what you can get done. Weekly homework online through cengage, gave us a free textbook link. Overall super wonderful teacher. Was very accessible through office hours, and always willing to answer questions. Teaches in a way so you do better in high level courses.

Prof. Almomani is a terrific professor who always looks out for his students. He gives out extra practice for each topic, which helps a lot and is sometimes even on quizzes or exams. Although the coursework is tough for those who take the course for Edu requirements, he makes sure to take time for students. Exam scores are given back in good time!

Professor Almomani is a great professor and person. Yes, this class can be difficult because it is a higher-level math course. However, professor Almomani does everything in his power to help all of his students understand the material. He is very understanding and gives a lot of partial credit and extra credit. He also makes Calc 2 fun! :)

I hated this class, I have never cried so much over a class before in my life. The tests were very difficult, it felt like he took the hardest examples from class and put them on the test for fun. During one of the exams he gave probably 45 extra minutes because no one was finishing on time. The homework assignments were very hard and took hours.

Absolutely the best professor I've ever had. This is a difficult class but he makes sure everyone knows what's going on . Made it clear he wants his students to succeed and obviously loves what he does. Really nice guy and a really great professor. Highly recommend taking a class with him, I would take every math class with him if I could
I have never had a math teacher who has made me not fear math but he creates a comfortable environment. He also is probably one of the most understanding and caring professors I have ever had.

Professor Almomani is amazing! He is always willing to help outside of class and provides his students with all the necessary tools to succeed. Tests can be challenging, but he offers the opportunity to replace your lowest test grade if you score progressively better on each exam. You must attend class to do well! He is a sweet, understanding man!

comment: I loved Professor Almomani!! I am a Bio major and Math is really my favorite, but Almomani made it enjoyable. The tests tend to be hard, but if you study youll do fine. I definitely recommend taking him if you have to take Calc 2.
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'Caring']

comment: El mejor profesor que he tomado en mi vida. No duden en tomarlo!

He has honestly been one of my best professors here at geneseo. He is very easy to read and his tests and quizzes set you up for success. He gives ample feedback on all of the responses and has a lot of opportunities to allow you to receive extra points. He wants people to pass and wants us to feel good about putting in the work and succeeding

Make sure you watch the movies she posts on the syllabus because they will be referenced in exams. Exams are online and you have ample time to complete them. There is a class participation grade but I barely went and still got an 80. Just make sure you do all the readings and questions for homework.

Maggie Rex is one of those professors that gets what it's like to be a student. Her lectures, tests and assignments are extremely straight forward and solely based on presentations. She does not allow any laptops however but for most people that was not an issue as she posts the presentations on canvas. Would defiantly take again.
Great professor! She was so passionate when taking about sociology.

Professor Rex is one of the most agreeable, interesting, and insightful professors I have encountered here at Geneseo. The class was very relaxed, but tackled super important issues in a really refreshing and interesting way. She is very responsive and easy to talk to, and has open note, take-home tests. She makes sure that everyone can succeed!

professor Rex is an amazing sociology professor, she makes the class so interesting with visuals and talks about relatable shit. tests are super easy but notes are definitely required. No computers or phones are allowed in class

He embodies kindness, dignity, and compassion, and has left a beautiful mark on my life that I will never forget. Despite my language difficulties, he excelled at teaching me and understanding my needs. Words cannot do him justice; he deserves the utmost appreciation and respect.

Dr. Markowski is a nice guy, but a bad professor. We skipped over many topics because he would spend weeks going off on tangents about small things. He doesn't allow you to make up unplanned class activities. Tests are impossible and asks questions about stuff that's not in the textbook or was never talking about in class. Avoid if you can.
Literally the worst professor I have ever had.

absolutely TERRIBLE professor, his exams are impossible and are not related to class lectures at all. Grade in class in only based on three exam scores and one group project which are impossible to do well on. He never responds to his email and is a terrible communicator. The class is not the problem, the professor is.
DO NOT TAKE HIM FOR PSYC251!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! I cannot emphasize this enough, you will 1000% be better off taking someone else.
Nothing like he teaches biopsych! Take home exams and not too difficult. I definitely recommend taking this class with him, but make sure you show up.

I love Dr. Markowski... however I also love to study. Dedicate 3 hours a day to studying you will get an A. He will tell you what sections in the text book are fair game, you have to read ALL of it. His lectures are entertaining to me... and he has lots of office hours. Grading is tight, only 55 points. Meaning no more than 5 points off for an A.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Test heavy', 'Graded by few things']

comment: If I could rate him a 0 I would. His tests are awful. His lectures are rambling and get so confusing. He doesn't accommodate you at all and doesn't care about you or your grades. IMPOSSIBLE to reach him outside the classroom, he doesn't answer emails at all. My experience with him is THE WORST experience I have ever had with a teacher/professor!!

Did not organize lectures well. Topics kept being pushed to the next test and the final exam covered a broad range of topics with not adequate time to go over them all. I got A's on the first 2 tests and D's on the last 2 bc lecture quality went down. Go into this course with any professor ready to spend a lot of time and effort
He was awful

He's a very knowledgeable, captivating professor who does more than a reasonable amount of work to help you learn the subject matter. Still, he made us watch a cringy video once. So, I have to give him a very negative review.

Dr. Markowski is genuinely one of the funniest most caring professors who really wants his students to do well in his classes. I had him for Biopsych which is a tough class but his lectures were so funny and entertaining. If you get the opportunity to take a class with him do it!!

Grade is completely dependent on test scores, attendance is mandatory. He doesn't use the powerpoint to lecture he just talks. He also does multiple choice questions in class that count for like 10% of your grade. Tests are only like 20ish questions so if you get a few questions wrong you're screwed. He does drop the lowest test grade which helps.

Vincent Markowski is the worst professor I have ever had. I studied so hard for his exams and failed every single one. There is only 20 questions on each test and no curve. You're only graded on exams and final project. I am a hard working third year student and I have not failed a course until this one. TAKE THIS CLASS WITH ANYONE ELSE.

I don't want to give him a bad review because he is a very good teacher but his tests are impossible. There will be stuff on the exam that the textbook covered that he has never talked about. The best bet is showing up to class but his lectures can be very boring because he goes through maybe two slides per class.

He is funny and very good at describing things, but biopsych will by no means be an easy class. Your grade is just exams, a group project, and attendance. If you don't test well, I wouldn't suggest taking him. With that being said, he very clearly explains things and wants input from students. He is a good professor despite being a difficult grader

Overall he is a good teacher, a lot of in class assignments with groups so if you don't show up it will effect your grade, although each assignment is graded out of 3 points. Good luck getting him to answer a single email, you have to see him in person in order for your questions to be answered. Gives good feedback on papers though.

Yes, he was a goodish teacher but he is so boring. so boring. He takes forever to answer email, you have to try and catch him after class or if you need to email him you need to do it days ahead of when you want him to answer. I like that he is helpful with paper feedback and that we did little partner things too. He basically reads off the slides.

I had him for a neuroscience class and he was awful. He's nice and not boring to listen to but you will not be able to get a hold of him outside of class. you only have 4 tests and maybe 2 other class assignments. You are graded by very little things so there is literally no room for error. He grades on a point system which makes 0 sense. stay away

Contrary to popular belief he is a good prof. Not only has he helped me pass this class and grasp a better understanding of the concepts, but he also is very dedicated to what he does. He gives great feed back on the paper that you have to write, and is always willing to help you if you put in the work. Its work but so is every psych 251 section.

comment: I was disappointed with having him as a professor. It never helped me when I wasn't doing good in the class; he listened to my problems but didn't help me resolve them or offer anything to help. "study better". Every test is worded horribly.

Markowski is an okay professor. Can be confusing when explaining things. Super long lectures and tests are extremely difficult. Also, there is no running tally of grades in Canvas, if you want to do well there is tons of work.
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Lecture heavy', 'Tough grader']

comment: Class is a drag, but that's due a lot to the subject matter. He is impossible to reach outside of class. He never responded to emails and provided zero support during online classes. Rescheduled our final twice and told us nothing about the format. The day of, he never posted the exam and no one could reach him.

The semester-long paper project wasn't too bad, but he provides the rubric he uses to grade it after you hand in the assignments. Would've liked a little more direction with the requirements for each section, but overall not bad. He seems like a nice guy, had him online so it's hard to tell

Markowski is a fair or even lenient grader, but he seems unwilling to give 100. He is clearly knowledgeable. He did not give rubrics or specifics about projects. He is not good at communicating via email. He also required synchronous quizzes for an asynchronous class, and was not good at communicating about resolving it for multiple students.

Dr. Markowski knows what he is talking about it and explains things in an effective way, often using examples. However, he is very unresponsive to emails and the class is graded mostly on tests. Use your TA for review. I took his class during COVID so Markowski himself wasn't very accessible.

Just dont. Dr. Markowski is the hardest professor to get ahold of. I could never find him for help. I felt disregarded. He said hed review my paper and then at the end of the year said haha I forgot. He is boring and the other professors available for the courses he teaches are so much better.

I really don't get why people hate Dr. Markowski so much. He can be tough with tests and doesn't respond much to emails, but he's accessible in office (which wasn't possible due to COVID, which sucked). If you take good notes in class, his tests are totally doable. The paper project is graded pretty easily too. Just show up and listen.

comment: He does not answer emails at all. He is inconsiderate and does not care about students. This pandemic really showed Markowskis true colors. He did not change his expectations or students, did not answer emails , and was not understanding of everyones unique situation of how being home.

I had him as an adviser. he is absolutely rubbish, does not help or care about his students, and very discouraging, talked to him first semester freshmen year about my low 3 GPA, he said my grade is to low for Med school, I did not listen to him and worked hard and now I'm on track to get into medical school. Don't let anyone bring you down!

He's unresponsive to emails. I do not like the lack of feedback he gives his students. He's lectures are decent. He explains the material, but he expects students to pick up on the information quickly as if biopsychology is an easy topic. I wouldn't recommend him.
tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Lecture heavy']

comment: Worst Professor Ever. He doesn't reply to e-mail when several students are confused and has to the most unclear directions for assignments and expects us to figure it out by ourselves. HE does not care about the student's success and is quite frankly a terrible teacher.
I really liked how during lectures everything wasnt written on the board. He talked slow so everyone could understand and process what we were learning.
If Lord Voldemort existed in real life his name would be Vincent Markowski.

You get graded on 3 exams, 1 group project, and "participation " points. His exams ask the most obscure questions, not on any of the main information in the book. His participation points aren't really just participation, he only gives you points if you are correct. If you ask for help outside of class, he just tells you to make flashcards.
I really dislike Markowski his tests are very difficult and specific

Take an intro bio class before Markowski's class... your grade will thank you. He is a great lecturer and will spend more than enough time on the slides and discussing topics and questions from students but you have to be prepared to study REALLY hard if you want that great grade. Overall he is a nice guy and you will learn a lot.

I don't know why he has such bad reviews! I love this professor, he's such a good lecturer, stays on the power points for like 5 minutes each and explains everything in lots of detail to make sure we all understand. It's definitely not an easy class at all, but its expected but if you work hard and study you will do fine!

Loved him in lecture. Solid lectures that were rarely boring. There is a LOT of material and you have to know it really well. If you don't read you will do awful on tests. His tests are very hard and extremely specific. Prepare to read and study hard.
tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'TEST HEAVY']

comment: Honestly if you put in the work and really try, a good grade is really attainable. He is pretty straight forward with what he wants and his tests are hard but manageable if you go to lecture and read the textbook. There is one group project which he grades very fairly and there are clicker questions in every class
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Tests are tough']

comment: Markowski is clearly very passionate about the subject, and he likes to tell a lot of really funny stories to help you connect ideas. Class is always interesting. A good amount of tested material comes from the textbook, so you HAVE to read. Also - he barely puts anything on his slides, he mostly speaks, so you have to go to class.
tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'TEST HEAVY']

comment: Do anything you can to take this class with another teacher. Half way through the semester he added a new condition to the paper that forced everyone to go back and reshape everything. He does not explain what he expects from you but is an extremely harsh grader. He does not test out of the textbook but doesn't give you enough data in class.

Great 251 professor! Very clear in what he expects from students. Grading is fair, and he gives helpful feedback. Tests are somewhat difficult, but if you attend class/read the book, they're manageable. Go to his office hours if you have questions. Speak up in class.  Lastly, if there's a TI, use him/her! Great class overall.
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'Clear grading criteria']

comment: I really liked Markowski at first - he's definitely better than other psych 251 professors I've heard about. Although it's a dry subject, he tries his best to engage students. He explains grades and is pretty clear in what he wants. I was getting all As and Bs which is why I was confused when I received a C at the end of the semester for no reason.

Funnyapproachable, very passionate about his field. You get assigned a paper and presentation (one due midway + other due by finals). Paper was a struggle but he's an easy grader. 4 tests drops lowest. Read the textbook over once and reread the notes from class and you're all set. In-class electronic questions are graded for attendance.

Worst professor I've had at Geneseo. He never even taught us the last 3 chapters, which was the entire last exam. He had us read it from the text. Dr Meyer is amazing she is so understanding and perfectly prepares you for all assignments also she is just a very good person

Really nice guy. Very accomodating. Slept through the final by accident and he still let me make it up. Statistics is very boring, but he knows what he's talking about. Pretty difficult grader, but offers opportunities to improve. Really nice guy, but perhaps look for an easier professor as this class is likely to hurt your GPA.

Pastizzo is pretty average. He teaches a boring subject in an average way. I would have been totally lost if I hadn't taken AP Stat in high school. Sometimes vague. Makes jokes that are so bad they're kind of funny. Not a bad guy, but you'll have a better time if you get Ruddy.

Real tough, but he's definitely softened since he had a kid (I took 250/251 with him). He's helpful, he can be a bit verbose (he looooves words) but class discussion was good and if you don't understand he will try other ways to help you get it. Easy to take notes in class, too. Just tough on tests and papers.

He is a very difficult professor.  When he grades your paper, he grades you on exacting style of writing and not content.  Gives you obscure comments that won't help you improve your writing to his standings. Taking his class caused my other classes to suffer.

I enjoyed having him as a professor & plan on taking him for 251 as well. His tests are hard but if you pay attention in class and/or have a predisposition to math/stats, an A is definitely possible. Does throw in tricky questions that require you to really grasp the concepts. Don't regret my decision to take him over Ruddy - I've learned a lot.
Made stats so much harder than it had to be. Hardly gives any partial credit on long answer test questions and I found him patronizing. Take stats with Ruddy, it will make your life so much easier.

He is a very nice professor & is more than willing to help if you ask him. You can tell that he wants us to succeed. The problem is that his tests are ridiculously hard. No matter how well you know the information, there is still no guarantee you will do well on his tests. I practically memorized the textbook and still failed most of the tests.

His powerpoints are very clear, and he is a very good professor.  Labs and quizzes are pretty easy.  He makes the tests difficult though.  He gives really hard questions, and is not willing to compromise.  If you're not a good test taker, don't take his class.

He is a great professor, knows his stuff, always willing to help... but his tests will beat you senseless - I'd recommend the class because I learned a lot, but you have to study study study and get his help in office hours.

horrible class. uses big words, doesn't always focus on stats. open to help, extra credit offered. he wrote the book, and I didn't understand a lot of it, plus if you didn't understand the class there was no way to understand the text. tests are very hard. other professors are much better.
nice guy, very funny and smart. teaches stats well and easy to understand. tests are wicked hard, remember to read the book and study!

he is a nice guy but for some reason his mere presence annoys me, and i get the feeling it does for other ppl in the class too. course doesnt have a text book and  focuses on empirical studies- makes it hard to take good notes from his lectures and the material can be hard to grasp. study guides are vauge but tests are not bad and hes a fair grader

Boring class, but Dr. Pastizzo was a great professor. Interesting, enthusiastic, and very fair. Tests were challenging but he let you know exactly was was going to be on it. Put so much work into class you could really tell. Clear, organized, and real pleasure to take a class with.
Stay away! Very very very subjective grader. I learned a lot in his class but I was miserable the entire time. He was arrogant and made me feel stupid.

dr. pastizzo is great. he is one of the most fair profs  i have ever had. his pop quizzes are announced a day in advance and they are open note. his test questions come right out of the test prep in the  book that he wrote. he is fun in class and loves what he teaches.

got a C+ even though i worked my butt off in this class. very interesting and challenging, but test questions are much more specific than what he teaches in class. Should't have to fight so hard to pass a prerequisite class like this on.

he wrote the book, very helpful, very clear, wants students to do well. the material can be difficult, but attempts to help with grades, open notebook pop quizzes-very easy, and tests with fair questions! highly recommended!!!
He wrote the book. read it, go to class. study.  you'll do fine.

Although he may seems nice in class, STEER CLEAR.  The teacher's tests ask vague questions that expect specific answers. His grading is subjective and often harsh with little room for discussion.  Your grade will reflect your how linguistically similar you are to the professor, not your knowledge of the material.

Dr. Pastizzo isn't easy, but it's doable. We didn't have a book which kinda added to the confusion,and made attendence manditory. Tests were challenging, but he searched through papers for extra credit. Papers are extreamly hard. You  *need* to write it early and let him read it over/correct it. He's willing to work w/ you so you get a good grade.
No Comments

The material itself is extremely boring but he tries to make it more interesting. His exams are pretty difficult and it's hard to understnad what hes looking for in an exam. I would suggest taking someone else if possible.. you cover the same thign but exams are easier i hear

great guy in and out of class, his material is absurdly boring but he is really cool and still makes class interesting and even fun. he's very entertaining and personally gives review classes the night before exams, which are kindof hard but he's very helpful if you just ask.  i def recommend

Dr. P is very intelligent and entertaining.  He tries to make the material interesting and covers the material thoroughly, at times his explanations can be a bit confusing.  He is always willing to work with you. I enjoyed having him as an instructor.
Dr. P is a very good guy and professor. but his exams are hard. i studied so hard for his exams but i got very low grades, which was very depressing.

I'm a big fan of Dr. Pastizzo...he's a great guy, funny, interesting and insanely intelligent.  He's really fun to talk to and is very approachable if you need any help with anything.  His tests are fair, and he personally does review sessions, which is awesome :)
No Comments
Great guy.  Goes off on crazy tangents but its fun.  Tries to make the class as easy as possible for you.
Great teacher, makes class very interesting! I love him!!
Very nice guy. Class is usually entertaining. Class was let out early several times. My fav pysch professor at Geneseo!
Great Teacher who made sure everyone knew what was going on in the class. Tried to get to know each student personally. Knew when students didn't understand material.
Very fun guy, Stats is a hard class and he knows alot but makes class tolerable with his corny jokes; also tests are fair and easy!
great teacher. outlines tests before test day. tests come from hw and in class assignments. very understanding and extremely willing to help if you have questions. i definitely recommend him.

Great teacher, although I've definetely become dependent on the notes he posts for the chapters, which can get scary when the test is a week a way and he hasn't posted 3 chapters...so remember to read your book
I hate math and this was one of my favorite classes ever!  I was dreading having stats at 830 in the morning, but i never missed a class and was always awake.

One of my favorite professors so far.  He is young, doesn't put the class to sleep, makes things as easy to understand as possible, lets you out early often, and there isn't a lot of HW.  If you are going to take this class, take it with him, he's the man
Very nice guy and lectures are engaging. Seems to me very easy but I used to be a math major.  Study guides on line that almost replicate exams; you can't go wrong.
Nice guy; hard tests.  Psych 250 is literally a math-course, but required for Psych majors.

Professor Abonado is the sweetest and kindest man you will ever meet. You will have to read articles and books throughout the semester but they aren't very long and they are easy to read and be prepared to talk about them in class. You will need to participate in class about the readings but if you participate a few times you will be fine.

Advanced Poetry Workshop Spring 23 was awesome! Workshop was great because of Al and the class itself. He's super easy going, lets you take your final portfolio any direction you want. He does want you to strengthen your poetry skills; workshops are great, laid back and teach you so much.

Professor Abonado is truly a sweet man. He cares about his work and shows that, and he makes the class interesting. While I did not love this class at all, I really enjoyed Professor Abonado. I would definitely take a different class with him.
This class was easy yet also interesting. As long as you show up, participate once or twice per class, and turn in your work on time, this class is an easy A.

Albert is a great professor and really helped me out when I had to take writing seminar. Writing has always been a challenge for me but he made sure that this class was more than just writing a ton. This class is really a hidden gem, he cares about his students. Thank u professor Abonado!

He's a great professor, very laid back and understanding about late work. The only complaint I have is that he got a little behind on grading but overall he's awesome and I would take a class he teaches.

Abonado grades everything based off of 7 very easy to follow criteria. Basically full credit on everything you turn in. He really cares about his students and was a great prof. attendance wasn't mandatory as long as you emailed him

Best professor I have ever had. I love the way I was graded for this course. You need to follow seven easy rules to get an A in the class. I have never loved or been good at writing but I loved this class and would recommend him to everyone.

easy grader, but gives amazing feedback. graded on just a few papers. comprehensive lectures, and he is endlessly patient with questions and analysis. papers do have a really quick writing oeriod, but theyre 3-5 pages max, so its manageable
really easy class, just submit the work and you will be fine. no real papers (just 1-2 page reflections) and like 4-5 interviews

Super easy and fun class, Abonado does not expect a lot out of you. He gives great feedback. Only negative is that it is super hard to contact him, he barely responds to emails which is tough during a pandemic.
he is a very nice guy but he is also pretty disorganized, the class is alright, gives good feedback for essays if you do the work you will get a decent grade

The most understanding professor I have had. He recognizes that life happens and will do his best to accommodate your circumstances. Help him out by being an active participant, which keeps the class interesting. He assigns interesting readings and will use his humor and input to ease into class discussions if no one is talking.

He is DEFINITELY the person to take 201 with! He really exposes you to different kinds of writing, gives great feedback, (whether you're still in his class or not) and inspires you to keep writing long after his class. The class itself was so enjoyable, and not too much work at all. Probably one of the best people I've ever met!!

Great class with a cool guy. There are papers and poems every week, but he makes them interesting to write. Readings due every class, but they are fun to read. Al is a great guy and loves talking about your work. Participation is almost half your grade so just make sure to talk. Would definitely take this again!
HE IS THE BEST. RATINGS DO NOT LIE.
Avocados are not only a superfood, they are a Super Food. In guacamole, cut up on crackers with a little nutritional yeast, teaching Fundamentals of Creative Writing, avocados cannot be beat.

Big Al is an Adonis amongst men. You may not like it, but this is what peak performance looks like. He has thighs for days and drinks ranch from the bottle. In all of my three months at Geneseo I can say that - without doubt - Mr Avocado is a true gem. He makes the English department a little better and my days a lot brighter.

My favorite professor I've had, lecture can be a tad boring but you can tell how much he loves the topic. As long as you do the readings and understand you'll be perfectly fine. Is very understanding about attendance and will make up exams on his time if you talk to him. Exam grades come back before the next one and are open book
Amazing professor! Really enjoyed taking his class. Didn't stress me out at all. I'd recommend taking especially for a gen ed.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Amazing lectures', 'Gives good feedback']

comment: Lectures were a bit boring at the end but its history...He's super understanding. As long as you do the readings and answer the questions he puts on Brightspace you'll be fine!

I really liked Jurnack and I'm surprised he only teaches like two courses...As long as you do the readings and pay attention to his lectures you should be fine. There's no exams, instead there's just responses which are honestly not difficult, just remember to print out the readings and use them in your writing.
His class lectures were a bit boring, but the workload was not bad and he is very understanding.
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']

comment: Very light work load. Very knowledgeable in his field. Unfortunately I find his field on the uninteresting side. Lecture heavy.
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']

comment: Honestly, super low workload. Yes, he is lecture-heavy but everything is pretty important and entertaining for the most part.

Rich is given a bad rep on here. His lectures were pretty interesting, albeit he only shows a picture on the screen while he talks. However, the class is extremely interesting if you give it a chance, and he is such a kind professor who gave us candy for Halloween, is an easy grader, and lets you redo your essay if the grade is low.

jurnack knows what hes talking about, but he is so boring and a horrible lecturer. he only shows one picture and doesnt ever know what hes talking about to explain it. all assignments are writing and are fairly easy, the readings are boring.

Gives great feedback on essays and lets you redo them after he gives feedback. Slides were very vague and lecture's were extremely boring. Class gets cancelled so often to the point where it felt like more classes were cancelled then actually held. Takes forever to grade responses and rarely responds to emails. But overall a nice guy.

Honestly, Jurnack is much closer to a 3 than a 4, but some of you guys are hating for no reason so I'm gonna give him some extra credit. Super chill guy and a very easy 100 level course with barely any work (which he lets you resubmit if you get a bad grade) and no quizzes/tests. Only issue is he's a pretty boring lecturer, but the content is good.
A really really nice guy. Very knowledgeable of his field, but isn't super interesting to listen to. The writings are easy, but he doesn't just give out good grades(fair).
tags: ['Tough grader', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Graded by few things']

comment: Do not take his classes. He will ramble the whole period about random historical figures and events with two pictures on the screen and that's it. There are 6 papers and 1 final research paper and he takes months to return grades for them. Not sure if participation matters bc I was sick of wasting my time by the third week of classes.

Do not take him. He drones on and on ab random historical stories and only has pictures in his presentations so there is nothing to keep your attention. He takes forever to grade the papers he assigns. There is no clear structure to the class. Attending class would help to know what's going on but it is such a waste of time.
tags: ['So many papers', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']

comment: He clearly likes history but very much dislikes teaching it, very unorganized, takes months to grade any work turned in and gives little or unclear feedback. I would not take him again.

Bad, bad professor, lack of organization and very unclear a lot of the time, take his course seriously, gives you a book to read 3 weeks into class that you weren't required to get, and homeworks are based on this making it hard to complete assignments. Assignments also take months to get grades.

The entirety of the class, I wished he was my high school history teacher because his classes are reliant on class discussion and towards the end of the semester, only 3 people were showing up to classes so it didn't work too well. He assigned a lot of reading but I learned a lot in that class. I wish he taught more history courses.

Prof. Jurnacks fine. I get the sense he loves history but might not necessarily love teaching it. Ive heard hes a hard grader but from my experience he wasnt that tough. He didnt give much feedback, which I wouldve liked, but he was nice and the class was interesting.

Prof. Jurnack doesnt care about teaching. You will pass just fine, but if you care about school youre going to be frustrated by him. He doesnt respond or give feedback. He barely grades. I got a 100 in the class, mostly bc I bet he didnt read what I wrote and just slapped a grade on it. Annoying, but Ill get over it and accept the easy A.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things']

comment: Really chill guy, but don't be fooled! He's a very tough grader for a 100 level class. only half the class shows up for the lectures. Def a good idea to go to class on discussion days. Class is comprised of 3 take home exam papers and 7 one page responses that should help grades. Pretty easy and straight forward as kong as you can write decently.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things', 'Tough grader']

comment: Jurnacks class style is very laidback, but his grading is not. Hardly anyone showed up to lectures and he cancelled class often. Grade was based off of 3 papers, response questions and maybe discussions. I answered his response questions and did essays based off of notes I tried to take in lecture and did kinda poorly, ending with a B+

Lectures can seem very long and dull. He cancels class all the time but that doesn't really set the class back at all. 3 fairly easy essays but he is a tough grader on them. 1 paragraph responses due each week which are easy to get 100s on if you go to class. Some reading to do that will help with essays
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Lecture heavy', 'Tough grader']

comment: Professor Jurnack's lectures were boring and hard to follow but the class itself was very simple and it was easy to get a good grade. If you know how to write a decent paper, you'll do fine on the 3 essay "tests" and the responses are really just checking if you know whats going on in class. An easy "A" class if you put in a little work.

Jurnack is the most boring professor I've had. He expects you to read more than you should for this level, and when he cancels class he expects you to understand what's going on without any sort of class discussion. His essay prompts are too vague, his feedback on papers isn't useful and generally comes off very rude. Wouldn't take his class ever.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS', 'LECTURE HEAVY']

comment: Professor Jurnack is a pretty chill guy. His lectures are pretty boring though. Quizzes every week based on the previous lecture so you have to go to class. DO all the readings as they will help you write your three papers. No tests. Overall a pretty cool dude

Take extensive notes on the readings. Five question quiz at the beginning of every class on last class's lecture. Take extensive notes during class. Often cancels class. Exam papers flexible and straightforward in content. Participation preferable, not necessary.
tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LECTURE HEAVY']

comment: Really loved taking his class. We usually had homework due every week. A few questions on an article of his choice. Tests were a little hard so you definately have to study. Also, two group presentations. Overall, he is super nice and pretty funny. He makes everyone feel comftorable and willing to participate. Would highly recommend.

I loved Professor Volza! His class ran the same everyday so you know what to expect. There is homework due every class but it's easy. You do 2 group projects during the semester which weren't too difficult. The hardest part of the class was the tests. He gives a review sheet that has all the terms that you need to know but is usually 80-90 terms.

Volza is a great guy. He's kind and funny! Class is straightforward, and answers for the exams essentially come right out of the textbook or his slides, which he uploads online- he will give you a sheet with all the terms you need to know on it. He likes to have you do presentations, so be prepared to work with other people. Would recommend!!

**THIS IS HIS IMMIGRATION CREATIVE WRITING CLASS**
it was the most boring thing I have ever endured.barely took attendance. each class was a useless yap sesh who knows the point of it. We only had 3 assignments total and the final was easy. nice guy but boring  stupid  useless class. nobody ever knew what was going on.

If you need a language requirement, do not take Latin with Wes. He spends half of class talking about himself, so you don't actually get to the important things he promised he would cover, which you will then still be graded on. He is arrogant and disrespectful in his office hours, so those are useless way to attempt to get help as well.

a very kind and accommodating man, cares about your wellbeing and wants to work with you. His essay prompts are extremely vague and he rambles all lecture so nothing ever really makes sense. Gives credit for the first three assignments as long as you do them. The final essay hits you like a truck- didn't teach us how to write and grades harsh.

A decent guy, rambles through the long lectures with absolutely no structure, could just sleep through class. Only grades based on 5 papers, three of which are "short essays" but are basically quizzes. Papers have zero prompts or guidelines. Harsh grader and can tell if you didn't read. Don't miss an assignment or your grade will tank. Good luck
tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things']

comment: I had Professor Kennison for only half a semester, and he is by FAR one of the greatest teachers I've ever experienced. He relates history to today perfectly and effortlessly, and always introduced new perspectives with absolute passion. If you remotely care about your education, take his course the moment it's offered. You owe it to yourself!

He's a great dude but has really unclear grading and assignment criteria, I literally never knew what his expectations were. I also didn't like how disorganized the class was, due dates weren't clear and he never knew where were were in the syllabus or what reading we were on.

Wes is very passionate about western humanities. There are only 5 grades for the whole class, and he only gives out 100s if you've taught him something, which is difficult considering he's been reading these papers since the 70s. Most of the class is spent listening to him talk about hyper-specific parts from the texts.
He is really nice, but the course is just writing so he can be a really hard grader. It's a course just based on books and need to pay attention to small detail.

Wes is a great professor and I'm very surprised by some of these ratings. If you enjoy a professor who can talk about anything and make it interesting, Wes is the man for you. Overall an awesome, caring, funny professor who makes learning fun!

Wes is a great professor, and although his class wont make you suffer, Ive ultimately learned a lot from him. Its a mark of him being a good professor that you can get a lot out of the class without feeling overwhelmed or stressed out.

Horrible professor. Don't ever take this class with him. Kennison loves to hear himself talk and cares very little about opinions other than his own. You will find yourself bored in class and struggling to stay awake. The course is graded based on 4 or 5 assignments that are based on little criteria and graded harshly. DO NOT RECCOMEND THIS CLASS!!

I recommend sleeping through class and just turning in assignments at his office. Lectures were extremely boring and not related to assignments. Prompts did not require any reading beyond the Sparknotes. Definitely an old-school style teacher. Nice guy though.

I took this class abroad and it was a great decision to take it with this professor. Wes is a great person, but as a teacher he doe ramble and go off on a tangent at times. His class abroad (different than at Geneseo) consisted strictly of papers as tests, and a personal journal. He is easy to talk to and if you do it will help you do well in class

Wes is wonderful. He seems a bit scattered, but that's because he's busy trying to make the school a better place for the students. He grades mostly on effort, so if you show up and turn everything in, you'll do fine. If you need structure and strict deadlines though, do not take this. He will take assignments for full credit the last day of class.

Wes is hilarious and kind, but he talks about himself a lot. The only graded work was portfolio, a final, and a research paper. Many people in the class rarely showed up and most of us still passed. If you want to get a good grade, focus on the vocab and learning the declensions. Study every week if you want to get a solid grade and do well in 201.

Wes is the classic image of the pseudo intellectual, foofy, arrogant professor type.  Listening to him ramble for 2 hours at 8:10am was borderline unbearable.  That said, the time and effort needed to get by in his class is little none.  You can basically push the class to the back of your mind and ignore it all semester, which is ideal for hum.

Do yourself a HUGE favor and take Humanities with someone else.  Kennison  puts in 2% effort all semester, and grades are pulled out of thin air with no justification or notes about what was wrong. You will be kicking yourself out of the shear intellectual stagnation and utter ridiculousness of this class. He really doesn't seem to care.

Taking a class with Kennison is like watching a one man show where he tries to intellectually challenge himself, and you die of boredom.  He is the most arbitrary grader I have ever seen using his own made up criteria. Now I know that taking a teacher who calls himself arrogant was a mistake because that is exactly what you're going to get. Easy A

Wes is an interesting fellow, and will certainly make you laugh. I've only taken 1 semester of Latin with him so far, but I learned a lot. I'm taking Latin Reading Group with him this semester hopefully. There aren't many assignments or tests or quizzes to speak of, just go to class and participate in his conversation and you'll do well.

Ken is all about participation and stimulating discussions. Unlike most HUM courses, you are not reviewing the synopsis of the book but connecting text-to-world and self. I would take this class again if it weren't at 8:05AM-9:45AM (1hr, 40mins). Sometimes he cancels, ends class early or shows up late. Regardless, I highly recommend.

People who think Wes is a good teacher can take a seat. He talks about (1) himself, (2) how he's better than you cause he traveled, (3) Italy, (4) how he knows more about everything cause he's been to Italy. Boring and not as intelligent as you'd think. Lectures reek of his blinding privilege. Take his brother, McClure, WAY better & you learn.

Great professor. Lectures aren't very structured and he does take awhile to get assignments back, but he's very entertaining and keeps class interesting. Put in the work and you'll learn a lot and do well.

I think that Humn in general is very useless for 95% of students by nature, and it seemed like even Wes didn't know what to do with a few of the books, since he would just ramble about random anecdotes that don't have anything to do with the course. So, lectures were somewhat pointless and the few assignments/exams were highly subjective essays.

Kennison is a great guy. If you make an effort in his class, he will treat you well. He is easy to meet up with if you need extra help and yes he is passionate about his going abroad programs. He did alot of work in Nicaragua to build a school and he deserves to be proud of it. He keeps in touch with alot of former students

I liked humn 1 and was looking forward to this class, but it was terrible. He just talks about himself and how he took students to Nicaragua.  He gives papers back months after you hand them in with seemingly random grades and useless comments. Take humn with someone else.

Wes is a great guy, but probably not the best of professors. Grades seem pretty arbitrary and he gives obscure paper topics. Class goes by fast, but mostly he talks about the life and times of Wes Kennison.

Just finishing my second semester of Latin with him. He fully understands that we're not going to become Latin translators, he's more interested in us getting something from the course that will help us in our professional lives. Gives stressful tests but "doesn't take the grade". He just wants to see that you're trying, it can be annoying though.

Wes is not all he's talked up to be.  Class is more interesting than other humanities profesors, but he talks alot about himself.  Grades seem pretty arbitrary, and our final grades seemed to come out of nowhere, considering three out of five assignments were not returned.  Nice guy, not the best professor around.  Hard to contact if necessary.

Wes Kennison is amazing, and has a lot to offer. I can understand how some may see him as a bit too talkative, but please do give him a chance. He is an incredibly smart and very nice guy, and he has given me a very refreshing perspective on many things. If you are an open-minded person, you will definitely get something out of his course.

He talks a lot of talk, but didn't deliver to my class, at least. Told us he'd help us write better and then didn't give feedback on half of the assignments. Infuriating for an English major, to say the least. My grade felt pretty arbitrary.

Kennison is by far the best professor I've had at Geneseo. He knows so much about so many different topics.  The information he teaches is usefull for every day life, and you walk out of the room feeling smarter and more worldy, yet not stressed.  He's very easy going and understanding- DEFINATLY take him if you have the chance.

I loved taking class with him. His lectures are really enjoyable. If you want to do well you need to think outside the box because he wants you to teach him something. I would love to take more classes with him in the future.

Consider yourself blessed if you get to take humn with Kennison.  I felt smarter just being in the same room with him, I would literally take this class WITH HIM AGAIN just for fun and to get all the things I may have missed the first time around.  Come to class, pay attention and think you will do well! Such an interesting class BECAUSE OF HIM!!!

he rarely worked off of students' ideas for discussions. he always went back to what he thought. he does tell interesting stories. VERY unclear about what he wanted for the essays. he was rarely there for his own classes and gave out pointless assignments! waste of time!
Extremely intelligent.  His papers are tough because you have to teach him something for an A.  If you do outside research on a topic that relates to the text, you'll be fine though.
Awesome teacher. Very knowledgable and fun to listen to. A lot of reading but he is open to answer any questions you have. Take him!!!

Take him.  Everyone hates humn, so don't judge a humn professor on the material.  However, Kennison does a good job of trying to keep the class interesting.  The exams are easy.  He likes participation.  He tells lots of personal stories.  He relates the books to the present day, often to politics (he is Geneseo's town supervisor). Good for HUMN!
Class was good.  He has lots of great stories and tries to make some of the incredibly boring texts interesting.  I thought he was great.  Definitly recommend him.
My favorite teacher so far.  He can really get you thinking.  He has entertaining stories.  He's great for political courses, as he's in politics.
i hated the class and didnt read the last few books and still did very well.  the material is very very boring but he is quite interesting, his stories were fun, i would recommend him
He is very good, i love him cos he grades reasonably and of course doesn't give too much reading but u still feel learned by the end of his class

absolute joke! hahahaha.  I thought i would have had to read for this class but nope.  Didn't even open the last 10 books of the semester, didnt read dante, hamlet, the prince, any of that****, and still got a B+.   hahahahahaha.  He thinks hes a real intellect, but no again.  He was beaten by me.

This was a frusterating class.  He was an interesting lecturer but got so far behind we were discussing books in class that we'd read over 2 weeks ago.  Tests weren't returned 'til the day before the next test, so we went into the final only knowing 2 test grades and neither of the 2 essay grades.

before i took the class i had a strong interest in st francis.  unfortunatly i learned very little about st. francis from class.  wes's lectures were irrelevent and he went on horribly boring tangents.  his grading was very subjective and he was never clear with instructions.
Very Good professor.  If you actually want to learn, take him

Wes was a great INTD professor! His grading system is perfect for INTD (he grades on how much you improve) I had so much fun with that class and the material and found myself wanting to learn more about the topic (St. Francis). I would suggest Wes any day
kennison is very interesting and loves to play devil's advocate. his classes are very entertaining even for an 8:05 class.

Farmer is the best professor in the political science department and it is a shame that she is leaving. She is a tough professor but extremely smart and available to help students. She is very effective at making a class like her so she can make everyone accept what she says even if it is downright mythical or based off her own form of logic.  She is very negative and cynical. You do not need a teacher that drags you down everyday.

Dr. Farmer is extremely understanding when it comes to assignments and the factors that might make an assignment more difficult to hand in at a certain time. Dr. Farmer is brilliant. Her class is challenging yet you learn a lot.Attendance isn't mandatory but highly recommended to do well as her lectures are very informative. I can tell how much effort she has put in by the reading materials.I have never met a professor who has so much concern for students. She was so helpful after class. Hands down best professor in the department. Shes engaging and interesting to listen to and she works her butt off to ensure that students fully understand the material.

Dr. Farmer was one of the best professors I had during my year at Geneseo. Shes passionate about the subject material and her lectures are always clear and packed with lots of important information. She grades fairly and her tests are easy if you go to class, take notes, and read the textbook.

Dr. Farmer's extremely knowledgable and will always assist students

Dr. Farmer is the reason I'm still at Geneseo. She is the best professor I have had here not only because of her outstanding teaching skills but her dedication and general concern for  students. Professor Farmer's Dev World politics class was extremely boring. You don't really learn much and the books are completely mindnumbing. The class is easy though but not worth taking professor's rudeness to students

Dr. Peterson is the best professor I've had so far at Geneseo. His lectures are clear and he always makes sure you can ask questions and he answers them well. Genuinely one of the nicest professors I have ever had. Very clear and concise when talking and is very passionate about what he does. Peterson is an excellent professor!! Very difficult course to do well in. Average test grades ranged from 50-60s and tests are very difficult. Too smart to be teaching general chemistry. Notes are very unclear and you must study hours just to get an 80. Very sweet and not bad to look at.
Peterson made Chemistry bearable, he was very specific on things you wouldn't be tested on and just an overall great professor. Highly recommend him.
He' s really passionate about what he does an genuinely wants people to do well. He ended up re-curving our tests mid semester.

Super friendly and approachable professor! Recommend him.

he is very nice and will help you with anything you dont understand makes a note to learn everyone in a lecture class' name doesnt believe in e.c but is understanding and does a huge curve. i went to class 1/3 times a week and just did the mastering chem hw the night before the test and got a had him for lab too and would recommend blogs r easy pts
one of the best professors I've had by far. tests are challenging but fair. as long as you read the textbook and go to class you should be fine.

Charismatic and cares about the success of his students. I took AP Chem so none of this is too difficult for me. Wonderfully helpful, funny, and the most personable freshman chem professor. His tests are difficult (average class score of about 50), but he curves them in a very fair way. Her lectures are not mandatory but I found them important to attend. She is very sweet and her homework is not very hard and allows unlimited attempts so very nice grade booster. Dr. Panda is the best! Midterm and final exams are always curved which always boosted my grade. She offers formula sheets and detailed study guides to practice. Chapters 11-14 were tricky, with lots of information and analysis.

This class is lectured based with weekly a homework and quiz.  Prof Panda explains topics very well and in an understandable manner!

Prof. Panda is really sweet and wants you to excel. The actual content is quite difficult, so be ready to study, and study often. Prof. Panda is an extremly good teacher for Economics, and while the class is hard, she does her best to make sure you succed. There are very generous curves, study days, and formula sheets for every exam. The class is very lecture heavy but she provides slides.

Professor Panda is so kind and really cares about her students. She is very generous with her exam curve! easy to learn if you show up, very kind and time efficient

Very nice professor, she really cares and knows about what shes teaching. Dr. Panda is a sweet lady who genuinely cares for her students. Her test are a little hard but she curves them pretty generously. I absolutely loved having Professor Panda for Econ 110. She was accessible outside of class and answered any questions fully and detailed. Homework had unlimited attempts allowing students to be more focused on learning the material rather than just getting a good grade.

Porf Panda is amazing. I honestly wish I went to class more often because she really knows what she's teaching which makes it so much easier to learn. Professor Panda is a literal angel sent to this earth. She is so intelligent, so sweet, and really really cares about her students. Panda is an amazing professor who really wants her students to succeed. Very standard workload. She makes her classes engaging and easy to learn. Highly recommend!

Professor Panda is a great teacher. her lectures are informative and she gives you chances to try problems and ask questions to get a full understanding. Her tests are a little difficult but she curves generously. overall great professor, would recommend.

Panda is a great professor, if you go and pay attention and read the textbook you'll do fine. also study from the homework for tests it really helps. Prof Bossung is Excellent! She spends a lot of helping students to make sure that we are understand the material and that we are learning. Very approachable outside of class for office hours. Avoid if you like to learn in class. All she does is talk about homework in the textbook in class. Professor Bossung is slightly scatterbrained in class, and her lectures are boring and confusing. But the book is excellent and she's very helpful during office hours. If you do the reading and assignments (which are often quite long) you will do well.

Class is confusing, but the book is really well written and help you learn everything. Her tests and quizzes are easy if you study a fair amount. Bossung is very approachable and helpful. She gets confused easily. Overall, her class isn't too bad if you can get over the boredom.

She's a pretty good professor.  She gives 3 exams, 4 quizzes (she drops the lowest), and comprehensive review problems (which take hours to complete).  You will have to teach yourself the material out of the book and use the class as a supplement.  Definitely a manageable class.

Lectures are extremely boring and there is a lot of work but if you do the work you can get a descent grade even if you bomb the tests. The class isn't hard its just extremely boring. That is the toughest part of the class is just learning about the material.

I love prof. Bossung.  She really wants her students to do well and trys really hard to work around anything that may come up during the course. Love Professor Bossung and her rolling briefcase (you can hear her coming down the hall)...Def. not an easy A with the comprehensive problems that take a good 5 hours a piece and the tests are hard but fair (she puts definitions from the book on her test)-see her during office hours, very helpful

great, sometimes overly enthusiastic (it may seem like shes yelling at you in class, but shes just really into teaching and accounting)

WONDERFUL in EVERYTHING!  You NEED to take him!  Believe me!
This is the first class that I actually looked forward to going to.  Very funny professor and an easy class if you do the review sheets.  I LOVE this man, he is so cute and funny!!!

Lots of notes and vocab but he is the funniest person ever. I really enjoy his class. If you study the notes and the stuff on his study sheet you will do perfectly fine.

best teacher ever.  all his tests come from the notes so as long as you study them youll do really good on the tests.  you also dont have to buy the books either cuz he goes over them at the review sessions.  hes really funny too
he is definately the funniest prof. you will ever have. i absolutely love this man. also the tests are pretty easy and he gives you a chance to get his feedback on the paper. Take a class with him!

A wonderul, energetic man. The material for Soc Third World is interesting but discouraging or "miserable" as he puts it. It's really not that bad, plus his specific examples make the class EASY to understand and he's a complete riot! HIGHLY ROCOMMENDED! This class fulfills 2 core requirements!
Coolest teacher on campus. Everyone should take a course with Dr. Tamura.
Tests are really easy if you thoroughly go through the study guide.  <--- Do not skip out on that.  The classes are really enjoyable since he is so funny.

AWESOME professor!  His humor matches his teaching ability!  Not only do his tests come straight from the notes, but his reading is not needed to pass!  Be carefuly with procrastination with the Weekly Analysis Essays though!  They pile up fast!

Such a funny and great teacher!!! As long as you go to class and study for the tests you'll be fine. Keep up on reading and the papers though or else you'll be crammed with work at test time! Highly recommend!!!

He is a great teacher. He makes class fun, dispite being a miserable subject as he calls it. The tests are straight from the notes... all I did was look over my notes and I got a 100! Too easy...but I won't complain!
Great guy, very interesting.
it's a fun & interesting class- he's such a nice guy! I definitely recommend taking his class, it was very enjoyable
A very happy man. Notes are straightforward. Tests fair. LOVES to have some intelligent participation.

Horrible avoid if possible he would convince students to drop courses if they are struggling instead coming up with ways to help. I nave had multiple students share the same experience

I would 100% try to get him again! Dr. M is dry during lecture but I still found the subject interesting. I loved this class. After doing terrible in Ecology I thought Genetics would be very intimating but in fact it has been one of my favorite classes because Dr. M was the professor. Don't take Genetics with Militello because you'll get a better grade - I was genuinely interested and worked really hard at this class and still got a B.  Take him because his lectures are clear and organized, he's engaging, and he really puts in the effort to be there for his students.  He knows his stuff and is a great guy in general.

Thank god I took this class with Dr.M. The class was always interesting and although there is a lot of reading, you learn about really novel biology that has been discovered in the past 5-10 years. Only 3 exams with 5 quizzes, so you are kept on your toes but Dr.M is really great during office hours. Participate because you get to argue that grade!

Dr. Militello is probably one of the best professors you can get for a biology course at Geneseo. He's very clear and concise with what information he expects you to know. Challenging tests with no curve, but you have plenty of resources at your disposal. Office Hours help immensely.

Dr. M is the man! He is very passionate about his work and teaches the material in a clear and concise manner. The exams are tough because he wants his students to really understand the material instead of rote memorization. However, Dr. M is always willing to help and loves to answer questions.

Dr. M is the best professor I have had yet at Geneseo. He wants his students to think  and critcally assess about what they are learning rather than memorize.. which can difficult for students at first. Helpful in office hours if you come prepared with questions. Militello loves what he does and I highly recommend every bio major to take him once!

Dr. Militello was extremely organized and his powerpoints were very helpful. Reading the textbook was not necessary as long as you go to class.
