Fair. Go to class, answer prs, make sure to write down prs questions they tend to help on hw's and tests. His voice is kind of annoying (imagine the dad from american pie) tests will cover all the material so they more than likely will show how much you know, how much you studied and if you should be in the class.

He's a great teacher, has the best accent, and his lectures ar helpful. Great professor. Tests are easy and he goes over most of the material.

Great professor. I had him for bio 117 my freshmen year and he was one of my favorites. Exams are hard, but he's very clear during lectures. As long as you go to class and read the textbook, you'll be fine. I recommend any course with him.

Awesome! Material wasn't too difficult, and he presented it pretty clearly. Dr. Militello is a great professor. He is very capable of explaining the material to what I felt, was a very interesting class. Very organized and great during lectures. Although he is the best option for this class, he's no push over; he still has tricky questions on tests and loves using application type questions. Although not as bad as Hoops, Militello still tried a little to make the tests very hard and weed kids out of the class.  His lectures were much more organized than Hoops, and his homeworks were easier than Hoops' also.

Class is challenging, but Dr.M gives great notes and lays everything that you need to know out on the table. If you just put some solid effort in studying, you WILL get a good grade on his tests. Quite the opposite of Dr. Hoops. I strongly recommend Dr. M.
The class is very hard, but Dr. M has very clean lectures and follows the slide almost exactly...best part of this class is the SI instructors though, they do a great job!

AWESOME TEAHCER!!! I love this guy, if hes teachin 117 TAKE HIM! This guy is great and his slides make sense, and he is NOT a hard teacher, all these losers who say that DONT STUDY, his tests are completely fair and hes a really nice guy, RECCOMEND BIG TIME!! I cant wait to take upper level classes with this guy especially genetics.
Dr. M is a really nice guy. Really helpful in office hours and will help you out if he sees that you really do care. Plus he's just a cool guy. Tests are very fair. Would absolutely recommend! :)

Really enjoyed this class, though it was a little trickier than I expected.  Dr. M is extremely organized and put together.  Lectures move along at a good pace, but plenty of opportunity to ask questions.  He really makes you understand the material to do well.  Definitely take him.

He is organized, explains things clearly, and answers all questions during lecture. I don't think I have seen a Professor as organized and as diligent about his work as he is. A very good professor.  Knows what he is taliking about and is always offering extras(help, credit et cetera)  Will murder you on tests so study a lot.  Homwork is unfortunatly in groups however that does help your score some.  Impossible to get the class unless you register pretty early.
Haney an lovett are so bad  they make militello look good. Doesnt say much. Take genetics elese were if you can!

Pretty good prefessor, bio is hard no matter what but he made it do-able. I found his tests to be very fair, not tricky at all.

Dr. M is very good at getting his points accross in lecture, and clarifying any confusions in the class. The only thing I can complain about is his tests were often not clear as to what the questions were asking. Overall, a good professr though
he is a great proff for lab!!!  hand the papers in early for lab so he can check it and you will get a great grade.  he is verrrry helpful.

AMAZING prof, I'm honestly devastated that she is leaving Geneseo

Good professor, but her exams are kind of ridiculous. There is so much material for this course that it is quite a pain. Not all the questions are straight forward. Tried making flashcards for an exam and there were about 200.

Dr. Storms is awesome! I learned so much from her. Lectures are interesting. She is a practicing therapist so we get to hear about real life examples. Highly recommend Dr. Storms! Can't wait to take her again next semester!

Professor Storms is awesome. She is a very fair grader. Her lectures are very interesting and she makes them easy to listen to. She is practicing so she tells stories of her patients. Take her class!!

Amazing professor! I took an 8:30 class was her but she made getting up early worth it. Kept class interesting, funny, really nice. Tests aren't hard if you study for a couple hours. Take her class!

the bomb. easy, and nicest lady ever.

Took points off of grades for her own mistakes, never gave clear instructions, not reachable outside of class, makes her TAs do all the work for her. Lectures consist of her reading the textbook, which we already had to read for homework, so class feels extremely boring/repetitive.

Tons of quizzes and discussion posts, based off a chapter from textbook each week. Quizzes are easy and at home, so textbook can be used even though it is timed. Attendance is mandatory, but TA's are the ones taking attendance. Lectures are boring and serve 0 purpose if you are only in the class for credit. Little guidance on final paper, use TA's.

I actually took XLRN-150 with her as an elective, but class wasn't available to click on here. Wouldn't recommend this class if you're actually trying to learn about identities. In my opinion, she makes everything about race. Which is fine if that's what you're into, but it got very repetitive and took away from learning. A lot of small projects.
shes awesome
HWs are easy, Speech is fine, lectures are boring as most. Overall just an easy A without effort. Professor Watson is caring and fun to talk to.

Dr. Watson is a very nice and easy going professor. However, her lectures got repetitive and boring because she would just read off the slides that were straight from the text book chapter that you read prior to class to do your weekly quiz. Relies on her TAs a lot so don't email her she doesn't always answer. Overall very easy just boring.

Class was super easy. Multiple assignments each week but they're not long or difficult at all, just tedious. Class gets boring and lectures aren't usually necessary, but she tries her best to make it entertaining and genuinely wants to improve as a professor. TAs are first point of contact. Just stay on top of your assignments and you'll do fine.

Watson is pretty hip, but her lectures were very boring. Attendance is mandatory but the content is just regurgitating what you read in the textbook, word for word, I found it hard to keep going after 2 months.The TAs do all the student interaction, very odd for Geneseo professors to stand back, but she did supply the text for the course online.

Dr Gonder has been one of the best, and most supportive professors I have encountered in my academic career. He is tough because he wants you to learn the material, but he is always willing to help you figure it out if you are willing to put in the work.
Always available for outside class consult. Really wants his students to succeed, so encourages them to complete assignments, and takes them up in class.
Excellent prof

One of my favorite profs at Geneseo. Why? He works even harder than we do - papers always graded by the next class, speaks intelligently, ALWAYS available outside class. He respects the nature of the interaction and his students.

Gonder uses language expertly, always brings materials for use in class, and spends every minute of time working. When I went to consult with him, he was pleasant and helpful. He does have a reputation for dealing strongly with students who cheat, and they are trying to trash him here. I only wish I could have taken more classes with him!

Gonder is a fine prof. I met with him lots outside of class - it was very helpful. One of the few profs that deals with cheaters - I heard one of them say they would trash him on RateMyProfessors. Personally, I think he should do something about cheaters. He is clear, bright, always gives extra materials to help us learn - if we do our own work.

He is absolutely awful. Dr. Gonder is condescending and boring, and will make you hate piano even if you love taking it. You'll find, also, that he does not help struggling students; he simply gets mad at them for asking for help. Dr. Gonder should not be a professor.
Gonder is an outstanding teacher. He works hard and expects you to. Very quick turnaround in assignments. Always accessible outside of class. Tough, but worth it.

As someone with a LOT of musical experience, this class was a lot less rough than it certainly could've been. The lectures are incredibly dry and boring and the homework takes forever, just the same questions over and over again. The pop song project completely destroyed the class for me though, it's a huge pain. Do NOT take for gen. ed. credit.

Professor really does know the content of the material he is teaching. Somewhat enthusiastic. comes off as a jerk at times, & a know it all. Talks in a way that seems like he's talking down to his students. Be on time to class when assignments are due or no credit. Lots of assignments, don't take very long. Learn quick or have lots of background.

Gonder is an excellent professor. A lot of material was covered very quickly in one semester, so I understand why it may be challenging for some, however it was very easy for me as I have previous music experience. He wants us to succeed and always answers questions to the best of his ability. Easy fine arts credit for those with experience.
Worst teacher ever, Id rather take 300 organic chem lectures then take this class again.. do not take this elective.

He goes through immense trouble in order to harm students grades. Most teachers are here to help us do well but I can say with confidence that he is not. DO NOT TAKE CLASS

This man is possibly the worst professor in Geneseo. I have heard many students talk baldy of him and now I have experienced it for myself. I have spoken to the dean about him to which he answered he always hears complaints about him. I question his agenda, if he is here to help students or hurt them. He says he doesn't care if you come to class, but he gives you a grade on your attendance. He begins the class at a very basic level, then gets difficult extremely fast.

comment: Gonder is very knowledgeable in what he teaches. If you have any basic music "theory" knowledge you could fly through this class. Attendance is not mandatory, but you receive a grade for your participation so you should show up. He is very specific in what he wants when grading but also tells you what he wants.

Truly one of the hardest and most tedious classes I have taken in my college career. Expects you to know the material without barely covering in class. The fact that this is a 100 level course blows my mind. Homework takes 1-2 hours minimum and tests are insanely hard. Frustrating that a fine arts gen ed is bringing down my GPA immensely.

comment: If you are looking for an easy 100 level fine art credit, DO NOT take this class. Thought I had musical experience, I was wrong. Loads of homework, and a "Pop Song" group project that is a total hassle. Don't even ask your friends for help on hw, he will accuse you of cheating and reduce your grade. The class avg. for the final was a C for 100level

If you have no music back ground or very little do no take. I did all the homework which is a lot for a 110 class he takes off 10 points if its not stapled correctly and u have to draw every note perfect or else u get points off. His test were impossible when i went to extra help he offered no help. I would spend hours doing the hw got a D.

I've been playing and reading music since I was 7. This class is more about theory than anything else, and even I found it difficult. He is a nice guy and clearly cares about music and his students but he doesnt take excuses. He is a strict grader and his tests are difficult. Take theater if you want an easy a. take this if you want a challenge

Very Difficult Class that is not even basic musicianship. This class is more of music theory. Even having 8 years of musical experience I struggled in this class. Hands out plagiarism charges yearly. (6 this semester.)

Took this class for my fine arts credit.... yea no take intro to theatre or dance if you are looking for an easy A. This class was made much harder than level 100 should be.... I expected a much higher grade because I had history in music yea no too much tedious work. This isn't an easy class, plus it was at 8:30... take dance... just take dance
Easily my least favorite professor I've had. I'd take a class Donald Trump before I'd take another class with Jon Gonder.

I'm pretty intimidated by the guy. You CANNOT show up to class late or be absent on days you hand in homework (which is almost everyday). Or else, you get a zero out of however many points it is worth (up to 300 points). Homework usually takes about 1-2 hours. I was late twice, so I had three 0/100 and had to work my butt to finish off with an A-.

My favorite class of the semester! He's a great guy and jokes around. I loved this class but partially because I already have prior experience in music. If you don't understand material, he's always there to help. Office hours are great! Tests are kinda hard but if you study, you'll do fine.

Great professor. Really knew what he was talking about and could answer any question thrown at him. Might be difficult for people with no music knowledge but he will help you. great class to take for fine arts credit

This class is not for someone without any prior musical knowledge - I did well only because I knew most of the material prior to taking the class. Professor Gonder requires you to come to class and be on time, as well as to submit assignments on time. He's not very lenient. However he clearly knows his subject and was a great teacher.

Although the class is labeled basic musicianship, it is far from basic. The idea that you don't need a music background is false. Worked very hard (3+ hours on some assignments) and still failed. Everyone else I know failed or got a D or C-. Course moves quickly and gets quite complex at the end. Be wary unless you really know music.

Great teacher. If you dont have musical background, this class might not be for you. Hes very easy to understand and very helpful, but music is music and it's very nit-picky. Unless you're super careful you will make careless mistakes. Havent opened the textbook for anything other than the hw assigned so I wish you didn't need to buy it but oh well

He loves what he does; if you do not take the class seriously, he won't reward you with a good grade. But if you put in a little time, or have any musical background coming in, he makes the class fun. Asks participation questions, so attendance is mandatory. But the tests are easy!
Super nice and understanding. Topics were well thought out although videos were often dated. He is a very tough grader for a 100 level class.

My favorite professor at Geneseo. Classes are a little bit reading-heavy but you can get away with reading a few pages to get the main idea. Makes all of the readings easy to access with pdfs. Imo the lectures are super interesting and he does a great job of keeping everyone engaged. Overall a great guy and great professor. 10/10 would recommend

Tough grader
top 2 best professors of all time wrd bro.

Reece is one of my favorite professors; he genuinely cares about what he's teaching.  There is a required textbook, but it is available as a pdf.  There is a lot of required reading, which is useful for the quizzes/memos.  However, he doesn't exactly check that you've read it.  His office hours should be used.  Only two tests, with a cheat sheet.

Reece is my FAVORITE prof I've EVER had the pleasure of taking a class for. Also took SOCL220 with him. Super approachable, office hours are very helpful, lectures are so engaging and never boring. He made me WANT to learn. I never felt awkward speaking up in class. He truly wants to see you succeed and will help however he can. USE HIS OFFICE HRS!
Nice guy. Boring class with too much reading

comment: Reece is such an enthusiastic and engaging lecturer. There's something about his presentation that really gets discussion rolling, and with gusto.

I LOVE DR. REECE TORRES. I wish I wasn't graduating so I could take more classes with him. His lectures are engaging so you don't even feel like you're in a class, he truly loves his job and cares about the students, he works with you, wants you to prioritize your well-being, and is super approachable (calls us gang). TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HIM!!!
I enjoyed taking Socl 102 with Reece. He wants all of his students to do well. Prepare to read but its very interesting and weekly papers based on class and readings

comment: Great professor, a choice of 3 Essays with 5 different deadlines and a midterm and final. ; Overall I learned a lot and would recommend the class to anyone interested in sociology and psychology.

Torres is hands down the best professor I have ever taken at Geneseo. He is very clear about what you need to do to succeed in his class and is very accessible in helping you get there. He is willing to go above and beyond to ensure you understand the content and feel confident in your work. Overall, a real asset to the sociology department

comment: Really really enjoyed this class- the lectures were really engaging and the tests were very approachable.

Reece is an amazing professor! He's very passionate about what he teaches and is very adamant about matching your energy in class, so don't be afraid to participate! The assigned readings were lengthy and the summaries due at the end of every class were sometimes difficult to complete, but Reece gives great feedback on papers and summaries.

comment: I really enjoyed this course. It is a lot of reading, but he gives us assignments that will help write the paper at the end. He makes the course very interesting an engaging to listen. There are a lot of books you need so i would reccomend getting them free on Z library, they had every book on there.

Reece is a great professor. Not only was the content itself interesting, but Reece himself made the class fun and always tried to facilitate good discussion. Be prepared to read a lot write a paper after. He's a great professor to go to office hours for, he will "match your energy" and make an effort to look out for you if you start to struggle.

comment: amazing professor and very helpful. as long as you read and put in the effort for the class you will do well, and the topics are very interesting.

His motto is that he will 'match your energy' and he does. After the first memo grade, I thought that I was going to fail the class but after talking to him and learning what he looks for, I got my grade up to an A. comment: Very valuable lectures that encourage open discussion on heavy topics. Welcomes criticism and opposing arguments with open arms. Very easy to work with in office hours. Makes you form your own thoughts and opinions, come to your own conclusions.

Reece is an incredible professor. He is incredibly caring and is very adamant about 'matching your energy'. He is so passionate about his teaching and gives great feedback on papers. Class discussion and participation is expected, however it is very engaging. Would 100/10 take a course with Reece again!

Bennett is an AMAZING professor! His lectures are interesting, and mandatory to attend if you want an A (bonuses for attendance). 3 exams, 2 papers, and weekly quizzes (ridiculously easy if you read the books). Start the papers early and he will help you with them. Rewards hard work when he sees it. Humn is worth taking with Bennett!
Love your intellect!
Tough grader, read the books!

Bennett is tough but fair. He has some pretty good stories to share and has an overall good outlook on life. Definitely harder than a lot of the other professors, but I cant stress enough what a good person he is.  Take it if you like to read and want to learn about how to put things in perspective.

Bennett is understanding to a point.  If you are upfront and honest he will work with you.  GO TALK TO HIM.  He is super funny, although it can be missed if you are not paying attention.  His lectures can be dry but he has a lot to offer.

This course was far too in-depth for a course mandatory of all Geneseo students, let alone a 200-level.  Bennett is an extremely well-informed professor but gave extremely long and relatively uninspiring lectures with a few hilarious connections to modern life.  I got little out of his teaching style. two 7-9 page papers and three 3-5 pg papers.

Had the PRIVILEGE to take humn with Bennett.  A kind, caring, and hilarious professor who truly cares about his students.  Gets you to think critically and not just merely regurgitate facts.  Yes its a lot of work, but his class is well worth it.

Bennett is a very funny man. He knows the material well and is willing to help you. However, his section is definitely hard. 3 tests(test+essay) and 2 papers. I have no idea how I didn't fail miserably because it's a hard class and he's not exactly easy. The readings are definitely necessary.

Gets you to think about real life and that can not be said about many other professors.  Is a lot of work, but a good grade is possible with work.  If you apply yourself, you will not only find him great but take a lot of the class.

From all the hype I thought this prof was going to be amazing. HE IS NOT! He talked about his ultra conservative views almost daily. He was late getting my papers back to me. If you have to take HUM with him just don't get on his bad side or you'll stay there.

Bennett is a great dude, really funny. I was dreading humn and he always made class enjoyable. I wouldn't really recommend him if you are looking for an easy A as he did require a good amount of work. Random quizzes were the worst but he gives a lot of free points. I'm happy I got to experience a class with Bennett, he is extremely genuine

Bennett the funniest and most genuine professor Ive had. He really makes the class interesting with funny stories and anecdotes. The only thing I didnt like was how long it took to get everything back and how much reading and essays he required compared to other profs. I would recommend taking his class. He really cares about his students.

Excellent teacher. Gives you a lot of perspective on things that you would have not expected to be interesting. Definitely a hard class, especially over the summer, but well worth it. He is by far the best humanities teacher that you will find....just read the books and you should be fine for the tests.
Had Bennett for Hum 1 & 2 and got A's in both. Fair grader, gives extra credit, and wants to help you get a good grade. Plus he's hilarious and his class is always fun/interesting. highly recommend

Prof. Bennett was a fun teacher whose lectures were always entertaining.  The tests weren't too bad if you read the books.  Daily quizzes were hard but they helped considering most of the multiple choice test questions were straight from the quizzes.  Bennett is definitely a great choice for Humn one.

I'm really upset that his hum 2 classes for next semester are filled. Took his first test, got a 96 and he told us that was going to be the hardest exam all year... WHAT? amazing teacher, hilarious, and he makes modern day analogies and really makes it easy to understand. tests are simple straightforward and nothing confusing.

Professor Bennett is a wonderful professor and individual.  Of all the professors I had at Geneseo, he influenced me the most. Genuine.  His lectures can be structured or discussion based.  They are always informative, engaging, and best of all they're funny and entertaining. The content/readings can be difficult but Bennett explained the concepts

BEST LEFT HANDED GINGER!Bennett is great! HE MAKES YOU THINK!  Didn't tell you how or what to think!  Summer Humanities aren't easy courses.  Especially if you have a life outside of college.  Tons of reading, several quizes, a few tests and a couple of papers.  Bennett made crappy boring Humanities INTERESTING.
Great Prof.  Was nervous about taking Hum I and II.  Bennett made it much more interesting that I ever expected!  Fair to all sides.  Fair grader.  HELPFUL.  FUNNY.  One of the best "Gingers!"
Awesome

Always go to class! Classes are interesting, he's a really funny guy, and the notes you take will help you on the exams. If you don't read and use Sparknotes instead, you'll do fine...if you consider a "C" fine. Tests are detailed and random, but he is an easy paper grader and offers extra credit. He's also probably the nicest guy in Geneseo.

Great professor, class discussions are sometimes informative but sometimes just philosophical debates. Attendance isn't absolutely necessary. Tests and quizzes are moderately difficult. Reading is not a must but will help.
Funny dude .. Tests and quizzes are tough .. can get by without reading as long as you participate .. real opinionated .. but funny

I took HUMN One with Bennett over the summer and absolutely loved him. He's a funny guy and, for the most part, keeps class interesting. VERY helpful outside of class and loves to talk about his subject. Tests weren't bad, as long as you listened in class and looked back at the things he stressed. Also gives interesting essays.

I had Edgar for Hum 1 and Bennett for Hum 2. Bennett was far and away the better Hum professor. Entertaining, funny, loved his sense of humor. Tests are far easier than in Edgar's class (Edgar had at least 8+ quotes each test in hum 1). His tests are choose 5 of 8 ID and 3 of 5 quotes or something like that. Good/fair prof. Quiz once/wk but not bad

He's a great guy.  I took both hum classes with him and enjoyed every minute.  He's funny, but in a dry and even self deprecating way.  He's immensely likeable and among my favorite professors at Geneseo.  That being said, his tests are very difficult.  I put up with it because he made two classes I was dreading a lot of fun.

Extremely difficult class, i took humn I with him over the summer (i'm an english major with a 3.8 gpa), and I ended up getting a B in this class because the tests and essays were so arbitrary. You need to spent A LOT OF time reading and rereading the books in order to do well on the test (got a 70 on the first test, 90, and then an 80)

Great guy. Geeky but in a good way. Makes the class really interesting, and helps you out in a big way. I'm taking both summer sessions with him and I couldn't be happier. Just go to class, read the SparkNotes, know how to write an essay, and participate in discussions (which you'll want to do) and you'll get at least a B+ in this class.

Oh my god this guy is a riot!  He's not easy, and knows his stuff, but he goes out of his way to make sure that you're doing what you're doing for the sake of understanding and enjoyment.  He does what he can to make things easier, and his sense of humor is so sharp and subtle!  Totally great!
Not fun
Best Professor I've had at Geneseo so far.  You do a lot of writing but it is not hard at all.  Class can be boring at times, but he is the nicest guy.

She is very nice and cares about her students. She is very helpful during lab. She always answers emails in a timely manner and will be flexible if you need to make up work. I would love to take other classes with her.

The best for BIO222. On top of being very likeable and helpful, she goes out of her way to review quizzes and exams after the fact and offers a couple grade-boosting opportunities. The lectures are very good too, and she tries to teach more than just the basic curriculum. Also the textbook is not technically needed.

I loved Professor Hutchison! She was a really good teacher. I took this class online (Covid) and the lectures were split among the 3 teachers. I always understood the material she taught best and the videos were 10-15 min pieces which made it easier to focus. She was also super helpful during office hours and very accessible. Definitely recommend!
tags: ['Accessible outside class', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Amazing lectures']

comment: Dr. Hutchison is the best professor I have had here at Geneseo. She is the kindest person on this campus, and she is always willing to help her students. The class was really interesting. However, her class was the hardest biology course I have ever taken. For perspective, I am taking cell biology now, and it is easier than Genetics.

In lecture she is pretty good, and really explains things. Make sure to go to class since what she discusses in class is not always in the online notes. Her tests are not fair, besides the final, because they rely on process of elimination not an actual understanding of the material. Literally memorize the notes and everything in them to do well.

Dr. Hutchison is an amazing lecturer. She does a good job presenting material in a way that is easy to understand. The class itself is difficult. People complain that she makes you know everything she says but isn't that kind of the point?  There is nothing on the test that she hasn't told you about. Reading not required if you go to class.

Grade only based on 3 tests, quiz and homeworks. Prof Hutchison was one of my favorites though and I'm planning to take micro with her. Her tests are hard but its possible to do well in her class if you read the textbook. She is the best and her lectures are really organized and easy to follow

Had her for both microbiology and genetics.  She expects you to memorize every single detail and if you don't mention every single detail she will take off points.  Very nit picky which makes getting a good grade difficult.

I have not one negative thing I could possibly say about Hutch. She  now my favorite professor! I have achieved goals I never thought I would be able to achieve in the class (I got a 95 on one of her exams) & she makes going to an 8:30 a pleasant experience. She gives topic sheets for every exam so you know exactly what to study. TAKE HER!

I was so sure that I wasn't going to be able to get an A in this class because of how hard the tests were, and how stubborn I was about getting help. However, Dr. Hutchison is the most approachable professor I've ever had at Geneseo! She literally saved me and never made me feel bad for asking really stupid questions. Definitely take her for class!

Professor Hutchison is the best biology professor I have encountered at Geneseo. She cares about her students doing well and gives you all the materials necessary to get an A. She is also very approachable during office hours. She assigns 2 homework per test, but they are very applicable to the material and are helpful when studying.

Dr. Hutchison was an amazing professor and made me love the subject. Genetics is a difficult class no matter who you take it with, so expect to study a lot. She is very helpful in her office hours and review sessions, and is always very friendly and helpful. I would definitely recommend for genetics.

I wouldn't say this class is a walk in the park by any means. You have to study really hard for these exams and there is a ton of material to understand and memorize. Class averages were pretty low and there is no curve. Wonderful woman, genuinely hard class. Don't take it lightly.

Micro with Hutchison was a great course. She is very organized and thorough, and there are usually no surprises on the exams as long as you study the material covered in class. Some of the material can get a little boring, but she does her best to keep you interested and allows for class discussion. She is also very willing to work with students.

She's an AMAZING professor!! I love genetics because of her! Somehow she made the subject very interesting. Her notes were very detailed and home works were very helpful. She's usually available in her office and super patient. I've learned so much from her in just one semester. She's definitely one of the best professors I had at Geneseo.

Excellent professor! Extremely helpful during office hours or by email. Her exams are challenging. A topic she spent 3 days on in class might have one question, while something she barely mentioned might have 5 questions. Overall she is excellent and very knowledgeable.

Hutchison is the genetics teacher to get, after taking her class I'm confident I would take her over Millitello if I had to retake the class. She's very organized, responds to emails much faster than any teacher I've had, and her class is not overbearing like Haynie and Lovett's. Go to class and do the hw's and you should at least get a b+

This class was the best place to get my notes on the reading done. I never listened to her lectures and used the textbook to learn the material and did well. She gets confused often, but she makes up for it by taking off questions on the test so your grade is higher. I would only suggest to take bio with her if you have a background on it already.

Even though I had to take this class for my major, I would never take it again. This professor makes the lessons hard to understand as she doesn't make the information clear enough to be understood, she makes power points that don't help. Throughout the semester I have had to teach my self the lessons. She doesn't know what she talks about at times

comment: When my bio class switched over to her as a professor, I was severely let down by her teaching style. She seems scattered with her lectures and often explains things in a convoluted way. She often spoke to the class as if we were children. I get that she has more experience than us, but we don't need to be treated like we're middle schoolers.

As head of the Bio department, I was expecting a lot more from Professor Muench. She was not a very good lecturer; she would often lose her train of thought. The tests are really difficult, so make sure you read the textbook if you want to get a decent grade.
I would have learned more from a rock.

Absolutely the worst professor I have ever had. She lectures like she just read the textbook the night before and makes things way more difficult than they need to be. Dr. Bailey was great and they split the semester teaching the class. I was extremely disappointed to go from Dr. Bailey to her. STAY AWAY!!!

Lectures are extremely confusing and difficult to find value in. Conflates her personal feelings with the evolution portion of the course, making it difficult to discern between scientific evidence-supported theory and external opinions.

She is a nice woman but extremely unorganized. If you read the textbook and pay attention you should do well. Tests are very ambiguous and she has many homework assignments but they are easy. She is never clear on exactly what she is asking for in class and on tests and very discussion heavy with a lot of group work.

She was a decent teacher. She made us do "think/pair/share" during class when we talked about genetics, but her ways of teaching did not help me retain the info. She has a monotone voice. I learned more by reading the textbook, going to SI sessions, than from her lectures. Overall, she's an okay teacher.

Insanely unapproachable, her tests are very ambiguous and subjective. I would study close to 10 hours a week for her class alone and i would see no results. Then, and alternating professor would cover certain topics in this section of biology and i would pass with flying colors. Avoid at all costs, it tanked my GPA that was originally a 3.7

I don't know why people have a problem with her. Of course the quizzes don't count much, they are there to make sure you read. The tests are pretty easy and the written response questions are based on the in class discussions. Not that difficult if you have a brain.

The class is very interesting, and not that difficult if you read the textbook carefully and study for the exams. She gives you a lot of chances to do well, but her style of teaching can be a little confusing. She can also be somewhat rude if you ask for help, but if you are good at teaching yourself you will be fine.

One of the worst professors I have ever had. Tests are ambiguous, and the books is not helpful much at all for them. Quizzes are based on reading from the book, but don't count much towards the grade. Classes are very unorganized and alot of pointless group "discussions". I am glad to get out of this class with a B so it didn't hurt my GPA too much

Teaches the humanities very well. Be prepared to speak up in class. He grades it on participation and 3 essays so make sure you can write well and take a stance. I'm glad I have him but I'm wary to recommend him as I don't think he works well with everyone

Good professor, lots of readings but can mostly be skimmed. Good discussions and lectures in class, and will help you if you ask for it. Very important to make comments and participate in class. All 3 exams are take home essays, ~5 pages, that require plenty of quotes and evidence from the texts, but require no citations. In short, take the class.
He knows what he is lecturing about, and be prepared to speak up in class. He asks really thoughtful questions, and overall I'm glad I have him.

His teaching style is very hit-or-miss. He has great discussions in his class and is very helpful in office hours. He knows a lot about his area, but not a lot beyond that. He has very strong opinions about things and he definitely lets you know.
Do the reading assigned and take notes.He may know his material but I found him to be rude in class.The good thing is all exams are take home essays,so that helps.

Comments saying that this is a hard class which requires reading are justified. This shouldn't be a bad thing, come on, this is college. Oberg is a excellent teacher and a fair grader, participation is extremely important. Show interest in his class and he will help you out. Extremely knowledgeable and funny
He is kind of an a** hole. But he knows his stuff. He has dry humor that makes the class fun, but he is arrogant in person and not very helpful. If you get stressed out easily, don't take him.
DO THE READING! The assessments are based on what you've read and Oberg can tell when you aren't prepared. He's extremely knowledgeable but a bit intimidating.

This is a great class.  Don't believe what people say about it being really hard. He gives out papers and no mid-terms. do the reading, write an essay with eveidnece, and speak in class, and you got nothing to worry about. Do those things and it is an easy a

A great professor and an awesome class. He is passionate about Native American history and it shows. Starting this semester he has decided to do away with tests - our grades consisted of 10 essays (the two lowest were dropped) for 80% of the grade and in class participation for the other 20%. Expect to do most of the reading and go to every class.
Dr. Oberg likes to joke, likes the Bills, and likes to hear himself talk but he is a good teacher if you like history you should tak him
Interesting to listen to, but kindof a **** when it comest to politics.  Needs to keep his own views out of lecture.
Very smart professor. Learned a great deal in his classes, but highly stressful as well.  Very helpful to some students, and absolutely useless and dismissive with others.

Took the INTD about the lost colonies of roanoke. Oberg is really knowledgeable on the subject and knows everything on the topic. The class focused more on the subject as opposed to the writing which defeats the purpose. If you're a weak writer, don't take this. If you're a strong writer the class is a breeze.

I really liked his class. I thought that it was very interesting. Yes, there was LOTS to read, but if you did the readings and came to class it was easy to get a good grade. Beware of the 20 page paper... not hard, just long!!
You always have to read every assignment he gives you in depth. It is best to always participate in class to get a decent grade.
No Comments

Seemed easy at the outset of the class. If you state something he doesn't agree with in your writing he may not adequately explain the drop in your grade. He's a nice guy and lecture is rather enjoyable. Sadly, he is a professor that allows or even helps foster an environment where you have to suck up to do well. Anticipate unnecessary stress.

His exams are take home papers and that doesn't make things easy. There's lots of reading to do and he's a very hard grader on papers. He does say a lot of interesting stuff in his lecture but his notes are useless in writing the paper. He'll really lower your grade if you don't participate. I don't recommend him if you're not a history major.

I give him credit, he is very into Native American studies and makes the material very interesting. However, he is an unbelievably hard grader and won't give reason to your grade.  He is also impossible to reach outside of class, never being at his office hours even when he says he will extend them, and not believing in appointments.

He is a hard grader. I felt like I learned very little and I went to just about every class. I think he has favorites. He's not very approachable for everyone. I give him credit he does try to make class lively. Don't take him if your not a history major!

Don't listen to some of these comments.  I hardly read anything, but by going to class and taking great notes, I received two A's from his classes.  He is an amazing teacher. Speak up in class, and just skim over the material, you will do good.

Native American History he is very passionate about the subject and it comes through when he is teaching it, expect a lot of notes, challenging reading and papers to write but you learn a lot. Don't ask too many questions he gets annoyed
he is not as hard of a grader as everyone says, i am not even good with history and i got higher than a B on a paper, and he didn't give any tests... i think he is interesting and worth taking
Funny guy, lively lectures.  If you go to class and he sees you, I think he'll be nice to you unlike what the other people are saying.  I think...

He is a very smart man, and very funny in class. HOWEVER he was very unhelpful out of class, and gave people attitude or talked down on them when they tried to reach him for extra help.  He is a ridiculously hard grader.

oberg is an amazing teacher! he knows everything on the subject and doesnt even look at notes! smartest man alive! and real funny.  he is kinda a tough grader, but if you try hard and do the reading youll be fine. he likes the Bills!
Oberg is a genius. The class is really hard but if you take the time to do the reading you will get a lot out of it. He is also really funny in a cynical and morbid way.
very hard grader, but I learned more in his class about writing then ever before- but be ready to work

Oberg is amazing- excellent. Really tough grader-has been known to give out Fs for really bad essays (a C means you worked hard and wrote an average paper), but you cheat yourself by not taking his class. He teaches really well, is fun and entertaining, and is nice if you are a serious student.

the guys amazing. he doesn't use any notes to teach, he just knows it all. but he uses it against you, and tries to make you think you know nothing. he grades ridiculously too. never got anything higher than a B on anything, didn't meet anyone that did either.

Knows what he's talking about, but that's the problem...  He's arrogant, and an unusually difficult grader.  For the most part acts as if his students will never achieve the same level of understanding as him.
Very interesting but a hard grader.
hard grader, but very helpful
You take a ton of notes and are not allowed to use them for his take-home tests.  He doesn't like to give anything higher than a B.
awesome teacher
No Comments
No Comments

There are only 4 tests in this class. That is all you're graded on. He doesn't really state what's on the test and doesn't always cover what's on the test in the lecture. Do not take this class with him if you can avoid it.

Do not take this class if you don't have to. Very tough grader. not very helpful on the papers even though he says he is. He doesn't understand that he's the issue when the class average on a test is a 68. You're pretty much on your own.

4 tests are your only grades the whole semester. They weren't too hard, but go to the TA reviews, they give practice questions that really help. All of the questions were from lecture, not the book, so I wish I hadn't spent money on something I didn't need. Overall, not a bad class and he makes it pretty easy to do well.

4 tests. Lectures were recorded and posted, we had a TA who did review sessions before each exam. Accessible via email and was good with accommodations, I needed to take my final early and he was very nice about it. Make sure you study the links and videos from class and don't buy the book! All of the exam questions were from lecture.

comment: I loved Bazzett's behavioral res class! It was synchronous zooms that were not mandatory, but most of the class usually went. He lets you keep handing in drafts for the papers until the due date/ until you get a 25/25 which is a huge plus to taking his class. He is super nice and wants you to succeed in this class.

I had Bazzett for a previous class and I thought I would enjoy being in his class again but no. He grades really hard for all the papers and if he doesn't understand something he writes question marks all over and barely gives any feedback. This is a tough class so be ready to write the way he wants.
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'So many papers', 'Tough grader']

comment: Each class period is a lecture and the notes are always posted online. He makes the subjects interesting and engaging and will tell you in class possible (very probable) questions that will be on the test. There are only 4 grades which are the 4 tests and while they are challenging he reviews in class and prepares you well. Very nice too!
tags: ['Clear grading criteria', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS', 'Amazing lectures']

comment: Bosch is my favorite bio professor. Attendance is not mandatory, but his slides do not always have the information you need to do well on tests. He can be a little disorganized but he makes lecture and lab fun! He is quick to answer questions through email. He is also very accommodating for student athletes and other school organizations!

Dr Bosch is one of the best science professors I've ever had. I studied abroad with him, and he went above and beyond to accommodate my directed study. He was so caring and helpful, you can tell he really loves what he does and knows what he is talking about. Lecture and powerpoint heavy, but is more than willing to help if you need it.

I had Dr. Bosch for the second half of my BIOL117 course. He has a solid understanding of the concepts but goes incredibly slow. We were always falling behind with the material. Other than that, he is methodical in his teaching and will ensure that everybody understands the concepts. Also, would clearly outline what would be on the tests.

I had bosch for the second half of bio 117 and let me say thank god. Yes, he might be slow but he does the work to help you understand everything and if you are willing to be on the same page with him I say you'll have a great time. His tests were hard for me but it might not be for you if you are a good test taker.

Goes very slow in lectures. Wastes time in lecture on confusing case studies. Approachable if you have questions. Tests are easier than Lewis's. Just read the textbook. Great if you are a bio major. Does not grade attendance but lectures are important, sometimes he teaches something slightly different than in the textbook

He is an amazing professor who is incredibly passionate about his work. One of the most approachable professors here. He is always willing to answer questions and really wants you to learn the material. Make sure to utilize his office hours. It will be save you.

I really enjoyed having Dr. Bosch for the second half of Gen Bio I and II. He speaks softly and comes across very caring. You can tell he is passionate about biology and he wants everyone to succeed. He is very approachable. He and Feissner make a good team, he goes slow in lectures, and tests, similar to Feissner's, are very doable.

Dr. Bosch gave great feedback on assignments and reports, and he was very considerate and caring in regards to my concerns. He genuinely cares and is enthusiastic about his teachings. I would definitely take him again

Absolutely amazing teacher. It's very obvious that Prof Bosch knows so much about what he teaches and puts every effort into helping his students excel. He does give a TON of homework and the tests are super hard but if you use the resources he gives you the class is easy

Dr. Bosch makes the subjects he teaches so interesting. When he teaches Gen Bio with Feissner, it is truly the dream team in action. He explains everything clearly, and is very accessible outside of class. If you don't do the homework though, you won't do well on the tests.

The nicest professor you'll meet on campus. Read the textbook and pay attention to lectures to do well in his class. He was very enthusiastic during lectures and he doesn't fly through slides so it's easy to take notes. If you're confused about anything, stop by his office and he'll break it down fully to make sure you walk away understanding it.
One of the nicest professors at Geneseo! Literally so nice and cares so much about his students.

While Bio 117 is a tough class, Dr. Bosch makes it clear what is on the tests based on what is on the lecture slides. However, it is still a lot of material to keep track of (and the questions on the tests include both application questions and questions based on definitions), so this class still requires quite a bit of studying.

Professor Bosch's teaching style is very boring and dry. It would be easier to have him as a teacher if he was first - instead of having Dr. O'Donnell first, who was energetic and kept the class very interesting. I had a hard time staying awake with Bosch. His lectures don't align with the textbook pages he gives. Overall, He is an OKAY teacher.

I currently have Bosch and O'Donnell (they switch halfway through the semester) and Bosch is just so caring and loves biology he gets so into it. He's adorable and he really makes an effort to help his students out! if you email him hell answer quickly and he wants everyone t do well, he isn't out to get anyone

Bosch is my favorite professor at Geneseo. He is so knowledgable and enthusiastic about what he teaches! He can be a little disorganized and takes a while to grade. However, he is a really nice guy and he actually wants his students to succeed. Also he has a very soothing voice. I highly recommend Bosch as a professor.

Great teacher! One of the only professors I've found at Geneseo that actually cares about you and isn't trying to destroy your GPA. He will really try to help you out and wants the best for everyone. Definitely recommend taking him!

Every other year Bosch teaches ecology when one of the professors go on sabbatical. The only problem is that he is NOT passionate about the subject an thus makes it an unpleasant to be in his class. Not very knowledgable about the subject and puts minimal effort into his lectures, can be interesting when he talks about research experiences abroad.

Bosch was one of the easiest professors I have ever had. Just take notes on the PowerPoints before the tests and you should be fine (although I don't think he teaches ecology too often). He takes one hundred and twelve years to hand assignments back, so you're probably better off badgering him for your grade so at least he'll finish yours.

Great class, great teacher.  Can be tough to understand what he wants sometimes, but if you put in the effort and talk to him if you're confused, you'll get a good grade.  Great with extensions or understanding if you need extra time with something.

LOVED this guy. I figured I'd be a ecology pro without studying, but after I failed my first two exams he actually reached out to me to come see him. After I started going to office hours my test grades went from 60's to 90's. Ended up with a B+ in his class, which I'm pretty sure he just gave me for my effort at the end.

He is very clear in class, but I don't find him extremely approachable. His grading on tests is sometimes very unclear, especially since his handwriting is illegible. He is very slow at grading things so it might be two months before you know what you got on an assignment. He has made it pretty clear that he cares about his other classes more.

bosch is the man went to class on average 2/3 a week and only crammed the night before each test, he jokes around and shows videos like everyday, some of the stuff he says in class is just facts that hes doesnt even test on, lab is easy and boosts your grade since they count together as one class, some of class material is boring but recommend him
Really loved this class. Learned a lot. Dr. Bosch has so much background in his field and is super approachable. You should definitely take his class.
Very nice, down to earth guy.  Very interested in the students work and loves to show little demonstrations during the bio lab even though he's just a supervisor.

Dr. Bosch is Great!!! He is so  helpful and he really cares about how his students perform in his class. If people put in the adequate amount of time they are sure to excel and do well! Also if they are having trouble he will be more than welcome to help.

Bosch was the only reason I took this class.  He is a great, enthusiastic professor and a down to earth guy.  Lab was the most unorganized but relaxed lab I have ever been in.  Lecture was good and power point slides were great.  Four tests, one poster research project, and the final isn?t cumulative. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED! BOSCH IS AWESOME!

Plays favroits. If you not one of them an you go to his office to ask a question an one of his favroits shows up, he will blow you off an talk to that other person. Practice exams are worthless as are the study guids. Also openly admitted to not wanting to teach a spring class which was mandatory in order to do research the following semester.

Dr. Bosch is very arrogant and is a fan of favoritism. I do not recommend him. If he doesn't like you, he's not impartial at all and your grades will reflect it. Take Dr. Harvitsen, the nicest girl you'll ever meet!

Dr. Bosch is a great professor to take. Bosch is constantly going out of his way to help his students. He is a great guy and works hard to keep his students happy. He is always willing to take time out of his schedule to help.

Really, really awesome guy and a decent class. Ecology isn't what you expect--but Bosch tries really hard and he's really passionate about it. I highly recommend him and I'll definitely try to get him for another class sometime soon.
you have to like bosch in order to take his class. Everyone who took this course liked him, even though the material was less than what i expected. He's a cool guy, did a nice field trip!!! :)

There is really not that much work throughout the semester, but the tests can be really hard.  You need to study a lot for them and there is a lot of info he expects you to know.  The review sheet that he makes does help somewhat.  Overally not that hard and he is a good teacher who knows his stuff.
Interesting lectures, some times. He makes the class harder than it needs to be and tests on random things. I didn't learn anything in his class. He also gives busy work.
A great professor.  Easy to talk to, approachable, understanding, and dedicated.  Tricky test question require thought and much studying.

i don;t know what the first 2 comments are about, obviously theyve got the wrong dr. bosch. He's the coolest professor. KNows what its like to be human and a college student, well sympthathize with you. Hey, he's super cool.

Makes an easy subject matter difficult, by not being clear on what he wants.  He lectures on one thing and tests on another. His questions on tests are often misleading, also.  He's a nice guy, just needs to improve on the teaching...
A very misleading man with very misleading questions with even more misleading answers. This man is evil, don't listen to everyone's lies.
Awesome professor.  Test do require studying but nothing to major.
great professor!  easy class, and definately fun! one of my favorite bio classes thus far
Simply Superb!
Dr. Bosch was by far the best professor I had at Geneseo.  Definetly a really cool guy and I learned so much from him!!
Dr. Bosch's class was tough at times, but his review sheets were awesome and very helpful. He's a reasonable guy and if you're genuinely interested in the class, you'll do well.
He's such a nice guy.  His exams can be a little tough, but if you go to class and read when you're supposed to, it's not that bad.  He's ALWAYS willing to help you out if you need it too.
I cant really say whether his class is easy or not because I was in his Bio 128 which basically just tried to help freshman bio..but he no doubt is a very helpful and nice person

Dr. Bosch is very willing to help students in office hours, but I find that his tests are unfair.  He tends to ask misleading and confusing questions that seem like 2 answers would be correct.  The book isn't much help, you must go to class to do well.
I absolutely adore Dr. Bosch!!  He is one of the nicest professors I've had, and he really cares about his students!!  And his classes are interesting too!!
he's okay, i didnt like his grading style but it was a joint class with another prof, didnt like the style of class at all

Very difficult to understand in lecture because he mumbles. Doesn't explain things well even outside of class. Test questions are very unfair and difficult to even understand. Also a tough grader. Nice guy though.
tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework']

comment: Dr. Bailey is decent with lectures. I did not read the textbook. The worst part was his exams were way too long for the half an hour you had to take them.  Also Dr. Bailey is very smart but not great at explaining things to people who are learning. Because of this going to his office hours was useless and you really can't get extra help from him.

Dr. Bailey is a great professor that actually wants you to learn the material and understand it. If you keep up with the material, read the textbook, are active in lecture and ask questions at office hours or in lecture, he will help you as much you are helping yourself. You do all those things, an A is easy to get

Dr. Bailey is a fast-paced lecturer, but his lecture slides are sometimes difficult to understand. Reading textbook is key to success and understanding in his class. Exams are difficult due to, at time of writing, short time to take exams individually (~35 mins). Has sarcastic sense of humor which is sometimes funny, sometimes intrusive to lecture.

Textbook is optional but he encourages to read along to clear any confusion but there was so much confusion. Lab is disorganized, lectures are word-heavy + overwhelming. He's a nice person, but he goes through lectures too fast + information on slides are too vague when looking at them out of class. Need to take good notes + ask questions to suceed

Bailey is a nice guy and great professor. Definitely for this class, READ THE TEXTBOOK, his lectures are good but sometimes you need a better understanding. Class is not hard unless you make it hard so do every little assignment to get your grade up. He's super accessible as well by email or before/after class. Would take his class again.

He comes off scary at first but then you pick up on his sarcasm. If you make a clear effort, he's always willing to help. He tries to give points anywhere he can. Sometimes he could be confusing when asked a question so just google it and he doesn't care. Labs are in groups. Super chill and funny guy, pretty easy lab
I enjoyed Bailey's class. He did a good job teaching the information, and his tests were similar to the knowledge checks that were posted online.

Professor Bailey is a nice guy but teaching isn't his strong suit. I found myself very confused during lectures because of the way he stated concepts. The textbook and learning curves will be your best friend in this course. His office hours are helpful though so go to them! SI sessions are also crucial.

SO, i technically didn't have him for bio 117 i had him for 117 lab but god was he amazing. He was better at teaching some topics than my actual teacher most of the time and he is so accessible and very nice! If you had trouble with anything he was willing to do the work to help you understand it so you can do the work better.

Bailey is supportive and wishes for everyone's success, but teaching might not be their strongest suit. There's an expectation to dedicate at least 15+ hours outside of class to remember the material covered. The lectures are repetitive and becomes challenging to retain and comprehend the class content.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lecture heavy', 'Accessible outside class']

comment: 5 stars for accommodation, 1 star for the way the class was run. Biochemistry with him was extremely difficult. Did not curve- most people ended with a c- to a c+ for the class. Gave you 30 minutes for each exam. Test questions were nothing like the homework. Exams actually tested your ability to extract from Google for 30 minutes

This is the class you will spend the most time on this semester. This guy seems intimidating at first but is actually a really nice prof and cares that you do well. To be honest I was so turned off by how dense the course was; you don't learn, you just spend your time studying and analyzing concepts before tests that you will not care to remember.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Lots of homework']

comment: Dr. Bailey is an amazing professor, he is very naturally smart and you can tell he cares a lot about his students doing well. He is always wanting students to come to his office hours, and he takes time before every exam to let us ask questions about topics we are confused about. He takes unfair questions off of his exams which boosts your grade!

Bailey is really cool- I think the issue lies with a 1 semester biochem course, which by nature has to be rushed. Everything is always confusing, but I feel Bailey could have done more to focus on the main ideas (which even those I didn't know). He curves so even though we all have learned nothing the grades look fine: good for GPA, bad for MCAT

Dr. Bailey was great. He gives very in depth lectures that can get confusing, but he is very accessible outside class and is always more than happy to answer any question you may have, no matter how simple. He clearly wants his students to succeed and it shows.

Dr. Bailey is the best bio professor I have had at Geneseo, mostly because he genuinely cares about the success of his students. He loves being asked questions and is very clear about what he wants students to know for exams. In order to do well in his class, you need to study for at LEAST a week beforehand and know the ins and outs of his outlines
tags: ['Accessible outside class', 'Get ready to read', 'Lecture heavy']

comment: Dr. Bailey is really knowledgeable on many aspects of Biology. He doesn't just read off the slides, but he covers a lot of information and his tests are difficult. Sometimes hes explanations for questions are too complicated to understand but he will work with you endlessly until you understand. Would highly recommend.
tags: ['Accessible outside class', 'Get ready to read', 'Test heavy']

comment: I believe Dr. Bailey is one of the smartest professor in the biology department and easily my favorite. He is a good lecturer although he can speak fast; he keeps the class involved with tophats and funny remarks. His in class book clubs make sure students read articles and come to class knowledgable. I would 100% recommend him.

Travis is the most amazing professor I have ever had, yet his exams are extremely difficult in order to live up to the standard the Geneseo Biology department prides themselves on. Yet, i urge you to take Dr. Bailey if you really want to learn Cell and have a fair chance at a good grade.

Take cell with Bailey. Easier than Hoops (but still the hardest class I've ever taken). Great man, helpful and very honest about intentions and expectations. Always asking students how he can improve lectures, not just at the end. If you put the work in (reading and the 5-6 group homeworks) then you can do well.
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'TEST HEAVY', 'GROUP PROJECTS']

comment: Dr. Bailey is a very nice guy.  He's helpful and reasonable, and gives extra credit questions on exams.  However, he is way too smart for his own good.  He doesn't explain things in a way that is easy for students to understand.  I pretty much had to teach myself the material from the textbook.  There is a lot of group homework but it isn't bad.

Cell biology with Dr. Bailey was the hardest class I have ever taken. Cell biology, however, will not be easy no matter who you take it with. I suggest Dr. Bailey greatly. He cares about his students, but is very direct. I read the textbook thoroughly and studied in every way I could. This class changed my life.

This class won't be easy. You will HAVE to attend class, read the text over and over, and review until you pass out. However it is completely worth it and you will thank yourself. Dr. Bailey is incredibly brilliant and worth taking this class with. If done right you will finish this class much smarter than when you entered

Bailey was a wonderful professor and Cell was a fascinating course. The concepts in cell aren't particularly difficult but there is SO MUCH material so success requires a lot of preparation and memorization. I only bought the essential cell textbook and I was fine and I recommend studying from the textbook, because his slides can be disorganized.

He's a good lecturer, but sometimes not clear. Office hours are great to clear up any confusion. Comes off as very intimidating, but he's actually a sweet guy who really cares about students and wants you all to do well. Only had 3 tests including the final - 2 fair and 1 hard. Definitely would take another class with him!

Again, I recommend Bailey. This was his first time teaching developmental here, so sometimes it was a bit messy, especially in regards to lab. However, he is a super fair grader and is extremely helpful in and out of class. There is a lot of material and it is very challenging. The textbook is a hot mess, but Bailey's helpfulness makes up for it.

Bailey is a really nice prof who wants his students to do well and isn't trying to trip them up. The class is difficult and there's so much material to cover that you will need to put in a lot of time if you want to get a good grade. He tries to keep the material interesting using videos and is very helpful/approachable during office hours.

Bailey is a good professor who cares about his students success. His tests were difficult.. but so is the class. He is the only cell bio professor I have heard of giving curves on exams. Study the textbook, go to office hours, d take notes in class and you will do well. Very helpful in office hours. I would definitely recommend Bailey over Hoops.

Bailey's class could be interesting, but I feel like the way he lectured made it kind of boring. His powerpoints usually either had no writing or too much writing to copy down. He's really good on taking student feedback though so I'm sure this will improve. Tests were difficult and you were never really certsin what would be on them.

Dr. Bailey's class was difficult but manageable. I did not put an extreme amount of effort in and got a decent grade. Use the textbook, follow his power points and know the learning objectives on the unit sheets. Very nice guy and very fair.

Though Bailey's teaching style is one of a kind, it kind of works. As long as you follow what he covers in lecture and his explicit learning objectives you will do fine. Tests are doable if you study well with a heavy reliance on the textbook- especially tables and figures. The final was a challenge. I recommend him

Good guy but boring. Spoke very fast, couldn't understand enough info during class. More useful to read the textbook than go to class. Good at responding to student feedback. Group hws relatively easy (grade boosters), exams insane, never knew what was on them. Frequently gave misinformation about exams. Reviews were more confusing than helpful.

Attendance is mandatory for this class even though the material on tests (by which there are very few and grades are heavily weighted on) is not from lecture. The tests are extremely difficult even if you have read the required textbook material. The time limit on tests is outrageous (35 mins and 70 questions). Nice, funny guy, not a good teacher.
tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Test heavy']

comment: One of the worst professor's I've ever had. Says he has office hours but never tells you the days or times. Comes to class late every single day. Is harsh about attendance. Lectures have nothing to do with exams except for the countries name, harsh grader on the final paper. Media journals are easy 100s, some of the exams can be found on quizlet.

He is an incredibly nice man and his lectures are interesting to go to. With that being said he can be lazy. He has told us that his lectures add "flavor" to the textbook but for the first exam neglected to tell us what we needed to read in the book until the day before. Exams are online and incredibly nitpicky and has many questions that are wrong

Tests are online and completely based on the textbook. As long as you have the textbook open in front of you, you should have all the answers. Media journals are an easy A as long as you do them. Final paper is time consuming but straightforward. His classes aren't really helpful but he's funny and he has an attendance policy so you should prob go.

All tests are online and come directly from the textbook. Virtually nothing you learn in lecture will be on the tests, but if you read through the chapter and keep the book open during tests you will be good. Lazy guy, which makes it easy to get a good grade.

Dr. P has a good personality. He cares a lot about attendance, and threatens to take points off FINAL grade for every absence. He tries to have interesting lectures and up to date references, even though most of the test info comes form the book. He's a lenient grader on writing assignments. The course load is fair, and can be an easy A .

Not very helpful, when I went to his office hours he just gave me the answer key and didn't explain anything. Tests are hard and he is very unclear in class. If you miss class, he will call you out for it and gives dirty looks at students all class. Would not recommend

Very nice person. Funny and friendly. Sometimes his lecture is not very clear, but he provides powerpoint so it is helpful. Go to his office hour, it defin helps. Review powerpoint, do hw, and review quizzes, you will get good grade.

Such a nice guy, but not clear at all in his lessons. The homeworks simply involve copying his answer key into an excel document. You learn nothing in his class, even if you pay attention. Class was very dry and his organization was horrendous. We never stuck to the syllabus and due dates were unclear.

Could not have been easier.  Would not call it a joke because you actually learn but if you get less than an A- you are doing something wrong.  His accent is sometimes hard to understand, but will clear anything up during office hours.  Also one of the nicest people you will come across.  Definitely recommend.

Professor Zook herself is a very kind person but her classes however are boring and they feel like an eternity. The class is so easy and it is very easy to get an A some parts of the lectures are interesting but most are on going and boring. Lots of note taking during class so you don't really need the textbook. Few quizzes and assignments 3 exams

Dr. Zook was a pretty good professor in my opinion. The class was really easy as long as you studied for the tests and did the homework. The only thing is that her lectures can be boring sometimes, but she is a really nice person.

I think this class is very easy if you go to class and look over the exam review sheets she hands out. Those literally tell you essentially what will be on the tests. The only thing is that the lectures are BEYOND BORING. I think this class would be sm better if the classes were 50 minutes, but oh well. But she's nice and I would take her again.

Psychology of Money course was super interesting and I learned a lot. Need to read before each class and she is heavy on discussion and in class assignments. Overall, great professor wish I took more of her classes.

comment: Zook is one of my favs at genny. Good personality in the classroom, HW responses to short articles on a regular basis but take little effort to complete and are an easy A. Study for tests and you'll do well.

Zook wasn't the absolute worst but the class itself has 4 test grades and a few 1 page writing assignments and thats pretty much it besides these in class assingments she does to take attendance. If you show up and take notes then you should do fine but her lectures can get boring and drag on.

Dr. Zook is a good professor. However, the class is lecture based and if you don't go to class you won't know what's going on considering she doesn't post the notes and there isn't a textbook. The tests are fair but you need to study.
