comment: His lectures are a little boring but if you read the mycourses articles and cite a bunch in your papers and write mediocre papers youll do fine

At first I couldn't stand the guy, but once you get past his dry lectures and monotonous voice, he's actually a really good professor.  Extremely clear on what he expects; tests are based on study guides but do have short answer.  Essays are dissertation style, but he will help you through them to achieve what he is truly asking for.  Boring & good

This was my least favorite class. Sitting through his lectures twice a week was painful because he was so boring. He is a nice teacher but is so dull. You have three test a semester but I suggest writing the optional essay instead because it is much easier than the test. Going to his class was so depressing.

Not a hard class but I think he expects a little too much from an intro 100 class. somewhat harsh of a grader on the essays but tests are very easy as long as you study the study sheet he gives which has ALL the info on the test. Attendance doesn't matter all his slides are online and the pop quizzes are extra credit. Pretty boring class though.

Really cool guy. I actually enjoyed going to his class. Lectures are a bit bland, but I mean, it's math. Make sure to work with people, ask him questions and use the textbook for the labs. There are 40 points worth of labs (3 points/lab) and 20 points for 3 exams. I didn't pay attention in class, but studied for the last two exams and got an A.

He is literally the easiest teacher for Soc Stats. The labs he gives is 40% of your grade and they're easy to get 100% considering you can ask him questions while doing them and compare with the whole class. Tests are like the practice tests. I don't pay attention as well as I should and I've missed classes being sick and still obtained an A.

He is a nice professor and tries to communicate clearly yet sometimes how he explains things gets lost in translation. I think for an Intro to Sociology class, it maybe goes too far into depth about the advanced theories and their origins. You really have to pay attention to begin to understand how the things he is saying connect back to sociology.

Its an introductory level class and he makes it extremely boring and you have to put in so much work. He is nice guy but the amount of work you have to do for his class is way overboard and extremely boring. He only grades you on three exams so if you do bad on one of them your grade is screwed. I wish I dropped the class when I had the chance.

This class is way different then expected, and was going to immediately drop it if it wasn't how interesting and intelligent McLaughlin was. I took this class because he's such an AMAZING professor. I learned more in my entire career. Hard if you don't understand but worth it. A plus in my book. Thank you professor.

He's a great guy, but the class is very boring. He gives pop quizzes 3 times a semester, but it's up to 8 extra points on your overall GPA (motivation to attend!). The entire grade is based on tests, but he is a generous grader and an even nicer guy. Also, the books are a boring read. Not the funnest class, but McLaughlin is fine.

McLaughlin is a great professor. He sets a date in which students turn in drafts of their papers. Its not mandatory, but extremely helpful. He will actually look through it and give you feedback. I honestly say I learned in his class, and I can't say that about many professors.

TAKE this professor.  Paul is one of the kindest and most interesting teachers i have ever had. if you actually do his work and are interested in the class the tests are really quite easy. he shows you interesting ways of thinking about the world and allows you to expand on important concepts

DO NOT take a class with him. He makes a simple 100 level class unnecessarily difficult, boring, and frustrating. He forces his opinions on you and argues with his students. He actually aims to piss you off. AVOID AT ALL COSTS! I went to every class and killed myself for a B...trust me, don't take McLaughlin. Go with Wahlstrom, or any other prof.

I've taken two classes with him.  Socl 102 was really interesting.  Tons of reading, 2 tests, 1 paper, and extra credit quizzes.   Socl 335 is boring for the first 2/3 of the course but the end is really interesting.  Tons of reading and writing (4 Papers).  Nice guy but not the easiest professor.

What's with the negative comments? Great professor! Tons of reading but manageable, and very interesting material. Tests aren't bad and one essay. If you actually want to learn something worthwhile, take this class! Very smart, has very good ideas that he's excited to share. Will make you a better person. Maybe.

Flies through power points so you can't write everything down in time. Has questions on things not talked about in class. Out of class essay (required) was graded extremely harshly because I didn't mention his favorite case study. Assigns a lot of reading which is required. Makes his opinion clear and constantly interrupts students
his lectures were so boring the readings were intense, and in the papers he just wanted to hear his own opinions. but always with a smile.

Absolutely the most tedious and mind numbing experience of my life. His irrefutable and self-focused grading policy did not allow much leeway for those who did not agree with his opinion.  Some of the texts were horribly written and almost unbearable to sit through.
I think everyone in my class had an A for Speech! He's such a great guy.

I don't personally like the way he taught Soc 100, but I feel like I'd enjoy him as a teacher in a different setting teaching a different topic. You could easily never go to class and still wind up with an A as long as you do some of the readings and study the review sheet he posts before every exam.

I think that he was a good teacher generally speaking. I'd take this INTD class over again, just makes use you go to him for comments on each of your essays so that you know exactly what he thinks is wrong, and if you do what he says and correct it you'll probably do well in the class. Don't miss more than 2 classes or it drags down your grade.
Tends to shoot down everything you say and assigns dense readings without explaining them well. Plays Devil's Advocate to everything, which gets very irritating.
Celia is great! super passionate about what she does and is hilarious as well. This was her last class that she was teaching before retiring, I'm so glad I got to take a class with her.

comment: The most amazing professor I've ever had in Geneseo. Her Austen class is a MUST. She is so quirky & lovely and makes class so interesting, wonderful, and entertaining. Her heart is made of gold too and she is so sweet and understanding. Very fair and generous grader & will do anything to help, even if busy. I will miss her dearly after graduation.

Celia Easton is an incredible professor. And while this class is not an easy A, it is not terribly difficult to get one if you actually get involved with the class. She is very humorous and kind, and offers real-world applications for the texts we read. If she is offering a class, I would snatch the opportunity!!

An excellent professor! She really knows her stuff and she has a great sense of humor. The class is a bit difficult because of the required material, but she's a fair grader and gives fantastic lectures. If you can take HUMN with her, do it!

Very condescending-if you don't agree with her, you're wrong. Had to read every book carefully and discuss it tirelessly. Useless comments on papers-not much room for creativity in writing. Didn't explain the final exam fully and most of the class came unprepared. Hard exam-made us quote from every book. Stay away if you have a brain or an opinion.
A very tough but fair grader, she is smart and witty and will not be BSed. An excellent professor who knows what she's doing, and more importantly, knows how to teach it.
deep, funny, stimulating, down to earth yet challenging

I graduated from Geneseo in 2001, but wanted to add my comments about Prof. Easton because she's great! She explains everything very clearly, and is a fair grader. If you put the effort in, you will enjoy the class and get a decent grade!

Amazing professor. Delivers a perfect balance of historical perspective and unique ideas. She has a very dry sense of humor which I absolutely fell in love with from the first day of class. Paper topics can involve fair amounts of creative writing and are infinitely more interesting than the essay in place of which I'm writing this review. *sigh*

Celia Easton was an absolutely amazing professor.  She had a wonderful grasp of the subject matter and was a lot more down-to-earth than other professors of her intellectual calabre.  Definitely not an easy A, though.  Then again, few courses at Geneseo are.

She's very challenging, but she makes you want to put forth nothing but your very best. She might be the most brilliant person I have ever met. She's hilarious but doesn't know how funny she actually is, which makes it great.

i dont know what the deal is with you guys but reading is not the end all be all in this class. i think its the difference between an A and a B, unless you dont know how to write at all. bull**** is an art that even easton can appreciate.

Have to read, of course, good class discussions, very interesting and interested.  Personally, I loved her, though I didn't read as much as I should have.  Oh, and she likes people who are involved in class discussions.
She's very helpful and actually interesting to listen to. Theres only so much you can discuss a book and she does it righ to the right level. No over analyzing. Overall a good choice.

she is the only teacher i don't ever block out with daydreams. her lectures are really interesting and she has a great sense of humor if you pay attention. she is very helpful with improving your writing. she's great.

You definately have to read.  She makes fun interesting some times but most of the time its not all that exciting, but not painfully boring.  tests arn't too bad as long as you read.  fair grader on papers.  i'd take her again.

I graduated from Geneseo in 1996, and I still remember Dr. Easton as being the best professor I have ever had.  She is truly wonderful, and knows her stuff inside and out. I would go back to school just to be in her classes again. I highly recommend her!
class is interesting, she's very excited about her job!! interactive, not just lectures, so you really should read for class.
Her lectures are interesting, her tests are pretty easy (if you study), but her papers are killer.  No lie, she is awful at grading them..
she's great
great with senior seminars.  very, very willing to work with students.
She gives great practice tests, and you don't really have to do the reading
Very helpful and knowledgeable. There were only two tests, but her reviews were always fair and she wants you to succeed!
Went through a ton of material way too fast and is a harsh grader. The exams as well as the cumulative final were weighted so much its almost impossible to pass.

comment: She teaches way to fast and isn't fair with the test at all.

Honestly the best professor I had all semester. She is great when it comes to office hours and just wants you to succeed. Has quizzes every week but they are just to make sure you are progressing. Attendance is mandatory but you can attend online. She is great, love her and her class.

This professor is straight forward and will work with you if you put the work in and participate. If you try you will do fine and this class was really not that bad. Just keep up and don't skip class!
Hated this class. There is 2 exams and they are very heavily weighted. Weekly take home quizzes that barely effect your grade. Very nice just not my favorite. Attendance is a grade.

Birgit is a good professor except she teaches really fast and does some of the math in her head. She does not grade easily but is very understandable about attendance and being on zoom. She doesn't give a lot of work but she gives enough and it is hard.

She does a good job preparing us for calc, it really does feel like a high school environment though. Weekly quizzes are worth a lot and there are only 2 exams and the final. Some extra assignments and handouts here and there. There is a review presentation but it's easy and worth 5% of the overall grade. Free online textbook, use a regular calc.

Highly recommend this class for a Gen ed! Fairly easy and interesting if you enjoy music. Kimball is very knowledgable and passionate about what he teaches. Course consisted of lectures and CD listening. No homework, just tests and listening quizzes. Study a lot outside of class to do well on the tests and quizzes. Offers a lot of extra credit.

Lectures are very boring, but he's a nice guy and very knowledgeable. He is an easy grader, and the listening quizzes aren't that hard if you study. There's a textbook, but we barely discussed it in class. Attendence is taken sporadically. My only complaint is that the lectures are really boring, and he isn't very organized.
Prof Kimball is super sweet and passionate about what he teaches. You do have to teach yourself some of the material, but the class is overall very interesting.

The workload is super heavy. If you're not a music major and just taking it for outside credits, it's really not an easy A. You have to spend a ton of time memorizing and preparing for the quizzes which are 100% of your grade. Although sweet, he is a very boring lecturer and doesn't really help you learn the content through class.

Professor Kimball is an absolute sweetheart that knows how to play every single instrument in that classroom. If you're looking for a music credit, an easy A, or just something for fun, definitely take this class. You will have to attend a few concerts (I think 5) and there 6 quizzes for the semester. It's a bit of memorization, but the same format

Professor Kimball is easily in my top 3 of favorite professors at Geneseo. He is the absolute sweetest man, and cares deeply for his work. He will have the nicest and in-depth conversations with his students when they want to talk to him. This class and Professor Kimball made me realize how much I loved Music, and missed it from high school.
Professor Kimball might be one of my favorite professors I've ever had at Geneseo. His quizzes aren't bad and he is the nicest man you will ever meet. Very passionate about what he does. Love him.

Although this class was a little difficult, I loved Professor Kimball. He is a very sweet old man, and it is very clear that he loves his job and what he teaches. His class was interesting and I enjoyed talking with him about my family traditions. If you take his class be sure to study for his listening quizzes or you will most definitely fail.

Dr. Kimball is a really nice guy. If you're interested in something he's teaching, take it. He can ramble in his lectures and sometimes you'll have no idea what's going on. Listening quizzes can be tough at first, but they aren't too demanding since he usually picks easy songs. Just listen to the songs he gives you and go to class and you'll pass

Withdrew after the first quiz because I knew I failed miserably. He talks about nothing important for the first half of his lectures then MIGHT get to something pertinent. You need one book from the bookstore and one from main street. You have to put a lot of effort into memorizing artist names and titles of songs. Really boring class.

comment: Kimball is probably one of the smartest people on this campus. His class is fun and he's a cute grandpa type but sometimes can be boring. Take if you're good with memorization.

He's a cute old man that can play basically every instrument ever but be prepared to study. He gives out study guides so you know exactly what to expect but tests cover a lot of content. Listening quizzes can be tricky but once you get the hang of studying for them you'll be okay. Don't procrastinate reviewing for a test till the night before.

Check mycourses for format of listening quizzes. Tests are all multiple choice and TF, pretty easy. Study for a few hours before quizzestests and should do fine. Don't really need to go to class. Class is more or less just watching youtube videoslistening to him talk.

I love Professor Kimball! He is very passionate about music! He makes the class interesting. He can play an assortment of instruments. I highly recommend it!

Class is pretty boring because kimball just goes on and on about randoms stuff but you should go because the notes you take are exactly what the quizzes are on. Quizzes are hard so make sure you study and memorize everything. Easy class if you go to class and study.

He is an amazing teacher who is quirky and really funny at times. He's very intelligent and you can tell he really loves his job. I would recommend him to anyone that wanted to take one of his classes. Very sweet guy.

My partner in a group project didn't contribute, I had to do it all by myself and ended up getting a zero for "a lack of communication" and "not following directions" despite the fact that I communicated with my partner best I could, and informed Professor Krumrine of the issue.

Dr. Krumrine is generally nice, but her lectures can be very boring and she gets side tracked. I really struggle with the exams and then the final was very long. Plus your required to complete 4 labs. And a discussion post weakly.
Get good grades on exams and labs. Open book tests

Amazing lady, all her classes she teaches are regimented in the same way so no surprises. She's very understanding only flaw really is that she can be disorganized sometimes. Tests you want to spend a few days studying for and attend class and take notes. Awesome lady

She is a lovely person. Her lectures are just her talking. I'd recommend taking notes and recording the lectures. Not much information on the slides. Exams are on her lectures. She lets you use notes for exams, but she might change that. Do not use AI in her class.

comment: Have had her twice so far, thank god I don't have her again. Her lectures are very dense, & the tests are kinda rough. The class average for exams was in the 70s range. Krumrine has a great class to fulfill WRTG105 credit. If you are interested in anthropology you'll enjoy. Since it is a writing class there are 5 main papers, but gives easy points to get your grade up if writing isn't your thing. Accssesible and gives good feedback, she's very kind and passionate.

comment: Prof. Krumrine is very nice and enjoys educating students on human growth and development.  She gives engaging lectures and relates them to personal experiences and examples.  There is a lot of reading required for this course that are needed for the tests.  The exams contain too much to answer sufficiently in the class period.

It was hard for me to do well with her teaching style as she just lectures everyday. Although class is not mandatory and she does post the slides not all the information is on the slides so you have to go to class and actually listen to her. Exams are open note but so hard to finish in the time slot. A lot of information for a 100 class.

Not much teaching is done over intersession- all prerecorded lectures dated from Covid.  Tests are based off reading and open notes, but too lengthy to complete in time adequately.  Additionally there was a group presentation, which can be difficult to make work over intersession.  I would suggest taking this course in person.

I took this class because I wanted to learn about the history of apes but boy did I regret my decision. Discussion posts were so boring to read and respond to and you had one every week. The tests were impossible to finish in time even though its open note. Labs were also graded harshly. If you are looking for a fun elective, this isn't one.

Prof. Krumrine is wonderful, this was the perfect intro course! Her class is laid out in a great way and she is so responsive to emails! Her class requires readings and lectures that are 100% necessary to do well in the class, don't skip these! Exams are long, but if you pay attention to readings, lectures and films each week you'll do well!

comment: I really enjoyed having Dr. Krumrine for anth 202 this past semester! There's definitely a good amount of homework every week, so you have to stay on top of assignments. I took this class as a freshman, so the workload was a little bit of a shock, but honestly if you attend all of her lectures and take notes, you can get a good grade.
such a queen. only problem is her tests are very lengthy and even though they are open notes there is barely enough time to complete them with the essay questions at the end.

Dr. Krumrine definitely knows what she's talking about. That said, in my class, she focused more on her personal research and would often have to rush through the lecture slides. The tests were extremely difficult even though they were open notes, and most people in my class would run out of time. She is difficult to reach via email.

Love her, this class was super easy. Tests are all open notes and online but pay attention in class, she doesn't always have everything written out on the slides so get ready to take notes. She is also super easy to get a hold of outside of class and responds quick if you need her help.

comment: Easy class.The tests were a bit lengthy but they were all online and open notes, the weekly discussion posts were graded on completion so all you need to do is remember to complete them. Professor Krumrine does a great job teaching. She explains her lectures very well and makes it easy for students to understand the material. I completely forgot to do half of her mandatory discussion posts for the year, and I still got out with a C+. Easy class, but you won't do well unless you go to the majority of classes.
She is a girlboss queen
really love professor Krumrine, her lectures are very interesting and theres a discussion post every week

Dr. Krumine is a very nice professor. Too many reading that take a lot of time to read them all for a weekly discussion board. Need to know readings for test. comment: Tests were way too long to complete within 1hr 15 min (25mc, 5 short answer paragraphs, and essay). Lectures the entire time and they are not very engaging. Some stuff said in class is on exams but you will not find in the powerpoint notes on canvas. Weekly homeworks are very time consuming and do not count for as much of your grade as they should

Her class was not too difficult. I did not do so well because of my own personal reasons. comment: I personally really enjoyed Professor Krumrines class. She is very attentive and accessible after class. She goes out of her way to ensure everyone is working to the best of their abilities. I believe anyone who has her would enjoy their experience. Shes a real gem. Especially towards the end of the semester

She has powerpoint slides that she gives to you but the best way to pass the class is to go and write down what she says during lecture (if you print out the notes). She was really nice and understanding. Easy to boost your grade if you read the materials that the one-minute papers are on.

This class is Forensic Anthropology and this is where she shines. She is truly engaged in this topic and knows what shes talking about. The class was super fun with all the labs and projects. comment: Dr. Krumrine is possibly my favorite professor of all time! She is so passionate about her field and really makes you feel super intrigued to learn more. She is also very clear and does not, whatsoever make you feel stupid if you do not understand something. I took this class online, although it was a lot of work I highly recommend.

Dr. Krumrine is one of the best professors I have had at Geneseo! She is extremely knowledgeable, considerate, and helpful. Her lectures are interesting and engaging, too! She gives great feedback on assignments. I look forward to doing research with her in the spring!

Her class was nice because I took it online during the summer and I felt an adrenaline rush of getting an A. It's a lot harder than it seems. Some good advice is to practice writing quickly and the second question is really important. You can lost a few points from that.

She is not bad but very boring. You have to attend classes because her power-points are just picture based so you can't study them without taking notes in class. She makes her classes harder than they have to be.

comment: If your looking for any easy INTD class her class is it. There are five papers for the semester. For each one you have to do an outline and draft. Each paper is peer reviewed and reviewed by her before you do the final. She will sometimes go of on a tangent during class which can be annoying. Overall she is nice and wants us to do well.

Extremely difficult. not because of the content but because if you miss five seconds of her lecture you run the risk of dying on the exams. 2 tests, gruelingly specific mult choice and 6 essays in a matter of 1hr and 15mins. never had to do so much work in my life. MUST go to class b/c its all talking and ppts have no words for the most part.

She's very down to earth and kind. Had somewhat of a hard time in this class because I never knew exactly what to study. Her lectures are somewhat long and dragged out. Easy project at the end of the semester (partner up), and super easy writing assignments!

This class was pretty interesting, especially the readings and films. The lectures  were sometimes confusing and didn't convey too much actual information, but overall the class was enjoyable.  Krumrine is very caring and helpful and is willing to work with you with any issues. Relatively easy grading and not too much outside work.

Absolutely horrible. No interesting content during lectures, useless powerpoints, gets off track, doesn't explain assignments. 300-level  amount of work for a 200-level class. Relatively easy grader, but it's not worth it.

Her lecture slides were just the important definitions from the textbook, and a lot of random pictures. If you read the books you don't really need lecture to pass the tests, and if you go to lecture you don't really need to read the books. Easy A if you read the slides/books, the material is really just common sense dressed up in terminology.

Overall not a terrible or mean professor, but takes up to 2 weeks to grade tests and sometimes even 1-minute papers. I understand that professors have lives, but they also have jobs and that is unacceptable laziness.

She is a really nice person, but very boring, her tests had horrible wording and 2 answers...i studied and knew all the material but the wording made it hard to do well, however, the short papers and project are great grade boosters! she really is supportive and nice...not bad at all...read the books

I was excited about taking physical anth and she completely ruined it.  I'm doing fine but I hate going. The questions on her tests are badly worded as if she purposefully tries to make it hard to understand what she means.   Also, she talks about her step kids all the time.  If there is a way to use them as an example, she does. Obnoxious.

I thought Professor Krumrine was great.  Class was kind of boring because she would drone on a bit, but I loved her as a person. She was very nice and helpful if you went to discuss and edit your papers with her, and even great for little non-academic chats.  You have to be a good writer to do well in the class, though.

I thought this was going to be a very interesting class, but it was a complete anthro lesson.  She is rather boring and pretty unorganized. There is alot less work than other INTDs only 5 short papers. She is a pretty easy grader but you have to write exactly as she wants.  She makes it hard to do well if you don't go to her office hours.
Shes just incredibly vanilla in every aspect. It would be easier to hate her if she was a bad professor, but shes not. Shes just so INCREDIBLY vanilla it hurts. Classes are boring but easy.

Classes can be very boring, she can be unclear at times. If you read the books, you should do alright. Focuses more on main points than specifics in the books, which makes it better. Nice lady, but not the greatest prof. I don't recommend her, but don't not recommend her.

classes are very boring, no need to really attend just because she posts all her ppt online before class.  Exams are difficult if you dont read the novels or know termonology. Goes off on tangents about her family a lot during lecture.

Wow, If you want someone to grade fair dont take her.  Its a complete Anthro lesson, My writing didnt improve. I had A's in all other classes but this because of how hard she graded.  She genuinely tries to be nice and everything, but its tough to take.  This was the whole class's opinion too. FYI she is Prof. Pacheco's wife.
Knows her anthropology, very helpful and nice, is a great teacher, good grader, grading style identical to pacheco's for tests.

Just a great guy. I didn't really pay attention in class or do any of the ungraded homeworks and still managed to do well on the exams. If you pay attention and show up to class and understand it I'm sure you would get an easy A. The exams were always just multiple choice and never no more than 35 questions. Most of the content is common sense <333

He's pretty tough on attendance. He was fair to me in the end though. I was graduating and failing his class. He told me what I needed to get on the final exam to get a C. He was very fair and helpful. I skipped to many classes, so falling behind was my fault

He's a very nice man with a hilarious demeanor. He pretty much teaches to the test but reading the definitions for each chapter in the book is helpful. However if you want to learn practical application for finance you might want a more challenging professor.

6 quizzes, drops lowest. Doesn't change them much from past years. 2 tests with short answer problemsmultiple choice, not too hard. Sort of cumulative final but not really. A few case study projects but they're easy. A lot of financial calculator use so need one of those and need to be good with it. Kind of an air head but really good guy.

Good professor sometimes forgets what he's saying but otherwise explains things pretty well. The material is a little difficult at sometimes but as long as you read the chapters and go to class you'll be fine.

This guy is straight up the man,   I laugh at least 5 times a class.  It's not necessarily verbal jokes but just his general demeanor kills me.  Class is easy, straightforward stuff.  He goes over the homework which is extremely useful.  TAKE HIM

Spends a lot of classes reviewing last class' materials.  Ask questions just because you want to change the pace. This class is one of the least demanding 300 level electives, esp. if you have taken 311 or Econ courses.  What a great guy, easy to talk to, funny.  Just make eye contact, you never know when that golf swing is gonna get ya.
love dr. schinski

This guy is Permanently stuck in slow motion.  A hell of a guy demanding a fairly light work load.  Class was a breeze.  He is one of those people that will make you canstantly laugh by watching him.  Good luck.  FORE...
I took like 4 classes with Professor Schinski. He was possibly the best teacher I had at Geneseo. Just watch out for his golf swing when he is thinking about a question.
nice guy. willing to help. good teacher
great
She's is vivacious, kind and helpful. Her accent is just beautiful. Need to attend class if you want to do well. A lot of homework...

Edgar passed away but he wasn't called the American Socrates for nothing. You were on-track in thinking better after his classes which combined a lot of close reading, open discussion, and research opportunities. Offered first independent class on Objectivism and interdisciplinary HUM. Check out his logic texts and student notes. They're classics.
The best philosophy professor.  If all philosophy professors are great and he's a philosophy professor, then he's great!
the best professor i had at geneseo, changed my life

I wish i had taken a class with him when he was in his prime.  Dr. Edgar is a great guy, and you can learn a lot from him in and outside the class.  It's sometimes hard to hear what he's saying, but if you ask him to explain something he'll gladly help you.  Truly a class act.
obviously a brilliant guy
He's an excellent professor and a great guy.  If you want to do well, just attend his TAs review sessions.
No Comments
One of the best professors I ever had!

The lectures his gives in class are completely unecessary and quite boring, but you get participation points for grade by just being there and listening. The papers are hard sometimes but he is as easy grader, you just have to think.
You have to REALLY listen to what he's saying, but always willing to help, whether it be with class, personal stuff, or choosing professors, and is always very honest.
He's a nice guy, but he should retire by now. I can't understand what he's saying most of the time.
He is incredibly passionate about his work and cares about his students. Pop quizzes weekly about lecture content.

comment: such a fun guy who made class engaging and informative. hope to take another one of his classes again
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Hilarious', 'Beware of pop quizzes']

comment: One of the sweetest professors Ive ever had. Weekly pop quizzes aka random online quiz that you need to do within 24 hours easy if you use ctrl+F on your *free* textbooks. There is a participation grade but I *never* went to class and still got an 85 (85 was the lowest grade he gave on participation as well). Easy A, great understanding prof.

I took Politics of Genocide with Professor Grace, and it was one of the most interesting classes I've ever taken. He's an engaging, intelligent, and very competent professor without losing any of his humor and general laid back attitude. If you can take a class with him, I highly recommend.

Very animated and lively. Keeps your attention and even though he is not a doctor, he has a lot of experience in his field. He is funny and entertaining. He really really knows what he is talking about and is great at teaching it. Only downfall was that he spoke very quickly, I would recommend typing notes in this class.

This was one of my favorite classes! Prof Grace made the class interesting and entertaining, however it is not an easy A. You must take extensive notes in his class and read a lot. Def would recommend!!

2 tests (40%), 2 papers (40%), 10 pop quizzes (20%). Grace is a morning person. 4 question quizzes consist of 3 hilarious pointless questions, one about an obscure current event you probably havent heard about. I really enjoyed the class until we started talking about IMF, World Bank etc., as his views lean toward Free Market, made me cringe a bit

Very passionate about this class. He will make you laugh in class, and he shares a lot of personal experiences that relate to the material that you're studying. He made our second paper optional. Make sure you pay attention in class, and take notes on the textbook (which is homework). Pop quizzes ?/4 points every class. Lots of reading.

Professor Grace is wonderful, and his class is my favorite one so far! His lectures are great, he goes super in depth and is very personable. However, the class comes with a lot of homework so be prepared. Each week has a chapter from the textbook assigned plus two or three outside source readings. 10 pop quizzes per semester, 2 exams, and 2 papers
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES']

comment: I took PLSC 140 with Grace as well and had a great time but Failed States with him was the best decision I've ever made. I'm getting an  average grade in it and I'm super proud of it because I've worked for it while simultaneously learning so much. If you ever get the chance to take it, do it. You won't regret it!

The best lectures and everything you need for studying purposes will be covered during class. Two easy tests (if you study), two papers, and random reading quizzes will be the basis for your grade, so I wouldn't skip class because you never know whether he'll give a quiz or not. Grace wants you to do well, so put in the work when necessary!
I love prof. Grace! He's so funny and smart! you can really tell he knows what he's talking about. 10/10 highly recommend.

Very knowledgeable about the field of international politics.  His lectures are entertaining, even with dry material. He gave pop quizzes, but most of them were jokes just to give us easy points. Uses only online readings so no textbook. Perhaps he's tougher on his upper level classes, but this class was pretty easy. Take him for 140 if you can.

Wouldn't have wanted to take international politics with any other professor! Lectures are kind of fast and he sometimes loses his initial thought, but will clarify if you ask. Don't let pop quizzes scare you, you'll grow to love them. Just go to class. Really humorous and engaging, everyone I know really enjoyed his class.

Great lecturer, but very one dimensional.  You will have a hard time keeping up and taking notes, as he talks fast and doesn't keep it simple.  He is knowledgeable and very demanding.  Has too many additional readings that are never available until the day of class or the night before.  Do not expect him to do anything but talk.  Rely on the book.

Grace is my favorite professor in the department! He is very helpful and explains things in a way that makes them click. He is very intelligent but not condescending in the slightest. Very approachable. makes class exciting even when you've been in school all day (night class). He expects a lot though and is a tough grader. Strongly recommend him!
One of the best professors I've ever had. He's intelligent, witty, and engaging. It's a lot of reading and studying, but totally worth it.

My favorite professor in the entire college. He is a really brilliant person and an asset to the school. He has worked abroad in so many countries which makes this class so worthwhile. There is a lot of reading but all you need to know is the main points in them. Take home final and awesome Model UN sessions. I recommend this to IR/PLSC or anybody
the worst professor i ever had. He rambles in tangents and you never learn anything.
Hilarious, brilliant, and fun guy to have as a teacher. Very intuitive, makes sense, really worth going to class. =)

Great teacher, great guy. Class is entertaining and interesting. Easy A but still pushes you to work hard. The reading is really interesting and do-able. He has lots of real world experience which is just friggin awesome. Everyone loves him!

140 should ONLY be taken with Grace. He excels at teaching international systemic theories quite different from is own in an unbiased informative manner that helps students classify their own political ideologies. He makes class fun and interesting, and forces you to learn how to take good notes QUICKLY. What a great Professor....

At first glance, he is a great lecturer, keeping the class captivated. However, he talks fast, to the point that if you stop to either jot something down, or merely think about something he's said, you are lost. He also goes off on complete tangents. It is impossible to keep complete notes. Make sure you buddy up for notes, or you will fail.
love him. best professor thus far. don't even think twice about taking his class. do it=]

Greatest prof I have had at Geneseo to date. Enthusiastic about material with a lot of real life experience to back him up. Very interesting lecturer and worth waking up for at 8:30. GO TO CLASS though. He tends to give VERY easy quizzes when a lot of the class is absent so really rewards you showing up.

His loud voice will keep you awake(most of the time) and he is very knowledgeable and experienced in the field. There's no written assignment, but you will be quizzed on the material every other class. Tests are pretty easy because he does a good review and you also have to write two papers. Overall, great professor and also pleasant to look at.

Wow. Where do I start? More specifically, where should I should with him and his "Ethiopian Coffee"? At 8:30 AM, he just has energy I wouldn't have, but it totally wakes me up. He seriously knows what he's talking about. The quizzes... yeah. Come to class and you will definitely just love his quizzes.

My best professor in college so far. Extremely experienced and knowledgeable in International Affairs. For IR and PLSC majors you will probably learn more in Goekel's class. For fulfilling the core req. it is a great class. Paper and tests are extremely easy. He spells out what will be on the test in a review session. Quizzes make class required.

Very interesting guy. One of the most energetic and fun professors I have had, and extremely intelligent to boot. He swears CONSTANTLY though, which is totally unprofessional. so far he has said the f-word 15 times. i think he thinks its funny, but really, it can get to be excessive and annoying. besides that great guy.tough tests but learned a lot
My favorite professor.  His energy in the classroom and ability to talk with (not at) students about class material makes him the best.

Easy class if you are at all interested in Political Science/International Relations. He is also an awesome professor; he teaches concisely, knows what he's talking about, and acts like a human (aka he has a soul).

This class is mad easy as long as you read, show up for class, and care about int'l relations. grace is an excellent lecturer, and the books he assigns for papers are semi-interesting to boot. best part about him is the career advice he can give because he's already been all over the world and done tons of stuff.

this class was not easy. True, he has ALOT of ENERGY and is an AWESOME lecturer, but his tests were hard/confusing, lots of reading, and lots of pop quizzes, good if you are a poly sci major but if you are just taking core try to get an easier prof. Because of this class and the amount of stress and work I am no longer a poly sci minor

Great prof.  International politics is not my area, but I loved his class.  He is so hilarious, I deffinitly want at least one more class with him before I graduate.  He is amazing, he has so much enery.  Even at 8:30 AM he is engaging, and has sooooo much knowledge, and is so active in world politcs.  Highly recommended!

terrific prof, is very engaging and knowledgable.  plus, he tells it like it is thanks to his real world experience.  he's also great during office hors, and is willing to read countless essay drafts and advise on career plans.
Great prof. Highly recommended.

A completely hilarious and crazy man! You can't possibly fall asleep in his class, he has so much energy and puts so much emphasis on certain words; it's great- he practically runs around the classroom. Moves quickly in lecture, so take good notes and go to class for pop quizzes.
GREAT GUY, FUNNY TOO. HE'S REALLY HELPFUL AND SEEMS TO KNOW WHAT HE'S TALKING ABOUT.AND I LIKE HEARING HIM TALK ABOUT HIS WORK IN THE UN

a very cool guy. very laid back atmosphere. you'll get out of class early almost everytime.  the essay topics might seem intimidating but he explains exactly what he is expecting and it very helpful.  he actually reads the papers carefully and makes a ton of comments on how it could have been improved. definitely a great guy.
Great teacher; full of energy and enthusiasm. You won't regret taking any course with him, be careful to not be intimidated; he knows more than you can imagine
This class is tougher than lower levels with him but still very doable

Very intelligent, knows his stuff, but sometimes expects the students to know just as much as he does.  Often talks fast and gives funny looks if you don't quite get something that he thinks you should.  Amazingly interesting and not bad to look at either.
Challenging but interesting and fun class. Reading material was difficult, papers were complex questions you had to answer with strict limits in maximum words used.

One of the most interesting profs there are. He works for the UN so he definitely knows what he's talking about + he's very passionate about what he teaches. Great guy, really funny and entertaining. A pretty easy grader too. I'm glad I got to take his class! For quizzes make sure to learn names.

Very intelligent and laid back, one of my favorite profs.Class is always interesting, though he certainly doesn't cut you any slack. He's heard every excuse in the book,so don't even try.Tough but helpful paper grader.He got me interested in Intl. politics.Geneseo's lucky to have him.
great professor, i strongly recommend taking his class
My favorite teacher at Geneseo by far. His classes are fun. If you're interested in developing world international politics, you should really try to take a class with him.

Grace classes are a blast. Not the easiest A, however. Really stresses your writing. Most detailed comments I ever got on a paper. He actually reads them! closely! and shows you how to do better, which can be a bit of an ego blow. Awesome real world experience and involves students. Talkstoofast.
He is funny and cool, however, he is a little bit hard on grading papers.
Funny guy who keeps interest w/constant voice fluctuations.  He isn't AS great as everyone says, but he is interesting and relatable.  I would take him again.

His class is interesting and he is a good, caring professor.  He does have quizzes, so you have to go to class.  But a lot of the test questions come right from the quizzes (hint hint).  You wil have to do a little work, but definitely will enjoy it.
Professor Grace is awesome. Very energetic, engaging, has lots of stories, definitely keeps you awake. Highly recommended.

Best professor I've had. So enthusiastic, and really loves his area. Lots of real-world experience makes him fascinating to talk to and listen to, and he's extremely receptive to students and input. I'm his research assistant, and I love working for him.
Not only is he really brilliant, but also really receptive to students' concerns. Funny as hell, and so knowledgable. The most engaging teacher I've ever had. Also, I want to have his children.
he's cool
AWESOME PROF.
Awesome Professor
Awesome. A non-stop fountain of information, insight, and inspiration. IPE w/ Grace is the best class I have ever taken. We need more like this man!
Best professor in this department.
EXCELLENT!!! Super human being, exceptional professor. Very interesting man. Best courses ever.
great teacher who KNOWS HIS STUFF SO DAMN WELL!  he can be very helpful and understanding too.  one of the best damn professors ever in history
No Comments
Amazingly energetic, esp. for an 8:30 class. Better than a cup of coffee and really got me thinking about the world. Tests can be hard. But overall, Best prof I've had at Geneseo.
Awesome! Don't miss the Jeremy Grace Experience! Best prof ever.
This guy kicks ass.
No Comments
Take the elementary level Spanish classes with her. She's so nice and her quizzes are really easy as long as you paid attention in class and studied the vocabulary. I wish she taught 201:(
I love Samudio! Take her, easy A. Such a nice person, quizzes are extremely easy & so are the midterm and final.
Tests are straightforward with what she wants. As long as you study the notes, you'll be fine. You cover 5 chapters throughout the class and it's enough to prepare you for 201.

Samudio is great and when people say she is lazy...I guess she comes off like that. BUT, all 102 classes are flip styled learning so she technically isnt required to teach, but instead answer follow up questions. 4 quizzes (20%), Mid&Final(40%). Expect hw from book hw and tarea in the book (2sets). Laid back professor. "Buenas tardes!" -samudio
take her, easy class
Doesn't post any grades, but she is a very easy grader.  Take for credit
She's one of the nicest and most understanding people I have ever met.  Totally recommend her to anyone

She's super cool and super laid-back. She barely gave homework over the semester and she's very understanding about showing up a few minutes late or missing class. Class is an easy A. Highly recommend.
Amazing professor, very helpful in and out of class. Class is not hard at all but you will have to study. I would love to take 201 with her but sadly she doesn't teach it. Highly recommend.

Didn't like his method of teaching. Told us to "think of the vocab words as pictures" since we were only learning a few letters of the Arabic alphabet each class! That's like telling someone learning English to memorize how to write 'apple' without teaching them A-Z first! But he is really nice and has fascinating life stories to share.

Professor Aljaysh seems like a great guy. He loves jokes and seems to care that everyone in the class actually learns Arabic. He's wouldn't be one to just try and give people bad grades and he's an engaging professor. Sometimes I wish he were a bit harder by maybe giving vocab quizzes each class Maybe it's  me, but I felt like I didn't learn enough

She is nice and responsive. All the modules are laid out on Brightspace but it was still somehow organized in a very confusing way. Not sure she knows how to properly use it. Her standards were clear, you had to meet online with 4 classmates to have a discussion on the reading each week. Easy midterm and final project, mostly lightwork.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Group projects', 'Clear grading criteria']

comment: I loved this class. It was an online class but there were no zooms with the whole class only one 30 minute zoom a week with your group of 3-4 of your classmates where you talk about your discussion boards. There is one discussion board due a week and only 2 tests which are the midterm and final. One big project but you have plenty of time to do it.

Dr. Kreutter is an incredible Professor. She never requires you to complete an unreasonable amount of assignments, her expectations are clear and appropriate for graduate level work, and she is, above all, incredibly kind. She is very understanding and approachable. If you ever need anything, she makes it known that you can always come to her.

Knowledgeable about the subject, but has absolutely no idea what she is doing in class. I'm pretty sure she doesn't decide what we are going to do in class until after it starts. Usually someone asks a question about the syllabus and she goes over the entire syllabus for 45 minutes and then randomly has an idea for a class activity and we do it.

Although the class is fairly easy, she has no idea what she wants from the students.  She has lost grades on lesson plans multiple times.  Our final was a joke (only 10 points and 45 questions) and the books contain everything she taught us.  I could have learned more on my own.

She was a nice lady and the class was fairly easy. she had trouble clarifying what she wanted and often you had no idea what the assignment was. Class was useless but you had to attend because she kept attendance.

Dr. Simmons was an amazing professor who always made lectures relatable. Participating in her class is important as every topic ties strongly into the instructional methods of teaching. The lesson plan assignment is a big part of the grade but if you follow the examples and pay attention in class it will go well.

Don't get me wrong Simmons is a lovely lady and had a lot of great insight when it came to teaching social studies to children. HOWEVER, she is easily the toughest grader I have ever seen in my career. The mean on our unit plan part 2 was a 33/40 and it's a fat part of your grade. Lovely woman, great insight; good luck getting an A.

Dr. Simmons is the best professor I have ever had. You will learn so much by going to her class and participating. There's a huge unit plan project that's broken into four parts, it's a lot of work. But, it's great practice for the future. No tests or quizzes.

Anyone who doesn't like Dr. Simmons can straight-up fight me, she is the most kind-hearted, open-minded professor I have had yet. Even when I disagreed with the content of her class she heard me out and we talked through it all semester and that is something that is a rare find in this world. She's the best and definitely worth taking her class.

Dr. Simmons is one of my favorite School of Ed Professors! She is extremely knowledgeable and very thoughtful. Every single one of her lectures is planned out thoroughly and is very meaningful. I learned so much from her class about social studies and multicultural education. I would love to have her as a professor again!

She is a great person, but not a great teacher. First of all, she is very specific in what she wants but does not give clear instructions on it so you won't know what she wants until you receive a bad grade. She also is a coordinator for student teaching so she goes to Ghana for 7 weeks rendering her almost completely unavailable to help you.

Dr. Simmons is a really kind and helpful professor.  Her class is low-stress.  She cares about her students and wants them to succeed.  She also cares about whether we become good teachers and wants us to reach our full potential.

One of the BEST professors I've had here! Dr. Simmons truly cares about her students and the subject that she teaches. All of her lectures were meaningful and well planned. The unit plan had soft deadlines so that you would be on track all semester and you could get feedback from her. I wish I could take another class with her!

Professor SeungJung Chichester is so sweet and funny. It was a pleasant surprise to have a professor that personble and makes class enjoyable. I enjoyed hearing about her personal experiences and I was able to learn a lot through her course and the field experiences.

Dr. Chichester is a caring professor, you can tell she is passionate about what she is teaching. There is at least 1 assignment due a week. Do not miss a class presentation day, you will get a 50%. The course is a lot of work, but if you come to class and put in effort outside of class, you will be okay!(ECED 352)

Dr. Jo is such a sweet person, she truly cares about her students. This semester was very assignment heavy but we did do meaningful work. If you do your work and submit on time you will do well in her class.

I took Dr. Jo last semester and she was great, deserved all of her fives she got. This semester we have at least five final projects. Multiple page papers were do every weekend. She also has started giving an exit ticket due at the end of every class date. She doesn't believe anymore that we have any other classes. Good luck!

She is amazing and you will not regret taking her. She's caring, kind, and very understanding. She tries her best to do fun activities and even does Kahoot!

Overall, She is the best and I love her, I wish I could be in her class for ECED 352 but they filled up quickly.
Professor Jo is so nice and understanding. She would always come in with a smile on her face and she is always wanting to talk to her students. I would 100% take another class with her again.

Dr. Jo is the sweetest person alive and I enjoyed every second I was in her class. She is so caring and seriously wants the best for everyone that walks in the doors. She is very responsive to her emails, and is always giving the best advice. She does like to use the textbooks, so please buy all the ones she lists!

Absolutely love Dr. Jo. I have literally never had a more kind and accommodating professor like her. She genuinely cares about her students and wants to see all of them succeed. She is so organized and has clear instructions for all assignments and activities. Hands down the best professor at Geneseo and she deserves a raise.

Best prof of all time. This woman seriously deserves a raise. She put our whole class in such a great mood even on the cold and rainy days. If i could take this class again I would. She could not have treated her students better. She was so accommodating and understanding if you care and show up you will get an A. LOVEEEE HERRR SOOO MUCHHHH

Dr. Jo is one of the sweetest professors at Geneseo. She came in every morning with such enthusiasm and made an 8:30 class enjoyable to go to. She was accessible outside of class and was always willing to answer our questions. Dr. Jo was so encouraging, positive, and wanted us to do our best. I'm extremely grateful to have had her in Block V.
Hands down best professor at Geneseo. She is an angel on earth and the best person ever. She loves her students and actually cares about you and your education. I am obsessed with her.
Best professor I have ever had. Absolutely take her if you can. She is hands down the best professor at Geneseo so caring. Gave us pizza on the day of the final
Took FSA with him. Final project is very long and demanding, tests are times and are fairly difficult. Very lecture heavy

Amazing professor. 
Almost everything from the reading (digital textbook) is on the slides he distributes after class. Had to complete a career exploration project (15% of final grade). Three noncumulative exams (15% each) are easy if you pay attention in class (and he curves them). Online quizzes are easy and you can find the answers online (30%).
dr. paku deals with my BS. I love her. very kind and cares about your wellbeing. if youre having a hard time, just talk to her! she understands and will extend anything if needed.

You do have to participate and sometimes it is graded, but Paku is the best and is super understanding. She will extend deadlines and allow you to redo assignments. She either gives you a 0 or 100, all you have to do is what is asked of you. She does not want to fail anyone and knows that it is an intro class, so it should not tank your gpa.

Probably the best prof I've had so far and probably the best I'll ever had. Very grateful for Dr. Paku putting up with my BS. A very intelligent and forgiving prof. If you care you will gain so much out of her class. Super nice too.
Best class I've ever taken.
Dr. Paku is a treasure!

I was disappointed in this class. I've taken Dr. Paku before and found her to be a reading-heavy but manageable and good class. Disability Lit was not that. Okay teacher. Kind of annoying to listen to and is very vauge about what she wants. You do the same thing every day in groups which gets a little boring, but at least she is very excited about what she is teaching.
She is an okay teacher. She is very excited about arts & careers but you don't really learn anything.
Wallace is a good guy. Notes are online in advance so you don't need to take them. Always willing to help. Can be a little dry with straight lectures but the exams are reasonable.
If ur willing to do the work and have ANY familiarity with calculus at all, its an easy  A. Always in his office and VERY willing to help when in there. Great prof. Highly recommended!

this class is seriously a joke. i have never been good at math but he explains things really clearly and gives a million examples so you know what to expect on his tests. the tests are basically the same as the study guide too. he can be a little boring, but it's worth it just cause it's so easy.
great, helpful teacher.  loved his classes... a little boring sometimes, but always answers questions and is very thorough.  good guy to take a class with.
THOUGH I AM NOT A MATH PERSON, HE WAS VERY HELPFUL.  HE IS A GREAT GUY AND I BELIEVE HE WAS FAIR.
Great guy, decent teacher.  He seems like he gets a little nervous in class sometimes but he's very helpful and very smart.  Take a class with him.
he is a really nice man, always willing to help you, if you ask questions, he will help you, lots of work, but i guess you have to expect that for a calc class, i would recommend taking his class
HORRIBLE HORRIBLE HORRIBLE.....do I need to say it again!!? Boring, Hard Tests, Does not answer questions correct. BAD BAD TEACHER!
Nice guy whose not intimidating in the least. Eager to answer all questions, even horribly moronic ones. Tests are pretty easy, helps to have done some calculus in high school.
Mad easy course, nice guy. Just take it. I suck and hate math, but am doing fine. He explains things well. Hes a good teacher and makes a course that could suck ass bearable and amusing.

Don't take calculus with him unless you are really smart or have taken it before. What he explains in class has no relevance to homework problems. He doesn't take the time to really material, if you don't understand it. Sweats a lot in class... pretty fun

Ok I don't know what the other raters are on, but he is not easy like they are saying. His classes are incredibly boring, and he loves trick questions. Most things he talks about in class are not on the exam. Overall, NOT GOOD!
Better than most, not as good as some
He is very helpful and his tests are easy.  He enjoys his office hours too much.

Talks so fast, mumbles, hard to understand. Honestly, I'm writing this during class because I'm just so sick of her. She just talks the whole time. I honestly love Okada. She is super chill and clearly loves what she teaches. This is my 2nd time taking her and I really respect her. As long as you do the work asked of you and participate regularly, I don't see why you would have a hard time in her class. She is great!

Jun Okada's teaching style sometimes makes me wonder how she was hired. Taking her for my INTD 105 course was absolute torture. yes she is opinionated but she knows her stuff. she made this subject so interesting that i'm taking another class w her. if you're not open to different opinions and interpretations, then you'll have a hard time with this class. but i totally respect her. as long as you contribute to discussions and participate, you'll do great

Rude to students that don't share her personal opinion on the subject material

Professor Okada rarely used clarity. She assigned busy work that she would mention in class but then didn't explain specifically what she wanted for the assignment. Several times she emailed the class late Sunday afternoon about a paper to be written or read/film to be watched for Monday's class. In addition, she repeatedly called students stupid.

An unprofessional teacher. Often unprepared for class, says "Um" before starting virtually every sentence. The kind of teacher who makes a mistake and acts like its the classes fault. Overly tough grader on her essays for an intro course. Midterm and final tests are pretty easy and probably the only redeeming quality of this class and teacher.
She picked the most boring movies for us to watch.  There is a lot of reading but if you put an arguement in your essay, then you will do fine in this class.
There are only three essays in this class, but the lectures are boring and she rambles a lot.  The class was not very enjoyable to be involved in.

She doesn't value her students opinions. Picks bad examples for movies. Her lectures are very basic but slightly varied from the textbook which makes for boring reading and boring lectures. The most unhelpful professor I have ever had. Highly recommend not taking any of her classes.
Babbles incomprehensibly at the front of the classroom, unable to use a DVD player, self absorbed, takes this class WAY too seriously. It's a boring, deathly class do not take.

She's very rude and doesn't take responsibility when she makes a mistake. Pushy, lectures are boring, and doesn't think anyone else's opinion matters.  Her behavior would be understandable if she had significant prestige, but her resume is not even that impressive. Horrible woman, only knows Asian film.
Tough grader and boring lectures, but a very nice woman who cares about the material and is willing to help. All you have to do is ask.

I loved her personally, however yes she's a seriously hard grader. She's willing to help her students though, and gives second chances on essays. The films are painfully boring, I had to staple my eyes open, so go to class. Not an easy A at all but at least she's friendly and willing to help.

It's a shame that she is the only film professor at geneseo.  I took this Intro to Film Studies for a fine arts requirement but she is an obnoxiously hard grader, very condescending, and often outright rude.

Incredibly Rude, Absolutely awful how rude she is.  Would not take anyone's opinion into account but hers on a daily basis for Film and DID NOT KNOW THE MATERIAL. Honestly not too difficult, but if you get on her bad side, good luck enjoying the class.

She cannot speak well and her lectures are completely pointless. There's two papers, and a midterm. The midterm is solely on information from the textbook and she is not very clear on what she expects from the papers. I went into this class thinking it was an english class and I was disappointed to learn it was actually a class for film majors..

Literally the worst teacher I have ever had. Her lectures are basically reading out of the textbook and directly repeating what her dumb powerpoints say. She chooses boring movies because she just does exactly what the textbook uses as examples. Never directly answers questions. Really dumb. Annoying to listen to. Class is painful to go to.

I don't seem to agree with many of the other comments on here.  While I can see where they might be coming from, I don't think they are very representative of her.  At times can be slightly condescending, but it's rarely uncalled for.

Okada's hard. Her tests are hard, she grades papers hard, but with that being said, it's still not a bad course. She knows what she's talking about and the movies she shows are (with the exception of Battleship Potemkin) enjoyable. Take her if you don't mind doing the work.

Horrible professor. Her lectures are completely pointless and devoid of sense. She is a rude person, a bad teacher, and an overall pessimistic, feminist nut. Going to her office hours is like a trip to the DMV: Extremely long wait and completely rude and offensive when she comes. Do not take this class.

Fairly misunderstood--her classes are for people who want to learn more about film, not those who just want to watch movie and get an easy A. Somewhat moody and not always lucid but between the readings and discussions, you can figure it out. Tests rely heavily on textbooks and discussion so attendance is recommended. Took 3 classes with her total.
Worst professor you could ever get. Makes no sense while she is teaching.
READ THE TEXTBOOK - all questions come from it verbatim. Her lecture is mostly pointless unless you don't read. Film screenings and recitation sessions are important. Very few grades, so be careful.

an okay class, but kind of hard. not really the best teacher, just kind of rambles on about stuff in no logical order. The topic is somewhat interesting though. I think this class would be better given to film majors, unfortnately they dont exist at geneseo... don't take this unless you are REALLY interested in film or it'll just be annoying.

Unfortunately, this class ended with a sour  note. She grades too harshly, and has a knack for creating confusion where confusion does not belong. Could be a decent teacher, but for this class, overall, she wasn't.
She is rude sometimes and doesn't make sense when she speaks.  Her classes are all lecture and she doesn't explain anything very well.  She grades too harshly too!  Stay away!

She ostensibly uses a rubric for grading, but more often than not arbitrarily assigns the average score for each category. She never explicates her ideas and is very condescending. I would avoid this professor!

If you are at all conservative do not take this class.  While I agreed with her views on topics, I often sympathized with students who do not; she zeroed in on such students in class and essentially refused to hear (or accept) their perspectives.  Moreover she cannot simulate class discussion for the life of her.  I would not recommend.

Nice woman, but cannot spit out a clear thought for the life of her. The class is mildy interesting, there are some boring films, but also some more recent interesting ones. Anyway, you don't really have to stay and watch the movies; you're never tested on them. Tests are made up of completely random multiple choices questions all from the book.

This is the worst professor I have ever taken.  She has the communication skills  of a frustrated teenage genius with PMS.  She cannot foster productive group discussion.  And she sits her office hours with her door closed while she talks on the phone about her personal life.  Avoid her.

I think she's very good. She's willing to put in the effort if the student will. If you are a serious academic film student wanting to learn serious film scholarship, this is THE class for you, but if you think Michael Bay is the acme of film making - look elsewhere.

She is really making an effort to make film classics better.  I can tell over the past 2 weeks it's getting easier and more interesting.  I think she was just new and is adapting.  By next semester she'll probably do a great job.

This professor is the most incompetent I have had in three years of school. This is a 200-level course with 13-14 pages of writing, pop-quizzes, shes asks long-winded, incoherent questions, alienates intelligent students in discussions, complains about students, will not respond to emails (even when I had mono), and generally has a poor attitude.

Not a hard class, all you have to do is read the book, but she is a pretty bad speaker. She does try to help you if you talk to her though. I thought the class would be more narratively based, but it is pretty technical, and not nearly as much fun as I thought it would be.

stupid film classics... BE WARNED this is NOT an english class.  Okada geared the class for film majors.  If you dont know anything about film already, DONT take her class. film classics may not be for people who aren't that interessted in the classics of film history (silent), but overall, its a good intro class on film.

Film classics, you think it sounds cool, but it's not.  Unless of course you are into an hour and fourty minutes a week of watching SILENT black and white films.  Then you're probably all about this class.

He is funny and caring. His lectures are not helpful as he goes too fast. He provides notes, but they are confusing as they don't go in the order of his slides. He gives extra credit if you ask. Professor yokoyama is one of the best chemistry professors at Geneseo. Struggle fest!Combines analytical physics and 1st year chemistry.Lectures were very equation heavy, lots of graphs with no idea of how to use them. Totally recommend this course to satisfy scientific literacy requirement. The course is clearly outlined and he is an extremely caring professor! He wants you to understand the material and succeed overall. Be aware the lab online is an additional 160 dollars for lab material and is time consuming.

Very friendly professor, willing to work with students! Tends to go through lecture material fast but provides a lot of in-class review before quizzes and tests. He also helps by giving you a personalized video message after quizzes to tell you what topics you need to work on. All in all a very nice professor, I would recommend him!

Professor Yoko is a really good person who seems to genuinely care about us and he always makes really good jokes. But, I haven't learned a single thing in his class. comment: Great professor, teaches a tough subject though

I absolutely love class with Dr Yokoyama. He tries his best to make class enjoyable and funny and at 8:30 in the morning that can really help to stay at least somewhat focused. He is very nice and conveys information well. If you put in an ounce of work outside of class it shouldn't be hard to do well. Dropped lowest test and not a lot of homework.

I took it as a bio major, so doing this class with other rough science was a time. I had to withdraw. He is interesting in lectures but there are tests basically every 2/3 weeks and none are dropped. Add on the homeworks and quizzes and it is a LOT of work. You have 50 minutes for tests with multiple choice and short answer, he does give partial.

Kazu is wonderful and so caring. He really wants his students to do well. Each time I would reach out to him with a question he would respond within the hour. Even though I didn't meet him in person because my class was online, he was so sweet. I HIGHLY recommend taking CHEM 104&105 online with him!

Very nice dude. Really wants everyone to do well in his class. May come off as intimidating the first day, but he does everything in his power to make sure everyone gets a good grade. All his lectures are posted online, which makes it easy to teach yourself if you skip class. Pretty thick accent though, hard to understand at times. Kazu rocks.

His lectures are straight from the textbook and offers no new information he actually leaves information out that is later on the exam. He then puts up slides of math problems for about 2 seconds and says "if you know this your good" and then moves on. comment: Its what you expect out of a lab, but he just supervises and teaches the pre-lab lecture but the LI's do all the work as far as grading (hope you get a good one). He has a great sense of humor and even the most boring labs always turn into a good time. Love taking Dr. Yoko's classes!

If you get the pleasure of getting to know Dr. Yoko he is very approachable and personable. He cares about you and wants you to be successful. His office hours are key!
