comment: She is one of the worst professors I've had at this school. She is also not helpful at office hours. I had to get a private tutor, and even then, still struggled as she is a tough grader and moves at such a fast pace. I would not recommend taking this class to anyone. Her only advice is to keep re reading the notes but the notes make no sense.

Professor Aguilar is super helpful and approachable. She's always willing to answer questions and ensure you have a good understanding of the homework problems when you ask about them, but doesn't just give answers. There's an hour long tutorial every week where she does practice problems separate from the office hour which is also very helpful.

Took her at the beginning of covid and she did too much. Cameras on lockdown browser which is crazy. She makes you take pictures and convert your work pages into a pdf and you still have to beat the time allotted for the test. Just overall annoying
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Group projects', 'Tough grader']

comment: She is very quick to respond over email. Only bad thing I would have to say is she is a hard grader, especially on homeworks, so going to office hours helps a lot.

I feel like Professor Aguilar teaches in a way that made it easy to understand. The lectures made sense and really explained each detail carefully. I was struggling in her class but every time I met with her after class I walked away feeling a lot more confident. She makes you work for it and is a tough grader but is very caring towards students.

Aguilar is a good professor but a hard grader. She will make you work for your grades but is willing to do everything she can to get you there. Wonderful woman but again a hard grader. If you are not willing to study you will not have good grades. If you put in the effort you will be fine. Also the review sessions are extremely helpful before test.

I absolutely loved having Professor Aguilar! She is so passionate about what she does, I especially recommend her for Math 141. She also really cares about her students and is quite accessible for help or questions.

Professor Aguilar is such a sweet human being. She really cares about all of her students, and wants everyone to succeed. Her homework is a little hard to do because she wants it done a certain way, but once you get used to it you'll be fine. The test and quiz questions are from the notes and the practice problems.

Professor Aguilar is very kind and caring. However, her homework is very difficult. Gives good test reviews before tests. For me it was more the class subject itself was very difficult, but I found some things she didn't explain well. Office hours saved my grade, but know going to the math learning enter will not help, you must go to office hours.
tags: ['Gives good feedback', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Tough grader']

comment: Very tough. I lived in the math learning center and even they were confused half of the time. The homework reflected material we did not learn yet and when having one on ones about my future in this course I was told math wasn't for me when I had gotten an A in pre calc a semester earlier

worst professor ever! class is extremely hard! I went to office hours once to get help with a homework question and left thinking I had to change my major (Math major). She tried helping me by giving me advice but in the end, she said that I don't have what it takes to be a math major and I should switch majors now before I get too far.
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Test heavy', 'Tough grader']

comment: Not only was Math 140 easy because of her, but she made class easy and specified what we needed to know before any test. She alternated between quizzes Andnit homework assignments weekly, which was nice. She is kind and understanding when you miss class. I loved her and glad I got to have her as my teacher.

Professor Aguilar is great. She is super helpful if you ask questions and go to her office hours. Her notes are pretty good but got a little confusing towards the end. She really cares about all her students and gives a lot of partial credit. Her tests are challenging but you can do well if you work hard.

Professor Aguilar is a great teacher. She is willing to slow down and go over a topic more than once if the class is confused. Her tests are a lot harder than her homework and quizzes, but she is very lenient when grading. She is a very caring person and is willing to help you at any time. I would definitely recommend her.

Professor Aguilar is so sweet! She is very clear during class and shows you really good examples, however her tests are always so much harder than the examples she gives but if you go to her office hours she's always willing to help!
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'Caring']

comment: Professor Aguilar was a decent professor. She is very organized and meticulous, but also nit-picky and specific. One time I solved a problem differently than the method we did in class, and it wasn't 'good.' Isn't the point of math to find different ways? I spent significantly more time on her 100-level course than I did on a 200-level course.

Professor Aguilar was the BEST! She so so nice and genuinely wants all her students to do well. Her office hours are also really helpful. However, her tests were very difficult. Sometimes she did add in things on the test that we never really went over. None the less, she is still an amazing professor and I HIGHLY recommend taking her class!

Prof Aguilar is new to Geneseo, and I absolutely loved her! She did a great job explaining everything you needed to know and had a clear way of grading, which she told you! She was great- 10/10 would take her class again!
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'Clear grading criteria']

comment: She really engages with students and material. Though provoking class!

I love her. She clearly cares about what she teaches. Does she go on tangents? Yes. If you're in a sociology class this high of a level, you care about insight from the professors. If you don't think you'll be really interested in this class let someone else take it. I really enjoy her teaching style and can't wait to take more classes with her.
2 papers (2-3 pages) a week, a group presentation, a book review(7-8 pages), and a final lit review(10-12 pages) DO NOT TAKE
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Group projects', 'Lots of homework']

comment: Dr. Braksmajer is a great professor, she is super passionate about what she teaches and you can sense it from her classes and the way she conducts them. There is weekly journals you have to submit based on the 2 reading every week, there is a group project but she makes you do a peer evaluation and its confidential!
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Graded by few things']

comment: Absolutely awful professor. Weekly essays over 25 different articles and research papers you have to read. Big group assignment at the end of the class (only reason why I got a C and not a B that I had all semester) She is awfully rude to everyone besides her “favorite students”. Lacks a lot of respect and empathy for others.

Cool class and different from the others ive taken. As someone who struggles sometimes with understanding sociology classes I am happy to say that this one did the best job at explaining the concepts in an interesting and digestible way. Braksmajer is very nice and I recommend it. The final and midterm are kinda hard and a lot of reading.
The class is very interesting!  There are weekly reading quizzes and a big group project that takes place throughout the semester.

She was nice enough and the class was genuinely so easy, but the point of a sociology class is to broaden your mindset, something although she verbally encouraged, she never followed through. If you ever ask a question and don't fit a certain visual demographic she will yell at you.

Honestly I did not enjoy this class. Her lectures were not engaging, and oftentimes she went on long tangents during class. She's not very accessible outside of class, and in class she could come across as rude and demeaning. She's definitely well-versed in what she teaches, but I never felt comfortable contributing or talking to her.

super passionate and makes topics interesting, her lectures are never boring because she always adds some humor and says wild things. really into activism and often talks about real world issues and how we can make a difference. she really cares about her students and the subject, for Sociomedical take Professor Braksmajer

The content of this class seemed cool but I didn't find the lectures engaging. The discussion boards every week were a lot of work. There is a large final project due at the end of the semester that you dont get time in class on and she grades harshly. I did worse on the midterm and final exams than I thought despite studying and attending class.

Very unorganized and unclear with assignment expectations. Took weeks to answer a single email. She also assigned a HUGE final project in addition to the final exam. No in class time to work on the project was given. I wanted to complain to the chair of the department but then realized the department chair is her husband so good luck.....
overall she is a decent professor. she does NOT answer her emails in a timely manner so be prepared to wait several days for a response -_-.

material is not hard (my crap grade was a personal failure, no issue of professor) but god forbid you have a different opinion than her, prepare to be passively aggressively ripped apart. also talks a lot about sex

Professor Braksmajer was very helpful throughout this semester. Her classes were engaging and you can tell that she is passionate about the subject that she is teaching. In terms of exams and coursework, you don't need to study too much, show up to class and PAY ATTENTION.

Overall pretty good, but will talk about her opinions on anything. There are weekly discussion boards that have three or four extensive readings to base the responses on. The tests were somewhat easy, but have to make sure you read the lectures. Group project at the end of semster is difficult and she doesnt even know how to do it.
Professor was amazing!!

Overall, this is not a difficult class if you do the work. The reading reflections were irritating at times, but not terrible. I think she's an okay professor, and the midterm and final were online which made it a lot easier. I did learn some interesting things throughout this class, and I would take a class with her again if I had to. Easy A.

Have to do a journal entry based off readings every week and write 2-3 pages about it. One group assignment and presentation. Will call on you in class, but this class is nothing without different perspectives. Final Lit Review 10-12 pages which was not fun. Overall, the material is interesting and she is very accommodating/nonjudgmental.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Lots of homework']

comment: Dr. Braksmajer is one of my favorite professors I've had at Geneseo. She is always willing to meet with you and work out any issues and keeps class interesting.
This class could have been more fun if she stopped including her opinion on things. Also, her exams were fairly easy but she contradicts her own teachings in class when giving you feedback.

Professor Braksmajer is awesome! While the class is extremely lecture heavy she makes them very engaging and easy to follow. The concepts you learn are incredibly applicable to every day life and very easy to grasp. She is super approachable and good about answering emails! Only weekly discussion posts, two tests and a group project.

Prof Braksmajer is all about participation, so if you don't feel comfortable talking in class then you will get a 0. When you do talk if its not the same opinions as her she will destroy you in a passive aggressive way. You have to lead a class discussion once for the entire class, weekly journals, and a final paper. Interesting class turned boring

Wesp was an amazing prof. He retired and only a month after last semester passed away. Basically, read the rest of the comments. They'd make a great Eulogy... We loved Wesp. He was a great funny man. Will be missed. Rest in Peace Wesp!
Lectures are a bit hard to  follow but you can see his passion for theater. Go to class, read the textbook and you will get an A. He also offers up to 10 bonus points on your overall grades.
Hands down the best professor at Geneseo

Nice, funny guy. Lectures are all over the place, he goes off on tangents for a majority of the class, which makes tests somewhat difficult. Studying the textbook in addition to the lectures is helpful. Not a terrible class but definitely not the best

I really enjoyed this guy even though I could have done better. It is a bit tougher than you would expect for an intro theatre course. Absolutely use the slides to study. I used the text books for the first 3 quizes and saw a huge jump when I switched methods. Will point out distracting/disrespectful people. Q's on play readings are easy points.

He is excellent at engaging the class and helping to make the plays more interesting than just sitting in a classroom and reading. He constantly engages with the class, so if you don't want to be called out sit in roughly the middle, on either side. Reading is NOT optional though, or you'll fail completely.

Fun theatre teacher. He only assigns a few noncumulative multiple choice tests which is nice. They can be a little specific but reading the book helps. The class is not demanding and he makes it interesting.
Wesp is okay.  It's a basic introductory class and I did get a basic understanding of the theater.
Take it. Just take Theatre 100 with him. Yes, it's at 8:30, but you don't have to go more than half the time. He doesn't care and you'll still pass. Just take it.
Wesp made an 8:30am class enjoyable. He is very outgoing and energetic that early in the morning. He is everything a theatre professor should be. TAKE THE CLASS!

Wesp loves to act and uses that to his advantage. But don't worry, his 5 "quizzes" of 25 questions are so easy. Just show up to class and read what he tells you and it's an easy A and GPA booster. He's funny and obviously loves what he does. Take it for a breather from all the other hard classes you're probably taking this semester.

Prof Wesp is exactly what I expected a theatre teacher to be like (in a good way). He's very animated, humorous, and goes on amusing tangents. I thought he did a great job making the lectures fun. Love his casual style of teaching. Class is a cinch and I'd highly recommend him for knocking out the fine arts courses.

Wesp is an amazing professor and man. He makes his classes fun. He pretty much only lectures, but due to his personally, they're fun to listen to. Sometimes he goes on tangents and you get a little lost, but it's okay because he acknowledges that he does it. Definitely take a class with him!!

Wesp is wonderful! he is full of energy, even though this class is at 8:30 am i was willing to get up for it every day because it was so fun! Wesp is very funny, even if your not a huge fan of the material you will still enjoy the lectures. also gives extra credit that requires some reading but goes directly to your final avg. TAKE THIS CLASS!

he is an amazing professor who is interesting and very understanding. Going to office hours and asking his about the tests beforehand are a huge help. He also gives extra credit that is fairly easy. He is everything a theater teacher should be, despite the few confusing parts in his notes. He will clarify is asked. loved him!

Wesp is an interesting guy. Tries his best to make the material interesting. He gives 5 quizzes that determine your grade. You must go to class and take notes. Most of the questions on the quizzes are from class. You have to attend a play. Easy A but must pay attention

Wesp is one of the most talented lecturers on campus. He is engaging, energetic, and passionate. I am by no means a theatre person but Wesp makes the class as enjoyable as an 8am lecture hall could be. The one thing I'll say is that for a 100 level class it is not as easy as many would expect. You have to really study to do well

Wesp is very engaging and looks to strike up a conversation more so than force what he thinks is right or wrong about the subject material. In fact, he's not against changing his own views in light of another good argument. He's a little zany at times but in a good way that keeps you on your toes and interested.

Wesp is a great professor. Although I have no interest in theatre, he makes the class interesting for a lecture. There are 5 short "quizzes" and as long as you read the textbook and the plays, it's an easy A.  He is also helpful during his office hours.

I really really liked him! Having it at 8:30 I thought would be a problem but he teaches like he acts and is very entertaining.  An A as long as you do the work.  I personally loved his class even though I have no interest in theatre.

Wesp is definitely passionate about what he teaches. He's very funny and easy to have a conversation with. However, I sometimes found him boring but that could be because I wasn't that interested in the subject. He's an easy grader though and always willing to look over your work beforehand.

Wesp is a great teacher. He really knows what he is doing and he loves talking about it. He's funny and gets to know his students. He wants you to do well and will help you get a good grade. If you put in moderate effort, you will get a good grade.

Wesp! He's great and extremely knowledgeable. It's really not a difficult class. As long as you have a pulse, you shouldn't have any problem getting at least a B. If you put in ANY effort, in addition to having a pulse, you shouldn't have any problem getting an A.
Great professor, easy class! Just show up to class most of the time and read the textbook/plays and you'll be golden!
Very nice man and entertaining. Tests are not hard, but his wording can be confusing. He is willing to clarify test questions if you ask.

Wesp was by far one of my favorite professors I have had at Geneseo yet. He made each class interesting and laid back. The class is an easy A with minimal effort; just pay attention in class. It was based off of 5 in class analysis writings and a final out of class 3-5 page paper. I HIGHLY recommend this professor to anyone
Mr. Wesp is so great and made each class interesting. His class is an easy A if you put in 1-2 hours a week.

Mr. Wesp was one of the most witty teachers I had at Geneseo. He made classes interesting; we watched movies and discussed plays. As long as one puts in an hour or two a week to do the readings this class will be an easy A.

Wesp is a good guy. I went to most classes and ended up doing well in the class. You need to read the plays and the textbook if you want to do well. If you do not study for this class it will be incredibly difficult. The extra credit questions on tests can add 10 percent to your overall grade, proving to be very important. Test wording is confusing

Wesp seems like a nice guy until you take the first test, tests are extremely difficult and he doesn't seem to care that everyone in the class failed his 100 level tests. I took theatre thinking it was the easiest course offered at Geneseo and found it extremely difficult with Wesp. Don't take unless you like getting C's.

Nice guy, but does not understand how to properly structure the class in a suitable way for non-majors. Lectures lack focus and do not touch upon major test topics sufficiently. Class involves too much work to be a good option for fine arts credit requirements.

In the begininning, he seemed like a funny guy, but his tests are ridiculously difficult for a theatre class. The questions are either small details he mentions once or completely from the textbook and not gone over. I would find a better professor for theatre unless you don't mind getting a C in a fine arts class.

This was her last semester teaching at Geneseo- She got a job out of state, but she was a great professor. The class topic was dull but she tried to make interesting, and always gave detailed handouts, and tried to answer any questions you have. She also gives a lot of grades so that if you do bad on a quiz, etc it won't affect your grade too much!
Her class is extremely easy with very little work required. She is a very nice person but hard to understand and you wont learn much from her.

Class is kind of worthless. I skipped a ton, and when I went, I usually was on my computer the entire time. Incredibly easy grader. I BOMBED a quiz and still had a 95. Slow at getting things back to you and sometimes it's hard to understand her, but it's an easy class.

I belive she has good intentions, but I honestly did most of my learning from the textbooks, not from her. She is not very clear about the assignments, and she does not give much feedback. All in all, the class with her was so-so.

my advice to you is to just do the assignments and dont freak out. you will get a good grade in her class as long as you do the work and attend class. even if you miss points on her little quizzes, you will still be fine. dont be uptight!

There was a good deal of reading.  She was willing to change the syllabus to help us out and spend more time on what we wanted to learn about.  The projects were hard but kind of interesting. She really helped us develop our own opinions on literacy.

I had Professor Liwanag for EDUC 215 and I think that she her class is an easy A.  People complain that she isnt clear, but they just wanted her to do the work for them.  You do have to think yourself in this class, but she is very broad in what she is looking for. Just use your intution in thisclass, and you will be fine.
No Comments

I had Prof. Liwanag for EDUC 215 and it was awful! She is extremely unclear about assignments (what she expects, when they are due, etc.) and when you ask her to clarify, she avoids answering you! I don't recommend taking this class with her...

I LOVE this man, but his class is pretty boring. He is very soft-spoken, which makes it very hard to pay attention. He is SO nice, though, and sometimes the cute old man things he says are BEYOND adorable. Rambly, though. Not sure what he's teaching sometimes.

Walter, and you must refer to him by his first name, is probably one of the sweetest professors at SUNY Geneseo.  He grades his papers fairly but if you want an edge just greet him with a smile and a "Good Morning Walter." :)

for a 100-level class he graded too harshly. even after i met with him prior to a paper being due i wouldn't do as well as i liked. he's soft spoken/monotone which can be rough. he can be cute/funny sometimes though. two papers and a presentation- not terrible but not great.

I'm not sure what the level was, but I had Freed for American Lit.  It was a super easy class that doesn't require too much reading and has few assignments including a fill in the blank midterm.  Although the class is a bit boring, Freed is a genuinely sweet man and is super helpful during his office hours.

I've had him for two classes at Geneseo. He gives a fair amount of work but nothing overwhelming. I've heard he grades harshly, but I've found him to be an easy grader personally. He can be very boring because he straight lectures, but he cares about literature a lot, likes his students, and can be funny. Classes would benefit from discussion.

Talks far too softly- you cannot hear him unless you sit in the front row and even then you will miss what he says when someone rustles their jacket in the slightest. Class is boring. Teaching style can best be described as "rambling". Subject matter is spurious. Grading is suspect. Does not assign much work: 3 papers, 1 presentation, some quizzes.
I've had a few classes with him.  He is nice and sometimes funny and clearly loves literature, but he may make you fall asleep. Not a very hard class. 3 papers, 5 quizzes, and a presentation.

The class itself is not difficult--I took it under Short Fiction.  My problem is with Freed's teaching style... he does not try to engage the class at all.  He simply talks about the reading for the day, and yes, sometimes his opinions are interesting, but he's practically asking us to fall asleep.  Easy A, yes; interesting course, not at all!

Very soft spoken, so sometimes it's hard to hear him. Extremely passionate about what he his teaching. Can be very funny often times dispite his intimidating apperance. My only complaint is the lack of structure for his papers.

This class is horrible.  He may be mellow and nice but as a teacher he's HORRIBLE.  He doesn't care to know who anyone is and claims class participation is important when he rambles the entire time about things not even relevant to the reading. Worst class ever. Oh and guaranteed every day he keeps talking for 10 mins after class has ended.

He is very mellow while talking until he finds something that he thinks is important, then will he raise his voice and wave his cane in the air.  Random quizzes about the stories that are to be read before coming to class.  Also has a specific idea in his head for papers, if your idea isnt what he is looking for, you will have to rewrite your paper

This class was pretty easy as long as you actually go to class.  He likes to have a random quiz once in a while.  Definitley drink some coffee before class, he's a bore.  Really nice guy.  Pretty random outbursts of interest in stories which makes for a good laugh when you're about to fall asleep. Nice guy, boring though.

While Professor Freed can be a harsh grader when it comes to papers, his midterm and group presentation are both fair and easy. As long as you put time into the class, and make a genuine effort, you should do well. He is also extremely enthusiastic, kind, and funny at times. There are a lot of notes, but that doesn't take away from the class.

This is the best english teacher I've had here. He knows the material inside and out and teaches it with enthusiasm. He makes it interesting and uses his cane for demonstrations. The group presentation is easy as were his tests. Fill in the blank for a midterm? It doesn't get any better than that.

SOOO boring, difficult to stay awake. He rambles on the entire class like students aren't even there. IMPOSSIBLE to predict what will be on tests, questions are soo specific even though there is such a wide range of material! STAY AWAY!!!

At first glance, Freed may SEEM boring. If you LISTEN, however, he really ISN'T; He's just soft-spoken. He has such passion! I absolutely loved hearing him talk, whether it was explaining the stories or telling his own personal anecdotes. He is extremely smart, VERY VERY well-spoken, and responds kindly to every response. Got an A, somewhat easily.

I had Dr. Freed (Yes, he has a PhD, he's NOT JUST a "lecturer") for Eng 200 and he was such a delightful man I absolutely had to take his class again. I love his talks and he makes me feel all nostalgic when he talks about his life. Yes, occasionally you will be behind the syllabus, but his talks are absolutely worth it. I absolutely LOVE this man!

He's got a ton of interesting things to say and real life experiences to share. This short fiction class is great becuase you read one short story per class (maybe not even that) and you have two papers and one presentation. He's rather soft spoken but very intense about everything he does.

read everything on the syllabus! he may seem boring at first, but he is very interesting  once you get into class a little bit. it is amazing how much he knows and how interested he is in the subject himself. take good notes and go to him if you need help on your paper. read everything on the syllabus no matter what he does in class.

HE is soo boring. He is unclear about the assignments, papers, and everything in general. HE doesn't give direction and specific advice, but gives bad grades. Overall, I would not rate this teacher very higly. He is a nice guy and is approachable, but as far as the topics and his insight...not very helpful.

We are way behind in class, not following the syllabus. Write a decent paper, you'll get a decent grade. Write a good paper, you'll get a good grade. Problem is the quizzes. They're random facts, nothing about the text. Easy, but disappointing because of the lack of focus/structure.
Indescribable lecturer.  Communicates his passion for the topic.

INCREDIBLE MAN. I got As on EVERY paper. I LOVED his lectures (well its different for everyone) and I was always on the tip of my toes when he spoke. Very funny and interesting. He grades pretty rough though. Be aware of that. Otherwise, this was my fav course ever. Freed is so awesome, I love this man.

well, he has some interesting stuff to share.  Lots of reading, papers have no guidelines except length requirements.  His quizes and test questions are VERY random.  He grades papers hard, but I got through the course alright.

I wouldn't recommend him, if only because I'm still not sure whether he really knew what he was doing or not. Essay assignments got little to no direction or mention in class, and tests were purely based on trivial facts about the authors, not about the texts themselves. Overall, an odd class.
Freed is the F'in man.  You won't be sad.

boring. boooring. booooring. he literally whispers in class, so the whole class can be quiet and listen to him. he's a tough graders, he looooves giving out Bs, so be careful. He's not clear at all with assignments, it seems like he makes it up as he speaks. anyhow, he's boring. take another teacher
Umm.. He doesn't seem to have any clear goals, motives, or themes in his lecture. He gives pointless quizzes to see if you did the reading so watch out.
A boring guy and not very helpful. Assignments were kind of juvenile which was disappointing for someone who actually wanted to get something out of the class.

He has a voice of a true poetl his tone is rich and indescribable. He is very intelligent and articule; this class is always my favorite class of the day. I used to hate writing, but now I like it- all because of him. He knows how to teach, teaches effectively, and entertains the rest of us as well.
his tests are pretty hard but you should be fine if you keep up with the reading. can put anybody to sleep within 10 min.

I took him for 2 classes b/c he placed me in them as my advisor. He is so boring it's out of control. Although he isn't a difficult prof, he is EXTREMELY boring and frustrating when you're trying to feel excited about the subject. His speaking voice is annoying as well.

Freed gives very helpful tips and encourages his students to explore new styles of writing.  I strongly feel that my writing improved a great deal during that one semester.  As long as you approach each assignment sincerely and as he librally directs, you will enjoy success in his class.

Really nice guy who is very passionate about writing & stories. He picks on little things in your essays, but does so because he wants you to learn how to write properly. You get only 3 or 4 essays & alot of time to work on & reivise them. The class can be boring if you dont like discussing stories.
Nice man, insightful and interesting.  Lots of lecture, little discussion.  If you like that type of teacher and you're an English major, make friends with Walter Freed.

Freed is perhaps the most boring professor to ever grace Geneseo. His dry, neverending lecture is supplemented by well timed cane thrusts. The class is not overly hard but good luck staying awake through it!

He is very intelligent, and if you pay attention and attend class regularly, he will teach you a lot. Take his advice when he grades... your writing gets better! He doesn't assign too much, so the work load is incredibly light.
Really interesting fellow.  loves to cut us off and his essay arent that bad
don't even bother going to class

He's quite a character, but he's remarkably intelligent though he may not come off that way to some. If you aren't put off by his slow teaching style, you may actually learn a great deal from him. I don't mean that in a negative way.
Definetly a sleep through. Likes to douse my papers in red, i hate grammar. Terribly boring, he's into it but no one else is.
Eeasy class, he just speaks so slow and don't get him started on the word "like" or "cool"

Well he knows what he's talking about if you can stay awake long enough to try and follow him.  Not a bad guy or a bad teacher, he...just....speaks....reallly....slowly.....and...in....a...monotone....
No Comments

I want him to be my grandpa/uncle.  He's so nice and gets so into it.

She's a sweetheart, and tries her best to explain things thoroughly in class, but her tests are pretty hard unless you've already learned the material prior to taking the class. Makes class very not-boring!

She's super cute and bubbly! I enjoyed having her as my professor and I'm kinda upset that she's leaving :( Overall this class was somewhat hard for me. comment: So hypocritical. Class gave me anxiety and PTSD. Take res methods with anyone else but him. Is never clear on what he wants for you, and no matter how much you try or go to him, he doesn't help you succeed.

Dr. Lynch is a relatively nice guy. His lectures are a bit dull, and lots of time is often spent on each minor topic with his soothing voice which makes it hard to stay focused. The tests are fair, but beware that he is a very harsh grader with any form of writing. The main paper has been a major struggle, but he cares about improvement.

Dr. Lynch's class was both the hardest and best class I've taken at Geneseo. Exams are extremely difficult (based on lecture material & studies). Bring your papers to him for feedback. Ask questions for clarification. Go to his office hours. Do all extra credit. Don't take it personally when grades are mediocre--this class is tough!
tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Gives good feedback', "Skip class? You won't pass."]

comment: Great professor although a lot of your grade depends on papers and short essay questions and he searches for very specific answers. The book is dull and the class is a bit slow paced but you take away a lot from the class. He's very approachable and offers some extra credit on tests but the extra credit questions are tricky.

Really enjoyed this class as a psych major and by the end of the semester I had learned so much about psychopathology that it changed my understanding of individuals with disorders in a positive way. He says at the beginning this class will teach you to understand others at psychological standpoint and it definitely does! Highlyrecommend this class

Lecture is pretty boring but straightforward. Papers are short, but he is a very particular and harsh grader. Only a midterm and a final for tests. Multiple choice isn't bad but takes a lot of points off on short answer. Take 321 with Kirsh if you want something interesting.

Very vague. Boring lectures. Class notes almost useless. Grades papers very harshly. Short answers on test impossible to get full credit. You could write down, as answers, exactly what he says in class and still not get full credit. Papers almost impossible to get passing grade. TAKE ANOTHER PROFESSOR.

Very specific test questions, but if you go  to class and write down everything he says and study very carefully, you can do fine. Bizarre grading of papers - wants something very specific for each one, takes off a lot of points for small mistakes. Tough, but fair if you really work hard.

Lynch is a very nice guy, and this class is pretty easy overall. He is a tougher grader on written assignments, but the multiple choice on exams are easy if you look over your notes. One of two questions will be on there from text companion website. Also gives choice of essay question on exam.

Professor Lynch seems like a nice guy but a couple things about him are bothersome.  He speaks in a whisper which is quite unnerving. It is very monotone and breathy.  His slides are not at all helpful and he doesn't put them online anyways.  You need to attend class because he tests on very specific things. Also an unfair grader, by a lot :(
Best Psych professor I've experienced at Geneseo. He's super nice and is passionate about the field. I definitely recommend Dr. Lynch!

He's super tough, but he's just as equally nice. Be respectful in class, participate, and sit up front (he talks quietly). He has a real passion for the material and it shows, and he is always helpful if you have questions or anything. His tests are rough though, but it's worth it. Great class!

This class is the hardest class I have ever taken, but Lynch goes above and beyond to help you understand the material. Be very specific on tests and thorough in your papers. Go to his office hours if you need help. He's a total sweetheart and will do anything he can to help. This class will kick your ass, but it's totally worth it at the end of the semester.

Exactly what the one below me said. So excited for this class and it was a HUGE letdown. Very boring, very hard essays and tests. Studied for the final for 2 weeks and got a C. Very vague about points as well as what to expect on tests and essays. If you can't get out of his class, go to his office hrs to show you care, he likes to see that.

I do not recommend Professor Lynch. His lectures are boring, and the power point slides are useless to study from. He's able to make material with the potential to be interesting really boring. He combined the last two tests into one final exam because he is unable to correctly pace the course material. DON'T take adolescent development with him.

Good professor to an extent.  He has poor time management, every semester he has to combine his last two exams and make it a huge part of your final grade because he is too far behind.  I would not take adolescent development with him if you value your grade

GREAT class! He is so friendly and helpful, and really makes the material interesting. Great classroom discussion, not too much work, tests are fair. If you have to take adolescent development take it with Lynch!

He grades the written portion of the tests and the papers hard, which would be fine, except that often he's not clear about what he wanted until after the fact. He also got swine flu, was out for a week, and doubled up our second test with the third, so that 200/375 points will be taken finals week. He didn't even try to find a different time.

Much easier than his 366. Papers and assignments are easy and he give lots of guidance if you go in to talk to him. Tests are a little more challenging. Fun and interesting. Speak up and get involved in class a lot and you really get on his good side

My fav prof ever. Classes are interesting & fun. He's super nice & really cares. You learn so much and the format of lec is easy to follow. He's an easy grader on papers but for some reason his tests really are impossibly hard, he expects such a specific answers. I was a straight A Bio major but got a C+ in his class :( Still, it was worth it.

Dr.Lynch is such a nice guy, and I'm pretty sure he's a great dad and really smart... but he is incredibly boring.  The class moves at the slowest pace imaginable, spends over a week learning what variables are.  Would make a great teacher for young kids!  Again.. really nice, but really blah.
Good instructor, learned a few things in his class. Though mid way through the semester, he decided to combine the last two tests into one. That 41% "final" killed my grade in the class.

You will love or hate Dr. Lynch, I loved him! Come to class, take detailed notes, discuss any questions or concerns with him and you WILL do well (you should also read the book)! Developmental Psychopathology is by far my Favorite class, I learned so many interesting things but I did have to work for it and it was so worth it! Remember be specific!

The class material is a lot of commonsense but you still end up learning something new in almost every lecture. Take good notes and use the review questions on the book's website when studying for an exam. The Virtual Child project that you'll have to do is a bit fun and you get a bit of an inkling as to what kind of parent you might become.

Dr. Lynch think that his class and his knowledge are the most important things in life, next to his children. So if you want a good grade learn his kids names, what they do on breaks and dress up as for Halloween. He plays favorites and harshly grades some people  more then others. His short answer question are impossible to get full credit on.

Go to class and he'll give you everything you need for the exam. Also reading the textbook would help. Gives extra credit on q on his kids. And is EXTREMELY helpful and on what he wants on the paper! LOVED him! He made me want to go to a class that is dry in material!

I think Dr. Lynch is very nice and helpful, both in and out of class. About the test thing, i think it's b/c people didn't study or didn't go to class. Dr. Lynch goes over everything and gives what his expectations are on the exams and papers, as long as you listen, you can do really well in his class. I will definitely take more classes w/ him.

I have taken Dr.Lynch for several classes now, and have to say that he is an amazing teacher and a terrific person.  I really have enjoyed every class.  He is very helpful both in and out of class.  The tests are difficult but if you prepare well, you should have no problems.  Always feel free to ask him for help!

hmm, I think that he is a nice guy, and the class is interesting but...  I agree with the test thing, even when he went over what he wanted on the short and long answear I felt that I wrote it but only got half the points? Multiple choice part is easy, but i find that reading four chapters out of the text won't prepare you as well as your notes.

Pretty boring and asks too many obvious questions... To the point where they're almost rhetorical. Time goes by slowly in his class... Tests are pretty hard though and a hard paper grader, don't let the easy things he talks about in class fool you.

Extremely unclear about what he expected on tests and papers.  Additionally, I found that he was not willing to be very helpful in office hours and placed emphasis on his view more than those in the text (which weren't at all helpful for the tests).  I would avoid this class if you actually wish to come out of it with anything!!
Pace a bit slow at times, but I loved this class.  Good information about something that's important.

Doesn't test what he teaches and grades short answer questions unfairly. Class is boring. Never has clear cut directions but expects highly specific answers... i don't know about you but i'm not telepathic. Take classes with another professor if possible.

Much of the class was obvious.  He asks very vague questions and expects specifics, making his tests and papers hard.  Very nice teacher and willing to help.  Class could be boring or interesting.  Not a bad class overall.

This class was really boring.  He is very nice, but does not know much about things outside of his narrow view of the developmental perspective, which I found really annoying.  His tests are very difficult even if you go to class and do the work.

Talks about his kids too much and rambles on. Class goes by slowly and is pretty boring, a lot of it is restating the obvious. Not very hard, not too bad a grader. Nice prof, but the course... Not so much.
I'm withdrawing from this class because I don't have time for it, but would want to withdraw anyway.  He asks very vague questions and expects very specific answers.
That person is not the only one... I don't like Dr. Lynch as a person.  Dull, boring, and kind of sketchy.
Really neat topic and really neat class!  He gives lots of great examples but the exams are brutally hard, but somehow grades turn out ok in the end if you come prepared and talk.
He was so understanding and helpful.
That last person is "the only one" -- he single handedly helped me to graduate on time.
i feel like i might be the only one, but i didn't like him as a person.
Very nice guy. Well organized, tests straight from notes. He can be very dry, so be prepared. But you do learn a lot, he is good at explaining at student level.
Very helpful!
No Comments
Very difficult and boring class.  But he is clear and a great professor.  Knows his stuff!
Good teacher, really nice guy. Clas can be tedious.
Fun class, makes stuff clear, uses good examples to make you understand the material, and is such a family man you gotta love it.
I didn't think his class was extremely hard. I thought he was nice, and would recomend taking him.
Very tough, but the nicest man you will ever meet, and he adores his kids!
hard as hell, good luck

Marcus is one of those professors that is passionate about what he is teaching and u can tell during the lectures. Even though I am not the strongest in physics, I was invested in his lectures. My advice for the class is know the physics conceptually and do Capa questions until you get sick of it because that's where the exam questions r from.

Marcus goes out of his way for all of his students to make sure that they understand the material. He will literally put down his lunch to help you with your work. He loves physics & clearly loves being an educator. Exams are literally straight from CAPA w/ different numbers. He inspired me to change my major. I would take his class 10 times over.

I liked Dr. Marcus, Analyt 2 is a challenging course but he made it enjoyable. The homework always seemed harder than the lectures but I learned so much by struggling through the homework. I will definitely take him for E & M in the future
tags: ['Clear grading criteria', 'Gives good feedback', 'Lots of homework']

comment: Dr. Marcus is the best lab professor that I have ever had. I am not good at physics by any means, but he was so enthusiastic in the way that he taught so it made me be much more engaged. He is very helpful and is eager to answer questions. Lab experiments were fun and he made them even better. Great sense of humor. 10/10 would recommend.
Professor Marcus is good at explaining things and his lectures are really useful. He does post all the slides on canvas, so you don't really have to go to class.

Marcus is very clear and is very knowledgeable about light and color. However, if you are not a science or math person this is not the easiest gen ed to take. Gives  research paper and homework to offset the test grades.

This guy explained partial derivatives clearer than any professor I've ever had. Half the kids hadn't taken a math class since high school, and he got them from zero-calc to partial derivatives and vector magnitudes in weeks, it was amazing.  I'm a math major so this was old news for me, but he still managed to hold my attention and interest. 10/10

I'll start by saying that I have NEVER been a science or math person. I barely passed Physics in HS. With Marcus, though, he makes everything so simple. He's an AWESOME teacher and I find the stuff actually really interesting. He also has dad humor so that's fun. TAKE HIS CLASS!!!!

He is the most articulate person I have ever known and he gives his students a LOT of his time in and out of office hours. He is VERY clear with what he wants and expects you to give it, so he's a little hard in that respect. That being said, he will help you with a write-up before you turn it in, so it's pretty easy to succeed if you try

Best science teacher I ever had. He knows how to clarify abstract concepts and simplify broad ideas. You can tell he really cares about your performance and if you pay attention to his lecture everything else will fall into place.

If you go to him with specific questions, he will be your best friend. That said, not a super easy class, be prepared to work and think. He'll answer any questions you have and help you get through the class but only after you've tried. Physics majors will do well.

I agree with all of the other comments, classwork does not translate to tests or homework. The class has no structure and the only reason I passed was because of a STRONG background already present in physics. For analytical physics I Freeman is a much better teacher whose tests are much more fair. Do not take this class if you want to learn.

Marcus teaches a class that is for a natural science cor on a whole new different level. His tests are pretty difficult and the only way you can understand the textbook and slides is if you go to class. If you're looking for a science core, don't take him.

TAKE PHYSICS SOMEWHERE ELSE! Although Marcus is a nice guy, he does not teach; he puts up random examples during lectures that are exclusive to other simular problems. I hear he is better than the other guy, so I would take the calss somwhere else.  Loved physics in High School and did well, but I scratched and clawed to pass this course.

Marcus is a good guy but the class itself is way too hard. As a bio major, I had far less trouble with organic chemistry than with physics. The tests averages are embarrassing. Material presented in class and on practice exams is 10 times easier than what shows up on the test. It's brutal. Take physics somewhere else.

Dr. Marcus is tough but very fair. He is really supportive of his students and realizes that it's a difficult class. If you meet with him 1 on 1 and get to know him he can really encourage you and help you out. I highly recommend him!
I enjoy learning Physics but I don't like the way he tests it. That's probably the best way I can rate this guy. Nice guy, but is too smart to be teaching a General Physics class

This class will be really hard no matter who you take it with. Dr. Marcus is a really smart guy who went to Harvard (where he was first in his class) then Stanford. His intelligence is his downfall in teaching because he assumes everyone to get everything as quickly as he does. Both test averages so far have been in the 50s.

Dr. Marcus is clearly a very smart guy, but that doesnt make the class any easier. He teaches assuming that people already have an understanding of physics, which sucks for those who are learning the material for the first time. The homework sets are soooo time consuming.  A terribly difficult class in general, and definitely not good for mornings.

As of 2008, he is no longer a brand new teacher. I felt i should add this, as he has appaently improved since these last posts.  He is very clear, his lectures are right to the point.  His classes are, however, very difficult and time consuming.  but it is not b/c of him, other profs who teach identical classes make it just as hard.  Recomended
Dr. marcus was extremely helpful and a great teacher.  He is great in office hours and really cares about his students suceeding. Plus he is the man.

I only had him for a lab, but he is VERY good at explaining things. I really enjoyed him. he is very willing to help you if you need it. his jokes are subtle, but it make the lab that much more enjoyable.

Had him for Electric Circuit Analysis.  He's a tough but fair professor.  Class notes were good, but he asked you to take the next step on the homeworks.  GREAT IN OFFICE HOURS.  Can't say that enough.  I would have failed the class if I didn't live in his office.  Great.  If you're willing to put in the time, you'll do good in his class. Take him.
He is not that bad. Just go to his office hours, he will be very helpful if you do go and ask questions. But i think his exams are hard, maybe it is because he has a high expectation on his students.

He is a new professor, so he's still finding his way. His notes have little to no relevance to homework or tests, and he is extremely hard to follow as he goes off on irrelevant tangents. I never went to his class and still got an A, so your textbook will be your best friend if you want a good grade.

Don't take anything with him now.  He is new and has no idea what he's doing.  It's very difficult to get anything out of his lectures and the capas/tests have very little if anything to do with the lectures.  Very unclear when presenting the material.

Dr. Marcus is very clear and helpful during his office hours. He is a new professor and still learning to find the best way to teach his students. Overall, he is very good and tries his way to help. I'm taking phys II with him.

Downright RUDE. Terrible professor. He is so unclear about every assignment and would change details last minute after i spent countless hours working on a project. The final project is sent to the school of ed and he gave us no direction at all and then graded it saying I didn't include things that he never said I had to do. Not worth the stress.

Dr. Jones was a cool guy, but unfortunately in this class that only got him so far. He has not answered my emails all semester and he basically makes the students teach themselves through the textbook and their weekly group presentations (You only have to do 2). He posts weekly reading quizzes as well which are kinda hard.

Don't take if possible! The class itself isn't even hard but I did not enjoy his style of teaching. It was unorganized, he would post weekly quizzes on random days, did not answer emails and would change things last minute. Details for a final project were very confusing. He is nice, but I was not a fan of some comments he has made about people..

Do yourself a favor & don't take John Jones. The class itself isn't hard but he's just an absolutely terrible professor. Doesn't answer emails within a reasonable time (if at all), unclear instructions, posts quizzes on random days & doesn't tell us when he's going to, adds assignments last minute & doesn't explain them. One of the worst profs....

Im pretty sure he only taught 3 full classes himself this semester. Each week he had students present the information read from the weeks chapter to the class then gives weekly quizzes on information (not always easy). He grades things about 5 weeks after they were due and gives very little feedback. Overall nice guy, new to this course, sorta easy
Super funny. Only had to participate during my two presentations.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things', 'Hilarious']

comment: You can't understand her and she try's to help and makes it worse.

Every time we had lab she wouldn't do it the way the rest of the lab classes did it so we were always doing it wrong. The point still got across but it was very frustrating. The lab assistant taught the class most times. If you can, avoid taking lab with this professor.

I took gen bio lab with Ifeoma. Honestly this was by far my most enjoyable science class. Ifeoma graded very easily and was super funny and caring. Even with the final presentation she graded super generously.

this professor gave unclear instructions and was extremely disorganized. Many times, she showed up late to lab or disappeared for extended periods of time, leaving students unattended. I feel as if she is a nice person, however, would not wish her as a professor upon my worst enemy.

Professor Ifeoma is a very nice person but not a good lab professor. She can sometimes be rude and very hard to understand. Labs on there own are not too bad, but her unclear instructions made the class 10x harder.

Our exams were super easy, and she tells you exactly what to study. Even on the multiple-choice questions on the exam, you could write an explanation, and she would give you partial credit even if you were wrong. She made groups that you had to sit with the whole semester, which was definitely awkward at times.

I took Yang for Bio 120. She is very sweet and does her best to make us love coming to lab. She is always very open to helping students, and will even sometimes tell you what to study for her exams in Bio 119.
Awesome professor, use the objectives Dr. Yang provides as a reference to what's on her test. Dr. Yang herself is a great lecturer and is able to help if it is requested.

She has a lot of group work in lecture, so it feels much like a highschool or lower level class. The material is extremely easy to learn, and her tests are one of the easiest between all of the sections. SHe is very understanding, and super nice. If you like taking notes and being lectured at I would recommend feisner over her.

Suann Yang is an extremely nice and caring person, though her lectures are not the best if you prefer to listen and take notes. If you love partner work and testing yourself in class, I would recommend Suann Yang.

She is a very easy grader, class was very much like highschool with lots of group work in lecture. The tests were one of the easiest between all sections. She does have an attendance grade though. I would recommend taking bio 2 with her.

Dr. Yang was an extremely easy grader. I think out of all the bio classes she had some of the easiest exams. She does do a lot of group work within lecture, and it feels a little like elementary school, but you can manage through it. I would highly recommend for this class.

Dr.Yang is a great professor! She is very in tuned with her students and provides thorough learning in many different ways. Her teaching feels very high school which can become slow depending on your experience in biology. Overall, I highly recommend her for biology courses!
I love Dr. Yang!
I think she is great, she is very interesting to listen to. Just expect group projects. She is always willing to help and very flexible with work.

She was very helpful when completing the labs and was very welcoming towards questions. She was very personable and did her best to set you up for success. However, she won't just give you the answers, she will try to help you answer it on your own. Overall, she was an amazing lab professor.
She's so amazing and she truly cares for you and your mental health. She wants the best for you and lab was great was her. 10/10 recommend.

I had Professor. Yang for my biostatistics class and she is so amazing. She is very enthusiastic about what she teaches which is nice to see. In her 288 class Rstudio is the basis of the whole class, I was not that great at Rstudio, but was able to catch on so its not that bad at all. Her lectures are so easy and overall would take her again.

I really enjoyed taking ecology with Dr.Yang! She made the course interesting, and she cared for all of her students and her needs. If you ever felt like you were going to get behind or something, she would always extend the deadline for you. Amazing professor, and someone who actually cares about you instead of just being a professor.
Professor Yang is awesome, she is super responsive outside of class and really does want to help you succeed
Dr. Yang is a great professor but she can be tough on you. If you're taking a major-related course with her I would recommend her.
great prof
One of the best profs ive ever had!

Dr. Yang gives a lot of work and can be a tough grader, but she really is there to help you. She always responds to emails quickly and is happy to help with homework during her office hours. A lot of her class is centered around group work- she has group projects that are 20% of the grade. Also be prepared to do the entire class in RStudio.

Prof Yang cares about her students and wants them to do good. I appreciate that she gives a lot of opportunities to raise your grade, but ultimately you receive a greater workload. It was reassuring that even if I flunked an assignment, my grade would not entirely suffer. An A grade is definitely achievable (I was 0.3 away).

She is super accommodating, available, and helpful. What will get you through this class is reaching out and using your resources. It was a heavy workload but easy material so stay on top of your time management and youre good. Shes an amazing professor if you arent busy being mad about your workload

Unreasonable amount of work. Don't take online with this professor, the amount of useless work I had to do took up all of my time for studying for other courses. She makes you write, review, take, and grade your own short response tests. The course isn't even about ecology content because she makes you focus so much on test writing skills.

You have to write, take, and then grade your own tests, FOR A GRADE(This will take you hours). Not to mention the numerous progress reports you have to send her just to tell her you completed another assignment. Do not take this class if it is given online. It will be the most stressful thing, especially when you have to write your own final

I would never recommend Dr. Yang. She is condescending and rude. Unnecessary amount of work. You write, take, and grade your own tests that take HOURS. She is very particular and if things are not done her way, she is judgemental and will tell you you're wrong. Struggles to give compliments to her students or make them feel worthy! Avoid!!!

I absolutely loved the lectures that Dr. Yang gave this past semester. She was so caring and was always available to answer questions during office hours. If you can manage to be lucky enough to have her for freshman biology, take advantage of the opportunity. She offers a great perspective on many concepts that make them easier to learn and absorb

NEVER take ecology with her unless you can get the tests from previous years. She'll talk about something in class for maybe 5 seconds and put an entire page of questions on the test. She literally can't teach and makes the class based off of group quizzes. Really difficult time passing this class and I'm usually an A student, good luck w yang.

While Mrs Yang is a very kind professor her ideas over group work are less than ideal. She will assign people to random groups at the beginning and at the middle point of the semester. Group work sometimes isnt bad but when you get stuck with a bad group it hurts your grade bad. The professor also did nothing as one or two groups had conflicts.

Suann was a good professor, she tends to go into detail on topics because she is very passionate about the material. Lectures are powerpoints mixed with group interaction that tend to be fairly engaging. Definitely a fair, and overall solid professor. Getting an A is not easy but not impossible if you pay attention and study.

The practice test is literally the actually test reworded. Tests are pretty easy even although she makes her own. Lectures are interesting because she applies the material well. Shes really passionate about the class

Dr yang puts a lot of work into instruction. That being said she also makes you fill in the gaps. No dry memorizartion, you must control your learning with lectures as a guide. Tests are straightforward and lectures are dry

There are a lot of quizzes and assignments, which means lots of opportunities to get points. She makes you work, but you will get the grade you deserve for the amount of work you put in. She's very good at entering grades into Canvas as soon as she grades an assignment, so you always know how well you're doing in the class.
Learned a lot, she's as nice as she looks.  Very hot

Professor Baer-Harper is my absolute favorite professor at Geneseo. She is very friendly and will help you anytime you ask. Her classes are engaging and fun, and she's very clear with the material she's teaching. I learned more French with her in one semester than I did in all of high school.

Professor Baer is one of my favorite professors at Geneseo. She is always so happy and excited to teach. I really don't think there is a mean bone in her body. If you are interested in the French speaking world def take this class. There is very little work and Professor Baer is really flexible when there is work.
A very good teacher. She speaks very clearly and has a good sense of humor. Make sure you do the reading though, because she does expect you to know the material throughly.

She is a phenomenal teacher. There is a lot of grammar but that is what she needs to teach to get us ready! She gives hw and you need to study for her tests to do well. She has high expectations and expects you to do your work but she also bends over backwards for her students. I learned so much French with her!

Not sure if the last user failed or something but that last comment could not be further from the truth! She is one of the most helpful professors ever. Study and work hard and you will get rewarded. Slack off, and you shouldn't be at Geneseo to begin with.

Amazing French professor. If you have an opportunity to take a class with her, do it. You not only learn a lot, she makes it fun and interesting as well. Be prepared to work though. Classes are full of activities and there is a large amount of homework. She is very understanding and her tests are not that bad. If you try hard you will can get an A.

She keeps you very interested in the subject matter by doing different teaching styles; however, you have to keep on top of your reading prior to class in order to do well. She'll know if you've done your work or not. Anyway, she is a genuinely nice and fun professor who knows her stuff and wants you too to be successful. I advice you to take her!

Hahn is just strange and can definitely make off-the-cuff comments.  However, he (boringly) talked about like 5 subjects, and for each one, you wrote a 1000-word essay.  He is more than happy to help you during office hours, and for each essay you have, you get 4 weeks' notice before it's due.

Hahn is a little odd, but he's very easy. It's not hard to do well on his papers and he isn't strict about formatting. However, his feedback can be very hard to understand at times. There's only a couple papers and some small assignments. Overall an easy class with a laid back professor.

I took WRTG105 with him, very easy class, not many assignments and you're given a long time to do them. Maybe you'll love this or hate this, but he is very negative in a way, like he just hates on everything we talk about but it can be funny sometimes
Awesome would totally take again
Great professor and lectures are entertaining. Easy workload
He is the definition of a diva. He is very nice and has a good sense of humor. The class was super easy and the papers were very manageable.

Professor Hahn is so funny, and his lectures were great. Attendance isn't mandatory but you sometimes have to catch up on notes. The assignments are fairly easy, and he grades fairly. I'd take the class again; Professor Hahn is great but sometimes his humor is very dry.

This class doesn't necessarily "require attendance", however, you won't want to miss any! He may suggest some books/textbooks, however, none are required. I loved his sarcastic sense of humor, he kept me engaged the entire hour and fifteen minutes of this lecture. Most assignments are papers between 60-200 words. I highly recommend this course.

Loves to go off topic during lecture but they don't often apply to the papers you have to write. Paper prompts are vague and you essentially write your own topic. He loves to leave passive aggressive non-constructive comments. He does not require attendance but pays attention to who shows up and factors that in when grading your assignments

Not really a class I was interested in, but I still enjoyed it. He had many participation opportunities, and was pretty flexible for grading as long as you met the criteria. Super nice guy though, pretty funny too.

He is vague with prompts for the papers, and pretty blunt and sarcastic, so be mindful of his tone. He's still a really intriguing lecturer, even though he opened the first day of class with, "You don't really need to show up." I still attended all of the lectures because of how interesting they were. Fair grader on papers.
Awesome professor, very funny and fun lectures. Easy assignments

This was the second class I took with Professor Hahn and it was great! There aren't too many assignments, just a few quizzes and some short writing assignments but he's a pretty easy grader. The best prof Ive ever had. Hes sarcastic and hilarious. There are papers, with unlimited rewrites. Hahn is a great guy. His lectures were interesting and entertaining. Very easy work

He is amazing, chill, nice to talk to outside of class too.
Having Hahn for INTD was the best choice I have ever made. He made learning about conspiracy theories entertaining and he wasn't that tough of a grader.

Super goated

Turner is absolutely fantastic and one of the better teachers I have ever had. Funny, makes class interesting, very accessible to people who may not be political science majors. I can not recommend this class enough.

Prof Turner is extremely engaging, personally as someone who despises lectures he's entertaining and informative, with more of a focus on discussion than an actual lecture. Easy grader, but groups suck and get ready to write like 6 15-page papers and three term papers. At least he's entertaining.

Great professor, fair grader and doesn't expect too much from students. I would retake comparative politics with him.
Great teacher. Wanted to go to class and enjoyed every lecture.

Professor Steinhauer is really laid back and chill. He's a super caring professor and tries to make class as entertaining as possible.

So, If you are really into astronomy (which I am) then you are going to love Professor Steinhauer. He gives great lectures, cares about your mental health, and makes sure he is able to meet with you whenever! He is the best! I will advise that you should only take the course if astronomy interests you, cause it can be boring for Non-astronomers.

Professor Steinhauer was very boring if you do not find astronomy interesting. I took this class because I signed up for classes late during registration and would not take it again. Be prepared to study and then not have that material on the test. The TA sessions saved me and I would have never finished homework if it wasn't for them.
Chill dude whos passionate about his teaching. Tests are difficult though and people usually average in the 70s.

The class itself was difficult. There is A LOT of math in this class so if that's not your thing, then drop it. Other than that, I liked this class, even if the tests were bonkers. But yeah, one of the easier science classes in my opinion. The professor himself is not that bad, but the material is the hard part.
he was good, it was a big lecture so it's easy to get lost in that but he loves what he's teaching. go to class because you get credit for showing up.

Steinhauer is a great professor. He's understanding if you can't come to class or submit an assignment late, very easy to communicate with. The classes themselves can be difficult. ASTR105 was difficult because it was a hard subject- if you're not good at physics, don't take it. But Steinhauer os a good professor.
I loved him! Truly amazing and helpful and just all around nice guy

Astronomy 110 with Professor Steinhauer is math-intensive. Each CAPA was difficult and took a while to achieve a decent score. He was approachable during his office hours and helped where he could. So, if physics or mathematics isn't your thing, then I'd avoid the trouble. His exams were straightforward, and he gave us plenty of time to take them.

Lectures were posted on Canvas and followed TR schedule. There were weekly CAPAs that were pretty easy, and tests were based on lecture notes, so lectures are important. The content of the class is super interesting, and if you like math and physics it will be more enjoyable. He has office hours for 2 hours twice a week. Easy gen ed class.
