comment: Very nice guy and willing to help in office hours if you go to them. Exams are based on homework questions but are still difficult. There are tophat questions daily so it is important to attend lectures
tags: ['Accessible outside class', 'Graded by few things', 'Lecture heavy']

comment: Great guy! Powerpoints posted online, but you need to go to class to fill in missing things. He really knows his stuff, and tries to get you to understand it. But the class and subject were very difficult for a 100 class, you really have to like physics

Very hard class, professor is accessible but since the class has so few grades and tests are so heavy you have to be on top of everything to pass. Would not recommend taking unless you enjoy physics and like a challenge. Must study.
tags: ['Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Graded by few things']

comment: Enjoyable class, and Steinhauer is incredible enthusiastic about the topic. There is an amount of calculations that you have to do for the class, and I'm terrible at all aspects of physics, but I did manage. He breaks down material well and makes the materials digestible. I would recommend him if you need to take a natural science.

Prof. Steinhauer is by far my favorite teacher at Genny. He is super down to earth and is really there to help students learn. The class is harder than I thought it would be for a 100-level but its because of the content not the teacher. He is VERY approachable and helpful. He truly cares about his job and his students. 10/10 best teacher yet.
Good guy decent prof, god Nat. sci. gen ed to take if you aren't good with sciences. Not easy, but easier than most Nat. Sci. gen eds. uses tophat for participation

Gave him the tag "gives pop quizzes" because he uses Top Hat, which basically quizzes for your participation grade. His lectures are pretty clear-cut; I took him for my Nat. Science Gen. Ed course. I feel that science majors would definitely do much better. ASTR110 was the easiest of all the science courses I've taken here at SUNY Genseseo, however

Aaron shouldn't have taught Physics 223. His weekly quiz was all about how you memorized the answers of problems from the homework so he even didn't bother to give enough time students to solve it in the class. He also has failed to set the difficulty of tests. First exam was too easy and the average of the final was 47%. The worst physics class.
He's a really guy. Engages the class well but he uses TopHat in his lectures. The TopHat isn't really helpful but it makes sure you're in class.

He has a love for science and it shows in his lectures. You don't really need to take notes because he posts them all online. Tests are a fair game. If you pay attention and study, you'll do great. Mastering astronomy stuff isn't really on tests.

I am NOT a science person, and unfortunately Dr. Steinhauer didn't do much to change my mind about science.  His lectures were occasionally entertaining, though often mind-boggling, and his handwriting is illegible.  Seems like a fun guy, and he puts jokes on the exams.  My distaste for the class had more to do with the content than with him.

Generally easy and exceptionally interesting science class, though the lab tends to be a bit more difficult than the lecture, depending on your TA. Steinhauer's love for Astronomy is immediately apparent and very contagious. All around best professor I've ever taken a class with at Geneseo. Would recommend for absolutely anyone.

Steinhauer's class was both informative and engaging. He brings an enthusiastic presence to the lecture hall every day that makes students more willing to learn. Very do-able class as long as you attend lectures, review sessions, and do the practice exams! I would highly recommend him if you need a natural science core.

Professor Steinhauer is such a sweet and funny man, I loved his lecture. He made it so very interesting, and gave great material to take notes on. As long as you study, the tests (multiple choice) are easy, especially as he gives out practice exams and gives a review session to go over them before tests. You will need a PRS clicker.
Fantastic professor. Lectures are clear and engaging. He has an intense excitement for astronomy and shares it with all of his students.

He is a great teacher and person! His class is challenging though if you're not a math or science person. If you need this for a natural science core and don't enjoy math or science expect to be going to get tutoring. But his class is always intriguing and if you take it seriouslyou can do well.

If you need a core natural science, astronomy is the way to go. Steinhauer is an awesome professor. He makes the class interesting, he makes jokes, and all of the homework (once a week) is online. I used the textbook maybe four times. Three midterms and a final, but they average together. Easy A.
Prof. Steinhauer is a great guy!
Steinhauer is a good prof but the tests are relatively hard to get an A on. I found that a B+ was relatively easy to achieve but I put in more work for this class than I wanted to slash intended to.

Lab with Dr. Steinhauer is awesome. He's laid back and really chill. He knows physics and goes out of the way to make sure that your data is how is should be. There are weekly quizzes and often a couple of things due the next lab. Some assignments are more challenging than others. Lab notebooks are collected and graded on very picky things.

I love Professor Steinhauer. He's genuinely passionate about astronomy and makes the material fun and interesting. He's pretty hilarious, too. The tests are ridiculously easy, and short. Only one homework assignment per week, and it's online. If you're looking for a pretty easy science gen ed, take this!

He is a very approachable professor, but the class itself is rather difficult. Unless you have a good grasp on physics and have an interest in astronomy, it's not worth taking the class. The tests are rather difficult, but Steinhauer is funny and makes attending class worthwhile.

You people don't know what the heck you are talking about.  This was one of the most worthless classes I've taken.  Notes given online and 0.05% addition in class.  My grade suffered from attending class and listening to his drivel.  Tested trivial facts and spent entire classes on topics that weren't tested.  Waste of time!!

I just had him last semester and all I can say is that his class was just plain fun. He is an awesome lecturer and he is also extremely helpful to any student who needs help. After that class, I want to T.A. his labs. Awesome

I would highly recommend this class to anyone who needs to get their Natural Science credit. I would also recommend this class to anyone who was ever wanted to learn about the stars. This teacher was amazing, and one of the most helpful in Geneseo.  He taught his own review sessions making studying for the tests simple and effective.

Steihauer is a awesome teacher. Very passionate about the subject matter and an obvious expert in his field. He's extremely helpful when you go for help. He's also very involved with the school - taking part in many events like a chicken wing eating contest held in the Fall. I highly recommend his class especially for the natural science credit.

such a nice guy, always willing to help, going to office hours helped me out a lot.  Steinhauer is is a great teacher just and you can tell he loves astronomy so much. The math section of the class can be pretty difficult if thats not your thing.
Yeah he's attentive to the students but I wouldn't recommend it for core unless your a big science/math person, seriously.  The lab depends on who your TA is b/c mine was ridiculously unhelpful.

Steinhauer is extremely motivated and dedicated to his subject and his students. If you need a science to fulfill your requirement this is one of the most interesting. Geology I hear is easier but I would take Astronomy over it anytime. Labs are not that bad. No Pre-Lab or outside lab meetings. Outside work is minimal. Class attendance is required.

This is the easiest science course you could possibly take. All his lectures come right out of the book and he posts his powerpoints on mycourses before class to take notes on. If you miss class all you really need to do is look over the powerpoint you missed and read in the book.  tests aren't so bad if you go to review and do the practice test.

Huge lecture, never went, got a B in the class. Tests aren't too bad if you study and have common sense (Sun is a star, Earth a planet, those sorts of things) Three tests and a final all worth 20% and a weekly online homework assignment also worth 20%. Go ahead, get that science credit out of the way...
Funny and entertaining.  Class is fairly easy if you do the work.

Do not take this class if you are looking for an easy science core! You HAVE to go to class to get a good grade. If you go everyday and take good notes you will be fine. The online homeworks were annoying and took sooo long. It was an ok class, he is a really nice guy and is pretty funny, the class was too early and if you miss class youre screwed.
He's so enthusiastic it's adorable!! Really easy and understanding grader, always overcompensates if he makes a mistake. Take him if you can!!!

Do not take this class if you want an easy science core! It has some very challenging material.  The online homework was annoying and took forever, and the tests were extremely difficult. Steinhauer was not very helpful in office hours. The in class clickers were fun though, and can give you extra credit. Go to review sessions before the tests!
This class is really easy if you go. He keeps you involved. Makes large lecture seem like small class. Very entertaining.
Great Teacher.  Everything is very clear.  He tries to make class fun.  He is excited and interested in Astronomy.  Be wary of your lab teacher though.

This class was really easy, but you do have to study for the tests if you want to do well. Know your notes, and you'll be fine. I took his class the first semester he was here, so I don't know how he's changed since then, but I thought he was a decent teacher for this level class.

Don't take this class if you're looking for an easy core science! There is so much information and Steinhauer includes a lot that youre not even tested on. Unless you're really interested in this science then go for it but if not, don't waste your time with this course and the professor.

I reccomend this class to everyone who needs a natural science credit. it's way more engaging than sitting through a stupid bio or chem course. do yourself a favor and take this class. i easily got a B with NO READING except some skimming before tests. also, take notes instead of staring at slides, you'll learn it better.

Steinhauer is awesome. His lectures are clear and well presented. He's a really nice guy, gives a break due to the length of the class. Test aren't to bad, homework is easy. A background in physics or an interest in astronomy will help you.

Really nice guy, tries to keep lectures interesting at times moves a little too fast through the notes, but is very approachable. tests are easy to do okay on (if you study!) but damn near impossible to do great on.(expect B range unless you put tons and tons of time in) If physics is your thing and you are interested, give it a try.

Really nice guy, it helps a lot to keep up with the readings. He makes valient attempts to make the class interesting with pictures and music. Hes young and pretty easy-going, good class to fill the natural science core.Its funny sometimes cause he knows jack squat about physics, just like you!

Aaron Steinhauer is a great professor and a really nice guy to boot. Geneseo has not ruined him yet! He brings in everything from beautiful pictures to hilarious songs to class. Sometimes the concepts get tough, but he is readily available to explain them. Take a course with him!!!

steinhauer was really good for lab. he's an astronomer not a physicist, so when we say "why does it work that way?" he just says "I have no clue!" and laughs. it's hilarious. I would definately recommend him for anything. He's also only like 30, and likes when you call him Aaron.

class can get boring, but notes are online incae you fall asleep. homework isn't too bad, work on it with others and get 100 everytime.  tests aren't too bad, just study!!  he's a good guy, and has a great sence of humor.  he's always willing to help you out if you need it, but wont just give you the answer.

I'll just say this: Astronomy is cool.  When I was a kid I was very interested in the stars.  Steinhauer is a very funny guy and explains things very well.  The class is a bit easier for me since I think its cool, but you cannot deny that Steinhauer is a good teacher.

He makes the class really interesting.  If you take your notes and do the homeworks then you should have no problem getting an A in this class.  If you're looking to get your core out of the way this is the class to take.

its an easy class if you have any sommon sense and/or took any earth science class in high school/middle school, theres A LOT of dumb people that take the class and for some reason they always talk even though they say some of the dumbest things i've ever heard, stienhauer's a good guy, he knows his stuff and he puts up with all the morons
Steinhauer is a nice guy, astronomy is not a nice guy...just read the text book, his tests are based on the notes and can get very detailed. the CAPA hw is not liek the tests

Basically just don't bother with taking astronomy unless you have some weird interest.  He means well but you really have to do alot of outside work...read alot/outline on your own.  Class isn't too exciting.
Really funny guy, good lectures. If you read along with the book you'll do fine. Extra help he is always available

Hes a good guy and means well but sometimes cant explain the material. If you are willing to do a little extra work (read and take notes on the text on your own) and really review the notes on your own time u will do well, otherwise u might have some trouble. In his office hours he wants u to answer your own questions. It all depends on the student

Who writes a review in the first month of class? To offset your unreasonably low rating, I'm giving him a 5.  You have serious problems if you cant handle ASTR 100, maybe u should transfer to a different college.
Very boring class. He's unorganized and confuses himself at times. Very unhelpful, never take astro 100 with him.

Professor Fallon treated this 100 level class like a 400 level class and expected analysis on par with English majors from a class full of mostly STEM majors. This made this class very difficult, but I experienced a large amount of growth from this approach and would take a class with him again.

I've taken Shakespeare and Milton with Prof. Fallon.  He is an amazing professor, and strong discussion leader.  If you do the reading and participate, there is SOOOO much to learn from him.  He's passionate about the readings and super caring.  When I was out for 2 weeks with a concussion, he did everything he could to help me stay on track.

comment:
Professor Fallon is one of the sweetest, smartest professors I have had at Geneseo. I took a class with him last semester and his organization of the class is the same, two papers, an assignment, and lots of pop quizzes (don't worry they aren't too difficult). Class discussions are super fun and interesting, like a book club! 
-grade last sem: B+

Professor Fallon is such a great person, but his class is very difficult if you are not paying attention every minute. He would give quizzes every week on readings, and encourages participation. His feedback on papers was not the best as it never elaborated specifically on what to work on. However, he is a very caring and passionate person!

comment: I loved Prof Fallon as a person, but as a professor not so much. Graded very harshly on the papers we had, and although he gave "feedback" you could never really tell what he was trying to say. If you asked him what you could do to improve, he would talk to you for 10 minutes and not even answer the question.Very caring person, but frustrating prof

Fallon gave helpful feedback on all of my papers and his lectures were pretty laid-back as well. Attendance is graded, but I maybe went once a week and still got a more-than generous grade on it. He is understanding and a great professor to take if you are trying to satisfy a gen-ed/other requirement.

Professor Fallon is a very sweet and caring professor overall. His assignments are not too hard, and you can always ask questions if you have them. His feedback is also extremely helpful and thorough. I always felt comfortable speaking up in class as he encourages participation, but never forces anyone to talk. Take his class, you won't regret it!

I really enjoyed this class, you get what you put into it. I was a bit of a slacker but also volunteered here and there and always completed my papers on time. His feedback and grades are very helpful and expected based on effort and participation in class. He is a very kind & sweet professor but does not force you to apply yourself or pariticpate.

The final and midterm are very hard. He doesn't like to give grades over a B. He is overall a nice teacher, but be prepared to read a lot outside of class. Overall day to day class is not hard papers are though. He will help you out if you need it, but don't expect it to earn you anything over a B+.

comment: Dr. Fallon is a great professor, very knowledgeable on Shakespeare's works and his life. You can tell that this topic is something he really enjoys. You have to do a sonnet recitation which he works into the class discussion, a couple of papers and a couple of discussion posts on the readings. Not too bad. He made reading Shakespeare enjoyable.

Doctor Fallon is a fantastic addition to Geneseo English staff. Shakespeare isn't easy, but Fallon makes the content extremely accessible through insightful class discussions and great paper feedback. You will be reading a lot of Shakespeare and writing a bunch too, but the class is well worth it. Fallon really cares and wants you to succeed.
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', 'So many papers']

comment: Very comprehensive and engaging class. He's very enthusiastic and appears interested in the subject he teaches, and this evokes that type of feeling in students. The class was run like an informal seminar. The feedback on essays is extremely thorough and helpful, and is probably he most impressive feedback I've received in my academic career.

Akman is hands-down the most influential professor I've ever had. He is endlessly brilliant, but so approachable. He makes it so easy to relate to unfamiliar ideas he's a champion of making every class and point relevant to our lives today. I've never been so impressed. He values student input. His accent is beautiful, and he is hilarious.

Akman is really intelligent, very passionate, and fair. However, for someone who is a proponent of contrapuntal readings and the subaltern, we read mainly male-centric and male-written works which was frustrating. Also, his quizzes were my downfall even though I always read. Overall though, a great class. I would definitely suggest him.

Great teacher! I loved every single one of his lectures, I would leave knowing a great deal more about the word. You need to take an active role in this class, he will respect you for participating, and doing the readings, not too difficult but I will definitely will be recommending him to other people in the future!
He is very smart and knowledgeable. I learned a lot about the world in his class. He was very helpful and friendly. The readings were a bit too much, though.

Akman was good in that he tried to globalize HUM, but he was extremely unrealistic (added 5 books to syllabus), acted quite childish when people weren't participating (nonsense quizzes), was a significantly harder greater than Cope (they co-taught), and he was very intimidating during office hours. I wouldn't recommend.

Professor Moore-Ryan was a great professor! He can be a little monotone but he seems to enjoy what he is teaching. He grades well and accepts late work with no penalty (if its only a day or 2) which is a huge plus! Attendance is MANDATORY and is part of your grade so keep that in mind.

Professor Ryan is the kindest professor I have had so far. His feedback was always positive and helpful. He is accessible outside of class, and is always willing to help. His classes are rather repetitive, and can get boring, but overall the class was interesting.

Prof. Ryan was really sweet and is probably one of the best professors you can get as a freshman. His class is super easy and you don't have to buy a lot of textbooks, but it can get really boring at times. If you ever have a problem, never hesitate to reach out to him as he is always there to help. Use your resources kids!
Great professor. Easy A and very little work. Speak up in class and you'll be fine. A little monotone but has good intentions :)
Professor Ryan is very nice and understanding, the course is very easy as long as you read the material, there is a couple of papers and the quizzes are all on the material

If you want an easy and interesting INTD, I would take Professor Ryans course. As long as you follow the prompts and keep up with the quizzes he gives once in a while, then the class is an easy A. He does take attendance but it doesn't count much for your grade. He really is the nicest guy ever though really recommend taking his course!
An amazing professor! Highly recommend! Easy class, he outlines everything clearly!
Very genuine guy, just do the work and hell more than likely give you an awesome grade. He is very easy to talk to as well. Highly recommend Professor Ryan
Prof Ryan is a great professor who cares about his students. He is very understanding and will respond quickly and kindly to emails. Definitely take from him he is the nicest
Such a great and understanding professor. So respectful and cares about his students. Always looks for your best interest

Professor Ryan is an amazing professor to take as a freshman. He is very kind and flexible, especially during COVID. The workload is very light and he's an easy grader. I highly recommend taking him!!!!

comment: He is a easy teacher he just speaks very monotone so if you take him be ready for that. Hes very understanding and for covid attendance wasnt needed but if you can show up to his class. The work load is very little to nothing. Recommend if you want a easy A.
Show up to class. Do the papers, easy grader. You can hand in stuff late without severe consequences. He is understanding, good dude.
took him or intd-105 writing seminar and is extremely understanding and class and readings are simple and easy. he takes attendance seriosuly so go to class!!

Ryan is a nice guy but his lectures are really dry and speaks in a monotone way. Reads are sometimes rather long and boring but some are interesting. However its easy to get an A if you do the readings. Overall I was very bored in his class and probably wouldnt take him again unless I absolutely had to.

I am convinced that anyone that complains about Dr. Mapes or her twin sister are people who dropped out of the history major or will drop out of the history major. She does not require anything more than what every history professor requires. I am also convinced that she literally only receives bad ratings because she is soft-spoken and passive.

This Mapes has more readings than the other Mapes usually, but she is incredibly understanding with anything you are unable to do. She gives great feedback and is incredibly warm-hearted. If you listen to her you are guaranteed to get a good grade. She made me so much more comfortable with primary sources and as a history major in general.

Dr Mapes easily became one of my favorite professors after taking 302 with her. Her assignments prepare you very well for the major paper at the end of the course, and she is always willing to help. She provides a large amount of time for you to work on the final paper and structures it very well. She is also a very sweet woman. 100% recommend!

Dr Mapes was a very fair professor. She was easy to reach and always willing to help when you struggled. There were a decent amount of readings, and the classes were mainly discussions of the readings and tips for writing the smaller and the major essays. She doesn't always take attendance, but it would be hard to pass if you don't come to class.
Super nice and understanding. Class is very discussion based. She makes sure the class is prepared for the 3 paper assignments and the final research paper as well.

Dr. Mapes was super helpful for 302. It has a lot of reading and writing and the research paper due at the end was not easy but I knew I could also get help with whatever I needed. I also liked the fact that this class is all discussion which makes it a lot more interesting. Learned a lot about research and writing and also women's history.

This class objective was learning to write an academic paper and the structure of the class is perfect for it.
First, you will read long academic papers to see how they are written, then there will be short essays to practice and the final 12-13 pages academic paper. This class is mostly discussion-based. 
This professors is nice and understanding

comment: Just a heads up the class is set up as 3 five page minimum research papers then a 12-15 page final independent research paper. She is not an incredibly difficult grader but definitely need to put in effort and know the content.

comment: This class is extremely participation heavy, so beware. You'll need to talk in class to get a good grade. Other than that, the first few weeks is a lot of reading and writing, and then you write your final research paper. Not the hardest class or professor. I feel like she gives good criticism and is a good teacher for this class.

This class was my first level 300 and I thoroughly enjoyed it, as difficult as it was. This course is very reading intensive, with a weekly quiz for the first several weeks. There are also about 4-5 essays prior to the big research paper at the end of the term. Mapes gives very helpful feedback, and makes you want to improve.

Okay heres the thing... I took this class in a 2.5 hour block and it was terrible. I think it wouldn't have been so bad if it was split up throughout the week, but that being said Mary lectured for most of the class and it was not fun. She assigns inconsistent amounts of reading each week so be prepared for high or low amounts of reading.
Expects you to be as knowledgeable as her, does not care about her students. Worst grader Ive ever come across. Quiz every single class. All tests are solely essays.

comment: She gives you an outline before class starts which is very helpful for the 2 tests.  If you write the outline with some details on the tests you'll get a good grade. Mention the movies on the test to get a better grade. Quiz almost every class, easy as long as you read the textbook. One paper,  write it early and she'll go over it with you.
The absolute worst. I have nothing else to say.

She grades the tests, which are essays only, as though you should know as much as she does. The textbook she requires you to use is awful and doesn't relate to the tests just the quizzes. The class is extremely boring. I sincerely recommend you fulfill your history gen ed elsewhere.

I honestly don't like history very much but Mapes is so interested in it she gets me interested. Make sure you can either write or type quickly because she has a lot of notes and doesn't post online. If you read and take good notes you will be fine. I really enjoy her lectures and it's a 2 1/2 hour lecture, she gives you a break in the middle too

So far she seems pretty easy. The first test didn't seem too bad but I don't know my grade yet. She's been through a lot but the chair of the history department told me she used to be a good teacher and she's taught at other schools. Her twin sister works here, too...if you think you're seeing double, you're not. All in all a nice lady.

Even though attendance isn't taken, you definitely need to go to lectures. He makes it fun and actually applies content to real world things so we can grasp them. He's funny and upbeat and is always good to answer questions. If you go to lectures, take lots of notes, and review in the slideshows, you're going to be just fine, especially on tests.

I love mounts. My favorite professor in Geneseo. He explains each topic very well, uses examples, and sometimes brings things in to give you a better understanding with a demonstration. There is a lot of material to learn and understand. 4 exams, and a quiz per chapter (online). More of a neuroscience course than psych. But very interesting class!
he talks so fast i can't pay attention

He's a really kind professor and always engages with the classes + explains things clearly. Exams are worth most of your grade but aren't hard if you go to class and study. He also offers extra credit and weekly online quizzes to boost your grade

Mounts is a really great professor and always engages with the class plus explains things well. Exams are worth a huge chunk of your grade but are pretty easy if you study. There are also weekly open note quizzes online to boost your grade.

He's really nice and definitely likes teaching the class. He tells the most painful dad jokes but it's sweet. Worst part is he's kind of boring to listen to and the test are most of the weight of the class so if you don't do well on tests this won't be your class. There are mini quizzes that offset it a little and 5 extra credit points available.

This class was graded by 4 tests and weekly quizzes which are open book. The class itself can be kinda boring but he does a good job of making it interesting. Study the vocab in the slides, write notes on the slides, and study the studies. Textbook is required but not necessary at all. He's a very nice guy.

mounts is a quirky guy he made lecture interesting, made jokes and was kind. tests r fair, and he responds quick to emails. he gave a lot of examples in class and does practice problems that help for the test. hes caring def would take again

Very difficult. Love mounts as a person but not a professor, goes sooo fast and just read lecture slides. Does not explain well. Should not be a psych course. It is basically advance cognitive psych but 100x harder. Basically when he goes through the slides he acts like we already knows

DO NOT take this course if you aren't interested in neuroscience. This is extremely neuroscience heavy and should NOT be a psych course. He is an ok prof but moves fast and expects us to know way too much info per exam. Each exam is worth 100 points which is insane. He doesn't drop the lowest one or curve even tho most students almost fail.

I cannot explain how angry this guy makes me. I am writing this in class instead of screaming. He moves SO QUICKLY through the slides that you simply have no chance of being able to write everything down AS WELL AS everything that he is spewing. I've never been so consistently angry with someone in my life. You have no chance to understand anything

Lectures were boring at times but he tried to keep the class engaged a lot. Weekly quizzes on Brightspace that if you do good on help your grade. I would recommend the class for sure, easy enough if you study for the tests.

Not the easiest class to pay attention to but he tries his best by doing in class examples of the notes. The notes are very broad and a bit difficult to understand. Tests weren't the worst but class averages high 70s-80s on most tests. Found him to be cold and hard to approach. Overall, not a super hard class just put a lot of effort in studying.

4 tests and some little quizzes are your whole grade. He reads the slides to you very quickly and I had a hard time keeping up often. But if you go back through and take time to study you will do well. In my opinion you just do not need the textbook at all. Just know what's on the slides.

Attendance is not mandatory, but try your best to go to class. His lectures aren't boring, and makes the concepts learned in class easily understandable, which I appreciate. Only graded by exams and unit quizzes (quizzes are online) but he posts the slides and all of the information needed to study is in those. Highly recommend his class!

comment: I really liked having him, it's important to keep up with the material because the tests have a lot of information. You don't really need the textbook; all the information is in the slides he has. He makes sure to have accessible office hours and is pretty entertaining.
Gives great feedback if you have questions and his lectures are very in-depth, so do not miss too many classes. He also does reviews before tests, ATTEND THEM! They are very helpful.

He was a nice guy, but not the best prof. He claims you can't pass if you don't go to lecture but he really just reads off of the slides so you can do that whenever. However, if you have a question I think he makes sure to explain it well enough to understand it and will use good examples so going to class can still be useful.

Only read off of board, claimed that you needed to read the textbook but even when I did I still did awful on the tests. You have chapter quizzes that are worth a good part of your grade, and are only 5 points each. Don't take this class if you don't need to

comment: genuinely a nice guy and easy to work with but the lectures and tests contain so much material and its really hard to follow in class sometimes. don't buy the textbook, you don't need it.

Mounts is a little odd but very easy class if you just go to lecture and study for the tests which are extremely straightforward and everything on the test is in the slides. Nice guy easy class made cog pretty interesting.

Lecture material can be difficult but tests are easy, never read the textbook and did fine. Mounts gets frustrated when nobody participates. Going to lecture is very helpful in understanding the material, you can skip the textbook if you want to just listen in lecture. Honestly was not difficult to get an A i totally recommend Mounts

He claims the textbook is required, just took his course in F23, never used it once (not worth the buy). He posts all his notes online and lectures all class, but you won't pass unless you show up to a majority of the classes. He only does small quizzes per chapter and then exams every 3 chapters. No work outside of that. Good professor though!

I love Professor Mounts. He's super easy to talk to and will actually help you if you ask him questions. He got to know everyone in the class and made it super engaging because of that. Show up to class and participate and you'll do great.

You are only graded on the 4 tests you take in class and 12 chapter quizzes that have 5 questions that are .5 points. He only reads off the Power Points in class, which he'll post onto BrightSpace. Honestly, you'll be better by teaching yourself the material and you'll have a higher chance of passing his class.

Not much to say other than he was a bit boring and rambled a lot. Its fairly easy to pass his class because the tests are about 50 questions and only worth 2.5 points each. Chapter quizzes help your grade as well and he drops the two lowest.

Prof. Mounts is a very good teacher as long as you actually show up to class. He makes lectures fun and for some of the experiments he goes over he will actually "do them" on you and it'll help you understand it better. The tests are kinda hard because it's a lot of information but he always has a study session the class before the exam.

Couldn't understand why about 60% of his students is all of his sections not just my class were failing the class. When we would ask him questions he would get annoyed that we didn't understand, but all he really did was recite what was on his PowerPoints. He definitely knows the material, but doesn't know how to explain it to his students.

Decent person, but told us it wasn't his fault that 70% of his students were failing the class. I barely made it through. Exams are very difficult and I failed almost all of them. He goes very fast in lectures and it is hard to process everything and take notes. Also there is way too much on all of his slides. Weekly quizzes too.

I don't want to leave a bad review because Professor Mounts is very nice and I enjoyed the class as much as I could seeing as I was not interested in the material. He does go through the lectures very fast but he posts them which helps. I thought the tests were hard but I never read the textbook. If you study and review the material you'll do fine.

This is difficult because Dr. Mounts is a great teacher and makes the material a lot more accessible and enjoyable, but the class truly is a beast. The ten page paper is a little frightening, but the biggest issue is being graded on only THREE exams. 3 exams + one paper is your entire grade, and will assault your GPA. But it's good fun! I guess...

He has quizzes for each chapter of the textbook which is fine, however, the tests all feel like he is performing a psychological experiment on you. It's a good way to learn the material but an awful way to test, especially with the material he teaches. If you don't do well with in person scantron tests or get distracted easily take a different prof

I really liked Mounts, but his class is not by any means an easy A though. Put some work in and he will help you out with extra credit. Go to class!!! So many people do not attend class and do not do well. The concepts were interesting to me and I learned a lot. He is funny and entertaining and uses demo's to help you understand which I love.

This class is one of the hardest I have ever taken, and Professor Mounts does nothing to help with that. He talks fast, does not go over material well, and is useless with extra help. I have emailed him multiple time for extra credit and he told me that there is nothing he could do. I had to teach the material to myself because he did nothing.

He is definitely a really nice professor! He cares to make sure his students understand the material. There are mini chapter quizzes online after each chapter but they are 10 questions worth 5 points for the entire quiz. The exams are not terrible just know what each person in the chapter experimented & what they found from their experiment.

One of those few professors that legitimately works to make classes fun and interesting- the tests are extremely easy if you take proper notes and study them a fair amount. My only issue is he seems to go through the slides quite fast and they have a whole lot of info so make sure to condense what you write (the tests are easier than you think).

Great class. Book was good for reference but not really needed. 2 exams, a term paper, and a presentation. Nothing was hard, class was interesting and the paper and presentation are up to you. Very available for emails, office hours, and after class. I have annoyed the absolute crap out of this man and he really doesn't care. Chillest psych prof.

I have no idea what hes like for in person classes, as Ive only had him online. He was kind of useless in the sense that he waited for us to have questions rather than actively teaching like other professors would. But he isnt a tough grader, and doesnt assign much work. Class also wasnt mandatory, so that all helped

Asynch, so no lectures just posted powerpoint slides with annotations. You do need the book for weekly chapter quizzes that aren't timed and he drops the worst 2. Otherwise it's based on exam grades only. He responds quickly to emails and does weekly review sessions and has q&a google docs. Was very nice and worked with me to take my final early.

Took this class during covid so it was fully asynchronous. Optional reviews once a week but you have to have questions to ask. He was friendly and easy to approach when I joined them which was good. This took a lot of reading, both the textbook and the lecture powerpoints which took a while. If you really read youll do well.

I loved this class! It was all asychronous (no videos, just slides with annotations) which was an adjustment because it takes hours to write down everything, but if you go to his weekly review sessions and/or office hours, he will explain the material to you thoroughly. It is a fun and easy class if you put in the WORK.

Mounts didn't do much for online during a pandemic, just assigned chapters & quizzed/tested us on them. Posted slides with some notes that were decent, nothing special. When asked to record & post a review session that I would miss due to work he denied which felt unreasonable. Could've posted/had zoom lectures for each chapter to deliver material.

He is an awesome guy and always willing to help. He is funny and all the demos during class help to fully understand concepts. He keeps class interesting. He does go fairly fast during lectures so be prepared to read and write the notes ahead of time so you can listen and move along with him during class.

Dr. Mounts is always willing to help his students, whether it's in office hours or in class. It is annoying, however, when he lets us out early the first couple classes after an exam, until its the day before the exam and we still haven't started a chapter on the exam.

He's a great guy says M'kay a lot so be aware that you will feel like your in an episode of South Park. His exams are fair but study the details, not just the big topics. He hints during class what the short answer questions will revolve so go to class. Pay attention to what he draws on the board that will be included in the short answer section.

Dr. Mounts is okay.  The topic is very challenging but the student choosing to take Cognitive Psychology with Dr. Mounts could choose worse.  Dr. Mounts is not the worse Cognitive Psychology professor at SUNY Geneseo.

Dr. Mounts is awesome. He's funny and his lectures are interesting. If you're confused, he will gladly answer questions (even if that does mean pushing back the test 2 weeks). His tests are fair but you have to study

Dr. Mounts is really nice but boring. He tries to be entertaining though. Lectures are him going over the powerpoint. The tests are predictable because he gives you the 5 possible essay questions before the test and lets the class vote one out, then one is chosen randomly as the test question on test day. Very fair. Can get extra credit.

3 tests and 2 5-6 page papers. Material is challenging but pretty interesting. There's a lot of memorization involved and you must take tests seriously to do well but with adequate preparation and his typical curve on exams, it is possible to do well.  Explanations of material in class was helpful in comprehension.  Don't really need to read book.

352 is a difficult class to begin with, but Dr. Mounts is there to help you every step of the way. He is always willing to go over papers with you and help you out with the stats you do in class. He made the class enjoyable. He is one of my favorite professors in the psych department, and I would definitely recommend taking 352 with him.

Dr. Mounts is a great professor. I think the most important thing to do is go to class. He works really hard to give examples and does many demonstrations. He is very knowledgeable in his field. He makes corny jokes that make the class even better. His exams are very doable. I read all of the textbook chapters in preparation. Take this class.

I didn't like Mounts at the beginning of the semester, but he definitely grew on me. I thought that tests were easy, except for the essays, which he always seemed to find points to take off for. He does go really fast and cover a ton of material, but it's pretty much common sense. Study the powerpoints and go over the textbook briefly and you'll be fine. Overall, I would recommend.

Prof Mounts is fantastic. You do need to go to class, but I just studied the notes without reading and did great. He always uses tons of examples and is willing to help you understand stuff or organize the paper. Not an easy class, but if you put in a little effort it's not hard to do well. Take a class with him!

I found the exams for this class very difficult to study for. So much material is crammed into 25 mc questions, 4 short answer and an essay. Thinks that because a few people do well on the exams that everybody should. Nice guy, fairly difficult class, probably because he switched to a textbook that he called more difficult.

I liked class with Mounts. Took cognitive psych with him and he was very straightforward. Powerpoints are clear and he gives tons of examples. Tests are relatively easy if you just study the powerpoints while you skim through the chapters. He's so funny, too. Mounts is always cracking jokes.

Dr. Mounts is a great guy, I loved Research Methods... he made a boring class fun. His exams are pretty straight forward and his papers weren't that hard. Reading the textbook and memorizing the studies he tells you to memorize really make the exams easier. I recommend Dr. Mounts and look forward to taking other classes with him.

Dr. Mounts is really funny, and a very nice guy. He talks really fast in class, so print out the powerpoint slides so you can write down his examples, which are often on the test. The tests aren't too bad, just study the powerpoints and use the textbook website (it has helpful review questions). Papers are easy. He's a good guy to take 251 with.

Talks very fast so print out the powerpoint slides before class! Makes sure students understand concepts before moving on. Gives plenty of examples to support/show theories/points. Tests can be difficulty- couple questions from the book that aren't talked about in class. Highly Recommended

Really interesting class. If you go to class, print out notes (he talks fast), and read textbook only if you need more clarity you'll be fine. He is always willing to help outside of class especially with the paper.

This class is one of the hardest I have ever taken, and Professor Mounts does NOTHING to help with that. He talks EXTREMELY fast, does not go over material well, and is useless with extra help. If you enjoy teaching yourself, then take this class. Otherwise, AVOID IT AT ALL COSTS!!!!

Going to his Research Methods class was one of the most painful things to do. I've heard he's better in other classes because the material isn't as boring... It's hard to pay attention after the first ten minutes of listening. Exams are very particular and even when you've studied for hours they never seem to get easier.

I absolutely hated research methods! I've heard Mounts is descent in other classes but I've got to tell you he was horrible here! I dreaded class, I learned next to nothing, and I really just wanted to scream when I had to sit there and listen to him sound like a babling idiot who didn't know what he was talking about. I definitely do not recomend!

I think this class is one of the hardest psyc classes. The materials are deep and Dr. Mounts goes so fast that you could hardly take any notes. But it is interesting once you understand the concepts. Plus, I did learn a lot from this class. Recommended!

Research Methods is a boring class no matter what, but Dr. Mounts really tries to make it interesting.  He gives good examples and thoroughly explains everything.  Tests are fair, and he is willing to help with papers.  Notes are posted online, but i'd suggest going to class because examples really help.
Hard class but great guy and great prof!! He tries to make everything really clear and always willing to help. Tests are hard; read the book and you'll do really well.

Couldn't imagine taking statistics with any other professor. Math is not my thing at all, but Dr. Mounts explained everything so clearly that I was able to earn an A. If you take good notes, and do practice problems from the book, you should do fine on tests. If you have to take statistics, definitely take it with Dr. Mounts!

Alright...this class is no joke and it is no tea party either. To be frank, the material is quite hard to grasp probably because it is deep**** biology and Dr. Mounts talks  really fast. There's no need reading the book... go to class b'c he tries really hard to clarify things. If u can avoid this class...do...if not..God have mercy on ur soul.

Mounts is the man. His tests are a little bit difficult, but studying in advance should get you a good grade. He's hilarious and you gotta love his bobble head motions after he tells jokes. Take his class!
I love Dr. Mounts!!!
Class was very cool, but his tests were on everything that was NOT covered in class.  Very unfair and difficult for a 200 level

I loved his class.I suggest finding a friend in the class and having a study session every week. Keep up with the reading and go to class, and you'll do fine. He's also great during office hours, he's stayed later than he planned in a day just to help me understand a concept.
Yet another teacher that just reads right from his powerpoint slides.  Makes it clear he would rather be golfing.
makes class interesting. tests are hard, know your stuff.
Great teacher, smart guy, but very hard you better knwo your stuff come test day
his notes are ok, just make sure you do the readings for his exams.
tough but fair, needs to work on his jokes

This professor proves to be extremely uninteresting and boring. The lecture puts at least half the class to sleep and the things he teaches us could be learned in at least half the time. I do not recommend this guy and avoid taking C++ taught by him.
Interested, dedicated, helpful. Extrodinarily approachable and available, whole-heartedly puts himself into subject matter. Definetly take his classes!

Really nice but very confused guy.  Granted he's an adjunct this semester and therefore new.  very boring and a great deal of the time you sit there wondering why he's showing you something.  Also covers materials multiple times which is good if you need it.  Lab book SUCKED!!!  Very lenient with due dates and he's there to help if you need it.
Heard good things about him for HUM, but if you can avoid taking his Shakespeare: Poem, Play, Film class, DO IT!!! He retires after Spring 2018, and it'll be safe to take it after that!

I took Shakespeare: Poem, Play, Film with Dr. Herzman, and he is very obviously passionate about the subject, but just not a very good professor for this class. His lectures are incredibly boring, and all of his classes are early so it's easy to fall asleep. He's not a harsh grader, but not available if you need help outside of class either.

Great class. I learned a lot, and always looked forward to the class even at 8:00 am. There are lots of reading assignments and they go fast, but he wont ask you anything on the test that wasn't covered in class--so take really good notes and read as much as you can.

Herzman is my favorite professor so far at Geneseo. If you want a brilliant professor who will throw in the random reference to Facebook or something completely out of left field, Herzman's your man. His class is not overly challenging if you do the work. He is extremely receiving of student opinions and feedback; highly recommend!
Easily one of the nicest, most intelligent, and most down to earth professor ever. Class is never boring and very thought provoking with a nice touch of appropriate humor.

Great professor to have in a small seminar style class. He loves what he does and that makes the classroom experience so much more satisfying. He keeps you interested, thinking and on your toes. Not to mention the fact that he's a hilarious old man.

Great guy! He is hilarious and very intelligent. He's approachable in and out of class, and if you do the reading and talk in class, he really appreciates it. Obviously cares about the subject matter. Not an easy A, but it's possible with hard work.

Herzman is a brilliant professor, a scholar for Dante AND Shakespeare but he has a great way of rehashing things in layman's terms. Your typical lecturer but there is just so much he knows it's an honor to take a class with him. Include DETAILS in your work. People say he's a tough grader, but that's because he can sniff out night before papers

I did not like him as a professor at all.  He was not helpful outside of class especially through email. When inquiring about anything he is more likely to negative criticize your work than give constructive criticism.  Perhaps he is a better humanities teacher, but as far as Shakespeare is concerned I would not recommend taking him!

Dr. Herzman is a really nice guy and he makes humn concepts pretty easy to understand. He gives you a practice test with half of the same questions as the one you get in class. However, he impossible to please on papers. This class killed my 4.0. If you're okay with a solid B then take humn with him.

Very intelligent, but speaks in a way anybody could understand.  However, material is very bland which makes the 8 o'clock class a fight to stay awake.  Tests are easy.  He is a tougher grader on essays compared to other HUM professors I have heard about.  Overall, a nice, modest professor.  If you can handle boring stuff in the morning, take him.
Monotonous, very knowledgeable, easy tests, you get a pretest with half the same questions before the tests, early morning class, difficult to stay awake.

Lectures were well-delivered for the most part.  Arrogant intelluctualismwas a huge problem for me. Reads the newspaper while you're speaking to him.  Well-delivered lectures but needs I would not take for a second course.

For 8 in the morning, this was an awesome class.  He is very clear and makes some dense reading material easy to understand.  Tests are fair, and the points he tests you on are always emphasized in class.  He's approachable outside of class. an incredibly intelligent, friendly man.  Plus you get to read Dante with one of the premier Dante scholars!

Professor Herzman was a fantastic professor.  Going to class is STRONGLY recommended since what appears on the tests and the paper topics is what is discussed in class.  Reading the books is also monumentally important.  Herzman is very approachable outside of class and is one of the nicest people I've ever had the pleasure to know.

I loved him as a professor for humanities.  He was easy to follow and he is a very intelligent man. I learned a lot from his class and enjoyed it too!  He's a fair grader and the papers and tests are very straight forward.

thought his class was GOOD even for 8 am. Hes a nice guy in class, not too personable outside of class.  FAIR amount of reading esp. for humn. He is really EASY TO UNDERSTAND. Take notes read most of the books or at least book reviews go to class. FAIR GRADER on essays and tests. class was easier than i expected humn to be cuz of him.

I loved this class.  It was not easy and he is a hard grader, but definitely worth it.  Feedback on papers will help you become a better writer.  He is certainly fair.  Herzman knows alot and if you can make a point for what you say he will listen.  Back it up though.  You have to do the work but absolutely one of my favorite classes ever.

Herzman essentially bulldozes over any opinions voiced that don't neatly coincide with his own, or modifies them until they do.  Seems friendly in public, but will savage you in comments on your paper, employing rhetoric including (but not limited to) "nonsense" and "horrendous."  Simply put, he can be too set in his ways, intellectually.

Professor Herzman is amiable and helpful, as long as you have done nothing to offend him.  He will accept late work if you explain its tardiness sufficiently, but will hold a grudge against absentees.  Grading is largely based upon favoritism, and he deals with students with a thinly veiled arrogance that implies, "I wrote the course textbook."
Def knows his "stuff" maybe this is why he assumes it comes easy to everybody else.  Willing to help, but not very approachable.  Tough grader.  Has a tendency to get off on criticizing students.

His classes are hard, but he is fair.  He'll listen and make himself clear.  He does like to hear himself talk, but he is always open for discussion.  The major criticism is that he refuses to branch out onto new subjects.  So anything you have to say about the subject is going to be something he's thought of already

Not the class to take at 8 am. The monotone voice is not conducive to staying awake. Does not explain grading, and its pretty much all about whether he likes you or not. Allows rewrites on papers. Takes attendance.

I went into this class thinking it was going to be awful, and it ended up being one of my favorite classes. Herzman is a fair grader, and if you try, you will do well. He is interesting, and the workload is not bad at all. I would definetly take another class with him. :)

Herzman is pretty awesome. Some people think the sound of his voice is dull, but he has some pretty interesting and amusing things to say about the content of the course. He's a tough, but fair grader. He leaves you plenty of feedback notes to steer you the right way. My favorite class this semester, hands down! I feel bad to miss a class or two...
Seemed like a really nice guy and was entertaining at first....but as others have already said DO NOT GET ON HIS S*** LIST! He def has favorites and if you are not one of them you will know.....

paper dates are arbitrary and capricious as to when herzman feels like making you write. dont get on his sh*t list at all costs. this class is useless if you want to do more than just read lots of material and not usually gain insight into it. h/o, tests are fair,reading list is decent, paper topics arent bad, at least he tries to be fun at 8am.
Nice guy. Great teacher. You will learn ALOT.

If you are trying to get by and pass all this old crap that you probably could read on your own or have read in high school. This class is a no-no. He will hold attendance against you for not wanting to show up for his boring lecture and take interest in his subject like him.

This professor is very overrated. The only students that something good to say are the ones that he likes. Believe me, if you get on his**** list, he will grade you very harshly. His boring monotone lectures don't help if your trying to take Hum I at 8:00am in the morning. I warn all students not to take this class unless your an English major.

One of the greatest teachers I've ever had.  I had him for Humn I and The Age of Dante.  He takes a great interest in both and is interesting to listen to.  You won't look at the clock all class.  He is funny and kind and adorable.  It helps if you are a g

Easily my favorite prof at this school.I took him for humn by chance soph yr and have made it a point to take a class with him every semester since then. A Tough but very fair grader, his classes are always interesting; just do the reading.Definitely turned me into a Dante lover myself.
hes a genius, real cool guy, real hard grader, tests a fair, papers impossible to please on

Herzman was my fav prof this semester.  funny, nice guy. his comments are witty but not condescending, he has respect for his subject matter and he LOVES teaching Dante.  take his Dante course or Medieval studies
greatest prof ive had yet. funny and intelligent man whose always willing to help and is very fair.  he turned humn at 8:10 in the am into a really enjoyable and interesting class =)
very overrated, but somewhat entertaining.  seems particularly nice to some and not as much to others.

Worth getting up early and memorizing the first 20 lines of Canterbury Tales. Smart, inquisitive man. Makes you love the subject. Interesting guy. Laid back. Wore the same sweater all the time when I was there. Go to the Italian Dante reading.
knows his stuff. great teacher, great guy, great sense of humor, great perspective. changed my bias against shakespeare and made it enjoyable.
i really enjoyed his class.
Best professor I've had so far.  Knows pretty much everything, but not arrogant at all.  Difficult grader, but if you want to really learn and see things in a new way, take him.
he is not a very nice man.. went to him for advising and he told me I was "dopey" hmmm? I am an A- student no way I am dopey

One of the most thoughtful professors I've had. Creates a relaxed, laid back atmosphere where you can feel comfortable talking and learning. One of my all time favorites. He knows what really matters, what teaching is all about, and is always there for yo
great guy especially in upper level classes.  Really has an interesting perspective and not afraid to make you discuss things.

he does cut people off an awful lot, and he doesn't explain why he gives the grade he does. hard grader. lectures a lot, but makes some really funny comments. nice, intelligent, quirky, dante-loving guy.
THE best teacher ive ever had. bar none.

The class is just him lecturing the whole time, he always cuts students off. Too much reading, you have no time to explore plays. He's a hard grader and doesn't tell you why you got the grade you got.

hard grader. intelligent. not too helpful. but somewhat funny in class.

Chang is BY FAR the best Chinese teacher at Geneseo. She is very helpful & clear in every lesson. Does not continue until every student understands the material. She is really great. Made me want to learn more about chinese language. moves slow enough for the whole class to get it. as long as you do the work for class and go every day, you're almost guaranteed an A. Highly recommended.
He is the awesomest english teacher

Ronny Tsang is like the funniest man you'll ever meet. He does give a fair share of reading homework but that's expected in any INTD and it's definitely do-able. He kept night classes interesting and I really enjoyed his class a lot. One of my favorite professors at Geneseo.
Borrrrrrrrring

His nightly hws will not kill u at first, but later towards the end of the semester, you shall feel the wrath. He did assign a couple of hws along wih 1 or 2 papers due on the same day which sucked. yea the hws are easy but u wanna focus on the paper more. Funny guy, he will keep u awake. beard game strong. kids in class participate to get noticed.

Tsang is quite literally the man! There is no doubt that he was my favorite professor. Extremely smart man, but he also cares so much about his students and that's evident daily in his teaching style. I wish he taught another class so I could take him again; I loved this class. Best English class I've ever taken, I'll definitely miss this class.

Tsang is an awesome person, not the best professor. His syllabus is really convoluted. His assignments, which are incredibly lengthy and due every class, don't make much sense as far as directions. He tries to connect certain ideas to the texts, but it ends up being incredibly difficult to make connections that are not there. Great guy though.

Tsang's class was great. The material is all modern and ranges from graphic novels to narratives about Hurricane Katrina. His teaching style is very entertaining and informative.The class also is discussion focused.The content is appropriate for all majors. He's a very smart and funny guy and has fascinating stories. Great choice for INTD.

Tsang is great! His class is always fun to go to- He makes class interesting and he has a phenomenal sense of humor! Though this INTD is significantly more work than many others, Tsang's personality more than makes up for it. ALSO- the work is NOT monotonous at all- Almost always interesting. He also gives MANY extra credit opportunities.

Professor Tsang is an AMAZING man! He is super interesting as well as extremely funny and captivating. You will not be bored in his class. He is a very fair grader, plus he gave a lot of extra credit as well!

Tsang is the man! You can learn so much more than what the class is required to teach. He gave give you great life lessons and also a great guy to grab a beer with. Tsang is super chill and will do his best to teach you the material and help you outside of class. He also teaches high school so he can relate to many different types of people Goodguy

A lot of homework compared to other INTD classes. With that said, you can get an A in this class if you feel like doing the work. Its not hard its just more work than others. Tsang is a good teacher in terms of fairness and he's a really nice guy. He'll buy you some stuff and make a lot of jokes about his parents. Interesting class w. a lot of work

Mr. Tsang is an awesome professor. His class is easily the best INTD you can take. He is SO chill and he was in phi kap! Tsang rocks!!! do not take this class -.-

Professor Herzman is the cutest woman you will ever meet! I had her for Women in Work and the class overall was quite interesting. She doesn't seem to give over a B+ but she lets your write the papers over and get you that A. Shes thoughtful and its a fun class!

She is such a nice lady. You people are ridiculous if you think she is anything other than nice and helpful. She wants nothing more than to help you with your writing and gives you every oppotunity you want to get the grade you want. Class is easy if you try at all
