She will call you out in class and shut you down leaving students afraid to participate, but then gets frustrated when no one talks. One good thing about the class is she does let you revise your essays but good luck...

I took her Black Humanities class and it was disappointing. Professor Lima is strongly opinionated and won't let you forget it. Any opinion or idea you have will be shot down. Her advice is non constructive and she is unapproachable. She will embarrass you in class and is easily annoyed. Unless you want to lose sleep over her grading, DO NOT TAKE.

I absolutely love Maria. She is very intimidating and strongly opinionated however this is what I really enjoyed about her class. Teaches unlike any professor I've had before, some students take that her being rude and unprofessional but I found her to be incredibly entertaining and interesting. She takes you out of your comfort zone, def worth it.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Graded by few things']

comment: Professor Maria Lima is hit or miss. She is very well respected in the English Literature department and is very very smart. She is extremely outgoing but if you show up and participate you will learn a ton from her. All your works are "works in progress" so you can revise papers as much as you want until you get the best grade you can.
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass."]

comment: Maria Lima is a great English teacher. Although she has strong opinions, she has an open mind and will hear out your arguments. Participation matters, but the class is so engaging it shouldn't be difficult. She will help you revise your paper until it's an A if you meet with her. She gives extra credit opportunities as well.

Dr. Lima is extremely offensive and unprofessional in the classroom. She shares too much information about her personal life and is so disrespectful to her students. If you don't have the same opinions as her then don't say anything because she will not like your papers. She is very rude and will call you out in front of the class. DO NOT TAKE!
tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Tough grader']

comment: Not hard to get an A in her class but not worth it. She can be super disrespectful, close minded, and unprofessional. She crosses the line, and you're doing yourself a favor if you choose not to take her. If you don't share her opinion or see something differently than her, get ready to be attacked about things irrelevant from class. AVOID.

Maria is a great teacher and will help get your writing in shape for the english department. She allows revisions until your paper is an A and meets with you to go over any revisions. Not strict about deadlines. She's very outspoken which some people don't like but is cooler than seems at 1st impression. Need to talk at least once a class for an A.
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass."]

comment: Maria is a little intimidating at first, but she really does want you to succeed and will work with you to improve. Will help revise your papers to perfection with no due dates, and is very understanding as long as you communicate with her. Class is very participation-heavy, though (she expects you to talk at least once every class).
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass."]

comment: Maria is an extremely bright woman and because of that her class can be very interesting but she is very outspoken and it can come off as rude and sometimes disrespectful.  If you are going to take her class be prepared to be told you are wrong/stupid, she only accepts ideas that she agrees with and there is no room for other opinions or ideas
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass."]

comment: My biggest issue with Maria is her use of scare tactics. If you have speaking anxiety or are just shy to speak in class or under a lot of pressure, whatever you do, do not take class with Maria ever. All she expects is participation, you could utter out complete garbage and it would still be better than not talking. Not worth it.
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass."]

comment: We read A LOT in this class, and I'm not a reader. But with that said, her "textbooks" are just regular novels so don't be too worried. I took her INTD 105 Haiti Noir class and it's my favorite class. Her classes are engaging and she's very humorous, just be prepared to work for it. You revise papers all the time and need to participate to do well.

Lima is a great professor, although very difficult, which she makes clear from the first day. This class will make you an amazing writer, as Lima will tear your work up and help you to grow with each new draft. Take her at least once.
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass."]

comment: I'll be honest, I'm terrified of Maria. She's very outspoken and is very strict on her classroom policies. She demands respect by intimidation, which isn't really the best learning style for me personally. With that being said, the woman is ridiculously bright, knows what she's talking about, and knows what she wants. You'll learn a lot.

Can be amazingly supportive when it comes to writing papers. She will literally help you revise an essay as many times as it takes to earn an A. However, if you're not good at showing up to class and being there on time DO NOT TAKE. She gets really annoyed with people being late, and won't take any excuses for absences.

Maria is a hilarious woman that cares to death about her job and your success in the class. She lets you write your paper as many times as you want until you get an A on it.  Reading and class participation are important but as long as you read the assignments and talk at least once a class you're guaranteed an A. One of my favorite teachers ever.

I love Maria's class! She is funny, lively, unusual. Participation is a must so if you think you're shy you might not enjoy her as much. She does not keep a gradebook and will not give your essays a formal grade until it's an A. Speaking of essays, she will let you rewrite your paper AS MANY TIMES AS YOU NEED to get an A. TAKE THIS CLASS!

This class is a mind opener, but in a good way.  You will learn things that you never have thought about and it really helps open the mind.  Maria doesnt even keep a grade book, and grades are based on paper comments that she reviews at the end.  she doesnt take off points for lateness either.  all you have to do is come to class and participate!

I am simultaneously horrified and fascinated by Maria. She is always entertaining, but can be a little harsh at times, and I don't like how she'll sometimes announce grades in front of the class. If you go to see her before an essay is due she is extremely helpful. Read the books, even answering a simple question will get you participation points.

She's easy, but nonetheless, believe the hype. If you find yourself an unobtrusive personality, she'll guilt you into feeling sorry for yourself for not having strong opinions regarding "world issues." A delicious quote of hers I can recall goes "all my white students look the same." Tyler Durden-esque in her views and ultimate hypocrisy.

The nicest, most helpful, and entertaining professor i have ever had. Not a dull moment in her class, and if you are willing to work, she takes accommodation for your effort. Go to class, and hand in as many drafts as you want and she will help you, because she actually cares. Awesome professor and like she will tell you "The best prof. at geneseo.

It is not hard to get an A in Lima's class. She wants you to get the A. All you have to do is talk in class, write some responses, and write/re-write assigned papers.  She never sets exact due dates, so you never feel rushed. Just do the readings for class and you're golden.

I'll be honest...Maria is an opinionated feminist, but what is wrong with being that?  NOTHING!!!  She can back up what she says (like she tells her students to do in her writing) and is one of the most intelligent people I've ever encountered.  She will help you with anything you ask her to and YOU MUST TALK IN CLASS!  Overall, she gets an A!

Maria Lima is a smart intelligent woman and THE BEST teacher at Geneseo.  She expects a lot from her students and will do anythind to help you.  She has made me a better writer.  We are all lucky to have her!

She will spend most of the class reminding you of her political views and how terribly novel they are; annoying only because she never shuts up about it. I dislike the way she does participation grading because making a frivolous comment every day will get you a better grade than making a meaningful concentration even slightly less frequently.

One of my favorite professors at Geneseo. I couldn't be more different than Maria, or have gotten in more arguments with her, and she certainly didn't hold it against me. I learned a ton about english writing, myself, and the rest of the world going back and forth with her. Her intensity leans towards hyperbole to prove a point; highly recommended
She's tough, but she's a real great lady that will help you along in your struggles.

I love her, but understand why people hate her. Pros: confident, educated, articulate, funny, passionate, intriguing. Cons: stupid participation points, will pick on you (sometimes unfairly... but it's humorous to me), can be perceived as offensive. It is not difficult to get an A, & you can rewrite the papers as many times as you want... DO THIS.
Very intimidating and opinionated.  I think some students would enjoy her class, but if you don't enjoy being absolutely required to speak to get a good grade then do not take a class with her.
Shocking hypocrite---preaches open mindedness till your ears blead----but only if you agreee with her. And for all her bravado, she's just doesn;t strike me as all that bright a lady.

Excellent teacher. Facilitates class discussion well, but the 2.5 hour time slot isn't always conducive to engaging opinions from classmates. Remarkably fair. Has opinions, but doesn't press them on students, greatly rewards effort, regardless of opinion. Respectful. Intelligent. Humble.
my least favorite teacher in all of my schooling

i loathe this lady.  she is  the most opinionated person i have ever met, and if you don't agree with her, you will not do well in this class. also places way too much importance on participation and attendance. i would never reccomend to anyone.

Crazy and unpredictable.  The once a week class seemed nice at first but can turn out to be boring after the first hour because all we do is roundatble discussion. You have to speak up and she likes opinionated people. She definitely opens up minds and loves what she does.
She is an absolute liberal freak. Likes to shove her opinions in her student's faces, and uses stereotypes like no other. I will never take another class with her again.

I also had her for ENGL 242 and I'm thinking about taking her for Humn and ENGL 318. I love Maria to death. Very friendly and approachable, loves to rant about sex and politics... there is not a more confident professor in the department. She really gives students a new way of looking at literature after taking one of her classes! Take her class!

Would have been a great professor if she wasn't so arrogant. Don't come to this country and live here and have a career here and then call it a "God forsaken country" she clearly chose favorites and her so called "cute" accent was really just annoying.

Meh. She's alright. She does tend to be very self-centered, and be warned: She gives NO DIRECTION WHATSOEVER writing papers until after she has marked them to death in her un-readable handwriting. She talks very fast and can be a brat. She's very energetic, but it borderlines on annoying most of the time, especially at 9:30am. She's overrated.

I took Literature of the African Diaspora with Maria, and she is definately an interesting teacher! She allows you to do papers over as many times as you want, and grades fairly. The grade you get is how much effort you put in. While she is arrogant, it doesn't take away from her excellent teaching.

Maria Lima is the best professor at Geneseo...no contest.  She inspired my teaching career.  I hate when people say she is opinionated as if that is a bad thing.  Brilliant! I can't put a value on what she has done for me.  I now live on Long Island but I always keep in touch with her because I couldn't have it any other way!

She has no compassion, and is thus hearless.  She will wonder through life souless as a result.  She lives an empty life because of this and she tries hard to fill thr void by making everything about herself.  Take her for one class, and then never take her again.  She is an abomination of human life.

Maria Lima is the best professor I've had in my 5 semesters at Geneseo.  I never zoned out in her class and usually left wanting to continue the discussion.  Make sure you verbalize your thoughts, and you'll be GOLDEN.

Yes, Maria is indeed very opinionated. But she challenges you to hold such strong opinions of your own.  Re-writing papers is a plus, and she makes herself extremely available to students. Because of her, I am more able to talk in class, more confident overall as a student/person... she really is an inspiration.
maria is an amazing person; class is never boring and she lets you rewrite papers as many time as neccessary
Maria Lima is amazing

There is not a more interesting and enjoyable teacher at Geneseo.  She is also one of the most helpful and positive.  My favorite thing about her, though, is the utter random rants about everything from politics to sex.

Take her classes if you want to take a class in Feminism and Marxism, not if you want to take classes in English.  Strong believer in the neo-feminist-pedagogical mode stating, "We aren't going to read books by dead white men in this class."  Easy class, shoves her views down your throat so hard it's easy to know what she wants to hear in papers.

Had Maria for every class I could, even classes I didn't need. She is dynamic, witty, VERY opinionated, but won't force it on you. She helps you learn by letting you correct mistakes instead of penalizing you. Best classes and memories of academia!
No Comments

Excellent professor.  Kind of a tough grader but if your willing to put an effort forth she'll help you get the best grade possible.  Class participation is a huge thing for her.  If you don't want to participate in class discussions don't take this class.  Not too much reading but the reading that is required is fun.  Awesome class to take.
She is the epitome of what an educated, strong, beautiful women is. Fascinating.

Awesome. Just awesome. She likes to have snacks in class and is very relaxed. She uses portfolio grading so even if you don't do too well in the beginning you can still get an A. Loves to chat about current events and is very lively. Allows you to revise your papers over and over again for regrading

utterly insane political views, but she doesn't mind if you just argue right back, she ejoys it actually.  requires a lot of participation, but it isn't tough to find something you wanna say in her class.  she doesn't really have any formal due dates, which is awesome, and you can always rewrite!

If you don't want to talk, don't take any of Maria's classes, it's that simple.  If you do enjoy sharing your opinions in class, be prepared to make Maria one of your favorite teachers.  Tough paper grader, but she's willing to work on multiple drafts with you, often even after the due date.

One of the greatest teachers ever.  Yes, she demands participation, welcome to college.  She's opinionated and crazy but don't let her scare you off to lower class size, you'll learn more than you thought possible from her.

Maria is definitely an ENGLISH professor, so if you can't hack it in the literary world, stay out of the classroom-- of course, this is just meant to make you want to prove yourself... so dive in! Maria is terrific, but does talk alot- fight her to get make your viewpoint heard!
I dropped this class.  This professor frightened me.  She may be an easy grader but she puts you on the spot and there is a lot of work.
dissapointing. If you just want an easy grade this class will do it for you--not demanding. you get the feeling she doesnt her stuff very well.

I liked this prof, but I should have taken a more challenging class.  One piece of advice: if she asks you what grade you think you deserve, give yourself the highest grade possible, because she might really give it to you.  I put A-, should have put A.
Definitely the most entertaining professor on campus with the best hair (and she knows this too). Maria would do almost anything for her students. She doesn't "profess," she educates.

She's a very good teacher.  Participation is 25% of her class grade though, so if you're afraid to talk, you might want to stay away.  She allows revisions on papers and no grade is final.  She's a bit crazy, but not too bad.
No Comments
The woman's a SELF-PROCLAIMED madwoman, but a terribly awesome professor.  Her classroom antics are a blast, but it isn't all fun & games.  Expect a good amount of work, both written and VERBAL!
Awesome, amazing professor. Learned a lot from her. Really opened my mind to new ideas.

yeah shes a little crazy but she likes those who read and talk in class.  plus the stuff you read is great, so thats a bonus.  you get to revise your papers and there are no tests, quizzes or final.  shes great and you'll learn in a creative way.
scary and intimidating as all hell.  crazy middle aged brazilian woman on a mission to drive students into insanity making a million revisions and forcing them to talk
Stalin was more tolerant of competing views than this one. Avoid unless you're looking to be indoctrinated.

Maria Lima is definitely one of my favorite professors here!  She makes you think and gets you into it.  Her grading is fair and easy to understand.  Warning to those who are quiet in class... your grade DEPENDS on class participation.  No shy ones here.

Maria! One of my favorite professors.  She really made you THINK and she was unbelievably FAIR.  Thanks for everything!   And hey, Maria....don't forget to give us a second to THINK!  Your questioning is very thought provoking, we need time to think. =)
Just connect everything to a movie to show that you understand.  It earned me an A.
she is great.  i don't agree with her politics but she doesn't hold that against me.  she is very humanistic.  thought provoking..
The best professor at Geneseo
Maria is absolutely the best professor at Geneseo.  She simply knows how to teach and inspire students beyond their capabilities.  This woman does not receive the acclaim she deserves.
No Comments
Very politically-mided; really inspired me to think and to be a conscious world citizen.
I took a class with Professor Chow and it turned out to be the hardest class ive ever taken at Geneseo. Seems like a great guy but don't recommend as a professor.

He was alright. He was an easy grader but would give so much attitude if you had questions about an assignment and would never give you a clear answer anyway. His lectures were boring and I could tell he had no planning and did not care about our class.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Lots of homework']

comment: Fairly easy class to excel in, lecture portion is extremely dry but nevertheless manageable. Two tests throughout the semester, both of which take place online and can be completed through one's basic Googling of the questions. As for Barry, alternates between being very accommodating to being surprisingly short and hostile when frustrated in labs

Barry is a great professor.  Funny, casual, yet highly knowledgable in his subject.  Word to the wise, don't try to BS him, he'll see right through you, but even still, he's very communicable and easy to talk to.  Assigns fairly simple weekly readings for homework, which are gone over in class.

He is not as bad as people say he is. He's pretty good guy. Course is rather semi-difficult but he's tests are easiest ever. I got 99 on the first exam, thought class was a joke, didn't study got mid 80s on next two tests, studied pretty hard got 100 on 4th test and final. He also gives you like bonus points.

If you are not a math major and are just looking for a good grade, do not take a class with him.  If you are a math major, you will learn a crazy amount of math but you will have to work very hard.  I kind of miss having classes with him.

Dr. Friedland is a extremely nice person.  I do have to admit that its not the easiest class because your grade is based only on  the 4 tests.  The tests are not the easiest ones either.  he is very helpful. recommended

Terrible teacher. The tests are only like 4 questions each and make up the entirety of your grade so if you get one question wrong there's 5% of your total grade. Plus he tests on material that he doesn't cover in class or with homework. And he blocks what he's writing on the board so the right half of the class can't see it

Dr. Friedland is easily one of my favorite professors at Geneseo. His examples are always clear and he leads you through the problems step-by-step. In addition, he's absolutely hilarious! Yes, the class is hard and you WILL have to work for your A, but if you go to class and pay attention, Dr. Friedland makes things clear and gives GREAT notes.

Terrible teacher, All he does is stand at the chalkboard and write math problems, he is extremely unhelpful in office hours. The tests are also extremely difficult and unfair, no partial credit or leway on anything. Worst teacher i have ever had

He definitely knows what he's talking about, but he doesn;t explain it, just writes problem after problem. He's so smart that he expects the class to get the material when he skips steps and rarely goes over the homework. The tests are hard and not based on the homework. He expects you to know what to do on the test and it's stuff you never learn.

Absolutely terrible teacher.  Paying attention in class, doing all the homeworks, and studying like crazy will get you an 80 if you're lucky.  His tests are the entire course, and each is only 4 questions long.  He's also about as easy to listen to as nails on a blackboard.  Don't take Calc III with him, even if you have no choice.

For the most part he stands with his back to the board and does problem after problem. For a question to be answered you need to just interrupt him and ask. Grades are based on exams only which are short and pretty challenging. Miss one question and you lose about 20 points. I DO NOT recommend taking a class with him unless you've taken calc before

This guy should teach only advanced classes, he talks like we all know what hes saying and hes about as warm and welcoming as tombstones. He stands in front of class with his back turned to the students and does problem after problem while the class looks at him like zombies.

Personality has a lot to be desired and could (at least when I had him) have been a lot more encouraging to his students.  Tests were short and difficult.  I ended up withdrawing and there were a good number of Es for midterm freshmen grades. I strongly do NOT recommend.
tests are short and really, really difficult. 4+ hours of studying equals about a 58. curves only if the whole class bombs it which happens a lot.

Grades are 100% based on test.  Tests are challenging to say the least.  They're short as well so if you miss a question you will get about 20 points off.  I'd bet he gives out about one A a semester.  Very good teacher though.

Nice guy.  Wouldn't reccomend to take if you're a bad test taker because those are your only grades for the class.  if you do the hw (which isn't graded/collected) as you go instead of all right before the test it may be easier to get the good grade

He gives excellent lectures with great, complete notes.  He drops some humor into the class to keep it interesting.  The grade comes entirely from the tests, which are straight forward and have no surprises. I learned a ton and enjoyed his class.
One of the best courses I have ever taken in Geneseo. Very straight to the point in notes and tests. No graded homework, grade is entirely based on tests, 3/7 of which is the final.
really tough grader.  i def learned a bit, but do not have the grade to show for it.  NO CELL PHONES
Lew is the man!  Pretty hard class, but he teaches it very well.  He is the best math professor I have had at Geneseo.  Very good at increasing knowledge about the subject matter

The materical is pretty difficult, but he is VERY good at explaining things and he always gives tons of examples. He doesn't check the homework, but I would suggest doing at least some of it. He makes the corniest jokes and he wears the same plaid shirt and vest every single day.

Friedland is one of the best professors at Geneseo. I learned so much from him. I got a 28 on the first exam for Calc 3, went to him discouraged, worked my butt off, and earned a B+ in the class. Don't give up if you're doing poorly, just prove to him you can do it on the final. Study the notes REALLY well and be able to do the homework problems!

Five cups of coffee couldn't make linear algebra exciting, and Friedland didn't exactly try to make the class entertaining. That said, he gives better notes than any professor I've ever had and makes the material very easy to understand. Stingy with grades, but if you study occasionally you should get an A.

I agree with the person below me. You really have to decide if learning a lot or getting a good grade is more important to you. Personally, I didn't think he graded fairly at all, but I don't know if everyone had the same problem or if it was just me. I did learn a ton in this class though. He gives good notes.

This is a very hard class. The tests are very short and difficult. He takes off 10 points for simple mistakes.. so it is hard to do really well. And he doesn't curve. But, he gives good notes and is always willing to go over homework problems. He tries to be funny and wears the same clothes the entire semester.

I think Friedland is a great professor and teaches well (don't know what the other raters are saying)It's not supposed to be blocks and cubes and 1+1=2, even though the math courses are filled with education majors! It's college mathematics! You don't get it? Then don't take it! He's great and nice guy, awesome tests, nothing or than that. PERIOD.
Although a very boring class, he explains all the concepts in it fairly well. The end of the year gets harder. He is a nice man in general.

This is defiently not the worst math teacher I have had here, but he's not the best either. He is a nice guy and the class isn't that hard, sometimes its just hard for him to teach well. Overall the class isn't too bad.

Wow what an amazing professor. His lectures are very clear and he always tries to bring things down to a level we can understand. He's always willing to go over homework problems. His tests are short, but not easy. However, if you get your hands on an old copy of the test, it'll save you because they are almost exactly the same. Take him for calc 3

He admited that he never took any teaching classes, but he's still a good teacher nonetheless.  He knows the material very well and is good at helping you to understand it too.  His sense of humor's not too bad either, if you appreciate corny jokes every once in a while.

Not bad...Aced calc because I loved calc...I slacked of in Linear Algebra and got a C-...when I desevered an E... not very personable but reasonable...but be careful...does not give much partial credit!!!
He's a different guy, but he means well. I don't think the same way as him, but it's nice to see things from a different perspective. I would recommend him for upper level classes.

Lew is a great teacher.  His notes are very clear and his tests are short, straight-forward, and predictable.  I had him for calc III, and decided to take him again for ELA.  Do the homework and you'll be fine.  Worst sense of humor ever...which actually makes him funny,  and he wears cool vests.

So far I like this prof.  He is very clear with his notes and explains things clearly.  He is not very personable however, but gets to the point..which is to teach class.  His tests  are surprisingly short but not easy.  take good notest and pay attention in class.

PEOPLE WHO GET Ds AND Es DESERVE IT!! I did well because I paid attention, unlike the other idiots who complain when they are naturally stupid. LEW IS AN AMAZING professor,Hes too intelligent for  idiots to comprehend. This course requires a lot of studying, don;t expect to get an easy A
I thought he was great -- one of my best professors at Geneseo.
worst ever. I dropped and taking again in the spring with a DIFFERENT prof.

he was a real jerk, I did ok on the first exam and went to ask him some questions about what I got wrong, and he made me feel like a retard.  Whatever you do DON'T take his class, I warned my friend...but she got a D too

Lew's the reason I went from a Math major with all A's in HS to dropping the major.  Got an E in Calc 1.  Very self-involved, no care for students. Is his wardrobe still 1 pair of khakis, 1 shirt, and a sweater vest for cold days! We tracked it!

I hated him. I took calc in HS and still failed. He likes his way and his way only. I was very confused - he was a D*** when i went for help too... don't take him... get towsley. I got a E in his course- Hey lew, please retire
I liked him. Gives the best notes, and takes you through all the steps. Tough grader, but his tests are pretty fair, and he curves.

horrible teacher. worked my butt off for a C-. He uses big math terms that no one understands, and when you ask him to clarify, he uses even more math terms. i taught myself calculus because he was no help.

Def. study hard for tests. They are quite short, and even though he curves, they can be a real *. Also, his final is a killer. So make sure you study a while beforehand. And I would reccomend going to classes, or else get notes from someone.
Very straight forward. If you go to class and study the notes there is no reason you can't get an A. Likes to wear the same clothes all the time. Curves tests.
he is really helpful if you seek for help.....work for your A!!!
i agree!  please retire!
No Comments
Please retire!
This was the only C I ever got and the only semester I didn't make Dean's list
course relies heavily on class notes, but is very clear
No Comments
No Comments
He's a good teacher, but you will have to work for your A
stay away unless you want your GPA to fall

Dr. Hall is a nice person, but checked out halfway during the semester. She canceled our lesson plans and then canceled class multiple times after that. Her lectures were not that interesting and not many attended because it was not mandatory. She does have a lot of knowledge to teach, but I think person teaching is better for her.
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class', 'Get ready to read']

comment: This lady is horrible. If I didnt need this class Id drop so quick. Her grading is absurdly difficult and she acts like assignments are easier than they are. Advice: Take most of the assignments as seriously as a major exam.
tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Get ready to read', 'Tough grader']

comment: Probably the worst Professor I have ever had. She will say one thing and do another. Despite her teaching a class on being professional, she is far from it.

A little clarification the class I took with her was a pass/fail. I feel Dr. Hall gets a bad rep because of how ridiculously hard she grades but at the end of the day she really does care about her students and wants them to do good in her class. I really had a rough time with a group project because of one of my partners and she was very merciful.

Feedback is poor quality and condescending. Grading is very tedious and specific although clear guidelines are not usually provided. She tends to contradict herself in terms of lesson plan grading even when you go to office hours. She is proud of her "tough" reputation. She will make it seem like you will fail her class and as a teacher.

She is nice but an extremely tough grader. I've never seen so many decimal grades in my time as a college student and you are literally left wondering why you lost 0.02 points on an assignment. Sometimes she'll suggest something to you and then take off points for it later. Her textbook quizzes are impossible. So yeah good luck..

Prof. Hall is at best a mediocre professor. Often inattentive to student emails (saying she never received them, etc.), flaky, and arrogant. Quizzes once a week, which began easy and progressed to be very specific & difficult by semester end. Expectations are ambiguous, especially when it came to the lesson plan. Overall, I would never recommend.

Dr. Hall leads you to believe that she is cutting you a break by giving ten question quizzes rather than exams, HOWEVER do not be fooled, since she makes the answers on these quizzes so ambiguous it can be hard to do well on them. Her expectations are generally unclear and the whole class, despite having read the material is on the brink of failing

For some reason that I do not know, Dr. Hall did not like me. She never wanted to hear what I had to say and was not nice to me when I went to see her during office hours. It was very disheartening. She is a truly bitter and mean person and will lead you to believe you're doing well and then she will give you a C.

Mapes is an amazing professor who I would definitely recommend to anyone. She really cares about the students and wants them to do well. she is very nice and cares alot about her students, one of my classmates asked for an extension on the paper for the class and she just said "um, ok yea y not?" she's very clear and helpful. it's evident that she wants her students to do well. if i take another history class im gonna make sure it's with her.

Also, she is an (admitted) grammar person so she'll also lecture about grammar.  She's a great listener and grades really easily, and very smart.

So-so. I personally loved the material itself so I found her lectures incredibly interesting, but I could definitely see how she could be really boring. She does put a lot of emphasis on what's important for the tests though. She's kind of a tough grader, and exams are lengthy. However, so long as you do the reading and just show up you'll be okay.

Very nice and a good professor. If you are like me and don't like Humanities, take her. Class may be boring at times, but gives lots of extra credit. I  got an 83 on my midterm that was bumped up to an 88 after attending a speaker. Exams are hard though, but wound up with an A.

If you want to take a class that leaves you with a pounding headache and a feeling of total confusion, this is the class for you. This woman may be nice outside of class, but she manages to make even the most interesting works boring. Anyone who can make Dante's The Inferno boring, deserves a medal of some kind. Avoid Faurot at all costs.

Oh my god, please never ever take a class with this woman. She is so boring you will literally want to put your head through a glass window, thereby cutting your throat and ending your misery. She'll go off on long tangents and you'll have no idea what the frig she's talking about. No such thing as lively class discussions. Stay away, stay away!!!!

Professor Faurot is a nice woman, but a terrible professor.  Her lectures are incomprehensible, and absolutely boring.  She often digresses for long periods of time, and then after you have spent ten minutes writing down her notes she will inform you that what she just said is a useless side-note.  Also extremely unorganized. BEWARE!

Very nice lady and a good teacher. Humanities sucks and she doesn't make it too easy, but I would still recommend her. You have to go to class and you have to read (simple quiz every class) but it does keep you on track if you're like me and puts off everything until the night before a test.
Professor Faurot is very nice and willing to help in any way that she can. She grades very easily, too. Class isn't exactly engaging, but I've taken much worse.

very into religious studies... has spent classes talking about the religious significance of inane things like pollen and grass... mindlessly boring indeed.  fair grader and generally nice person. she does make the books boring as heck though, so be prepared to be bored. i pass the time playing games, try to get a seat in the back.

Not going to lie, haven't read any of the books, yet still have an A.  Go to class, but dont necessarily have to play attention...if you can form a generally well written paper (and bullishit a little bit), you will do fine.  Also, she is opinionated and obsessed with religion studies.
mindlessly boring class. mindlessly boring.

Profe Adams was one of my favorite professors this semester. Though her class was challenging at times, she wanted to see her students succeed. She was more than patient with all of her students, understanding that we all learn at different rates. She was beyond helpful and constantly checked her e-mails. She was a strong support system overall.

This was a online class that was supposed to be in person but the other teacher left.  Videos and Ppts  and she drops the lowest 3 grades and offered extra credit which helps. Responded to emails and offered extra office hours for help.

Professor Adams will not offer you any accomodation for mental health or otherwise. I would not recommend taking a course with her. She cares more about making things easy for herself than she cares about her students and what they experience. The class is also taught at a much higher level than 102 would have you believe.

Professor Adams offers no accomodations whatsoever despite the fact that her course was never meant to be an online course. She offers ZERO flexibility in terms of the course schedule and DOES NOT CARE about when things are due and how it affects you. One of THE WORST courses I've taken in terms of it's impact on my mental health. 0/10 if not less.

For never have taken Spanish before, Professor Adams was very helpful. I enjoyed her lectures and powerpoints. She added fun videos into the class that aid in understanding the subject. She is a very caring professor who really wants her students to succeed. the homework wasn't super clear but she was very easy to reach out of class for questions.

This class is very participation-oriented, so if you're quiet you will be called on. There is lots of homework, but it is simple and easy to stay on top of. Make sure you start the review projects early. Prof Adams is so sweet and wants her students to succeed, and will help when she can while challenging you.

comment: Love her! This class is the highlight of my mornings! There is a good amount of homework, but it's relatively easy if you stay on top of it. Be prepared to be called on/participate periodically because it is an interactive, smaller setting language class, so communication is bound to happen. She wants to see her students succeed and she's so sweet!

She is a really nice person. And yes you need to do lots of works for the class but you learned!!! It is a class that you need to put your efforts in order to receive an A.I am taking Spanish as my third language while I am still struggling with English:(She helped me a lot. If you want to learn Spanish, take her class, it's very helpful.

Taking this class would make you rub your eyes and look again to see if it's actually 101 class because it isn't. Do not take this class for spanish if you are not familiar with spanish and if you're looking for a class that actually matches the level of the class itself.

comment: CLASS IS NOT A BREEZE, YOU HAVE TO WORK FOR YOUR GRADE. YOU ARE REQUIRED TO DO 3 CULTURAL ACTIVITES PLUS SHE CALLS ON YOU RANDOMLY IN CLASS. EXPECT A LOT OF GROUP WORK AND SHE CHECKS HOMEWORK DAILY. I WOULD RECOMMEND IF YOU'RE WILLING TO PUT IN THE WORK FOR THIS CLASS
Love this professor. Definitely take his class!! You will love it!!!! His exams are fun, also lecture is amazing.

If you have the opportunity, take the course with someone else. Attendance is mandatory and you were graded based on how much you talked in class. Lengthy assignments that you could only get full credit for if you go to office hours because there's no rubric for how he wants anything done. There's a final project and a Final exam.

Jeff respects education majors but does not convey material clearly, leading to regular confusion. Participation is key, other than that, you're only graded on lengthy weekly questions and three tests. You also must go to office hours to succeed so keep that in mind. Class is very self-directed; do work in groups without his help.

I have never taken a worse class with a more difficult professor in my life. He is extremely difficult to talk to, not helpful, rude, and inconsiderate. There were multiple times when he was disrespectful to students during class. His lectures are also extremely hard to understand, yet he expects you to know everything that he goes over.

You have to read the entire textbook. After EVERY class you have to write 5 paragraphs reacting to the lecture, and then 5 MORE paragraphs  reacting to the reading (10 total per class, twice a week so 20/week), the reading which mind you is mad long. On top of that he is such a passive aggressive nitpicky grader and his office hours are unhelpful.

I would not wish a class with Jeff Johannes on my worst enemy. For an introductory math class for non-majors, MATH 113 was the hardest class I've taken at Geneseo. There are so many tests, and none of them are easy. He encourages you to ask questions then mocks you for doing so. No professor has made me feel smaller.

Jeff might seem pretty rude at times but he really does care a ton about all of his students. If you put in the effort he expects he is a great professor. I don't like his teaching style but he is very helpful in office hours. His exams are very fair and he wont throw any curveballs at you. Lots of partial credit. Also offers tons of extra credit.

Would not recommend taking this class with him first the first semester of your first year. This class requires you to think much more abstractly with very difficult concepts. Assignments are VERY lengthy with very difficult problems. Start them early. It is essential to ask questions to comprehend topics. Jeff can come off as very overwhelming.

As a freshman I took math topics/Elm ed 140 with Jeff Johannes and failed miserably. Jeff does not make it easy to ask questions and expresses himself with a tone and matter that makes you feel little and dumb. He expects a lot from you and when the work is done it's rewarding yet almost impossible. Take the course with a different professor.

Jeff is so passionate and wants to make sure you succeed and that you become a better teacher. Office hours are super important and he offers a lot of help and flexible timing. The class focuses on group activities like hands on in class assignments and a group portion of each exam. If you want help in the class you need to ask for it. Be vocal!

I'm not gonna lie, Jeff is a hard guy to work with sometimes. His method of teaching is for you to do homework, then he teaches you off the questions you have from that hw after. He also gives nightmarishly long assignments at times, and very hard tests. But he's also a super caring guy who will help you if you put in the time and work necessary.

In class, he is a very good teacher and explains content very well. Out of class, weekly questions are assigned that are near impossible, told its incorrect and gives a failing grade. Very blunt and disrespectful when giving feedback and it is extremely discouraging. Office hours are mandatory to pass, if you don't go, you will fail.

Jeff is a very amazing person with a clear love for math. I enjoyed his class, however he is a very difficult grader and not very open to helping you out. I feel as I learned the concepts well with him but I got a worse grade then I would have got with a different prof. I would recommend switching teachers for lower level math classes.

So much work and he expects you to know stuff that nobody knows. Graded by only tests and 20+ question assignments. Very hard to even have a good grade in this class. He teaches all over the place and is really hard to understand anything he teaches and keep up with him. Do NOT recommend.

Jeff is a passionate professor who really cares about his students. However, his class requires a lot of work - be prepared for challenging weekly assignments and a lengthy final. Unstuckstudy was helpful for practice and prepping, but attendance and office hours are a must to succeed.
Lot of reading and homework and so hard to understand what he's teaching

comment: I learned the most in this class with Jeff out of any class in college. Yes he expects a lot from you but puts in the same amount of time and effort that he expects students to. I dedicated countless hours to his class which is what he expects but his class was really rewarding. If he sees that you put in work he will respect you and help you pass.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework', 'Lecture heavy']

comment: Jeff is one of the most interesting professors I've had. Yes he is blunt, but that doesn't mean he doesn't care. The weekly questions that he has you do help so much and prepare you so much to be a teacher. He helps you understand why the math you're doing is important. Don't base taking his class off the negative reviews, make your own opinion:)

The most caring professor I have come across. He has a genuine unconditional passion for his students. I have struggled with school (particularly math) my whole life and his patience and accessibility taught me much. Jeff is a wonderful person and will be BEYOND happy to help:) (He may seem harsh, but that is how he communicates it isn't personal).

I am not a good math student, so this could be why I didn't do well in his class. But Jeff made me feel more unable to do math than I felt before. His class is more so self-taught in groups, but he will then go over after. He does have very accessible office hours. But instead of encouraging me to come to them, I was told to drop instead.

Initially, I really enjoyed this class, but that changed pretty quickly and I wish I had just dropped it. Jeff is EXTREMELY condescending, told me multiple times that I do not put any effort into the class when I had almost 100% participation and turned in the assignments. You will fail the weekly questions if you do not do them his way. AVOID!

You will never have a more passionate professor, Jeff cares so much about his students. However, if you are not a math student and are simply taking this class because it is required for your major do not take it with him. This is the most work I have ever had for a math class. The final alone was over 70 pages written out.

When I first looked at Jeff on rate my professor, it terrified me. Jeff is the most caring professor I have. You do have to attend his office hours in order to do really well in the class. There are few assignments but they are hefty and you have over a month to complete. I would honestly recommend Jeff to anyone considering taking his class.

Jeff is a great professor. He really cares about the well being of all of his students. He has office hours Monday-Friday and was willing to help with whatever needed. He tends to have a dry sense of humor which I feel some people tend to take the wrong way. This course was very work heavy, but he was always willing to explain everything again.

Jeff is a super nice guy. He is blunt and will tell you exactly what you're doing wrong, don't take it personally. There is no homework besides weekly questions which are due every month. If you do not attend office hours, you won't do well on the weekly questions. He is very accessible outside of class.

let me start by saying avoid Jeff at all costs. He is a terrible professor and an even worse human being. He is extremely mean to students who don't understand his obscure work. He makes office hours mandatory and they go very late into the night. He will assign very long and complicated assignments that he will grade very harshly. STAY AWAY!

The weekly questions are hard for no reason and he grades them like you're in an upper-level math class. If you don't answer the questions in his way then he will call it wrong and make you redo them. He makes really harsh comments to the class and is known to class out people for not understanding the material. Office Hours are mandatory !!!!

Class was extremely difficult and upsetting. Weekly questions are unreasonably hard, and grades them like you're in a 400 level math class. Things ALWAYS need to be done his way even if he tells you they don't need to be. Makes harsh, passive aggressive comments and is not at all sympathetic. If you do not go to office hours you will fail.

math majors should take this intro class. participation is big part of your grade. requires to write 2 reports and 2 short presentations. you can tell jeff really cares about his students and wants to help. dont know how he is with teaching actual math courses, but i can tell he is passionate about what he does.

If you want a professor who will give it to you straight, then Jeff is your guy. The class is centered around self-teaching among groups. There are lengthy projects that he is deeply picky about. If you show him you want to learn, he is easier going about things, but he will never coddle you. Not my type of professor, but maybe someone else's.

jeff is really scary during class. he gets angry when people are confused. if you go to his office hours you will do a lot better. basically, they are mandatory bc if you don't go you will almost fail. there isn't daily hw but there are group projects which are always confusing but not graded.

comment: Jeff was very encouraging to us as future teachers and seems to really respect the profession. Thats about the only nice thing I have to say though. comment: I absolutely love Jeff! I took Math 140 and 141 with him. His class is definitely a different experience. There is no HW but these weekly questions. He is VERY accessible outside of class!

I took this class not knowing that corona virus would affect it however. In the beginning everything seemed pretty easy, but it gets harder and you have to study. His officer hours was also really late till almost 1am on Monday night!! Also when everything became digital we were literally teaching math to yourself and the exams were unreasonable.

comment: Jeff's classes are hard- he wants his students to understand ideas, not memorize. LOVES participation. He wants you to figure things out, but NEVER expects you to figure it out alone. Emails back FAST, and answers questions for hours. Best with specific questions. He cares SO MUCH, but sucks at recognizing emotion. He is never, ever mad at you.
Took his Elm Education Math course and struggled with the work load. He is a harsh grader who wants things done his way. Do not miss class or you will fall far behind.

Jeff is by far, the worst professor I've ever had and nearly ruined my college experience. Extremely condescending to those who aren't on his good side / do not attend his late office hours. The absolute worst experience of my college career. Horrific teacher, lacks all communication skills. He is extremely rude and does not know how to give constructive criticism in the slightest way. The only way you will pass the class if you attend every office hour session. He does not believe in giving A's. Seriously drop the class asap!!!!!

Jeff acts as if he wants you not to understand the material. His grading criteria is unclear and seemingly arbitrary. When you go to him in office hours he often refuses to help you understand the material as "That would prevent you from truly learning". He has a nice holiday party though.

comment: Avoid at all costs. A class with him is not worth sacrificing your emotional health.

Teaches nothing. He just gives chapter readings for hw and then asks the class what they thought of it instead of a lesson. He thinks way to highly of himself and is condescending when you ask for help. The textbook dictates his class and he is to lazy to do anything that isn't right out of it. An online class would be better than taking his class.

This class is 90% group work, tediously figuring out ways to find answers to questions instead of him teaching. Although the weekly questions didn't sound like a lot the first day, THEY ARE TIME CONSUMING. Johannes has super high expectations.  You much show up to class and participate daily. I worked hard & this class still managed to kill my GPA.

Rude and condescending. Will not help you at all, honestly enjoys that his students do not understand whats going on. Does not even teach, the whole class is just the students teaching themselves and each other while he stands in the front of the room being creepy. Awful experience with this professor. Will never take a class with him again.

Jeff is a tough professor that has high expectations for his students. He can come off as rude and unsympathetic but if you can get past that he isn't awful. To do well in the class you need to be willing to put in the time in/out of class and don't get discouraged or offended when working with Jeff. You spend most of the class working in a group.
In a word, creepy.  Speaks as if he was a god.  Just weird.  Kept staring at my body.

He is verywilling to help you outside of class.  The final project grading doesn't seem to make any sense. ALWAYS come to class five minutes before hand. comment: This class is constructed of about 85% group work and 15% lecture,& you have to spend a lot of your time figure out the answer to things by yourself. He can come off as rude but it's because he wants you to truly understand what is being talked about. He holds a lot of hours & your grade will definitely be better if you go to them. Won't take again

Where do I start with this class. I have had some tough professors in my day especially as a biology student going into the medical field. But it is not even his toughness which is why I am leaving this negative review. His rudeness and outright disregard for students feelings was too much to ignore. I felt it was my duty to warn others!

This class was honestly traumatic.  I would avoid it unless you can read a math textbook like a novel and don't struggle with math anxiety. You will be teaching yourself. Johannes is the least personable human I have ever encountered, and his complete lack of social skills /compassion makes asking for help extremely painful.

Jeff expects a lot from his students, but if you are willing to put in the time and effort, you will do well. He's extremely knowledgable and passionate, yet gets a bad rep for pushing his students, and for his cut and dry manner, but he only wants you to succeed and is so dedicated to helping you do so. Show him respect and he will reciprocate!

The class was set up entirely using group work and problem solving, and we never had lectures. That made it really confusing sometimes, but if you went to talk to him during office hours it could clarify things. He can come off very abrupt but he really does care about all of his students. Hard, and frustrating class, but you'll end up learning.

He's a harsh grader and office hours are essential. He can be rude and condescending towards you, but he can really make you see calc abstractly. His tests are practically insane and you probably won't do well on them, but problem sets will help your grade boost up. Don't really recommend taking him, especially if you're not a math major!!!!!
Jeff makes you work harder than any other math professor. If you're not into to going to office hours and giving a measly 1000%, this isn't the class for you.

Jeff is honestly a good man, however, he is very intimidating. His class is extremely difficult and I basically taught myself from the book. Help is readily available if your willing to subject yourself to harsh comments. Overall, my work ethic and ability to learn alone has been strengthened and for that i am thankful.

Jeff's an amazing professor. One of my favorites. He's had a tough rep the past few years but I promise, if you put in the work, you'll get an A. IT'S hard in any of his classes but he will walk through step by step with you until you get it right. Which, because of that, you'll get 100% on your homeworks which is a huge % of your grade. TAKE HIM.
Do not take if you cant avoid... he has enrollment issues for a reason. Jeff also gets personal enjoyment from watching students struggle.

Hardest professor. DO NOT TAKE A CLASS WITH HIM IF YOU CAN AVOID IT. He wants perfection & as a Cornell grad he likes to show how smart he is. He runs a reverse classroom where students do a wkst before class then he goes over questions. This method does not seem to work. He enjoys finding the hardest questions in the text & assigning them for hw

Probably my favorite math professor at the school. Super caring, would stay til 2am to work with you. Work is hard but rewarding, he's a fair grader, the way the class is structured is very nice and gives lots of opportunity to make up a bad grade. Only catch is that asking questions in class is intimidating bc he really makes you work for the ansr

Jeff is a very intelligent man. You NEED to take a class with him while you're here at Geneseo. He cares SO MUCH about his students. As long as you participate in class, go to office hours, and work with classmates, you will do well. He is hard to connect with at first, but if you make the effort to show you care about class, you will learn a lot.
Dont take classes with Jeff. He is not good at communicating his thoughts and will talk condescending towards anyone who misunderstands the material.

Calc II is difficult no matter who you take it with. At the beginning Jeff may seem harsh, but over the course of the semester you come to realize just how much he cares about you. I had a tough first semester of college, yet Jeff was completely accommodating. Jeff is not about easy A's or "regurgitation", he's about conceptual understanding.

This class is one of the hardest classes I have ever taken, and yet it is worthwhile in the end, I promise you. Jeff can come off as rude, but what other professor would stay past midnight for office hours if you need him? If you are willing to work I highly recommend him for the amount of stuff he can teach you.

Imagine if the Karate Kid had looked at Mr. Miyagi and said, "I'm not waxing anything, you crazy old man" and left. Everyone would have said 'You're so dumb, this guy obviously knows what he's doing'. Jeff is just like Mr. Miyagi, except he has a ponytail instead of a mustache. His classes are a lot of work, but eventually you will sweep the leg.

Jeff is the most challenging professor I had for both math and education, but by far one of the most dedicated. He is always there for his students - staying hours after office hours to ensure you understood the material. One of the greatest things he taught me was how to think. Put the work in and show you care. It will make all the difference!

Jeff taught more than content, he taught us how to learn.  His class is not easy, but you'll be a better student and mathematician after you take a course with him. He doesn't "hold your hand" which many students find frustrating; instead  he somehow gets you to think beyond how you normally would about mathematics.

Never have I learned more useful information in a class than I did with Jeff in INTD 301.  He has taught me more about secondary mathematics than any other professor. If you work hard and work as a class you will do well.  If you are becoming a teacher, you owe it to your future students to learn from him.

Jeff is the most challenging professor I had my entire time at Geneseo. However, with that said the materials, the social skills, and the level of caring and interest truly makes an impact in my own classroom everyday. The entire class came together to work, and we were successful. You will not just be handed a good grade, it is rewarding work.

One of the hardest math classes but also one of the most rewarding. Jeff is a brilliant professor who doesn't just give you the answers in office hours. He makes you think.  He emphasizes conceptual understanding so you truly understand a concept. If you put in the work and ask the right questions, you'll learn a lot and earn a good grade.

Here's the thing about Jeff- he expects you to work hard. If you do so and ask good questions in class and office hours, he will take note of it and teach you way more than any other professor. He actually makes you think. He's not one to just give you the answers.  One of the best math professors I've ever had. INTD 301 was the most useful class.

Rarely do professors have such a positive impact on a class like Jeff. Only you can decide how well you do in it. It will not be easy so you must preserve. Jeff is extremely honest, if you do something wrong, he will let you know. If you and your classmates work together then you will be praised and every class will be simply amazing.

The thing about Jeff is that you get out of his classes what you put into them. If you work hard, you'll learn more in one course than in all of your others combined. If you're not going to work hard, don't enroll - if you want to TRULY learn, sign up right away. He is extremely invested in his students. Best professor I've ever had, hands down.

If you have thin skin, you will feel insulted by what he says and hate the class. If you get past that and want to learn, he will challenge you and you will come out his class knowing a lot of mathematics. He does teach well, but if you are easily offended, he isn't for you. He is not a bad person, he just says things that can hurt people.
He is the worst man ever. DO NOT TAKE ANYTHING WITH HIM. Avoid at all costs!!!
i would rather peel off my eyelids than take another class with Johannes

I have never written a review on this site but couldn't let this one go.  By far, the worst teacher I have ever had at any level of education.  The guy reported 3/4 of our class for plagiarism off of a website I had never seen before.  All creepy comments seen in other posts are 100% true, all while licking his bottom lip. Terrible person/teacher
Worst professor ever. Made me change my major. avoid him, avoid him, avoid him.

When you first meet Johannes, you get the vibe that he is a really cool, chill professor who has a ponytail, likes to be called by his first name, and doesn't believe in "tests." However, you soon find out how condescending he really is. I have never felt more disrespected or belittled in a class before. DO NOT RECOMMEND.

The worst professor on the face of the planet! He is arrogant and rude. He does not teach. He makes you go home and read the textbook and then come to class and he asks if you have any questions. Not once did he actually teach a lesson. He also makes you feel stupid when you ask a question. AVOID HIM.

I've used linear algebra for a long time before taking his class so whenever I went I never really paid attention to whatever content was being taught. I did notice that he was kinda rude to people. Teaching aside, I don't think he understands the basics of reading other people. IE: When a quip is funny, and when it is derogatory.

do not take a class with him!! he will spend the entire semester insulting your class' intelligence. tests and problem sets are ridiculously hard, the problem sets take forever, and you're pretty much forced to go to office hours if you want a decent grade. he's actually a good teacher but he ruins it by being such a condescending prick

Not an awful teacher in class, but expects way too much for calc II. Problem sets take hours to do, and you HAVE to go to the office hours to do well on them. Exams are ridiculous, and he is very very condescending.
He was not approachable at all for me and took off a ton of points for silly mistakes on tests. Basically, he ruined math for me.

He is arrogant but approachable. He is not a good prof. There are 6 problem sets(5%/each) and this is the hardest part of the class. Tests and quizzes is very very easy because he takes the easiest questions from the book.If you can't do the problem set, go ask anyone and get the points. Again, tests are so easy

Worst professor I have ever had, by far!  If you care about your grades, do NOT take any class with him!  He is extremely arrogant and condescending.  Office hours are pointless, because he just makes you want to cry.

DO NOT TAKE IF YOU LIKE EQUATIONS, HE IS STRICTLY CONCEPT!! Loved Math before I met him. He is very condescending and only confuses you more. He chooses a book out of print, doesn't understanding Maple (program used for lab) Problem sets take forever to complete. His exams are IMPOSSIBLE and harshly graded. Simply the best teacher I've ever had in any context. Challenging, takes your work seriously, holds you to high standards, and pushes you to THINK. Also incredibly helpful and an excellent mentor.

Dr. McCoy is absolutely fantastic.  One of the smartest people I have ever met and someone that has taught me so much, going beyond the classroom.  You have to work hard, but it is well worth it as the knowledge you obtain at semesters end is what college is all about.  Highly recommend.

She's an absolutely great teacher, but be warned, she expects A LOT. McCoy wants you to work hard to improve as a writer, but as long as you're willing to put in some effort, it will pay off. I recommend this class to anyone who wants to become a better writer within a semester(And is able to work hard!)

Extremely intelligent woman who will challenge the way you look at the world. Don't expect everything to come together at the end of the class - she wants you to start asking questions in her class and begin answering them afterward - and on your own. GO TO CLASS - she doesn't give reading quizzes, but her classes are an experience. Be there.
Best teacher at Geneseo. Changed my life.
Her material is really complex therefore her papers were difficult to write. Gives a lot extra credit opportunities. Extremely helpful. I enjoyed going to her class.
Best class I have taken so far  at Geneseo.  Even if you are a horrible writer, if you work at it you will improve by taking this class.  Definitely go to all of the conferences, they help a lot.

Beth was personable and fun.  The texts were all relevant and useful.  Her feedback was helpful and thoughtful.  She makes you think outside the box and find what really interests you.  I learned so much from her and I'm very impressed with her as an educator.  The coursework could be very challenging, but not stressful.

She didn't focus much on the topic at hand in class discussions but instead talked about whatever made her sound smart at the time with only a few people.  Be warned that jumping into class discussions is difficult unless you want to get your intelligence assaulted.  Boring paper topics and most of the class was focuse around the text, Cane.

A fantastic teacher who really wants to help you. A must for Intd 105 because she will help you understand how to truly write and analyze. She really knows what she's talking about and the class will go by very quickly.

Smartest woman in the world. Very respectable. Hilarious. Class flies by. Does everything she can to make the class a community. And if your writing doesn't improve after one of her classes you obviously didn't go. Shes a tough grader so a good grade on a paper is incredibly rewarding. Don't expect an A in this class without a lot of extra work.

Unlike anything I've ever taken.  The readings are all useful, interesting, and accessible.  There are four response papers and one final paper (5-7 pages).  The point of all of them is to really get you thinking.  Beth is BRILLIANT.  She's also open-minded, approachable, and always willing to help.  Hands down the best teacher I've ever had.

She is a great professor.  I learned how to become a much better argumentative writer because of her.  She was always there to help whenever I needed it and I would definitely take another class with her.  She is a tough grader, especially on the first paper which I got a D+/C-(which wasn't recorded), but by the end of the year I got an A-.
She's really awesome - she really knows what she's talking about. Even if you take the class and don't get A's, you'll benefit from the class overall. She also gives extra credit opportunities.
Let's just say that after one of Beth's lectures back in 1999, she got a standing ovation. She inspired me to be THAT kind of teacher. She rocks!

Absolutely an amazing professor!  Classes were always interesting, well structured, and enjoyable!
She'll blow your mind.  Make you think in a whole new manner.

I LOVE BETH!!!  She really makes you think.  She's awesome during office hours and I LOVED the class.  She can be a tough grader, but as long as you "Unpack" your thoughts in your papers you'll be fine.  TAKE A CLASS WITH HER! It will be a challenge but IT WILL BE WORTH IT!!!

McCoy is not a bad person but she's a horrible teacher. I learned more about Af-Amer lit in my other survey classes than in her Af-Amer lit class. She's not very open to other ideas. Don't take her unless you like being told that you should feel shame for being white.
Great prof. "Think outside the box" kind of person. If you don't like class discussion, avoid her classes, but if you do like it, definitely take it.

Beth is an AMAZING professor.  She challenges you to think outside the box and question what you have known to be true or taken for granted in your own life.  She's big on participation, and truly appreciates and excepts your comments and different interpretations. Don't be intimidated, she's great!

Very nice professor, but also sometimes intimidating.  She is very into participation and "unpacking."  She really appreciates it when you come and ask for help on assignments.  As long as you get into the discussion in any way, you'll be fine.  Also, she had no final which is always a plus!

There are a few assignments that may seem major, but she frontloads the course, and there isn't a final, so the end of the semester is very easy! She tends to be lax about due dates, so just let her know if you have a problem. She's alway willing to help. She encourages discussion, so beware!

Very engaging. She'll make a huge deal out of participation at the first class, but don't be afraid. It doesn't end up being bad at all. Good material and discussion. Sometimes she's a little over people's heads. It's hard to take Af. Amer stuff with her cuz the class is all white.

Beth is excellent--cares about your ideas, not your grades. Very into discussing your own personal interaction with texts, and very idea-oriented. Smart and provoking, and does not think anyone is stupid. I love her even though she could assign more hard-core work.
Highly discussion oriented, if you don't like talking avoid Beth's classes.  Other than that, outstanding in every aspect.

AMAZING prof- will work very hard to get you to the point where you're examining everything in your own life you previously took for granted-- gets even the most reluctant students to contribute to class discussiong without any force, just by peaking their interest- goes far above and beyond her job
amazing, smart, witty, beautiful, passionate, energetic, all with a touch of class.  She drives the point home.
I never thought I could enjoy hum so much.  She's a great teacher, encourages students' own perspectives.  Classes were interesting, and I was SAD when it was over

she is awesome-a very cool woman who pushes you in an unorthodox way.you don't really care too much about your grade in the class, she gets you too wrapped up in the lessons that make you question things you never did before.feel exhausted after her class
i totally disagree with the advising comment.  she is a dedicated advisor.  she expects responsibility tho

Beth was fantastic.  She was the best prof. I ever had at Geneseo. She made us think, she challenged us at every turn, and she lost herself in the lit. She also created a comfortable classroom environment.  Thanks Beth!
I appreciated her enthusiasm and passion for cultural literature, but it was hard to discuss all viewpoints in my white-only class. She pushed too much for answers we couldn't come up with.
not very helpful as an advisor, either

She is AWESOME! I love her. She engages you in topic and you come away with something meaningful. She's the best prof.
Beth McCoy rocks my intellectual world.
tough but helpful and makes things matter

Very Engaging, challenges you to think and speak your mind...An asset to school
