She is willing to help you as long as you ask for help and are willing to do work. Projects can be tedious but they help you to understand how kids feel.
Extremely disorganized and it is frustrating to navigate her class.

I think she is a kind person, but her directions and layout of the online class was so disorganized. There are many typos and technical errors. It wasn't clear what was explicitly expected. This caused stress among the class. It takes a while to communicate with her.

Absolutely abysmal, and incredibly frustrating. I don't think if I were a weaker person I could have made it through this class as I did. Just makes the same ridiculous suggestions over and over even if your student will stuffer from them and doesn't care about growing you as a learner.

She is the very definition of "disorganized". The due dates in her syllabus are incorrect (because she never changes them). She's an easy grader but doesn't hold back on providing useless criticism. If you are ever confused about an assignment and need any clarification, don't expect an immediate reply. Oh, and do not take her for clinic. Godspeed.
Very disorganized!

Dr. Peck was awesome for my first summer taking classes at the graduate level! She was very accessible and always available when you had questions. Dates sometimes got mixed up but this was understandable since we were taking a summer course that was only 4 weeks. I loved attending the optional weekly conversations about reading. Love Dr.Peck!!

Dr. Peck was incredibly unorganized throughout our entire semester. Her responses indicate that she doesn't read your work for content or context but is mainly concerned with your margins and font size. Dr. Peck gives out constructive criticism about once in a blue moon and all other comments (there are many) are snarky or just mean. Don't take!
Totally disorganized. Wants everything to be fun but then doesn't teach us anything.

While the class itself would not be difficult taught by another professor, her lack of organization and communication makes it almost impossible. Directions are unclear and scattered, not to mention how long it takes to get an email back from her. I have had to email her for clarification almost everyday. Do not take her class if you can avoid it.

Dr. Peck is a very enthusiastic teacher. She really loves to practice what she preaches when it comes to play-based learning. Her class is interactive and inspiring. Im now obsessed with play-based learning! She does assign quite a bit of reading for during the week, but you can get by if you only read what you are presenting that week.
The most unorganized professor I have ever had!

One of the worst professors I have EVER had! She hands out the syllabus and that essentially is supposed to tell you what to do for all your assignments/projects. It is unclear and so is she. I have had to read 100's of pages of text only to have NEVER discussed them in class. She also doesn't have a lot of meaningful activities, also disorganized.
Great, loving teacher. Knows her material well.

One of the best professors in the Education Dept, for sure. She knows what she's talking about, and she's so happy to share her knowledge with you. If you have any questions, she'll help you in any way she can!
No clear guidance and direction... Sometimes I feel disappointed and don't want to attend this class.

Wow. I do not know where to start.  Guidelines (if you can call them that) are unclear... you basically have to draw upon several different sources to have a remote idea of what she wants from you.  Many long term projects.  She's enthusiastic about the material, but not enough to cancel out the frustrations you will encounter because of the class.

She's a nice person, but she NEVER gives directions and she NEVER explains assignments. ASK LOTS OF QUESTIONS if you get her. If you ask q?'s about the work you'll do ok. Once you know what to do the stuff is EASY. She grades EASY too. Lots of the stuff is groupwork too. It isn't vital to read the textbook or assignments to do well. ASK QUESTIONS!

You literally have no idea what is going on. the least clear teacher i have ever had. she is in love with the subject matter but cant help you at all. does not make class useful for secondary ed students at all. avoid if you can but if you cant just go to class and email her a lot. kinda useless assignments and a lot of them

Teaches exactly how she says NOT to teach. In front of the overhead projector. Little to no hands on activities. Drones on about nothing, very boring and unhelpful. She should stick to puppets because she can't teach. Little experience in the real teaching world (what is she only 35?)
He's awesome! Lecture based, easy quiz's, entertaining classes. 10 out of 10 take his classes. There is a lot of group work but it is graded very fair

Harnish is hands down my favorite professor in the business department. He grades very fairly, his tests are easy and he does review for them. Literally a college level course in terms of material but with high school level difficulty on tests. He wants your grades to excel while learning the material, and not to bury you in nonsensical work.
Not hard, did not have to show up to class besides exam days, only hard thing was the final

Dr Harnish is great! He is extremely accommodating; when the final got switched to in-person instead of online last minute and I told him I was past the deadline for the testing center, he allowed me to take it at home! Such a kind person, funny, tests are easy if you pay attention in class, and lectures are engaging. Very reasonable grader as well
Harnish is amazing. There are 3 speeches in the class but it's easy and overall the class is easy. He's funny and nice too.

Harnish is one of the best professors I have taken a class with here. His goal is for you to get something out of his class but not making it unnecessarily hard to do so. His assignments are fun and straight forward. I highly recommend taking a class with him.

Dr. Harnish is awesome. Lectures are easy to understand, assignments are always clear, and tests are easy if you just study a little bit. He always ends class early, super chill. Would 100% take a class with him again.

Harnish is a really chill guy and loves to teach. His lectures tend to be short and follow the reading pretty well. He takes attendance before every class and usually ends classes early. There are many speeches in class The final group presentation is pretty long but easy. He gives usually at least one assignment due on Friday.There's only one test
He's a great guy. He teaches the basics, but makes sure to help you ace it so you have a strong base to stand on in the future. 10/10, would take again, even if he graded tougher.

INTD 205 is mostly presentations, mixed individually and in groups. The hw is online and is usually one assignment a week. Harnish is respectful and professional . No quizzes/tests, just one final exam and he gives you a study guide for it. Presentations aren't bad. Take the class. Easily one of the most down to earth professors on campus.

Good professor. Means well and respects all students. Direction in the class was slightly unclear at times but that's not too big of a negative. Has a good perspective because he currently works as an executive for a non-profit.

Professor Harnish was super caring and made his class very enjoyable. He does take attendance, and it will help your grade if you go. Lenient grader, assignments were not too difficult if you put the work in. Highly recommend him, and I plan to take future classes with him.

Wonderful professor. Shes very knowledgeable about the topics you study and tries to make lectures as interesting as possible. Study for tests and you will do fine. She wants you to pass and will try to help you if needed. I cant explain how much I loved her class!
Lecture heavy, not specific, big on participation. Good luck finding her outside of class

Amazing professor!! Great lectures, full of personal experience from years of clinical experience. The class is work; there is a lot of content to learn and she assigns 4 papers, but any abnormal section would be a lot of work and she makes it so worth it.  Gives out study guides for the test and has very clear, well organized slides online
She's amazing

Professor Forbes is absolutely amazing. I have been sick most of the semester and she really went out of her way to help me succeed regardless. Her lectures are really great and she puts all the slides online as well as some of the quizzes. There are a couple papers but they're actually quite fun to write.

He is such a sweet guy but I would not recommend this class if you are not good at memorizing (or you feel good about cheating like most students) because the tests are not easy. He does not really go over anything that is required for the tests and he constantly pushes them back. He does give makeups which is nice.

I enjoyed having Professor Kimball. The format of this class was 3 listening quizzes and 3 exams. If you read his notes and listen to the CDs he posts on Brightspace, you'll be fine. His lectures won't really help on the tests but if you enjoy the history of music, you may find his lectures interesting. He also gives a ton of extra credit.
really sweet guy, but does not focus on the actual content for quizzes in class. people cheat on the quizzes and he doesn't care

Kimball is amazing! He cares about his students, and will usually give extra credit (at least for the 100 levels). His listening quizzes are mainly based on the CD's given in class so they can be challenging, but usually as long as you listen outside of class and pay attention you should be fine.

He is a very nice man and has a lot of musical knowledge, but all class we would sit there and he would talk for 40min then play like 3 music examples then our entire grade was based on really really hard listening quizes. I'm a music student and I've had many listening quizes before and his were exceptionally hard for absolutely no reason

Prof Kimball is a nice person, however, his class is pretty difficult for a Music Gen Ed. Overall, I would not take this class again and instead take a different Introductory Music class. The quizzes count as 80% of your grade and are pretty difficult if you do not study. Do the extra credit write ups. Also the lectures don't go with the quizzes.

Jim Kimball is the sweetest man in Geneseo, without a doubt. The class had little to no outside work, with one short paper & presentation being about it. We watched movies and just discussed whatever he felt like discussing that day. Greatly increased my appreciation of folk music too! Love his class!!

Easier than expected. Kimball is the sweetest old man, very knowledgable about all things music (particularly folk music). A lot of the classes were boring since he loves to talk, but we had fun in a class of 5 playing the recorder/metal spoons and square dancing. Graded assignments are few, so definitely study for the listening exams.

Kimball is old, but hilarious. He's very charming and straight forward with the information, and really knows his stuff. The class requires a little more effort than expected, and the quizzes can be tough if you don't study for them. Nice guy, somewhat bland class, and textbook isn't required at all.

Adorable teacher and so nice and understanding.  Extremely boring and the tests are so hard.  You have to memorize like 40 songs.  Deff NOT an easy A.  Wouldn't recommend the class unless you're willing to work very hard. But he is a very nice man and will definitely help anyone who asks for it!

Prof. Kimball is a very nice and passionate person. He loves his class and is very knowledgeable about music. The class was boring but the music tests were simple as long as you studied and memorized the songs. The tests were right out of the notes. Class attendance was not mandatory.

For an 8:30 class, it was pretty interesting. Kimball is enthusiastic about what he teaches. Quizzes consist of memorizing songs, which is easy if you take an hour or two to study. He tells you everything you need to know on the test. Easy A if you apply yourself!

The best professor I have ever had. He was so knowledgeable about each and every topic we learned. The material is really interesting if you like music (who doesn't). Exams are a piece of cake because he basically tells you what's going to be on it. Take any course with him!!! You won't regret it.

He is so knowledgeable!  He reminds me of my grandpa! He is extremely understanding about missed quizzes, but this class is not an easy A, however, there are lots of opportunities to do well.  The best part of class is when he brings in instruments to play, or dances around the room by himself, I loved this class, and this professor.

The things he knows are beyond anything you'd ever imagine. He's intelligent and very knowledgable in what he teaches.  However it tends to be about things irrelevant to tests/quizzes/grades.. while interesting, not always helpful.  Study for all quizes they're not easy to BS your way through and they're 80% of your grade.

Jim Kimball is by far the most interesting professor I've come across on the Geneseo campus. To be in a room with him is to learn something new, almost without exception. He draws from an immeasurably vast bank of both knowledge and love. I think that everybody on campus should take Music Of the World's Peoples. Maybe that's just me talking, though
Very interesting class, you can tell this professor is passionate about what he does. Kind of boring and dull at times however. Tests are hard, so study, especially the listening.
He definitely knows his stuff, but trying to see him during office hours for a question a waste of time.  Takes forever to grade things.

Nice guy, knows so much about the performers and their music. Despite this, his tests are not as easy as those in a b.s. core class ought to be.. over half the tests are made up of T/F questions..which he makes tough. He also has listening quizzes but they're easy. I don't know where my grade is at, which is unsettling.. hoping for at least an A-
He is an amazing teacher.  He has old song sheets from every artist we learn about and he can play every instrument!  Super nice and helpful.  Easy to get in touch with.

Kimball is a genius when it comes to anything on music. He's also really friendly and a great teacher! You have to be good at memorizing songs to ace his tests. If you can do that (i put them on shuffle in itunes to test myself) then an A should be easily attainable. I really enjoyed this class.

This class became a lot harder the I had anticipated. I thought Professor Kimball had a wealth of information and appreciated what he had to offer. He did however go off on tangents sometimes that didn't have a lot to do with the class. If you take this class the memorizing and listening tests are def. harder then you would think! Study!!
Very fun teacher, Hes good at getting the entire class involved.  He's not shy about playing music or singing in falsetto (Pretty Funny)  Anyway, great experience all arround.
He is such a nice old man.  He was really into the subject matter.  If you know a little about music, this is an easy class.  Attend class and you'll be fine.  I had a lot of fun in this class.

He is a very intelligent man, and provides many details, but his tests are hard, I felt there was to much emphasis put on listening, and if you don't have listening memorized it hurts you big time, but other than that his class was fun, interesting and can play just about any instrument!

Very intelligent man, quite eccentric. Whatever he writes on the board make sure you put in your notes. Pay attention to what he says in class because he gives answers to the rev. sheets. Know all your notes and your listening examples because he tests on it all.  Easy A if you memorize everything.
Very nice, just make sure you memorize alllll of the songs, what country they are from, etc for tests. The tests are ONLY easy if you study for them.
If you think this class will be easy, think again. a lot of work and the tests are hard! he's a nice man and very smart, but this class was not easy, by any means.

I've taken two classes with him and want more.  He knows so much about anything involving music and has done so many things.  He's a treasure.  his classes are easy and interesting at the same time- unbeatable.
I'll never forget the day I walked into Popular Music and he was blasting Public Enemy.  He's a great professor.  Take folk guitar with him if you get the chance.
Interesting guy but presents a lot of information....there's lots of listening so study up
Very interesting guy. This was one of the best electives I took at Geneseo. He's funny, entertaining and extrememly talented. Don't pass up a chance to learn from him.
I've taken multiple classes with him.  He is funny, interesting, and knows everything about everything.
I have never been so amazed at one persons talent in playing soo many different instruments!  His love of music gave me a higher appreciation of music

I found him to be really confusing for this class.  but makes class interesting by bringing in his collection of random instruments from any given era.  know your listening rep backwards and forwards for any of his classes!

Professor Hart is a fantastic professor. Hart is deeply passionate about what he teaches and his lectures are very engaging. His course is very challenging, but he is dedicated to helping each of his students learn the material. Professor Hart is always very accessible during office hours and will help you with any questions about assignments.
genuinely in love with this man

Intelligent, knowledgeable, and caring professor.  Knows all his students by name.  Gives great and entertaining lectures which make morning classes easy.  Engages in discussion with students and has great metaphors/explanations that make it easy for different people to understand the same ideas.  Lots of respect for him and I would take again.

Professor Hart is probably my favorite professor at Geneseo. Despite PLSC 251 being very difficult and boring, I never felt that way when I was in his class. He kept things interesting, and was always available for extra help on the content. Could not recommend him enough!

He is energetic and gives engaging and fun lectures so although you don't hAvE to go to class you should and he really appreciates that. Gives very specific instructions and detailed guidelines for papers and studyguides. He is really very helpful, especially if you go to Office hours

comment: Professor Hart made a tough subject manageable. I really appreciated his feedback that pointed out both the good and any "goofs" on assignments. Awesome educator. Made me want to actually learn Statistics, which is no easy task.

Professor Hart brings a great energy to his lectures and seems excited to teach. This class is heavily writing based. comment: He is a great professor. He was very energetic and engaging even during the early class. comment: Notes can be confusing, but he has the students' best interest at heart. Encourages office hours, posts supplemental notes, nice guy.

Nice, but as a professor, he is not that good. He belittles his students with sometimes insulting comments and the course very heavily textbook based. His example problems are good, but it is hard to understand what he is after sometimes. The course is outcome based, as in the long, confusing tests basically determine your entire course grade.

McGarrah was such a great professor! Some people are just upset because they don't realize you need to do work outside of class to do well.  He was very attentive to the needs of his students and wanted everyone to do well. Everything covered in class was straight out of the book, and his review sessions were so helpful.

He was NOT a bad teacher, I learned alot from him. However he often had a belittling attitude toward his students. It was intimidating. On the other hand, he is a really sweet guy deep down, I think he means well. If you go see him in office hours he's helpful. You can tell he really has a passion for teaching and chemistry.
Enthusiastic about the class, tells you exactly what you need to know to get a good grade in the class. Most Fair teacher I've had at Geneseo.
Dr. McGarrah is a very passionate teacher. he put a lot of effort into making sure every student succeeds. I would strongly suggest taking a chem class with him. I got an A+
I thought he was a very good teacher. He made the class interesting as well as easy to comprehend. He used methods besides just lecturing to help use learn.
disorganized, unclear. Read the textbook, come to class sometimes, you'll do fine. That said, he said he's never teaching this course again so dw about it

Dr. McGarrah is definitely NOT the professor you want to have in an Intro to Chem course. He gives a lot of time consuming homework and his exams are hard and take forever. He's not helpful at all because he just can't teach. Take a different teacher for Chem. You'll thank me.
Terrible professor. Being fired/let go/whatever after Spring 2014. His lectures are so awkwardly uncomfortable. Try to get McKnight for Chem 116 instead.
does not explain the material well...he doesn't care if you go to class but yet he gets angry when you tell him you missed a class. office hours were not very helpful at all.

A nice guy, kinda geeky nerdy, but a sweetheart and honestly one of the only professors not within my major that made the effort  to know my name. Chem 118 is more challenging than Chem 116, but he goes over harder material in class. Do the HW and his old tests and its an easy A.
McGarrah is a very easy teacher, but is poor at explaining the material. He gives fair tests and is a very friendly person, just not the best teacher

Mickey-G was one of the best professors I have ever had! He is very friendly, and is always offering bits of advice, mints, and smiles! Seriously - take class with this man and attend his office hours! You will NOT regret this.

Although Dr. McGarrah may not be very clear with presenting the material in class, his tests are fair and he sincerely wants his students to do well. Of course, you need to be able to do some outside work on your own; keep up with the suggested readings and ATTEND OFFICE HOURS! A little awkward and quirky but a very laid-back guy. I got a B+.

Terrible professor.  Class isn't hard, but he doesn't teach anything so it's up to you to learn it.  Blames you for his lack of teaching skill.  When he goes over a topic, it starts with the most specific and briefly mentions the general. In the last test, it was 40% based on something he showed in 4 Power Point slides. Stay away at all costs.

This professor is TERRIBLE. Avoid him at all costs. Rather than admitting he does things wrong he blames everything on the students and, in turn, makes them feel bad about themselves. He makes mistakes all the time and if you read the book he makes lectures MORE confusing. If you have him, I'm sorry. read the book, and try not to listen to him...

So confusing, terribly disorganized, insecure and rude. You cannot ask questions, slides are always filled with mistakes. Do not expect to learn anything from lecture, teach yourself and you might do ok. If you have to take him, make friends with a chem major.

taking the class was the worst mistake of my life. He is a terrible teacher, doesn't know how to teach and expects you do to all the work on your own. He always has mistakes on his slides and spends a lot of class time fixing it. The tests are very hard, and the class will destroy your GPA. Taking his class would be a foolish mistake.

He is not the most organized. You MUST do the homework and read the textbook, he is not interested in summarizing. If he gives a worksheet know how to answer the entire worksheet. I dont have much about the professor, considering at least 90% of the class was taught about another class by someone other than the professor. comment: Quinn Is able to keep lectures interesting with stories and examples that relate back to the topics he's going over. There are only 4 quizzes and 3 tests and he hints at what is going to be on them. Definitely one of the best professors here. Highly recommend taking a class with him.
Very caring professor. Not a lot of homework. Test and quiz questions are a little difficult but he uses a good curve. Love him

Quinn is a tough professor. His lectures are heavy and he often goes of on tangents and strays away from the important material. Only three quizzes and two tests the entire semester and those are the only assignments. I have studied so hard for everything and have still managed to fail every quiz and test. Offers up to three points of extra credit.

Professor Quinn goes on long tangents during his lectures that make it very difficult to pay attention and get a general idea of what he is talking about. Professor Quinn is very knowledgeable and passionate about Business Law. Very few assignments, 3 tests and 3 quizzes. Very easy tests/quizzes as he basically spoon feeds the questions on test/quizzes throughout lectures. Very amazing guy who makes law very interesting. Loved the class and professor!

Amazing Professor, he genuinely cares about his students and wants to see you succeed. Lots of experience and tests are pretty straight up, just make sure to write down any of the small details he adds in during lectures. Pay attention in the lectures and youll be fine.

Jim Quinn is one of the best professors I have had so far. The class was based off of 3 tests and 2 quizzes, so you have to do well on those to get a good grade. This wasn't hard to do as his lectures were very informative and actually interesting. He cares about his students and was very accommodating during the pandemic.

Prof Quinn is by far one the nicest and best professors I have had. The class grade mainly comes down to the three exams, each are based highly on his lectures, at least for his online zoom class. If you pay attention, take notes, and study, this class should be a breeze. I highly recommend taking his classes, he's the best!

Professor Quinn is by far the best professor that i have ever taken a class with, his tests are modeled after his notes which he makes very easy to follow and accessible outside of class, I look to see what classes i can take with him being the professor, 10/10 would recommend definitely take his class

He tries to make lectures fun and engaging. Sometimes class can get a little boring, but the cases are pretty interesting. He has two classes, one where you take a midterm and don't have hw, and one where you write a paper, have hw but don't take a midterm. His class is very doable if you study. Very intelligent and has a lot to share.

Everyone seems to love him. I thought he was ok. Tests are difficult (its law cant blame him) and graded on a curve. But the curve gets messed up because so many people cheat. I dont know if he lets it happen, but it was incredibly obvious he either literally couldnt see or didnt care. His lectures were good, entertaining to an extent.

Quinn is one of the most amazing people I've ever met, let alone taken classes from. Fantastically conveys information in a way that is engaging and memorable. He inspired me to go to law school. Even if you don't think you'll be interested in the material, TAKE HIS CLASS. You definitely will get something out of the class. Can't recommend enough.
Good lectures, he makes it interesting. But his tests and quizzes are filled with trick questions where you have to know very specific things.

comment: Very good teacher, have to put in the work to do well. Not easy A or A-, but if you put in the time the results will defiantly show. Recommend going to cllass

comment: Didn't LOVE this class but he does his best to try and make a boring topic interesting He shows videos and lets us bring a cheat sheet to the midterm which is nice but I found the tests very difficult and a lot more advanced than what we went over in class I actually would study and still struggle with the tests

Professor Quinn is a genuinely good, smart man. However, he had a very difficult time controlling unnecessary and useless questions throughout the course. There would be class discussions about material that were not part of the curriculum. As a result, the lectures were difficult to follow and we didn't cover 4 units listed on the syllabus.

Probably one of the best professors in Geneseo, Quinn is a great guy. He has easy material (only didn't get an A because i got a 73 on the midterm. He is open to discussion on quizzes and such, and if you plead a good case he will change your score. He has a lot of real world knowledge, put up with my dumb questions, and makes lectures fun. Take it

Jim is a great guy! He is very sweet and cares about his students, sometimes he brings food in and gives it to you for answering questions. The material is very dry but he tries his best to make it a little more interesting. He's very accommodating as  well. There are 5 quizzes and 2 tests, all are curved and you can have a cheat sheet for tests.

He's the nicest dude out there. Gives out cupcakes, candy, food for answers sometimes. He's so intelligent, but not an ass about it. He will admit when he's not sure about something and he will 100% have a better understand of it by the next class and give a better explanation. So helpful, so nice, gives extra credit and curves quizzes.
NICEST MAN ALIVE. he is so kind and willing to help anyone. it's a boring class, but he tries his best to make it interesting. if you need to take Blaw, make sure you get Quinn.

Took MGMT263 as an elective; it was very interesting. His powerpoints are dull and long, but the quizzes are generally easy. What he presents is what is on the test. Nothing is that confusing as long as you study. He gives extra credit opportunities and allows a cheat sheet for the final.

Quinn is a great teacher, tried hard and suceeded in making a dry class more fun and interesting. I always attended class but more than half the class never showed up and it didn't matter because all the power points he used for class were online! Didn't really need the hefty textbook that the class required so skip out on it-it was pricy!

Took him for 263 and now 264. He's the man. You can get a 1% grade boost and the curve is very generous. Participation is important because if you're between a letter grade (he rounds up from .5, though) such as having an 89 instead of 90, he'll give you the boost if you participated. Quinn is the best professor I've ever had. Take him.

I think Quinn might be the nicest professor at Geneseo. You won't do well on his exams if you don't adequately prepare, but he is clear about what is on them, so study and you'll do fine. He lets you have large index cards or a half of a notebook sheet for the midterm and final. And again, he's the sweetest man ever.

Only two tests for 60% of your grade but he has a phenomenal curve. Class average gets curved to a B+ so just beat the class rather than beat his tests.  He is helpful, gives good feedback and is an all around amazing professor. Recommend highly.  Basically all test questions are covered in in class lectures so the textbook is a bit unnecessary.

Definitely by far one of the best professors at Geneseo. BLaw is difficult but Quinn tries really hard to help students understand the material.  He helps you by allowing a cheat sheet for the two exams, holds multiple review sessions, offers extra credit and quizzes are always curved. He is always available for help. Would definitely take again.

Quizzes can be pretty difficult, but he curves to an 85, so it can be easy to get a 95 on a quiz you didn't study for just because everyone else bombed it. Jim makes law a lot more interesting than it really is and I can't imagine having a much better professor for the class.

Quinn is honestly the greatest professor Ive had at Geneseo. Makes a boring class interesting and cares a lot about his students. Midterm and Final with quizzes throughout the semester. Tests are hit or miss with difficulty, but overall not that bad of class. Took a class I dreaded to making me consider law school upon graduation. Quinn is the bomb

Quinn is a really nice guy. Its a law class so generally the material is pretty dry and boring, but he does his best to keep you interested. His test review sessions really help. Study for the exams and you'll do well, also lets you bring an index card in with notes. Only a midterm and a final, and quizzes throughout the semester.
Professor Quinn is a fantastic professor.
He's one of the best professors in SUNY Geneseo. everything about him is so great. He always brings foods to class as well.

He is an amazing professor! He helps everyone out and is very clear about what is expected. Very good about letting you take exams the following class if you have to miss and quizzes are very easy. Midterms and Finals you're allowed an index card. Material very interesting as well and very clear.

Professor Quinn is THE man. He will do anything and everything to help any of his students. Took this class as a requirement for my Accounting major, and was not looking forward to it. By the end of the semester he has me thinking about law school. Cant wait for MGMT 264 this coming spring with him! Definitely take his class- you wont regret it!

Professor Quinn cares more about his students' success than any other professor I've had at Geneseo. He does everything he can to keep students interested in topics that are commonly thought of as dry. Since he allows an index card "cheat sheet" on exams, it isn't too difficult. Definitely take a class with him- he's a really nice and cool guy.

Quizzes: 30%, Midterm: 30%, Final: 40%. The two exams are curved. This guy is the man. Graduated from BC for undergrad and Cornell Law. Very laid back. Makes class enjoyable. By the end of the semester, he will have you considering law school. I definitely recommend

Definitely one of the best professors I've ever had. He is so good to talk to if you are interested in law school and he really wants everyone to do well in his classes. Tests are curved nicely so doing well is not hard as long as you put in some work.

LOVE HIM! I took this class on a whim wondering if I wanted to be a business minor and literally fell in love with this class and now maybe even law school. The class is not hard! A midterm and a final (which you're allowed to bring an index card of info with you) and 6 quizzes. There are bonus points, and he is so helpful! An AMAZING professor!

Professor Quinn is a great professor. He's funny and really wants his students to succeed. He used to be a lawyer and has a lot of personal experience to add to the class which keeps you interested. He's pleasant, clear, approachable and responsive. Highly recommended.

Great class! It's helpful to read the textbook, but Quinn's lectures are very thorough. He also holds review sessions and law school info sessions! You can tell that he is passionate, and you will appreciate his humor! My favorite teacher! Highly suggested!
So helpful, went out of his way to hold review sessions and even a law school information session for interested students.  Pretty funny and truly passionate about law.  Highly recommended

Easy grader but the trade off is having to deal with an egotistical person who loves belittling students. Imagine if Dwight Shrute was your professor. Will literally comb through your excel and take points off for a wrong parenthesis.  The reasoning given for taking points off is so vague.  Put wrong grades into the grade book that I had to pester him to change.  beware

He needs to retire already. He's very rude and not considerate. Very tough. He sleeps through most of class.
For a class that was supposed to be an easy A as a lab, Adelson made my life a living hell just so i could scrounge around for a C

His lectures are very general and do not apply to the homework or the exams. The homeworks are so far fetched and take hours to complete. Exams are similar to homework but harder.He has trouble addressing questions in class and out of class.

Does not understand the material he is trying to teach. Class and textbook are both useless, tests are taken from the other section's teacher and so not related to class material. Gets angry or frustrated at in-class questions. Exams and final completely from homework, which he cannot help with and gets wrong himself. Useless and shouldn't teach.

Very thankful this guy was available to teach this section of physics, which is usually not offered in the fall. Tests are hard need to read the notes he gives and the text book diligently to do well on. Having notes and text book out also helps with online HW problems.
Bad bad bad. Doesn't answer questions with any clarity, talks down to people that ask questions. Tests are a few notches above the homework that he gives.
Wow... just wow. Never seen anything quite like him.

Still wondering why he is a professor at this school. This guy makes no effort to teach, instead he zooms through his slides and assumes we know what he is talking about(Im sure he doesnt even know). Made Physics lab a lot harder than it needed to be. He will help you a little if you visit him in office hours but he was't very friendly toward questions. I love physics, but this class was a BAD experience for me.
Worst Professor ever. The end.

kind of a corky guy but he means well he just shouldn't be teaching. doesn't try to trip you up on exams class is straightforward but certainly not rivetting

Really nice guy. Puts up all of his powerpoints online after class. Unfortunately he sometimes gives you online CAPA assignments/quizzes on topics that he hasn't covered in lecture yet... If you use your textbook you'll be fine. It's a hard class. He's not going to hold your hand.
He is actually the least helpful professor that I have ever had.

He's not your standard professor and many kids in the class were upset by that, but if you overlook that and realize he's not as serious as you may think he is, he can be enjoyable. Pretty easy grader and found that he did well in lectures.
By far the worst professor I have ever had. Kept me at a B+ even though my average was an 89.85. I don't think he tries to be rude but just comes off like that.

Cannot recommend Professor P enough. So sweet and caring, uses personal anecdotes of raising her children to connect to course curriculum. Exams are easy and follow the practice quizzes, she even makes Kahoots of exam content to help you prepare. An easy grade and a good time.

By far my favorite professor I've had so far, it is very clear how much passion she has for teaching and all students. She talks a lot in lecture, some not relevant. she has quizzes and ASR's that reflect what's on the exams. She is very understanding and I highly recommend taking her class.
Very easy class but the elementary style teaching is very aggravating at 6 PM on a Thursday.
lowkey half her lecture slides have nothing to do with what were tested on. just read the textbook and look over the ASRs/ other study materials she provides

She is not at all accessible outside of class. Prof P is the most caring professor I've ever had and I'm so thankful I had her for PSYC215. Quizzes are all online, sometimes tests too. She is the sweetest professor and super understanding. She is here to teach her real world experience not just lecturing off slides. She has exams but she prepares you really well. She gives you lots of materials that you can go over like kahoots and study guides that really help.
Professor Piscani is the nicest lady ever, I am not even a psych major and I took this class as an outside major requirement. Super easy and sweet! I would definitely take from her again.

She was awesome. Easily the best professor I have ever had at Geneseo and in general. Her class is mandatory to attend, but it is very engaging. I had one super easy paper and four exams including a final which she gave us online!!! Would definitely take her.

Loved her. She was so sweet and always had good lectures. I learned more from her in a semester than I did in high school. Any question you have she will answer. She ties content in to real world scenarios which helps. She has online quizzes and 4 exams, including final. Only the final was in person. Cancels class often. PowerPoints are distributed
Literally so kind, I learned a lot about teaching from her. Always gave candy and I always found myself thinking about what we talked about outside of class.

Piscani is by far the best professor I have ever seen. She is caring, thoughtful, and fun. She makes sure every question is answered in depth as well as committing so much of her time to make sure we understand the material. Her lectures are interesting as well as informative. Also she gives out candy, which is a huge bonus.

Sara Piscani is the most amazing inspirational professor ever. She does everything she can to learn more about her many professions. She cares about her students and when a student comes up to her with a hypothetical she helps figure it out. Lectures are so interesting and easy to follow. Take her class.
She was an incredible professor. Take her class

I have never in my years of school life gotten a good professor that actually teaches in a way that everyone can understand. Piscani is very understanding and genuinely loves what she does, if you need help DO NOT HESITATE to contact her, she will be there for you and is extremely understanding!! I can assure you, you will have fun in this class!!!
She is just the best, so caring, loves her students, and is incredibly understanding!

piscani had to be the best prof i've had so far at geneseo. she's extremely understanding if you need to make up any missed work, and is willing to listen to you with all ears. she has got to be one of the sweetest ladies i've met. the lectures are always posted, and the exam questions come right off the notes. 100% would have her as my prof again.

She is the best professor that I have had so far at this school. She is super enthusiastic about the topics and makes learning about them interesting. I definitely recommend taking a course with her. She really cares for her students and wants us to succeed.

SARA PISCANI IS THE BEST PROFESSOR AND PERSON I HAVE EVER MET. She is SO empathetic, kind hearted, understanding, and fair. On top of that, she is an amazing teacher and makes learning fun. This is the only class I've enjoyed this year, all thanks to her.

comment: She is an extremely rude professor, yells at students all the time. However, she is a fair grader and very passionate about her Animal Behavior Class. DO THE PROBLEMS IN THE BACK OF THE BOOK to prepare for her tests, GO TO THE REVIEW SESSIONS before the test and you will be fine! Help is always avail!!!

Very easy class and GPA booster. Do like half the problems at the end of the chapters in the textbook and go to the review sessions and youre golden. Easy A. My lowest test grade was a 93. Definitely would recommend her over other 250 professors. Others are very hard.

Completely unapproachable and demeaning. She has no consideration for other human beings. I love animals which is why I took 338 with her because she is the only person who teaches it. Probably the easiest class I took at this school. She is very clear and knows what she's talking about. She can be condescending and unapproachable though. If you go to class and do the end of chapter problems that's an easy A!
This class is a must before you graduate! Get on her good side!

I tried my best, but I do not like Ruddy. She is unapproachable & is condescending when you ask her questions. Thankfully, her syllabus, study guides, & notes are very straight forward. A goddess. If you have an extremely low self esteem you probably think she's not approachable. You just gotta know how to talk to her and trust me she's very nice.

Ruddy is the easiest teacher, its like being back in 3rd grade. She's not approachable or polite, but go to class and you won't have to read the book or ask questions. CRAZY LADY!!! Her notes are helpful and the textbook is the most important part of the class. I am terrible at Math and I managed just fine. Don't bother asking questions in class or out she is not appreciable.

Really great professor. Lecture is easy to follow even if you're not great at math. Doing the problems in the textbook guarantees you an A on the test because  the test questions are way easier. Class is easy and sometimes interesting but she needs to leave Geneseo. Easily the most unapproachable PERSON I've ever met nevermind professor. Love this woman. I have no idea how anyone can call her rude or what have you; she is one of the most helpful and carrying people I know. Dr Ruddy is by far VERY INTERESTING....she is.... like  a Quinten Tarentino movie, multi-layered. Please by all means read the other reviews & chuckle.I did. Her class wasn't too hard and reading the books isn't necessary to do well and participate in class discussions. Make sure you participate cuz she goes on and on about participation. Overall she wasn't too bad but I thought she was kind of fake and not as nice as she acts.
She is a pretty good teacher, but the books we read aren't the best. It is just a lot of work in general but she is a pretty good teacher.

Although I thought she was a great teacher, she is an English teacher.  I loved this about her, but if you have trouble writing papers then take humanities with someone else, she grades them like she would in an English class and does so harshly.  A brilliant teacher with a good sense of humor, if you can write, you have nothing to lose.
Superb. If it weren't for the 8:05 timing, I would have been all over this class. This gal is passionate about teaching.
not bad to look at either

Prof. Beltz-Hosek is amazing!! One of the best teachers I've had at Geneseo!! She's very intelligent and really cares about her students. She's a hard grader but college is supposed to be challenging.
Ridiculously hard grader. Just regurgitate everything she thinks and you'll do okay.

Dr. Scott requires a weekly discussion post that she will absolutely pick apart. She grades harder than any English teacher I've ever had and seems like she will never give out a 100 by how much she'll pick apart your work

Was condescending when leaving notes on work and seemed rude. Made sure to tell us not to contact her first with questions and to ask a help desk since she was busy and might not get to it. Wants specific answers even though it's more of an opinion-based class.

one of the worst professors I have ever had. very judgmental and unapproachable. gives you the grade she "feels like you deserve" rather than your grade average. openly talks badly about students in class. an overwhelming amount of reading, and writing. very closed minded about many sociological topics.

comment: This professor uses out dated articles and is never accessible. She is disorganized and disrespectful. She has her TAs do all the grading and does not keep  with how her students are doing. comment: Needs to retire immediately, overshares about her personal life, doesn't grade any of her own work, it's all done by these sophomore TAs who don't know what they are doing. Overall I would avoid taking any classes with her.

DO NOT TAKE! tough grader, goes off topic all the time, TAs grade stuff really hard even though they went though this class. makes you buy 4 books and has so many other articles to read. group discussion lead once a semester where she will dominate the conversation and then bash on you for not talking. i learned nothing from this class. DO NOT TAKE

Very tough grader and is not at all cohesive as to what she is looking for. She grades based off of opinion, not facts. she has her own grading system- the tests are fine if you go to the reviews. She gets distracted and WILL cut off students when presenting to go on a tangent. this class is extremely heavy on the readings so must read everything.

She creates her own grading scheme so don't think your number grade is what you finish with because it is actually lower. comment: Test are impossible and everyone failed the first exam

Her tests are awful as she does not make it remotely clear on what specifically she is looking for. Her lectures are all over the place and she gets side tracked so easily. It honestly is a lot of work just for an intro class, I would not recommend unless you want to cry yourself to sleep every night.

One of the worst professors I have ever had. She has no grading criteria, and only grades based on her own opinions. Weekly discussions have readings with 40+ pages long. Way too much work for an intro class. Immediately shuts you down if you disagree with her. The tests are hard and specific. She takes off points for not agreeing with her opinions

She is a very confusing human being. She gets very distracted when she talks. Her discussion posts are NOT clear, she doesn't give clear instructions on how the posts should be. Being in her class makes me want to give up on my college career.  Take caution!

comment: Taking this course gave me an extreme disliking towards sociology. I did not like the way the class was structured. She is constantly all over the place and is super hard to follow, you get graded on weekly discussion posts which you can not repeat a previous students post (even if you have similar thoughts/feelings about a topic) Also every week you get into a group and discuss the readings for the week and there is a lot of readings for an intro course

Honestly, stopped attending her lectures after the first month or so, because she tends to go on tangents and we run out of time for the lecture. She posts the PowerPoints anyways. Every week there is a group meeting, split into 3 by last name, where you discuss the readings for the week, so just a heads up. Overall, it was a fairly easy class.

comment: This class has way more reading and work than an introductory class should have. There's a 2-3 page paper due every week as well as a weekly discussion day for class participation. comment: Her class is way too much work for a 100 level class. You will spend HOURS doing every assignment just for her to give you an awful grade. You never know what she wants for an answer. This class was awful. Professor Scott assigned a weekly paper due at the beginning of class, had weekly student led discussions, and tests were hard. Do not recommend.
The amount of shade she threw at people was very annoying! The class material is not hard, but there is a lot to read. I did learn a few interesting things, but it was not worth taking the course :(

during the online class, the recorded lectures were easy to follow and not repetitive or boring. professor scott spaced out the material and assignments in a way that it was easy to follow. and there are 2 exams that were fair since we were able to use our notes and there wasn't a final exam. she is very easy to follow and accessible out of class

comment: the way she teaches and sets up class, especially when it was online, was easy, straightforward, and set you up for success. she gave weekly videos about what to expect and what was due. Her workload was manageable and she was not strict with responses in papers. she is very accessible out of class and one of the best professors at geneseo

Shes a sweet little lady. She makes funny comments sometimes, and shes very understanding about grades. She will stress to you herself that she is very very approachable and available. The class itself being so easy helps a lot too. Theres nothing that you wont already know, she just dives into more specific details.

The TA's grade your reading responses. And being a conservative, I'm not happy with the lack of inclusion for other viewpoints that disagreed with the liberal political agenda. I understand that the school itself is liberal, but tolerance for other views would be validating. Also, it's impossible to do well on tests. They're too harshly graded.

There are little to no instructions, the TAs grade your weekly reflections ( on sometimes 70+ pages of reading.) Her tests are extremely particular, and almost impossible to succeed for most unless you can remember everything that happens in the readings. Some comments she says are inappropriate and sometimes offensive, shes very stuck in her ways.

comment: This class has been torture. She provides little instruction and grades harshly. You are expected to do all of the learning on your own. This is a 100 level class and she treats it like a 2-300 level class. Simply put, its horrible.

comment: Just not a good professor. She's nice and is a well educated sociologist, but doesn't even teach! She reads off of a powerpoint that are facts from google, has the weekly discussion group lead the lecture, and the TA's grade the weekly essays! not to mention she often makes comments that aren't super appropriate to bring up. But, not a hard class

Lectures one day a week and group discussion on the other day. 2-3 reading passages a week but if you read them carefully you'll do fine on them. comment: Prof. Scott is a nice lady, and her class is pretty good, but she not once posted grades the entire semester so it was impossible to figure out where you stood in the class. comment: This was one of the worst professors I've ever had in my entire life. her grading criteria makes no sense and is so specific that its as if she's setting you up to fail. you cannot disagree with her even if her information is a bit outrageous and she's spouting nonsense. Basically, if you are of a diverse ethnic background, don't take her class.

comment: Good professor. In this class rotates between lectures and class discussions. Weekly short papers based on readings, very easy. Group project at the end of the semester leading a discussion. Important to go to class or read. She covers main topics of the readings in class but still need to read for an A.

Very sweet person, but has unclear grading criteria, very mean feedback. Exams are all essay based. You have to read 3-4 articles a week to get points in group discussions but you dont have to read the novel for the final exam just understand the theme. go to class, she notices when youre not there. I got solid B- on all exams, got an A- in class
tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Get ready to read', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS']

comment: Professor Scott is such a sweet lady but not a great teacher. Her classes are easy, meets twice a week the lecture then a group presentation. Have to read 4 articles a week then do 7 out of the 11 mandatory journals about them. However, her exams are all essay based. She gives a study guide but her grading system is arbitrary and makes no sense.
tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass."]

comment: Honestly one of the worst professors ever. She has no idea what shes talking about. She often goes off on tangents and says stupid things like "nazis shouldnt be punished". She specifically picks on students that disagree with her and has gossiped about them. She cuts people off so she can "correct" them. She also grades based on who she likes.

The grading scheme is completely arbitrary. Information in class is factually wrong. The discussions are important. There is a ton of reading and the homework picks up around the second half of the semester. She is completely out of touch with reality. Would not recommend if you're not a soc major.
tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK']

comment: Denise is a very kind person and a wonderful and understanding professor. Her class was very interesting and I learned a lot during the semester. There was a lot of involvement with the texts and she does not spoon feed you what you need to know, you have to read the materials in order to get a good grade and participate in discussion.

I learned a lot in Scott's class. Sometimes she can come off a bit condescending but she has a solid base of knowledge and cares about the topic. Lectures are intense (a LOT of writing, so don't skip) but her tests aren't too bad (the study guide is literally the test). She also has you write journal entries every week which are a grade booster.
tags: ['Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LECTURE HEAVY']

comment: She is set in her ways on how she thinks BUT if you just look past that and realize that is how some people are you will learn a lot and you will do well. Her study guides are literally her test questions.  She lets you pick 3/4 questions, giving you space to show off what you know.  Honestly, if you don't do well in her class then thats on you.

Dr. Scott's class is one of the best I've taken so far. There is a lot of reading but Scott selects them really well and you actually learn so much. Only a couple of tests and the study guides are very clear and great tools to do well. This is a very manageable course if you stay on top of everything and Scott is an excellent professor.

TAKE NOTES DURING CLASS. I cannot emphasize this enough. In order to do well on the tests you have to take notes she does not put power points online. Also do the study guides. Beware that there is a ton of reading. Overall this professor is pretty boring but the class is fairly easy.

Dr. Scott is very expressive when you answer questions, but not because she believes you're wrong, but because she is trying to understand your POV. She has 2 exams and a final. For her exams she gives out a study guide along with terms. Rewrite the terms a million times and DO THE STUDY GUIDE! The final: READ THE BOOKS SHE ASSIGNS AHEAD OF TIME!

Denise is a good teacher. It is an easy class. You will have assigned weekly journal entries on the readings that are just a reflection. There are a few essays thrown in instead of tests. All the writing helps you to analyze the readings and contribute in class discussion. The topics are interesting and the class encourages critical thinking.

She's really nice, but the way she sets up her classes make them torture. Students teach on Thursdays, but she dominates the discussion a lot of the time. Weekly 2 page papers and 3 6-page papers mixed in there. One group project. Don't take this class unless you're ready for that. Overall, pretty easy besides the busy work.

Must be well-prepared for tests because they are short answer/essay questions but the study guide she provides has all the potential questions so as long as you outline that and incorporate class notes into it, it is really easy to do well. Also, the journals are a huge grade booster. If you do them, you get credit and lots of feedback.

Professor Scott was very friendly, but the lectures were very dry. She relied way too much on her teaching assistants who grade your journals and exams; every week a different person grades your work and they all have very different expectations which made it very hard to improve. You have to use a ridiculous amount of detail in the essays to pass.

She's an enigma to say the least. Lectures are sometimes entertaining. She says things that are oddly inappropriate (e.g. talking about her infertility issues) but funny. She's a difficult grader and is insistent on examples and lots of detail. Tests are all short answer questions and essays. The class was overall more difficult than necessary.

Class was a drag.  Scott, is not one to accept different opinions from her own. If you feel a certain way she'll let you know that you're wrong. If discussion was short, you stayed the entire time. Very little leaving early. Material was dry and focused on women in India rather than Gender in South Asian societies. Wouldn't recommend her to anyone.

Dr. Scott is amazing! This course isn't going to be roses and lilies as one might expect. She gets down to the grit of it very quickly! I like that she tries to make people understand the importance of accepting and knowing about various types of families that exist and the role this plays in shaping public policy! Great course! I highly recommend!
Absolutely hated her. Gives off a bad attitude and is condescending. Always wants more out of you and is overall a boring class and terrible teacher.
Very interesting class. Thorough study guides are provided for all tests.  Easy if you go to class, do a fair amount of the readings and apply them to your tests/papers.

Great Professor who gives great study guides.  Each lecture is full of information that is directly connected and supports the reading.  Somewhat biased when it comes to some topics, and is not open to opinions that do not support hers but a nice person who genuinely cares about the topics she teaches.

Gives out a helpful study guide for the exams so you know what to expect. I feel like she didn't lecture as much because all she really did was lecture once a week and hold class discussions the other day... even when it was her lecture days, she would just show a video the whole time... journals do help boost you grade though.

Really interesting class, just don't forget to think for yourself. She is a bit biased during discussion, there is really no room for your own opinion. She genuinely cares about the subject, but she is odd in that she smiles when presenting depressing statistics.

Prof. Scott was very...interesting.  Definitely recommend going to see her if you don't do well on her tests (you'll improve your score!) And do all the questions on the study guide to prepare for the tests it'll help you so much!! Nice, but odd at the same time.  Likes to debate and is opinionated. In private she's not as intimidating as in class.

Dr. Scott's Political Sociology class is interesting and structured in a discussion setting, but it's definitely not a walk in the park.  The final essay is really difficult because you're not given any direction, but overall it's a good class.

She's a really nice person, and super intelligent, but she has a really hard time controlling large classes, and if everyone else's interest wanes, yours will, too. Going to office hours really helps your grade- she likes it if she knows who you are

Professor Scott is awesome! She's super nice, the readings are almost always interesting, she's a fair grader, and she hands out outlines before tests so you know what to study. She has class discussions every week, so it's not always lecture either. Overall, I highly recommend her and this class!

Prof Scott is a very nice lady, she tries her best but can be a little scatterbrained at times. Class is easy if you put some time into it, an A is achievable. She gives study guides, making the exams pretty easy. I would recommend the class, I learned a lot.

Overall, she's a good professor.  She's not difficult and really kind and friendly.  At times, she makes sociology interesting but then there are other days when you just want to get out of class.  Weekly journal articles can get annoying but if you do the reading, you should be fine in class.

not terrible but not good. she doesn't give you enough notes. she has group presentations each week, so she doesn't even teach you for 10 class periods. she puts a feminist twist on everything. expects you to use the minutest details on tests which are all essays. i probably would not recommend this class.

I had her this year for intro, and I easily got an A for the class. She tells you ahead of time what readings you have and most are interesting. If you study you do fine (she gives a study guide and picks from that)Two tests and final paper and 8 out of 12 journals on reasings). It's not hard! :)

I took this class my sophomore year as a psych major & human develop. minor.. & thoroughly regret it! At the expense of sounding arrogant, I have to be honest and say that the woman has no idea what she's talking about. She relies on the texts, rarely gives useful notes, & it really seems like grades are given arbitrarily. Take with someone else!
Not a bad teacher, however she relies heavily on the texts and will base much of the exams/papers directly on these. Not good for people who don't do their reading!

Bored out of my mind every class. She goes on long, meaningless rants completely irrelevant to the class. Lots and lots of readings. What she writes on the board during class is completely useless and rarely makes sense. Didnt study and got mostly Bs. Easy grader on papers.

She doesn't let you know what you really need to know for tests, you just have to take notes all the time in class pretty much about everything. You have to do the readings and take notes on them becuase they are tested on. She is a fair grader and as long as you stay focused in class you should be fine.

this class was really easy. she doesn't use a textbook, you read  articles instead, which were fairly interesting. paper and tests were very easy. she is a nice woman and very intelligent, and if she talks about her son, it's only to say that he's fat, which is kind of awkward.

she does talk about her son too many times, its annoying-she just doesn't get it-she does not have the right amount of social skills. She’s the weirdest of all which is probably why the ratings are diverse, but she loves sociology & it shows. she's full of opinions & information. Give her a chance & you’ll learn a lot. If u like socl you’ll do well

I cannot express in words how sick I am of hearing about her 12 year old "wonder son" or her impending divorce. However, her class is ridiculously easy, and if you do all of the reading you will coast through with no problems. Her tests are all essays (short answer/one long one), and she grades ok.
Great teacher.  Tells you exactly what you need to know for her tests and grades fair
Wonderful teacher, cares about her field and her students. Fair grader. Makes every effort to get students to fully understand material, which is usually not too difficult.

Overall, I enjoyed the class.  I registered for this class at the last minute because the required courses were all filled.  I thought it was going to be a lot harder but I learned a lot and she is a great professor who knows what she's talking about and makes class interesting.

Dreadful teacher. She's so creepy when she smiles because you know she isn't really happy. Students never went to class. Her tests are unbelievably easy. Before this, I had never fallen asleep in class. So much for that...

She never dots her i's correctly and that drives me crazy. She smiles for everything but she's not very smart. Her tests are unbelievably hard. I went to every class and did all the readings, and still didnt do well. You think you know one of the essays but she takes off points literally for no reason. She can't spell either.

I LOVED this class. Denise Scott was one of the kindest profs I had. The class is not too in depth, but she gets you motivated on the topic. If you want an A go to class. I had poor (read freshman) attendance and still did well.

Very boring. No one ever went to class and so everyday she would say "now i know it's hard to come to class because of (weather hot/cold, tired, beginning of the semester, end of sem.)" It's not the weather! It's you! Yells and smiles at the same time.

I also took her for Intro Soc. I hate her. She is very subjective, a lot of the grade is based on her personal feelings for you. I scored perfectly on m.c. and would lose unfounded points on an essay. One essay would get an A, another a D. It made no sense. I almost went to the dept. head about her
Great teacher!  Very interesting and if you pay attention in class, you'll ace the tests.  Loved it.

Good class.. if you're not concerned about grades! The material, readings, and guest speakers are very interesting, however, her tests are rediculously diffucult to do well on.. 3 essays in 1 hr. 15 min. which should be given 2 and a half hours to do
Very easy class, if she doesn't like your writing style you might have a hard time.  Only 2 tests, really easy!  I plan on taking more classes with her.

I hate this class more than anything in the world, and I hate her teaching style. She lectures on and on in the most awful tone that makes me want to NEVER EVER go to class! Don't take her if possible
Made Soc. very interesting, and is a really nice women. I would TA with her if I could.
No Comments
very good teacher...i got an A- with little effort
Very nice and funny. Forgot my name once but not in a mean way. He cares about his students and his lectures always have good flow and conclusion and I always feel like I learned something.

The class made no sense. Two large assignments were practically the same thing, but both had unclear directions, making it easy to mix up the two. The syllabus had no information about assignments or due dates on it, only Brightspace. Unclear due dates and assignments made the class overly difficult for what it was.
one of the sweetest professors ever! the class was quite boring but he made it bearable.
Really pushed the boundaries of what I knew. Super enjoyable and valuable experience.

Ken Cooper is honestly the sweetest man ever. He cares about his students well-being and takes the time to get to know them and how he can support them. Just today he took my class to Starbucks to treat us for actually showing up. I would definitely recommend taking a class with him if given the chance.
The sweetest guy. Felt very comfortable speaking in his class

He is a very sweet man who is always very understanding. His class is a little hard if you don't read a lot but his class is like a breath of fresh air in comparison to other college courses because of how nice and understanding he is.

This class was quite boring for me, but I did really enjoy Professor Cooper's enthusiasm and kind-heart. I had quite a bit of fun writing the short story based on an image, and writing the paper based on an architectural site that we had visited and enjoyed. His directions were confusing at times, but he is an overall enjoyable person.

very boring class, but he tried to make it interesting. a few response papers, one 7 page paper, and a reflective final based on what youve already done. easy class, but he gets sad if people dont participate.

Ken Cooper is such a sweet and caring man who loves what he does! His whole class is discussion based so there's no point in going to class if you haven't done the readings. He is extremely leniant with due dates and so understanding of certain circumstances. This being said the content of papers is sometimes difficult.

comment: I loved having Prof Cooper for a teacher! He made a lot of involving discussions to the material through readings/movies/videos. The novels we read were very intriguing. He gave lots of good critiques and always made sure to give positive feedback with his constructive criticism. Would highly recommend!

comment: I absolutely adore Dr Cooper. He is the sweetest, funniest, and kindest man alive. If you are struggling he will help in such a nice way. He makes classes enjoyable and will listen to his students needs. 11/10 recommend Dr Cooper!!!

Professor Cooper is always available and makes you think the best of every assignment. He can be sometimes confusing, but that is easily resolved if you just talk to him. Flexible and considerate, I recommend this professor.

Tends to have long confusing lectures, but office hours help, and he often gives more. Kindest prof you'll meet. unclear essay prompts, he assumes you always know what he's talking about. takes criticism easily. 3 essays + 2 self reflection (mid/final) make up grade, as well as 20 percent participation. easy to pass and enjoy if you do the reading

I love Dr. Cooper! But his class isnt easy. We read a book a week and had a paper a week. The highest grade he gives on anything is a 95, no 100s. He also grades in increments of 5 (85,90,95). If you put in the effort, you will love the class and he will love you. Go to his office hours too! Hes very fun to chat with.

comment: Cooper is really nice, assigns a ton of reading within a short timeframe. Really easy to chat with and makes sure to try to get to know his students despite being online.

Ken Cooper is rad. His Graphic novel class was a really interesting way to take an intro class and get kinds into writing. As an upperclassman I found it to be a breath of fresh air. It isn't very difficult to if you get the chance and want a fun elective to take, do this one!

The nicest guy ever. I took the Graphic Novel class with him and it was so much fun. We had weekly online discussions and then there was one essay, a research proposal, and a 7-8 page research paper. The books were good and he was always available to meet if you needed help on an essay. SO NICE!

I appreciate the topic and care and attention he gave to class discussions to make sure this was a repeat of high school lectures since it was a primarily freshman taken course. He gave me the SPECIFIC and tangible changes and direct annotations on my papers earlier one and is a great professor to share work with outside the course.
tags: ['Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Group projects']

comment: He is kind, very sweet and understanding. With all these things going on in world like corona virus he gives the student a chance to be able to succeed on their grades if they need to too. Also it was a free textbook. Just do all the school work and participate on discussion then you will suceed.

Remembers you as a person, not a grade. Taken two classes with him, and he always makes the class feel open to everyone. Afraid of looking stupid by participating with a half baked idea? He makes you feel comfortable sharing. Just wants you to try your best, and isn't afraid to be authentic with feedback. Makes you excited about your own ideas.

Cooper is a kindhearted soul who really wants the best for his students, but his class is all over the place. he expects unrealistic amounts of reading to be done for his classes and his essay prompts, as lengthy as they are, are not clear. his classes consist of him lecturing about numerous topics and not really leading a discussion

Dr. Cooper is an awesome guy but you will only succeed in his class if you attend office hours. Lectures are unstructured and he basically just talks at your for the whole two hours. Essay prompts are not super clear and usually are open to heavy interpretation. Go to his office hours you should gain clarity and be able to earn a decent grade.
tags: ['Accessible outside class', 'Get ready to read', 'Tough grader']

comment: Professor Cooper has good intentions, but he talks in circles and his lectures are unclear. He is a thorough grader but his feedback makes as little sense as his lectures do. His book choices are very dry. The essay prompts are literally a paragraph. He's not a bad guy - he just makes no sense most of the time.

Ken Cooper is the sweetest! He cares so much about his students and genuinely wants you to succeed- but he is not an easy grader. Go to his office hours for every paper and it won't be hard to do well.

Dr. Cooper is a genuinely great human being. The class itself (nature writing) wasnt exactly enthralling first thing in the morning, but hes honestly one of my favorites. Extremely understanding, humorous and kind.
Amazing guy. Gives great feedback, but somewhat of a tough grader. Prompts are sometimes too vague.
tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read']

comment: Cooper's a great guy, very suburban dad. Pretty chill about late work (I got an A- on a major paper that I turned in late). But there's just too much work. You have to get like 9 books and have a new one read each week, along with a short response paper. It's certainly not difficult work, just dull and repetitive. As long as you do it you'll pass.
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', 'SO MANY PAPERS']

comment: Such a beautiful man. So nice. So accepting.

Professor Cooper is a great professor. I thoroughly enjoyed his class and he made each and every lecture fun and interesting! We had three five-page papers to write on the novels we read and I know that I would have gotten an A if I went to see him more for office hours because he is very approachable and really cares about his students.

Ken Cooper was easily the best professor I've had. He's an overall interesting person. He is easy to have a conversation with and takes the time to get to know his students. One of the smartest people I have ever met. He gives great feedback and helps you become a better writer. I highly recommend!

Hands down my favorite professor at Geneseo. He's very approachable and makes class fun and interesting. This was my second class with him, and I'm taking his class again next semester. Seriously, if you can, take one of his classes before graduation. Very chill atmosphere and interesting discussions; office hours are very helpful.

Took his 70's film class, half of the films are awful. For response papers write about how you feel, he grades each with a check, +, or -,  to "reduce letter grade anxiety", but this grading scale only made me MORE anxious! Research paper is worth 35% of your final grade! Confusing lectures, struggled to break a "B", he's just okay at best.
