comment: I took his Pynchon class and loved Dr. Cooper as a person. I think he's a great guy, very kind and understanding, definitely knows what he's talking about. But there is TOO MUCH reading. Cooper does a good job ATTEMPTING to make this as easy as possible. But I found this was WAY above what I'm capable of. The reading level is impossible.

I loved Professor Cooper's class. Easily the most interesting professor I've had yet. I get where others are coming from regarding his lectures (you gotta focus or else you'll get lost), but damn I learned a lot. Really admire him as a person and professor. Super flexible about essays (I wrote a personal narrative!). Go to his hours for essays!

Cooper is funny and a nice guy but impossible to follow. There were only two essays and a final for the class so it's incredibly difficult to raise your grade if you mess up. The lectures are incredibly dry and it's difficult to participate. He often goes on tangents and I could rarely understand his message or point. I wouldn't take him again.

Cooper is a great guy, I don't doubt it. And he cracks great jokes and has clear dad-humor. However, his teaching style is confusing and vague. We are reading 9-10 books and often it is difficult to particulate in discussion. Confusing teaching style, seems all over the place, but offers his help. I probably won't take his class again.

His lectures a little dry, but it's a 400-level class. He seems to be passionate by what he's teaching and has really good dad-humor (haha!) He was always there for me when I needed him, but his papers are a bit lengthy! Make sure you get a head start on them. Group projects were essential to the class. But no exams - just papers.

I can't believe Cooper's rating isn't higher. He is easily one of my favorite professors on campus. I went to his office hours countless times just to talk with him about the class because he's such an enjoyable person! Highly recommend his 70s class. The movies are good if not interesting and the discussion days are great.

I don't know why people think Cooper is boring--his class was always very engaging and very interesting. It's refreshing to take a class where the professor's instructions for the papers is: "write something interesting." Love him.

Cooper is excellent.  He's the first professor I've had who is a genuinely nice guy, without pretension or arrogance.  Go to his office hours, just to chat- it's awesome.  The class is pretty easy; two essays and some responses to the books, all of which are interesting.  HIGHLY recommend- a class on comic books?  Where could you go wrong?

Ken is wonderful. I took my INTD with him fall of my freshman year, and even though I am a chemistry major, I really enjoyed his class. Walden is a bit dense, but he goes over the readings in class. Read the book and listen in class, and the papers shouldn't be a problem. He's also great about proofreading etc during office hours. Great professor.

This class is the best class I've ever taken! Cooper was engaging and intelligent. He's really into sharing ideas and he wants to see you excel. It's not an easy A, but it's not an impossible one. You have to be doing no work to fall below a B. I have a tremendous amount of respect for him and if you get the chance you should defiantly take him!

He is an awesome dude. The readings are difficult at times but he talks a lot about them in class to clarify things. There are only 2 essays, and he's a fair grader. He's also really funny, if you have to take Amrican Lit, take it from him! :)
He's a nice guy, but he's very boring. His writing assignments are vague and confusing, but he's not a hard grader.

Cooper is laid back, easy-going, and interested. his classes are typically centered around an idea he's been brewing over the course of his career... so at times it's hard to get on the same page as him, but overall, he's very accessible and open-minded. he does guide lecture, but thats to be expected, he's a professor. i recommend him.

I'm an American studies major, and taking this with Prof. Cooper was horrible, he did not teach it to the specifications of what the course is supposed to be, which was interdisciplinary. He did not understand that none of the students had seen the films as many times as he had, and had formed opinions that left no room for students ideas.

I was shocked to see that Ken Cooper doesn't have one of the highest rating at Geneseo! He is so engaging, so intelligent, and well.. a cool guy. I have him for an American Studies course titled Filming the 70's.. It really doesn't get much sweeter than that. It's an 8:30 and I don't think I've ever missed if. Great insightful professor! Take him.

Where to begin? Very easy going and easy to talk to. His classes are mostly lecture and very boring. He will use words that sound made up and will lose everyone. A lot of reading but his tests are semi easy as long as you read and attend class. He is a pretty fair grader.

Had him for Major Author: Thomas Pynchon. Got to give him credit for attempting to teach this author, especially his most recent novel which came out just last semester! Funny professor, classes are enjoyable and make you want to attend. Pretty easy grader, too. It's hard to get lower than a B, but challenging to get an A. Definately reccomend him.

Cooper's faults: He understands the text a little too deeply at times and then asks his students about their opinions on the concepts he has constructed through years of individual interpretation.  Essay assignments are vague and up to the critical reasoning of the writer.  His class can be tortuous if you aren’t prepared with the reading <3

nice guy but so boring. takes the majority of the class saying, yeah..thats a point id like to discuss next class. then what the heck will we talk about this class? stands scratching his head saying hmm for minutes at a time.  justifies people not coming to his class becuase the reading was hard. but its really because his class is pointless

I can give you a thousand reasons not to take this professor. he is very unclear on assignments and expects you to read his mind. somehow the whole class got some sort of a B, no As. horrible teacher.

Ken Cooper is pretty much a hippie. As many hippies do, Ken Cooper believes he knows everything about everything. Classes are pointless. He doesn't even give grades on his papers, instead he grades all the work at the end of the semester in one portfolio. Unless you want to revise everything aimlessly or you too are a hippie, avoid Ken Cooper.

Great guy! Hillarious, easy going, helpful, makes you think more in depth and forces you to improve your writing skills. Take a class with him you'll have a great time and he could care less if you miss class!

Cooper is probably solely responsible for enlightening me as a human. His classes are hard because dumb kids can't comprehend the idea of thinking beyond what is actually given in the specified texts. If you are looking to learn, definitely take his classes; if you want an easy grade and someone who hand feeds you the answers, don't. he's amazing.

A jerk.  Although my grade wasn't bad and the class wasn't hard, he'll do nothing to help you out.  He taught two of the same class.  I asked him if I could take the final in the earlier slot so I could drive my girlfriend home so she could have more time with her dying grandfather.  He told me that would require too much paper work.  Seriously.

Honestly, I didn't go to class much, but I kept up with the reading and did all the papers- steady Bs. But the classes I did go to were alright, despite its earliness. Good luck going to see him at office hours- I went once and there were a million other people waiting to talk to him too. Your best bet is to schedule an APPOINTMENT.
Lectured far too much for a literature based class. Annoying manerisims, says "you know" all the time in place of explaining whatever he's talking about. Avoid if possible.
you would thing it is hard to make terrorism a boring subject, but he did so without even trying. very boring, not really clear with what hes looking for in papers and tries too hard to sound smart.

He talks like a surfer. Says "You Know" more often than he actually gives information. He's only a professor because he likes to hear himself babble. He gives assignments and when you ask about it says things like "Write this as if you aren't a student in this class and haven't seen the syllabus". If you don't mind being bored/annoyed, take him

Amazing professor!  A lot of people say he's dry and boring, but you've got to be a little open.  He's tons of fun!! The class and reading has nothing to do with the papers, which is actually a lot of fun.  You get to write what you want, and he loves new ideas!  Very helpful in office hours!
Nice guy, all over the place as a teacher.  Excruciatingly boring more often than not.  Always gives B's to everyone on everything, which is frustrating if you ever try to do better.
I could never follow this guy. It hink he thought he had DEEp thoughts, but really he may have been in his own literary world

Cooper is the most hypocritical, close-minded man. He raves about being openminded, tells u to speak ur mind, but shoots you down if u dont see eye-to-eye with him. Class is easy, but insanely boring, all he does is ramble. He was probably beat up alot as a kid, deservingly. I never again will take a class with this man - waste of my time.
Great guy but can be very boring. The readings he assigns are incomprehensible but it's not like you really have to read them for the class anyways.
He goes off into these random tangents about his kids...it's great... a lot of people think he's boring but it really isn't so bad, he does tend to babble sometimes though
He's really boring, but nice and funny sometimes.

He seems almost condescending sometimes. Constantly gets off topic and can't crack jokes very well. Seems nice, but he's difficult to understand when you want a question answered. Classes are boring, and I wonder if he likes the sound of his own voice. Constantly tries to read facial expressions.

He will not give you below a B I swear. His lectures have nothing to do with what you read in class, but his attempts at cracking jokes are worth the effort of going to class, because you feel bad for him. Take his class to assure yourself a B.

Always my favorite. You need a discerning, intellectual mind to stomach him. If you're slow and don't understand big words, forget it. He does lots paper conferences in INTD, and it's really enjoyable to sit down and talk with him. Very into beat culture, obscure films. Horribly intelligent :)

Horrible class. Lectures are extremely boring and don't even pertain to the material that you are reading in class.  He is willing to help but will tell you to do one thing in an essay and then when you do it he will decide he doesn't like it and penalize you for it.
Hum at 805 with him is not recommended, but at any other time he'd be a great teacher. Do-able assignments and work, enjoys class contribution, talk to him and you'll do well.
He is a great guy with a great sense of humor

In 1994, Ken Cooper co-taught Hum with the late C.R. Bailey.  I loved the dynamics the two shared with one another and brought to the class as a history/english dual approach.  I remember Ken as encouraging, friendly, and always open to new perspectives.
he's a good guy with an unconventional way of looking at things-- he will surprise you. very polite and amiable. looks like will ferrell.  ;)
He's a nice guy and is always trying to help, but his classes can get so boring. I wouldn't really recommend him.

He's a really nice guy who wanted to make you think about how these Humanities connect to real life.  On another hand, however, his classes tend to get a little boring.  He's really interesting, too, talk to him about Gaza.
No Comments
Thinks he is much better than he is...lectures are unengaging
Frau Houghton was easily one of my favorite teachers at Geneseo. Her class was fair but definitely not hard. She is very kind and understanding. Definitely recommend her!

An absolutely wonderful professor. I had a rough time with German before I transferred to Geneseo, but now I love it! I am very sad to be done with German, and I would love to have her again! She is very kind and helpful. Very clear. I actually understood what I was learning. I highly recommend her.

She's wonderful. I feel like I'm actually learning German this semester. You most likely won't get an A in this class, but it's a lot easier to get in the B's than with Klima. She's a much easier grader and she's much clearer in lectures. In 201, she doesn't speak a lot of English though so it gets confusing at times.

Frau Houghton is  wonderful professor.  Her classes demand the amount of work needed to understand a language, and she's an extremely fair grader.  She generally has an attendance policy, but if you go to classes and pay attention you will do well.

I have Frau Houghton for German 201. I haven't taken German in a few years and looked to get back into the swing of things. She's very helpful and has the interest of her students in mind. Put some effort into this class and you will be rewarded with good grades and an immense knowledge of the language. I recommend this class to all!

Professor Houghton is one of my favorite professors at Geneseo. She is a really tough professor but if you want to learn a language hers is the class to take. Dont take the class if you just simply want to get the requirement over with take another professor. She is a pleasure to be around and loves teaching.

too difficult for what should be basic french. tests are incredibly hard and unfair. she ended up curving everyone's grade just so that enough of her students would pass. i took 4+ years of french in highschool and barely pulled off a C+. a kid i knew grew up in canada and struggled with the tests. i do not recommend taking any classes with her

Professor Ferguson is truly an inspiration. She is an amazing dancer and always reminds us to get comfortable in our bodies so we can dance better. There aren't many grades in this class so everything counts and make sure to follow the rubric! Taking this class has made me more confident and comfortable in my skin. Highly recommend!

Her lectures are very boring, usually dragging out the same concepts every unit and venting about her personal trauma every class. There's a group activity at least once a week and they're literally the worst unless you have friends. Tests are okay, but the short response portion is graded too harshly and will drop your grade significantly.

Sikka was an okay professor. Her lectures were heavy, and the tests were not based on remembering material but on applying your knowledge to situations. If you take the time to go to her office during office hours, she will guide you if you are struggling. Read the book! I didn't and my grades were suffering. Good person, bad teacher.

I learned more from Sikka than I have anyone else, that being said something I didn't like was how tough the tests were compared to the classwork and exam guides. Uses the textbook material on the exams too. Overall lots of good material but tough at times.

Dr. Sikka's lectures feel extremely unorganized at times, but overall the class was relatively easy. She gives two essay exams which she dosent grade harshly as well. In the beginning I thought the class was going to be hard but it wasn't and I learned a lot.

I love Dr. Sikka as a person but not as a professor. Cross-Cultural Psyc is ALL lecture-based, but she just reads from the textbook I needed to buy. You don't need to buy the textbook Two exams but graded heavily. Since it is her just going through 30 slides each class can get very boring and disengaging

Do not take this class. You know what? Take this class if you want to test your passion for psych. She never shuts up about her niece and great nephew. I've been confused since september. She started crying when we watched a video about malnutrition, which i suppose is understandable but rather dramatic.

She's nice but she doesn't cover enough from the book and the first exam is always a disaster because the essay questions are too hard. You are graded on exams and 5 in class discussions and write-ups. The exams cover a lot, but she gives you a study guide so as long as you study really good you can get a good grade.
A very kind professor who cares about her students. The tests are simple if you read the textbook. She has many funny stories and is always in a great mood.

heard so many bad things about her but she was one of the best psych professors I've had. she's very passionate about her class. people say that her tests are hard but if you just follow along with her in class you should be able to pass without studying. she's also very accommodating if you are struggling.

I adore Professor Sikka, such a kind professor. This class is not hard at all, material is simple and Sikka provides many examples from working with children and her own childhood. I absolutely would take a course with her again. Loved her lectures. Absolutely take this with prof Sikka she's the best

Sikka is great. My biggest piece of advice is to read the textbook and to pay attention in class bc she gives great examples and the textbook helps you to further understand. Her class is very test centered so if you're not a good test taker- try a diff professor. She keeps the lectures interesting but stay off your phones (she will say something).

comment: Every class is extremely boring and she only talks about her nieces. Tests are hard there is always more than one right answer. She isn't understanding and hard to reach outside of class. However she did boost my grade like .2 percent so I would pass and didn't have to retake the class.

Dr. Sikka was by far my favorite professor. She's hilarious and actually cares about her students. The lectures are heavy and attendance isn't mandatory, but she does randomly take it. She creates study guides for all of her tests, which includes a study guide for the final exam.

I think people are a little harsh on Sikka, I had her for stats this semester and it was definitely a difficut course, but she taught the material very well. Make sure you go to class, or you will fail. Super nice too if you ask for help during tests and stuff.

So terrible. You have 4 tests throughout the whole semester and very few assignments you are graded on besides the tests. If you get one bad grade on a test it is very hard to get that grade up. Her lectures are very fast paced and get off track very often. She is a nice woman but the tests are so difficult. Dont show up, won't pass. READ THE BOOK!
tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things']

comment: The tests were unbelievably hard. 40 multiple choice (mostly apply) questions on 3 chapters filled with information and 2 essay questions. What are the essay questions? I dont know becuase you have 10 possible different ones and you either do all of them or guess what 2 questions are on the test

Professor Sikka often interrupted her own lectures with anecdotes that she described as examples but it was really an excuse to talk about her grand-niece and make imitations of babies crying. Other than that she was a decent professor but I wouldn't take her again

Prof. Sikka cares about her students but has a hard time translating that into her teaching. She tends to say offensive or rude things and calls people out a lot. Her tests were full of errors and at one point a question didn't even have the correct answer listed.

Professor Sikka is a nice person; however, I found it difficult to learn anything of substances because she mostly discusses things not within the course material. Additionally, there are several assignments all worth 0% of your grade, while the tests are 75% of your grade. The tests in my opinion are not fair, difficult, and never updated.

Professor Sikka is not horrible but definitely not the best. To do well you need to read the textbook and study a lot but I would not say it is that difficult of a class if you read the textbook. She prepares you well but takes little time to get to know her students. She will give extra credit on the tests so study because I had over 100

Professor Sikka is a very nice women and means well, she tends to go off on tangents about her great niece and other random information quite often, she complains that we are so behind so she skips a lot of slides in her lectures, the tests are very difficult and you really have to understand the material to do well.

Dr. Sikka is a great woman.  It is obvious that she cares about her students and tries to make the class directed towards how the class learns best.  The tests are very hard which is why I gave her a lower rating but she gives make up exams which will help your grade.  There is barely any homework besides reading.

Yep. No. Don't do it. If you have already signed up to be with this professor, switch immediately. I can't begin to tell you how bad of an experience I had in this class. The textbook and the professor use different formulas. Email communication with the prof is good though if you can get her to respond. Run, and run fast. Save yourselves.
tags: ['Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass."]

comment: She lectures all class and then gives exit tickets at the end so you have to go to class to get class participation credit. We had 3 exams and a paper. The exams are based on textbook reading, so you don't need to go to class to do well on exams. The paper is super easy. She is so flustered all time and class is very confusing.

Sikka does not need to work with people. She is insensitive to students and is making negative impacts. She started using the wrong formulas and doing things incorrectly for "the sake of time." We were constantly confused and never got a clear explanation. Do NOT take this class.

I was texting about a death in the family during her class and she called me out on it, which is fair since she did not know the reason. I told her after class the reason and she told me that not to sound unsympathetic, but I can't listen to her lecture and text about the death at the same time. She's always been awful, but this is unacceptable.

Dr. Sikka is one of the most passionate and professional teachers Ive ever had. She creates such a safe space for her students and deserves so much more love for the work she does than the love shes getting right now. I study in that classroom after hours just because I know that it is a safe place to work freely. 100% recommend.

Dr Sikka is the most caring and compassionate professor here at geneseo. If you are struggling with any of the tests shes always available to help you. She holds review sessions and records them for those who cant attend and sends out study guides. Yes her tests are hard, but she will never leave you unprepared. She truly is the best.

Do NOT take this class. SAVE YOURSELF. I would give her 0 stars. We have one class before the exam and she hasn't taught all the material. The material shouldn't be as hard as she is making it. She not only confuses us, but herself too! She talks about how she hates early classes (class at 8:30a) and yet she still signed up to teach one.
The class isn't too difficult. If you go to class and read the textbook and take notes, you will pass. Professor Sikka is super kind and cares about her students. It's an interesting class!

Professor Sikkas online class consists of little lecture and a long break out rooms. If you want to do good on the test you need to read the textbook and take notes! Other than that, you can tell she really cares for her students and such a sweet person.

Lectures consisted of breakout rooms and barely any content is discussed. Basically read the textbook on your own and take exams, no lectures helped. Would not recommend her as a teacher. Nice lady though.

I think it's a harder class than it should be. The content is very interesting, but the exams and quizzes have tricky questions on it. It is very possible to get in the As for this class though. She is nice and wants you to do well.

She's tough but so is the content and to a certain extent, she tries to make it easier to swallow. She can be funny and upbeat but also confusing and a little scatterbrained. Overall shes okay but the class moves fast and you wanna stay on the readings as much as possible.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass."]

comment: Prof. Sikka is amazing in other classes but manages to make statistics even more confusing than it already is. The textbook is necessary in understanding the concepts. Copy down the slides before class. There's only about 1 HW assignment a week. She is a very approachable, easy-going and kind professor that wants to see you succeed.

Professor Sikka is very empathetic & does a great job of clearly explaining concepts in class. She provides a lot of real world examples that allow you to further understand the objectives. There is little homework, other than integrative notes assignments, which you are assigned well in advance. She is also very approachable and intelligent.

Terrible professor. She is a very sweet lady but a very bad teacher. She, herself knows statistics well but she cannot teach a classroom filled with students who have never seen this before. People were constantly confused and would correct her and she would fight on how she was "right." This class was a joke because the entire class was confused.

Honestly one of the worst professors I have ever had. She is so all over the place and is unclear in all of her examples. She makes very simple topics confusing by her explanations and shouldn't be a professor that teaches math. She gets confused herself at the board and doesn't explain what we have to know.

She is a great professor who came to teach in our school for a year. She made the learning fun. Attendance was not mandatory but she gives daily quizzes which are very easy if you study her power point. The course is very straightforward. She is extremely helpful.

HE IS SO NICE!! Great prof. does like to ramble about his life which can sometimes be boring. Read his books, and participate, bc he wants to get to know you. Although his class required 5 papers, you will do well on them if you put in some effort and try to write something decent. Never got below a 90 on them, gives great advice. TAKE HIM!!!

He is honestly one of my favorite professors. No matter your skill level in writing, he grades on how much effort you put in-- which is important in a writing workshop class. I really enjoyed his lectures (since he's from philosophy dept), and he genuinely cares about his students. Every paper was interesting and challenging, but never impossible.

Wasn't really excited about the topic of the course going in but he has honestly been my favorite teacher here.  He is very engaging and easy to follow.  Very fair grader.  Take him if you have the chance!
Sauter is awesome. Class lectures are easy to get engaged in, and he is very understanding of your schedule. Always kind and always helpful. I would definitely take another class with him

He's a great professor! He's so kind and so helpful, I would take him for Humanities if he teaches it again. He is very passionate and really into the material. I found him to be a very easy grader at times but overall he does grade quite fair. Papers were around 5-6 pages long each time, the usual!! If he's available for any class, take him!!!

The class is pretty easy, but sometimes it is difficult to understand what the teachers are saying.  Also, there is a lot of singing, dancing, and acting so for people who don't like to do that in front of the class, it might hurt you in the end.  Otherwise, it is pretty fun. and Ana is extremely nice and funny.

Honestly he is a hard grader and refuses to give clear directions. Beware of CAPSIM it is the hardest thing in the class. Also study for a national exam. If you score less than average he just gives you a flat 0

He is a nice guy, but be sure you're with the right people for your group project. Also, don't ask him any questions on CAPSIM, because he wont answer. Overall, one of the nicest and easier professors I have had, and he loves to chat and make class fun and engaging (even bright and early).
Nice guy, but doesn't explain group projects very well, in which there are a lot of. A lot of group work, quizzes aren't bad.

Pouya is one of the nicest guys ever. Class is lecture heavy and he takes attendance. Weekly quiz on Friday's due by midnight but they are taken remotely and open note. CAPSIM simulations weekly. Big group paper and presentation due at the end of the semester that is very challenging. Class is relatively easy and he is a great guy to talk to.
Drones on about stuff that doesn't relate to quizzes or group projects which make up most of your grades. Also don't try to email him because he will not answer.

The most engaging professor I had in Geneseo. His course was really well structured and the course was taught in the most practical way. Participation really matters and although there's lots of work to be done, grading is very fair.

Went from having open-note exams to non-open note, all book based which he did not even touch in class (most failed). 10% of our grade was based on the school of business exam, which no other professor includes. He tries to be interesting, but class is a complete waste of time since we're not graded on anything that occurs in it. Do not take.

Amazing professor. Keeps you on your toes. You need to participate in class discussions every session. I learned more in this class than from any other. He's a great addition to Geneseo and boosts your experience in the business program. Great personality too.

Classes are engaging and require participation. He knows every student's name by the second week and will call on you to weigh in on class discussions. Shows great knowledge of the subject matter and answers emails very quickly if you have questions. Course syllabus is very detailed and self explanatory, so make sure you read it through.

He's incredibly disorganized constantly changing/ editing assignments after the class starts them. Every post, assignment, and announcement has typos or is impossible to understand. His wording is overly complicated, I have to reread things 10x just to figure out what he means. Lectures are unorganized & sloppy. Take this class with another prof

Lectures often felt unfocused and difficult to follow, he often seemed confused about the materials he was actively teaching. The class included frequent in-class writing assignments and homework, but the instructions and prompts could be unclear because he would change them after we had already started writing.

Do not take class with him. His bright space is so freaking confusing and I keep missing assignments that aren't main ones. Requires full undivided attention all the time, his lectures never make sense, and I can never find the right info that I need for major assignments.

Extremely hard to follow during lectures, is all over the place and expects you to pay him full attention, laptops shut, while he gives instructions at a mile a minute. Picks on you if he thinks you aren't paying attention and corrects you even if just to restate to be right and make you wrong. If you can take it with anyone else, DO SO.

He's nice but lectures are random and all over the place. His Brightspace was so confusing, I kept missing assignments and readings bc of it. His assignments are very confusing/random and don't make any sense. Participation matters, but no one will talk except for the same 3 people. He will call on you if you aren't paying attention

comment: DO NOT take this class. He seems like a nice guy (a little weird) but I ultimately withdrew because his lectures make no sense, no feedback was given and he doesn't explain what he wants you to do. I have a good GPA and taking this class with him was causing too much stress to try upkeep. TAKE IT WITH ANOTHER PROF

Easy class but try to do the assigned readings so you can participate in the class discussions. Still pretty easy if you don't but he can be hard to listen to and seems like he's coming up with the point of his lecture while he speaks. He does tell you what to study for all quizzes and tests so as long as you study you'll do well.

comment: Very unorganized and has no idea how to lead a class or a group discussion. It is very hard to engage with him and the class material unless your classmates make it interesting. Super confusing professor overall and makes you read heavy with barley discussing anything in class.
tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework']

comment: This class was horrible. He is very unorganized and his readings are not understandable. He will randomly call on students if you are not paying attention. Would not really recommend taking this class.

ENGL101: Memory, Trauma, and Space. Reasonable workload, homework and in-class writing. Lots of reading. Clear instructions for work. Mainly discussion-based class, which can drag on but that's inevitable for 100-min class and he leads discussions well. Every student does need to facilitate a discussion once. Good professor overall.

very boring and the professor himself is very unorganized doesn't explain things fully and is very confusing during lectures there is group projects and solo projects. the readings he assigns are somewhat confusing and is a big step from an easier class even though it is only a 200 level

Class was good. If you like environmental or are an environmental minor its deff one of the better options to take. Go to lecture and pay attention to what he says and it should be able to get a good grade.

100% the most boring lecturer ever. Not very clear with what he expects on homeworks/on exams. Class is not too difficult because the subject matter is basically high school earth science. So boring but an easy B, A is definitely doable.

An articulate professor who isn't very difficult at all and understands what a 100-level class should be. He uses mycourses to its full potential, and that's definitely a plus when it comes to following your progress in his courses.

Very boring.  His voice tends to put you to sleep. Easily one of the worst teachers in Geneseo. The mid term and final were extremely hard and almost impossible to finish. In his lectures he talks about things that are completely unrelated to the course 99% of the time. Your grade for the class will be based solely on how much he likes you.

Useless teacher, he comes to class and tells you nothing. Better off not showing up and just reading the book and articles. Grades are based on 2 hard Tests, and a simulation that was poorly written (that you have to pay for!) and time consuming. Take class with any other professor, or offer him money for a good grade because he always hints at it.

Ridicously vexatious Professor. You have two tests that encompass 200+ pages of article readings, 500+ pages of textbook readings and then 30 pages of in class notes. Then he adds random stuff because he feels like it. He gives lots of random and arbitrary extra credit so someone that worked half as hard as you can get an A for no reason.

Beyond terrible. I was looking forward to taking OB because it's something I'm interested in, but his class was awful. He was extremely disorganized, he would go off on a lot of tangents that did not apply to the class, the simulation we used was awful, I could go on for days. This class was very frustrating because he literally taught us nothing.
great case studies, bring props and go all out. he just wants to see how you'll make people solve the case study rather than tell it to them...test's are hard just take good notes in class

If you don't want a lot of work and a huge group project with some test, take Markulis. His lectures are good, , but if you choose not to take his oral exam (2), the paper exam is not anything you can study for. Likes outspoken people, even if you are able to say anything, this will pay of greatly at the semesters end.  Good Luck!

I had Markulis for strat this semester and he is a great teacher. He has a reputation as a difficult grader and someone who makes his tests hard on purpose, but I don't find this to be true at all. It's not easy but it's not hard either if you put in effort. He makes the clas really fun and it's never boring so I always went. Take him if you can!
He is really funny and helpful.  You have to be active in class or he will not grade well.  Do your part and you get a good grade.

No real basis for the grade, only 2 exams, and a large group project.  Reading the chapter before class isn't necessary, but extremely helpful.  Very knowledgable man, his stories, and cases help to pass the time.  Not a lot of work, just study hard for the exams!

Peter is prolly one of the best prof of my life.  His class is hard yes but it will force you to learn and make you want to learn about the subject matter.  He likes people who are outspoke.  Dont be shy and you will have the teacher you have dreamed to have.  Amazing man and a inspiring person.

Very nice guy but the class was a bit unorthidox.  You have to read the chapter before class, then in the begining of class you get a quiz, and then he teaches the material you were just tested on.  there is no final so after the quiz you might as well leave the class.
He never stays on topic and his directions are so vague.
His tests are very difficult but he is a funny guy and makes lectures intersting with his sense of humor and enthusiasm about the class.
I think this guy had a great head on his shoulders, and wanted students to learn what was important.  Extremely intelligent

This guy was the worst professor that I had in the school of business!  His stories went nowhere and it was obvious that he had absolutely no "real" world experience.  His exams were ridiculous and I learned nothing from this guy!
Best and most kind professor I have ever had. Such an awesome, respectful, and funny man.

This class has taken up all my time this semester. Do not take it with other work-heavy classes, because there is so much outside of class work. His brightspace is impossible to navigate, so just accept it. This is probably the most work heavy class I've taken in Geneseo, and some was just unnecessary busy work.

All lectures are from research articles, which are then turned into assignments that must be completed in your group, so hope that you have good partners. He assigns a lot of essays with vague instructions in how they must be completed. However, he does look out for his students and is flexible with expectations.
very easy to talk to but assigns a lot of work for the level of the class. feedback in class rarely matches the grading

Dr. Allen is genuinely one of the sweetest professors ever. His class is very heavy on reading and projects though. Group work is a big portion of your grade, as well as outside classroom work. Miss a few classes and you're behind on class assignments. Try to be at every class, and don't take the course if you're not good w deadlines and group work

His expectations are 300-level based. The amount of work for this class made it difficult to maintain my study schedule. I appreciate his approach but it did not feel like a 200-level! His grading slowed as his assignments piled up but you always had a grade within two weeks. Don't take this class if your schedule is packed.

comment: I love Dr. Allen because he is such a sweet man and the class is interesting. However it is a lot of work, I think, for a 200 level class and a lot of group work. There are peer evaluations he considers when grading but still can be frustrating depending on who you are with.

DO NOT TAKE I dont understand how he has such a high rating. doesnt know his students, will try AI Detecting your group papers, but the one he uses gives different results than all the others and takes 20 points off the whole group without talking to you. TA said it is really hard to do just OK in the class. NOT WORTH YOUR TIME!!

I love Jim Allen. Attendance is technically not mandatory, but you have an in-class assignment with your group each class. No exams but group projects, also there are popquizzes and he gives you a heads up. Very kind and wants his students to do good!

too much work for a 200 level class. makes you order the book HE wrote and pop quizzes you on the little analogies from the chapter that you don't pay attention to. every class has one or two group discussion assignments and doesn't give 100s on them. 3 group papers but doesnt give many instructions on it. it is not an easy class. should be 300
tags: ['Tough grader', 'Lots of homework', 'Beware of pop quizzes']

comment: He's a passionate educator and a REALLY kind, understanding man. This course was very interesting when I was fully engaged, but it was hard to give 100 percent everyday with multiple group assignments per each class. He teaches down to the last min.The layout of this course can feel draining but it really encourages you to learn and stay engaged.

Dr. Allen is one of the best psych professors I've had so far. His classes are mastery based so instead of exams he gives out a lot of class work thats divided between your group. Also all of his classes are formatted the same so It can be a lot if your taking two classes with him at the same time. Overall amazing professor and I would recommend.

I would not recommend taking him if you do not do well in a "flipped classroom". You pretty much teach yourself everything and in class you work on group assignments which I hated because I always got stuck with people who did not want to do anything. There are pop quizzes but you get the questions beforehand so they are not hard.

Allen is an amazing professor and person. His classes are relatively easy, no exams. 3 group project papers that seem intimidating, but hes super helpful and provides everyone with the necessary resources to succeed. He does "pop quizzes" but honestly tells you the class before. I would recommend if you're an okay writer and can work in groups.

Jim Allen is a nice guy. There were many assignments in this class but he's not too harsh with grading so as long as you put in effort you will be fine. I would highly recommend attending class because there are occasional pop quizzes and regular group assignments. He is very approachable and gives good feedback.

Dr. Allen is sweet and he genuinely cares for his students; for example, he read and gave me feedback on a paper the night before it was due. The reason I didn't give him a 5 is because the entire class is group work/group projects, which is exhausting. However, he makes up for this by offering unlimited revisions (so you can fix your own grade).

I love Jim Allen, he's very dedicated and passionate. He loves it when questions are asked and he is always willing to help. However, keep in mind it is all group work, I lucked out with my groups most of the time but it could suck if you get stuck with bad groups. 4 papers total. Lots of pop quizzes but he isn't too harsh of a grader.

comment: Group papers and unreliable peers.Grades depend on their content, so if ur stuck with a bad group, ur done for.Pop quiz after every reading, 3 tbooks to purchase.If u miss class one day, your grade drops by a lot but he lets you make it up only if u email him.Nice guy, but no lecture (slides) whatsoever.U only learn whatever u read.3 papers total

This was not the class for me. It's all group work, and when you get stuck with a bad group there is nothing you can do about it. He assigns readings for every class and often quizzes on them where he asks for very detailed information even if what you wrote made it clear that you read the text. I recommend buying a digital book to use as notes.

I really think Professor Allen is a wonderful person, and I learned a lot in this class. Overall, I enjoyed the class, but I personally dislike group papers. When people in your group don't have the same work ethic, it can be frustrating and if you're an introvert, being in groups every class may be hard. But, I would take a class with him again.

comment: PSYC 452-Super super sweet man. Will always make sure you understand the material. Very apologetic. Graded group work every class. Three papers and final exam. Papers are a lot of work, but his feedback is super helpful. SPSS heavy, but relevant for research

The class is necessary bc it is a flipped classroom, there's very little lecture and lots of group in-class assignments. Allen is a very sweet professor, always comes around to each group to ensure you understand and will help in any way. 3 group papers which are very tedious if you have bad group members. Overall a cool and interesting class

Professor Allen is understanding when you're confused. Class is highly recommended because it can get confusing if you don't show up + classroom is flipped so you do a lot of assignments with a group in class. It takes a bit to get used to, but it actually helps when you're trying to understand difficult concepts. TA is also very helpful!

Love this man. Was VERY understanding during remote learning. This man is honestly the nicest professor in the whole school. A real sweetheart. Everyday, he separates everyone into groups for discussions. However, his lectures are pretty heavy so DO THE DISCUSSION QUESTIONS AND READ HIS TEXTBOOKTHEY ARE A LIFE SAVER.

Dr. Allen is by far my favorite professor at Geneseo! He is so caring and really wants his students to do well. He goes above and beyond to help you in his office hours and is always available to help via email. While research methods is a challenging class, if you put in the effort and go see Dr. Allen you will do well.

He's one of the kindest and most knowledgeable professors at Geneseo, and the class was really interesting (but relied heavily on group discussions and textbook readings). The tests were difficult: all essay questions and he grades them so specifically that it's hard to know what he wants from you.
tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'TEST HEAVY']

comment: He is friendly, approachable, funny, and loves psychology. Make sure you go to class because he loves in-class group discussions/reports. I struggled with exams because he is very specific in what he is looking for, even though you are allowed to bring notes in with you. It might be worth looking into social psych with another prof.

Dr. Allen is the greatest Professor in the psychology Department. He is passionate about what he teaches which makes it hard not to be interested in the material. He is also very understanding and open to discussion about anything. This professor is one of the few reasons I have remained in college. He is a paragon of what every prof should be.
Study guides he gives really help for the tests

I  enjoyed taking 350 with Allen last summer. The most difficult part was clearly understanding the material we were given. Lots of statistics and charts, which made me lose interest a bit. However,  never hesitate to participate, he is very helpful and wants you to understand the material. He isn't scary at all, just an awesome guy with passion.

Pretty much the nicest guy in the department. The subject is really interesting and Allen teaches well, though we were perpetually behind on the syllabus and spent excessive time on some topics and minimal time on others. Class proceeds by study rather than by topic, so that could be painful. Lots of work, hard grader, would still recommend

I honestly don't know if I've learned anything at all. He is extremely unclear with what he expects, and when you ask him to go over something, his answer is always, "y'all should have that in your notes." I don't know if I've ever been so bitter towards a professor before. Heard he was good in other classes, but NOT in 352.

Uses the word y'all way to much to the point where its just ridiculous. The phrase "dont beat a dead horse" fits this class perfectly. He'll go over the most simple topics soo much but then the test is on a specific detail and if you dont include everything in it its wrong. This class really dragged on. Most of it is common sense.
Really enjoyed the class. Professor Allen is very nice and really approachable. His tests take some studying, but are not so hard that you cant manage them. Highly recommend!!

He is just perfect. His exams are hard but if you take good notes in class and read the assigned books you will do fine. If you have problems with the material just go to his office. He is very helpful

Dr. Allen is quite frankly the nicest man alive. He is just a fantastic person to know. His areas on interest are social and environmental psychology, and this class uses a lot of these issues as examples. Really supportive of students and the department as a whole. He is highly recommended.

His exams are difficult but he is fair grader. I didnt really use the book in his class at all. If your not great at math, no worries most of the test questions rely on knowing the logic rather then the computations. Make sure you attend all classes I skipped once and was lost for weeks.

He is a really nice guy, really cares about the students, I felt like i learned alot about statistics b/c he makes you learn all the logic behind the stats, tests are all written, I'd say if you go to class, pay attention, try hard, & put effot in, you can def do well : )

Dr. Allen is a great person but I was not interested in his class, at all. At 8:30 in the morning, it can be difficult to focus. He wants students to print out the studies but for an env psych class, it seems like a waste to me. The textbooks were interesting, I just didn't like his teaching style. The exams were okay, easier w/ the  study guide.

Allen is one of the sweetest professors I have ever had. He is willing to do so much to help you understand the concepts he is teaching, because he cares about them so much. I took it at 8:30am, but turns out it was worth it because of how interesting everything was, and how well he taught.

The logic and mechanisms behind stats are his primary focus - computations take the back seat in his class. Expect to write a lot (in English) for his tests. No homework, but there's an in-class activity almost everyday, so come to class, pay attention, and you'll be golden.

Very nice guy, extremely helpful out of class. Looks over paper as much as you want and willing to give comments. Tests are extremely hard as is his grading on papers. Be prepared to not do as well in this class as in others. Still recommend because the topic is interesting and Allen is helpful and nice

Social Psych with him is an interesting course. He always makes absolutely sure that everyone understands a concept before moving on to the next one. He is extremely helpful outside of class. However, he really is a hard grader, so be sure to prepare thoroughly for his tests.

Also had him for Psyc 288 & audited 251 with him. Heck of a nice guy, extremely willing to help explain things in class or outside. His tests are not easy- usually consist of 5 short answer questions (a choice out of 7 or 8). Gives study guides, but is a really critical grader on tests & papers. Be interested in the class & you should do well!

I never opened the book. Mostly because he doesnt look into the math portion of stats. Basically writing an essay in the bluebooks every test. definitely need to go to class to know the definitions. Need to be able to memorize the definitions and how to do certain things and why they are important. regular stats mad easier than this

attendance counted towards 10% of grade. nice guy, but extremely hard grader on tests. you'll never do as well as you think you did. throws a lot of studies at you and expects you to know outcomes and effects. passionate about what he teaches, funny guy. don't necessarily take 275 if you don't have to

Go to class. tests are difficult, know everything on the study guides he gives out, but still go over all of your other notes. only wrote one paper, easy topic and he pre-read essays and gave comments, which was helpful. very enthusiastic. highly recommended.

his tests are incredibly difficult, he's a tough grader. but he's willing to help, a lot. his class is very boring, I took it at 11:20 and I was still falling asleep in class...overall a difficult class. take it with someone else.

Professor Allen is definately one of the better teachers at Geneseo. He loves his material and not only teaches it passionately, but he dedicates time to making sure that you understand what he is talking about. The tests can be difficult, but as long as you study and put time in, you will be fine. He is very lenient and helpful. Highly recommended

Really hard grader, hard tests, hard papers. Willing to help but it's hard to find times he is available to help.  Subject matter is dry but he tries to make it interesting. He is unclear on many test questions and expextations....be sure to ask. Nice guy.
Overall good teacher. Hard grader, must go to class and take good notes. Tests can be a challenge and you must study. Makes the material half way interesting considering the subject matter.

Social with Allen is a pretty good class to take. He's a hard grader that gives alot of notes and you have to go to class. However, he makes sure that you know everything completley before he moves on. The tests can be prepared for since he gives you then questions to prepare for and allows you to bring 2 cheat sheets. Allen makes the material fun

So dry. Is obsessed with research methods and thinks you should be too. Knows his stuff but assumes you know nothing - teaches down to his students don't take him as an upper level student or he'll make you feel stupid because he assumes you don't know anything about psych tough grader even though the tests seem easy at first
No Comments

Jim is a great professor. He is very organized and will teach you a lot, but he is a really tough grader. You need to give him lots of detail on exams and he'll still find somewhere to take points off. But he's an awesome guy and a great professor, you just actually have to enjoy the subject and try

nice guy but a bad prof. merciless grader. absentminded and unorganized. i wish social was offered w/ another prof. 10-15 pg paper AND you have to turn in full text copies of all your sources. everything about the class was annoying. the book is more interesting than class. avoid if possible.

A very nice guy. Lectures are clear and he makes sure that everyone has the concept before he goes on. He lives up to his reputation of being a tough grader. The class is tough but you learn so much. And he's really helpful and lets you make-up if need be. He does play favorites, which sucks.
He is the nicest guy...  I love everything about him except he is a tough grader in my opinion.
Not my favorite psych professor, lets just leave it at that.
Class is challenging but fair.

Hands down one of the best professors in the psych department.  Very helpful if you put forth the effort,also very understanding of any circumstance you may be going through.However he is guilty of having the absent-minded professor syndrome.

He can be a real jerk, for lack of a much more fitting word if he doesn't like you, and although he is very helpful in the beginning he gets worse with it as the semester goes on, and his clarity is terrible!
I think he's great - very clear - very enthusiastic about the subject matter - you have to work hard and ask questions - if you're dedicated, he'll do his best to get you through.
his stats course is incredibly hard...if you miss one simple concept you can be screwed for the rest of the semester. and don't make my mistake- don't take his class as a first-semester freshman!
He sucks as an advisor and as a STATS teacher...
No Comments

lets you make up tests if you're sick.  :o)  very confusing during stats--spends more time telling you about how ANOVAs and other stats are derived rather than how to solve problems (and expects you to know verbatim how they are derived on exams)

Shes very all over the place when talking through the mechanics of each topic. I dont reccomend because she also claims things would not be on the test and then they are which is why may people did bad on a test. Means well though and is super kind to you if you talk to her. Make sure you go to Si sessions and tutoring.

Very sweet women. Hard to understand in lecture but if you go to her office hours, she's really good one on one. Lot's of homework that can be overwhelming at times especially before a test. Overall recommend she's very caring
good luck. she is hard to follow and talks about all the wrong things. it was hard to understand what she wanted you to do and genuinely couldnt answer half the questions asked in class.

Her slides make no sense, there is no explanation and half the time when she is explain she is confused herself. Very test and quiz heavy and she gives a study guide but the information on it, is nothing like what is going to be on the test.
She wasn't always clear in lectures, but the book cleared any confusion up.  Tests weren't always worded very well, but she is genuinely such a sweet woman.  I enjoyed her class.
A nice lady but not great at teaching. She gets very confused. Tests were pretty easy though and if you read the textbook you'll be fine.

I had Dr Lewis for both Bio 117 and 118. Extremely nice woman, but just not meant to teach. Awful lab professor, never had a clue what was going on, but was an easy A. For lecture, she often rambled about random things and would teach wrong info. Read the textbook, go to SI sessions and do the homeworks and you can get a decent grade.

Dr. Lewis is overall a great person but not very fit for the role of a professor. She taught alongside Dr. Bailey, and even he was confused in some lectures by how she would explain a concept. The concepts she would teach us were a little confusing because she would rant and rant. in general she is not that bad of a professor to have.
Professor Lewis is really nice and cares about her students--go to her office hours!! However, I did find her lectures hard to follow so definitely good to go to SI sessions.

comment: Really nice lady, decent professor, course was split between two professors. Work was manageable.

Shes nice but gets confused about what she's talking about. Sometimes she messes up while lecturing. She also has difficulty with running a classroom, she was not able to get this one kid to stop talking. Overall she's not like the worst professor ever, I just did not love her class and would not take a class with her again.

Lewis is a great professor. You do need to put a lot of work in and going to SI is what saved me. She cares deeply for her students and is accommodating and flexible, I know some people in my class were not a fan of her teaching style but it did work for me. Overall I heavily enjoyed having her as a professor and would highly recommend her.

Dr. Lewis has difficulty explaining crucial topics taught in the BIOL117 course. I relied heavily on the textbook information and knowledge from my previous AP Biology course. Lectures were a disaster. Tests are easy so long as you have a solid understanding of the concepts.

comment: Do not take this class if you are not a bio major. She is a sweet person but extremely difficult to follow and does not have great teaching methods. I frequently felt completely lost during lecture. I would not have earned an A- if not for the TI. Must purchase Achieve, which is online textbook & homework for about $100. Does not grade attendance

She was very easy to understand and helped map out difficult concepts when asked. Her lectures were decent and tests were fair. You can tell she is really passionate about her work and cares about her students. Like any course, studying will be your best friend, and she gives you all the resources you need to succeed.
Good Person, Not a good teacher.
Gets confused and often gives misinformation. Nice lady but very hard to follow. You have to study ALOT for her tests. Gives fictional case studies that are not helpful.

had her for intro bio lab, she always seemed unsure of what was supposed to be happening. very forgetful and often left us confused to do our assignments alone when she forgot to tell us something, then we would be unable to submit. also had to ask the other professors about every little thing. very nice person but would not take her lab again.

incredibly rude in her comments on tests; not helpful at all, her lectures are incredibly difficult to understand and to follow. She does not prepare you for anything in this class. must've thrifted her phd.
Definitely doesn't have a strong grasp on chemistry and her lectures are very boring. You need the textbook to pass the class. I changed my major after this not gonna lie
Gets mad when asked to re-clarify any concept covered in class. Only grades students based on test performance. Avoid.
worst professor to ever walk out of a university. i believe she got her degree at walmart. having ptsd thinking about this women.

She was a good professor, we went through lectures fast but that's understandable since there's so much material for this class. Found it easier and more helpful for her half of the semester to actively listen instead of write down notes. Overall she seemed friendly, I didn't find the homework or quizzes to be too hard, as long as you study!

She's not an awful professor but in order to get a good grade in this course you really need to read the textbook and make sure you know the material. She tends to get confused a lot during lecture and will give the wrong information sometimes and wont realize until 1o minutes later which is very annoying.
Quizzes are extremely difficult

You either have to go to class and take good notes or read the textbook. I did the former and did fine in the class. Her exams are quite tough and her grading is even worse. You have to make sure she graded your exam correctly because she probably didn't and makes you bargain for points. She gives you a notecard so write everything.

She is NOT good at teaching or being responsive. She taught with Regina Clinton and made tests insanely difficult. You do not have to go to do decently on tests though. She teaches far more than Clinton though and makes your life much harder. I wish that the school would have told me they taught together so I could avoid her.

I took Lewis for Gen Bio lab. Feissner's pre-lab lectures helped me through it because Dr. Lewis herself wasn't too helpful. She would confuse herself during the labs and explaining them, and she wouldn't be able to answer some of my questions. She wasn't terrible, but she wouldn't be my first choice next time.
The class work itself wasnt hard her test were super hard. And she would have a lot of trick questions.
A little bit difficult for being a 100 level class, but she gives question stems before tests and drops a lot of your low grades at the end of the semester. It's not difficult pass if you do the work

This class was hard for a 100-level non-majors bio. However for each test she gave us question stems which helped me get a good grade. Probably would've done worse if it wasn't online. Make sure you read the book

Worst professor I've ever had. Was condescending in our introduction prior to even starting class?? Her exams are crazy hard with only slightly different answers per question. Makes you use lockdown browser to add to this already difficult exam. Last exam average was 67. With 2 points of extra credit. Ridiculous. Not taught like a gen ed.

Case studies are ridiculous and terrible to learn from. Exams are unreasonably hard. Will be tested on material from these fictional case studies, and also from material not taught or mentioned anywhere. Will admit to you that she aims to weed out biology majors early on through these unethical and unacademic tactics.

Bad professor. Condescending, rude attitude. The exams are like reading a foreign language. Slightly changes each multiple-choice question to only leave out one option to confuse you in this class she already teaches like a level 300. Ridiculous.

This is a warning for any student who is about to take Lewis. She does not look to give you points on exams which make up almost 70% of your grade. She is one of the most inconsistent graders and some people will get points for an answer and others won't get any for the way they word it. She acts nice but she really does not care about students.

By far one of the worst professors I've ever had. If you take this class thinking you are going to learn about the introduction of human biology you are in for a rude awakening. She treats the class like it's a level 300 class and the tests are super hard. You will not pass the class if you don't read and practice on mindtap. She does not teach.

Its a large lecture class, so you get four tests and that is a large chunk of your grade. MindTap and tophat help a lot though. Shes great. The comments about her speeding through lectures is true, but shes funny, sweet, willing to work with students, and drops your lowest test score. (Keep in mind her tests are crazy hard though)

comment: Lectures do not help you learn anything, talks about things that are not important and always uses metaphors that do not make any sense. Tests are really hard for a required course.

Jani Lewis is a nice lady, but does not know how to teach. She often gets off topic and goes through the powerpoint crazy fast without explaining much. Go to SI sessions and make your textbook your best friend. Keep up with the reading and quizzes if you want to do well.

comment: you will learn nothing in class because everything is explained through weird unrelated metaphors but you have to go to class because attendance counts for your grade. if you read the textbook you'll get an A and she drops the lowest test but going to class was torturous tbh

Nice person and all but WOW she flies through her powerpoint slides way too fast. I always go to class, and I go to exam review sessions and study for hours before the tests but it's literally just memorization of facts that are super detailed. This was her first semester teaching this class & should be her last. She goes way too fast & doesn't give much indepth detail on the material. comment: Mrs. Lewis was probably the worst teacher I had. She means well and is kind, but really cannot teach well and her lectures are pointless. comment: She's a really nice women, but she teaches through case studies which doesn't work for everyone. Really read the book and take notes from readings in case it is not covered in lecture and you'll be fine. Study really hard for any type of biochemistry related test she gives, they are a lot harder than the usual exams.

This course in general is designed to try to kick pre-biology freshman out of the course because Geneseo is unable to handle the large amount of biology majors. So naturally this course is very difficult. Lewis does not make it any better. She gave us a test on 9 Chapters while other sections of 117 had a test on 4 chapters for exam one.
