comment: Lectures are all over the place and often do not cover what is in the book or test. Read the textbook religiously and you'll have a better chance.
tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Get ready to read', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS']

comment: This class is intended to be a weed-out class, so the tests are pretty difficult. I started to realize that all of the material was in the textbook and that lectures weren't all too important. The best way to prepare for exams is to find practice questions online. As long as you keep up with the material outside of class you'll be fine.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS']

comment: Pretty laid-back in class, but her tests are kind of all over the place and kinda tough.

She's a fantastic teacher (MUCH better than Muench). I wish she taught the whole year. Do quizzes in groups, readscan the text before every class, go to class (duh), and go to the SI sessions and professor review sessions. Dr. Lewis is very kind, approachable, and knowledgeable so don't be afraid to ask her questions as you go.

Lewis is my favorite bio professor I've had. She is a great lecturer and very understanding. However, this is not high school anymore; You have to read the textbook if you want a good grade. There is a lot of info in gen bio and you it's up to you to understand it. Go to the TA every week for review and go to Lewis' review sessions before the test.
Tests are challenging, specific and somewhat confusing. Not very good at explaining things.  Online quizzes and chapter tutorials will help your grade, most answers are already online.
She doesn't tech what's on the tests, too specific.

I love her! She is very approachable and a fair grader. Biochemistry is a tough subject, but her class is taught straight from the textbook. Just do your readings, understand the material, and you should be fine. Very helpful in office hours too. Take a class with her!

She is a pretty good teacher but only teaches half the class while another teaches the rest. Prs questions are a joke and they hardly ever work. Online quizzes are a pain if the wifi doesn't work you can't go back. Very difficult tests that ask specific questions not really relating to class discussions.
She is so nice and knows a LOT about what she is teaching. Also has a lot of energy. Made me excited to go to class. Tough grader, but it is an upper level Bio so I believe it is fair as well.

How can you all rate a professor on a class that's run primarily by the ULIs? Dr. Lewis is a phenomenal professor and incredibly personable. She is more than willing to make time for students that make the effort to meet w/ her. I've taken courses specifically because she teaches them. I HIGHLY recommend her for someone with a true passion for bio!

Pre-lab was awful and the only point is the 10 minute quizzes.  She lectures about random stuff that usually have nothing to do with the lab of thr week.  In lab, she doesn't really do much because its mostly your ULI.  But when grading lab reports and stuff, she takes forever and doesn't explain your grades well.

Very grating, annoying voice. She seems completely unprofessional and couldn't do simple math but expects us to do concentration questions without teaching us about ANYTHING. Posters and presentations were extremely annoying, freshmen bio just tends to suck.

Depends more of which ULI you get, the Lewis basically didn't teach anything we didn't, all the teaching was done by ULI's who are also students mind you, not teachers. You need to follow instructions word for word to get a decent grade. This class was so annoying but I guess necessary

Pre lab lecture breakdown:   10 mins on a multiple choice quiz,                       30 minutes of her talking about things not pertaining to the lab at all and making horrible jokes,             10 minutes talking about the actual lab,               then leave 10 minutes early. Needs to calm it down with the microphone and laser pointer.
Really nice lady - but not a great professor. Not very organized.
Excellent prof.  A bit wacky but definitely keeps my attention.  Hard but fair grader.

Grating, microphone-amplified voice and a deadly boring pre-lab lecture, covered by powerpoint and laser pointer. Many people leave right after the quiz, but Dr. Lewis expects more respect than that. Chances are you can't avoid her. Stay through the lecture to avoid being scolded and for potential extra credit. Use your computer only for notes.
She's nice but the class is confusing to follow

Dr. Lewis insists on using a microphone in lecture which is clearly not needed. When she answers questtions, no one answers because we can't pay attention.  It is easy to get bored.  She tries to make jokes which don't really apply to class.  Is very particular about her rules in class unlike other professors.

Pre lab seems like a pointless class. The lecture is pointless because the same information is repeated in lab.  The only reason we go is to take a quiz, which is given every week.  Many people leave early right after the quiz.  You can get by fine in this class without paying attention to lecture, just print out notes and study for the quiz.
She is extreamly annoying, rambles a lot, I felt like I was wasting my time every week.

she's nice, but annoying. quizzes are random and have a lot of errors which can cause a lot of confusion and poor grades.  her lab lecture was useless; there was a quiz everyday but then most ppl left right after it instead of staying for the whole hour.

She's very nice and seems to know a lot about biology, but not much about anything else. Its funny to hear the dumb things she says sometimes and to watch her students take advantage of her poor classroom management skills. Not very clear but tries to help if you dont undertand something.

The class may not be mandatory, but there are quizes every class (1/week). There are numerous errors in her quizes, which she chooses makes public after most of the class hands them in. Not to mention the fact that the material on the quiz is completly random. They could be based on lab(s) or whatever she feels like that week. Dont take her!

She is very loud and can be incredibly annoying. I'm glad I only have her for lab. Sometimes, I think she just talks to hear her own voice. On a more positive note, she really loves what she does but she should tone it down a bit. Prides herself on being so difficult when all in all, you just need half a brain to master her class.
Being outwardly nice alone doesn't make a good professor. Her feedback isn't the best in terms of editing. She's satisfactory, but I'm sure somebody else could do a better job.

Very enthusiastic.  It is clear she loves what she does which makes class much more enjoyable.  She is helpful and nice.  Class is difficult but not impossible.  Labs are fun.  Wish I had more professors like her!
questions r very unclear. very flaky. prides herself on being a difficult teacher, but shes not so much difficult as unclear. very nice.

DON'T TAKE LABS WITH HER! she is ridiculous; i dun care how nice she is. she doesnt know wht she's doing in lab. might be a smart teacher, but def not a fair grader. handing writeups to her in advacne doesnt work--one group did that and they still got a 65 on it. im very diappointed that i got A's for all my classes except for this stupid lab.

She super sweet and a really great teacher. Always gives great analogues in class to help explain things and you gotta love her powerpoints! Hard tests, but if you know the material, definatly passable.
No Comments

She stumbles around a lecture too often, plenty sleepers in class... If you like a professor that dances around an idea without being too clear, Lewis is your professor. Her exams are "higher application" based (barely textbook context based) She's really nice though. Almost too nice. It's scary.

I actually miss this class. She is very energetic and an incredible people person. Her tests made you think but allowed me to develop my study habits in such a way that I retained more material and learned challenging skills. She made it interesting, and I would probably recommend her for an upper level course.
A challenging but amazing teacher...she is always very understanding and very approachable.  She is always very helpful when you go to her.

Very nice Professor. I had a TA but Dr Lewis came and made appearances frequently. She's a tough grader, but extremely helpful. You can hand your lab writeup in early and she will pregrade it and give it back to you with comments. A smart lady with high standards. Choose your lab group wisely!
More than willing to help with any questions you have on the material. Friendly and really smart...the stuff you learn from her will help you later on even though it seems tough while your taking it.
Print out the powerpoint notes, and read the text.  Freshman bio at Geneseo is a course you need to study a LOT in in order to succeed.
No Comments
will help you a lot with write ups but sometimes thats not enough- she could be much clearer

Very picky grader, but you can go to her in advance and she will look over your work and give it back with comments before it is due. Even after that it is sometimes difficult to understand what she wants.

hard and unapproachable.has a superior complex over the less smart students.extremely hard tests at first gets easier gradually but not by much.assigns too much work too quickly.does not understand that we have other classes.takes forever to return papers
She teaches at a very quick pace, print out the lecture notes to follow along.
She was middle of the road for me. I did not enjoy this class but its more the topic and how it was taught by her than the professor herself

This class actually helped me become more interested in geography and the whole world. Took this class as a chem major for my gen ed. Her tests were quite challenging, especially the wording of questions/answer choices, but I would've done better if I paid more attention. Overall, it was awesome learning about some of the less-developed countries.

Her lectures are the best I've heard and seen from any professor while here at Geneseo. The time and effort put into them, and the presentation slides clearly show she enjoys teaching and making sure everyone can succeed in her classes. Would take again.
I wish I could share my full experience here but there is word limit. do not take this professor she is not worth it. She was not willing to understand or help in any way.
She was very professional and had interesting lectures.
simple class, posts slides but doesn't put a lot of text on them, no problems with her

Rogalsky is by no means a bad professor. Her class is quite organized in Brightspace, and instructions on assignments are clear (and she goes over them in class). The entire class consists of 3 exams, 6 mapping exercises, and 2 extra credit opportunities. It wasn't difficult by any means but to pass you should show up and listen to her lectures.

I think many of these low ratings are unfair, likely because they are people who don't attend class :/ (only 40 of our 75-person class attended regularly). Jen is super nice, and this is an easy class, assuming you show up. We even reviewed test questions/map exercise questions in class. There are 3 exams and 6 map exercises (**Lowest M.E. dropped)

Dr. Rogalsky is clearly interested in this class and makes her students as well. Two actual tests are difficult, be prepared to study. Other assignments in the class are straightforward and pretty simple, but she does hold her students to a high standard on all of them. If you spend the time she expects doing reading and projects, you'll like her.

Dr. Rogalsky is a delightful professor who is very clearly passionate about what she teaches. She is experienced and extremely knowledgeable. I am convinced that most of the negative reviews are from people who didn't go to class, since she gives answers for the assignments in class. So, if you just go, and pay attention, it's really easy.

I had to go home halfway through the semester for COVID reasons and she made it her goal to try to fail me. Failed to accommodate me on assignments when I gave her perfect alternatives. Had to eat a 0 for a test because she wouldn't allow me to take it online. Barely passed. She thinks her mediocre geology class is way too important. Stay away

comment: Rogalsky seems really nice at the start of the semester but she kinda turns to a demon later on. Feedback on maps make no sense. I sit in the A- -> A's for every class but this sucked. Boring lectures. Only way to do okay is reading every word in the book and annotating heavily. Her map exercises, or "hw" never are graded well. VERY tough grader

comment: Will only give u full credit on the Mapping Exams if you write down what she's thinking word for word.  Her instructions are unclear and the powerpoints have NO information.  Genuinely just one of those professors who don't care how you do in the class.

One of my map exercises I borderline failed because I did not understand the instructions I guess, but that grade got dropped. I was scared to take her, but I found her pleasant. I like her honesty and she does give workdays occasionally. Only essay is flexible, 3 tests that arent cumulative, and no real final. Very responsive to questions.

Outrageously harsh grader
Deducts points from work for criteria she hadn't stated
Deducts points by falsely correcting grammar
Unconventional and inconvenient due dates
Assignment instructions and lectures are less coherent than writing/speech she herself deems unacceptable
Always sounds like she has no idea what she's teaching
such a harsh grader, she will take points off for very weird things like where you have placed a comma. doesn't care about students and sticks all her work on her ta
Awful. Terrible. Do not take.

Do not take geography 123 with Rogalsky at all costs. She teaches incorrect information, she is such a harsh grader yet her comments make absolutely no sense or she will dock you off on things that weren't even in the instruction. Her homeworks are so time consuming and are graded so harshly, it is way too much energy and criticism for GEOG 123.
HARSH GRADER

Professor Rogalsky is very harsh on the grading and will nit pick every little thing you do. When I did take her class we had an assignment due and I ended up doing it 2 weeks earlier just to make sure I got a good grade and even though I tried my hardest on it she still picked out the weirdest things to take points off.
Does not listen to student feedback and is not helpful when going to office hours.

goes over things in class not mentioned in the reading for test. Map exercises are time consuming and graded harshly. Current event discussions are a large part of class. Occasionally she will let you have time in class to work on projects as a reward for actually showing up, with free answers as well. Go to office hours if you want her to care

Very overly critical with grading. Seems nice at first but youll quickly see that she can be very harsh. Lastly she treats her students in her 100 level class as if they came in with a background in it when most are there to fulfill credits
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things', 'Tough grader']

comment: Dr. Rogalsky is a decent professor. She is clearly very passionate about her field and is great at explaining concepts in-depth. In class, she's not very personable, but is wonderful for one-on-one help during office hours. She's a very critical grader for the map exercises. Also, make sure to read the textbook as many test questions are from it.

Everything this lady teaches is from the syllabus so there are no surprises, but she is a rude, uncooperative, and uncaring teacher. She wont work with you if it affects her life at all and she is extremely selfish. 75% of the test answers are online so you really dont even have to go to class, but if you have to ask her a question, be prepared

Meh. Seems nice but when it comes to grading your stuff she's pretty tough. Exams are okay but she takes specific questions from the textbook so make sure you read that. Sometimes she will reveal questions that will be asked on exams so i suggest going to class. Allows two opportunities for extra credit. Decent professor but TOUGH grader even on HW

Dr. Rogalsky is very kind and knowledgeable. I learned a lot from class and enjoyed the content. We had to read a lot of scholarly articles, though, and write about them. If you have a background in geography it would make the course much easier. The grading is very meticulous, specific, and semi-harsh, but we received quality feedback of our work

For an intro course, this professor treats her students as if they all have experience in urban and regional planning, and have explicit interest in the field; expects way too much considering many students are non-geog. Lectures are all spoken word, with little information given on slides, making it hard to keep up and to reference when studying.

Rogalsky is so great. I learned so much from her this semester. This class does not require too much work, but going to class and doing the readings will help you pull off a good grade. She is so knowledgable and I hope to take her again at some point!

To be blunt, Dr. Rogalsky is NOT an easy professor. She has very high expectations for her students, even in intro/non-major classes, and her essays and tests are thorough and somewhat challenging. That being said, Dr. Rogalsky is by far one of the best and most knowledgeable professors I've had at Geneseo. I would highly recommend her.

She is the worst professor I've ever had in my college career. She doesn't care about her students at all. I never skipped a class and always kept up with the readings but i still got the worst grade possible. She isn't helpful at her office hours. DO NOT RECOMMEND !!!!!!!!!!! This class brought my GPA down so much

She is an extremely harsh grader on mapping exercises and essays. Tests are not too hard, all are multiple choice with two maps to label, questions can be tricky. Definitely take advantage of extra credit opportunity that is added to the final paper.
As long as you read the instructions closely, you should do fine on the homework assignments, and the tests aren't too hard.

She comes off as a very nice person on the outside but beware that she is an extremely tough grader and will not hesitate to tell you how bad you did on something. she also take points off for not liking the way you shaded maps or the colors you used. There are 3 tests total all multiple choice with mapping and one 1500 word essay. Good Luck

It seems like her intention with grading papers is to make the class feel horrible about themselves. She doesn't care how her class does and the tests have details in them or things that she's only mentioned one time and you'll be expected to remember it. Nice lady but tough class.
Overall easy course, only one long paper during the entire semester. Homeworks are simple and rarely assigned.

Rogalsky is a very friendly professor and more than willing to help if you go into her office hourse. Her lectures are interesting and engaging. The only negative thing is that she doesn't give clear guidelines for what will be on the exams. She tests on information from the lectures and book but she is vague about what she will ask from the book.

I loved this class because if you are not good at taking tests there are other ways to get your grades up. The mapping exercises are an easy 100 if you actual put the time and effort into it and don't blow them off.

I cannot stress enough how much I disliked taking her class. To begin with she expects far too much for what she assigns. When given an assignment directions are generally vague, but then when you get it back she will take off (too) many points for not giving her exactly what she had in mind. She also acts as if you are not taking other classes. :(
Expects too much
Rogalsky is very nice, friendly women who has much experience in what she teaches.  Not a difficult class at all.  Read the chapters the day before each test and you will do fine.

Class isn't hard, but it's annoying. Rogalsky takes this class WAY too seriously for a 100-level, tests are mostly book-based even though none of it is mentioned in class, and you have to buy a review book that is in comic sans. Grades are 3 tests, participation(in-class, online, and mapping), and a 1500 word essay.

pretty easy grader for a 300 level class, but that's about it. she's not too helpful if you're not a geography major (esp if you're an education major). somehow my final grade went from a B+ to a B-... not too consistent.
Very good teacher
You can't get much worse than prof. rogalsky. We're talking about bottom of the barrel as a teacher. I actually got a good grade in her class but wouldn't recommend her to anyone.

She really needs to work on her teaching methods.  It's obvious she knows her stuff and the text is an interesting read but she reads straight from a powerpoint that she later posts online so attending class isnt necessary at all.
VERY HARD class! DO NOT take 377 with her unless you don't have a choice or, don't care if you have a life!!
she uses the same questions in the study guide. Just read the review questions and memorize the terms. Every lecture was interesting and it was my favorite course my first semester

She's a good professor.  Tests are easy or hard depending on whether or not you keep up with the reading or if you come to class or not.  She likes to generate discussions during class and we've watched travel channel shows a couple of times so class isn't always boring.

Every lecture of hers is interesting. She is a very animated speaker and has mostly pictures in and maps in her powerpoints. Since she wrote the study guide, if you go over the review questions in it, you ace her tests.

One word...YIIIIIIIKKKKEEEESSSSSSSS!!!!!  She was by far the worst professor I have ever had (including from the Community college I transfered from). When it came to the tests, all she would say is "it's from the textbook", even though we didnt cover any of the stuff. Then she would ask the smallest details from the textbook. WORST TEACHER EVER!!

This class can be super easy or super hard depending on your knowledge background. Her tests require really specific knowledge. If you know a lot about the developing world and read international newspapers weekly the class is an easy A. Rolgalsky likes to toot her own horn a lot and is sometimes wrong on facts but is generally a good professor.
she is a really nice lady and really easy to pay attention to, but her tests are just ridiculous. they require you to know little facts from the text and its just too much information to remember
Made topic relatively interesting.  Workload is manageable, students aren't really punished for not reading.  I would recommend to friends.

Big lecture so you don't have to go very often. Light workload: coloring("map exercises"), one paper, three tests. Tests are pretty straightforward and are mostly current events related questions. Fulfills two requirements, and you learn a bit of geography and current events. recommended

Loved this class and the way she teaches, but got a C because there is so much matching on the tests that if you screw one thing up, you basically fail. gives 8/10 on mapping exercises without any explanation for points lost besides "more detail more detail". you really have to devote yourself to this class to the the grade you deserve.
Class is sometimes uneventful, but its pretty simplistic.  If you do the activities and essay you should have no problem getting an A
Boring class. No motivation to study. Easy if you do the work, but she's very specific about grading. Lots of group projects, mapping, etc. I'd avoid this if you hate classes with 60 or more people.
Honestly thought the class was easy and Rogalsky was nice. LOTS of extra credit oppertunities, and she tells you exactly what to study for the tests. If you go to class you will do very well.

Fun. Smart. Loves Geography.  Not the nicest woman in the world and isn't all that understanding unless you really show her a reason she should believe you. (Basically- very strict)  Lots of in class projects. Tests primarily based on book and things that she says, not notes. Not a good idea to miss class. However, I still liked her a lot.

Stay away, stay away, stay away.  No matter how hard you try to do well in her class, it's pretty impossible.  She does not go out of her way to help students do better.  If you do poorly on the first exam, good luck trying to get your grade up.  Slim chances.
No Comments

Prof. Rogalsky is a very informational person. She is always full of current events and she expects us to keep in touch with the news too. Her tests are definitely MORE from her class than the text, and she likes giving those "Not not" questions so beware! She gives out some extra credit though.
Very easy if you know anything about current events and have any common sense, nothing really challenging about this class.

Great professor.  The book is interesting.  Her lectures are different from the book, which enhances the class.  You must go to class and take notes.  Lots of times test questions are based off discussions in class.  The tests are not bad if you study.  There are no quizzes.   The only homework is to read and 5 map exercises.
easy if u study. she doesnt teach alot from textbook

boring, unfair, unorganized and unfriendly. she definitely gives good grades to her favorites so your grades depending on if you can get along with her. if you don't think you can(or you don't want),don't take her class. the class will be torture.

Two-faced and chooses favorites.  Once you're on her bad side you are doomed to fail.  She tries to relate to youth because she is young but it doesn't work.  She's fake and thinks her class is the most important... avoid her.

So far i have read three books in that class, and none have been the text. The text is a waste, and so is going to class. Before each test she tells you what will be on the test. Look up vocab, know you're physical geography, and glance over at the guy next to you. It's easy, but i hate her

Easy class its all complete ****. u can do good on the tests without even going to class.  she manages to fill and hour and fifteen minutes up without saying anything.  take this if u want somethin easy, but dont mind not learning anything

very easy class gradewise. she tells you exactly what is on the tests.  most of the time you feel like you've accomplished absolutely nothing when you leave class. a very nice person but not the greatest lecturer.  an easy grade if you just do the work and study what she tells you to.
She's ok, she can be a hard teacher to take notes from because she can be all over the place, but her tests are pretty easy, and map exercises are easy too.

Amazing professor, brings in guest speakers so students can see the practical usage of the class material.  Encourages class participation and loves the "extra effort."  Her lectures are well thought out and organized easily, and she even tried t

She's pretty ****y, unfriendly, and not that easy.  You have to read the text and the maps are boring.  It was possibly the hardest class to stay awake in.  I hated the outlines she gave, and she would throw info out 100miles a minute. good luck keeping up

i think people are being too hard on Jen, the material can be boring and i did skip a few classes but shes an involved professor if you take the time to talk to her. exams come from class notes (go to class!!) and workbook samples and the maps are tedious but theyre not worth the bad comments
not the most flexible teacher ever, but really organized and clear on what she wants, there's a lot of stupid work she assigns but it's pretty easy to do well.

Jen is the sweetest teacher ever, although i agree with the fact that you're never exactly sure what to study.  I personally think that she's a fair if not easy grader.  The class is a little boring but not terrible

All you do is draw maps, write 2 papers and take 3 tests in this class. It is very simple and Jen makes it intersting with shocking statistics and facts about current events that she will share with us. We watch a lot of intersting movies too.

These ratings suck!  What did they expect, an easy A?  Quit your complaining, she gave you an easy assignment.  Jen knows her stuff and can be very accomodating if you do the work.  She is rigid with due dates, but her students actually learn things...  what kind of crack were these people on??

Very unhelpful and rigid, yet ambiguous requirements, class is boring and general knowledge based, never really has a point and you never know what to study or know. Overall very childish class (map coloring) taught by very childish teacher.
This class was a little dull, but she was very nice and helpful when you asked for help.

Class is interesting, but she wonders off into too many current events.  Never really sure what is pertinent for the exam. It is pretty easy- coloring maps- and she is extremely nice. Just never sure what to study
unfair grader, boring work, not hot at all

very bad teacher, very unclear, and does not grade fairly. i felt like i was in gradeschool again w/having to color maps in. very boring. if you want to take geography,do not take it with her, she will make you not like geography,that is how boring she is

She is not a very good teacher, theres no point in going to class you can just read the book and teach yourself. Shes really boring and acts like your in middle school. its not the worst class in the world but i wouldn't suggest taking her.
Jen is a hard grader, however, her classes are well structured and interesting, and the discussions are great.  Also no tests in Urban Geography!!!
the class is a waste of time its like middleschool social studies, wtf - color in maps?! are you kidding me!

Seems like we're talking about two different people.I had an awful experience with Rogalsky along with many of my peers.All that I truly learned from her were some current events.I stopped going to the class and instead just used the book.She doesnt teach

If it's at all possible to fit into your schedule you should take humn with Frahm.  He genuinely cares about students and puts a great deal of effort in himself.  Hum can be one of the worst classes, but with Frahm he makes you think and it's interesting, even if hum isn't your thing.

Really cares about students. Adament about having group discussions and ensuring that all groups are completely random everytime. Quiz everyday, but you can work with your group. Overall, great HUM experience. Highly recommended.

Highly recommended for HUM.he makes the class very interesting because he is so enthusiastic, yet he's a pretty fair grader, which is rare for HUM.  He genuinely wants his students to succeed and will put in the effort to make this happen

I was dreading humn!!!!  But I love Frahm!!!!!  He is probably one of my favorite professors at geneseo and i hate everything about humn...  i hate papers, reading, writing, tests, politics, history and philosophy but as long as you read you can do fine in his class!!!  I suggest him to everyone!

Great orgo professor but his accent takes a little to adjust to. I would say he was more than fair on exams considering they were practically identical to the quizzes given prior. Orgo is just a challenging class in general so its not his fault that the material was difficult. Engaging in lectures and regained attention by cracking jokes.
Porter was a great professor for orgo. Fair grader and gave a lot of opportunities for graded assignments. Wish he was still going to be here next semester!

Great personality and a good lecturer. I had him at 8;30am, and I didn't fall asleep. The class is organic chem, so of course it's going to be hard. Helms is the hardest and his test averages were always higher than Porter's class because the kids actually studied more. Great professor! Sad he is leaving

A very nice guy but a very harsh grader. He wants very specific answers and will take of points off on anything he can get you with. He will rip apart multiple part questions even if you get the right answer in the end and show you understand the subject. At the end of the final the 40-50 range ended up being about a B-....are you serious?

Quite possibly the worst professor I have had at during my time here at Geneseo. He gave absolutely no partial credit on tests, in a class that definitely requires some partial credit to do well at all, Organic Chemistry II. If I fail it will be due to very little shortcomings on my part, I studied my butt off and I still have yet to "pass" a test.

He takes the simplest concepts and turns them into 45-minute rants that leave you more confused. Says grades don't matter/learning should be the ultimate goal while never actually teaching/providing his students with resources to learn. His classrooms are stripped of engagement as he repeats the phrase "am I making sense" while never making sense.

Tough online quizzes made up much of the grade. Group assignments were used to practice long-answer test questions, but we were to answer intricately, with particular expectations and zero guidance. Despite my doing most of the groupwork, we received one grade based on group functionality. I have not received a B(+) or lower until this class.

Dr Lei is a great person to talk to but I didn't learn well from his teaching. Savellos is an amazing teacher! I took him for Phil 217 and went abroad with him for the Med Roots Humanities trip. awesome guy. extremely smart, very helpful and kind. Took him for metaphysics, phil of lang and phil of law. I'm not a phil major. Really challenges you to think.
He is cool! A true philosopher with true insight. A very smart guy. We take the classes not to get through the exams and the core requirement, but indeed we are there learning a lot.

AMAZING Professor! Absolutely adorable.  Gives a very precise study guide.  He grades fairly, both tests and papers.  However, he does notice if you skip class, but class is fun so it doesnt' matter. He is hilarious if you really listen to him, not to mention he has a great Greek accent.  If you're stuck, take Humn with him.  Def. worth it.

Very interesting man. I hated him at the beginging of the semester, but loved him by the end. He knows A LOT. Trys to get the class involved in the lecture and has a great sence of humor. He does give pop quizes on the reading. His tests are non cummulative and you get study guides for them (USE THE STUDY GUIDE). I would definitly take him again.

What can I say...Savellos was my secret weapon...only professor who thought I was an 'A' writer (I wrote my first paper for him hours before it was due and got an A!).  His tests come right from his study guides...pre-write most topics and you will be all set! Gotta love the cute Greek accent

Eh...good teacher, very smart and funny, likable guy who knows what hes talking about. Terrible grader- gives tests back the day of the next one, doesnt give feedback on your work, only a grade...Kinda leaves you with impression he didnt even read your work/test.

I love this guy! His accent is so awesome. But also hes a great guy and he really wants everyone to get something out of humn. He keeps it interesting and factual even tho he's a phil professor. Gives study sheets for exams and picks q's right off it. Best professor to take Humn with, definately.
i LOVED HIM!!! come to class, ask for help on a paper and he'll remember it when grading. study notes from class for tests :) p.s. he loves that he's greek. chat it up with him
I had professor savellos for philosophy of law. He was very difficult, but a genuine nice guy. Very approachable, but tests were insane...
Hilarious guy.  Tough though, due to the fact that if the correct answer is point A and point B, and you say B then A, you'll be wrong!  Fairly unapproachable...:(
One of my fave professors ever! Very engaging lecturer and nice/funny guy.  Provides study guides for exams and moderate grader on papers.
Nice guy, makes class interesting.  He's there to help you if you're interested but he's a pretty rough grader.

It has been several years since I graduated, but I can genuinely say that Prof. Savellos was one of the few professors I liked while at Geneseo.  Excellent grasp of the material, intense interest in the subject matter, FUNNY, and a good guy all around.
He was a great professor -- made class exciting!!
Best lecturer ever! Can't fall asleep in that class.
best lecturer ever
Unprepared for class.  Disorganized.  Not available in office hours.  Not fun.

excellent.

Lectures are pretty boring. Most people write notes ahead of time and sit on their phones in class. Mini-quizzes at the beginning of every class, but they are pretty easy if you look through your notes.

Mr. Baecker is a fun, student-oriented, influential, and educated professor. It is important to study the lecture notes, as the test questions he gives are quite obviously based on them. I thought this was the best prof I've had this semester; he was nice and was able to help me when I needed it. Very friendly and nice guy.

one of the worst professors here. Pretty bad at teaching and gives endless amounts of these in class participation assignments which are fine but they are due every single day which was mad annoying. not great at explaining things or teaching in general to be honest. not a great speaker and his slides are so vague. i'm a great student and got an A- in bio 1, got mostly As on my bio exams except his, which i failed.

avoid if possible

SO FRUSTRATING! He is so condescending and gives packets to fill out every single class. this man never stopped yapping yet it was never relevant info for the tests he assigned. even when he claimed somethign would be on the test and told us what to study, it was never on the exam. you'll prob know more ab his personal life than bio itself so ur better off just reading the textbook!

DO NOT TAKE A CLASS WITH HIM. Talks fast and at you for an hour and 15 minutes. Takes 3+ weeks to grade scantron exams. Nice guy but overall very boring class.

I don't see what the problem is. Funny guy who's nice and cares that you do well. Yeah he's a little scatter-brained but it doesn't really affect how well you do in the class if you put the work in. The lab is hard but it's not his fault. It's A+P what do you expect?

Fairly easy grader and very nice, approachable, and funny. HOWEVER, he talks SOOOO fast. If you ask a question, he will go on crazy tangents and take 20 minutes to answer your question. Extremely knowledgeable but be wise when asking questions lol. Fun class overall though.

Wow. What an absolutely awful professor. He speaks a mile a minute. I dont think he actually breathes. When he takes a breath its like the whole class looks like like is he ok. All he does is talk. comment: A good professor!

The class was easy. However, the majority of the grades you'll get will be through your one-on-one meetings with him about your thinking process. Lecture can be boring as most of the time it is him taking notes from students' answers.

He was a good professor and easy grader, it was strange being in a math course with no tests, just weekly meetings. However, he has a very busy schedule and when I couldn't meet with him because his schedule was full, I talked to him about it 3 times and he dropped my grade a whole letter.

Professor Baldwin is a great professor. The course structure is based around weekly problem sets rather than exams. He focuses on students' mastery of the unit (understanding) so you do the reading, go over it in class with some examples, then do the problem sets. He allows remakes as well, and very easy to reach through office hours or emailing

I took Math 104-01 (Mathematical Ideas), a course designed for liberal arts students. However, if you prefer submitting work online, this class might not be ideal. The professor requires an office visit for grading. This guy also uses Calculus Math instead of basic math, and talks about Machine Learning or AI.

There are no exams in this class only problem sets. You always have enough time to do them and if you need to move a meeting he is very accommodating. Lectures can get boring but it is an easy class to do well in. You do not need to be a math genius to succeed.

The class is now writing 105. This class was so easy. Attendance isn't mandatory, but participation is a part of your grade. I skipped a few times, and he didn't care. Your grade is based on three essays, which you can revise for a better grade. Overall, he's a very nice man and an easy class, although it can be a bit boring.

comment: i don't think i would have found theory of computability interesting with any other prof. it's pretty easy to get a B-C in his classes, but hard to get an A. also can be difficult to schedule meeting times. no tests, so pretty much nothing cumulative you have to really try hard to nail down. definitely one of the easier math professors here

Professor Baldwin is a really nice guy and cares about his students. Explains things very in-depth and hard to follow. Instead of tests, you will have problem sets. You have a week to do them and have to get it graded the week after. Has a free textbook online to use. I was always good at math in high school but found this class to be difficult.

Awesome!!! The only grades are from once a week problem sets and you are allowed to re-do/do another one to replace that grade. You have to be able to explain your work because you get graded by meeting with him to go over the problem set and he will ask you variations of the questions on the spot. He is super helpful, I feel like I learned a lot!

Prof. Baldwin is a very caring professor who wants to see his students succeed and it is very clear. This class tends to be a very repetitive class and essays can be graded toughly, but you always have a chance to fix them. If you are looking for a easy class with a good prof, I would take this. You just may be bored.

Nice guy. 3 essays due. Has bit of a process with essays. 2 one on one meetings needed, peer reviews, a draft, revisons, and a final draft. Attendance doesnt matter. But you need to read the books because all the essays are based on the books. Does ask for a lot of peer conversation and asks lots of questions in lecture (doesnt call on ppl tho)

I started with Professor Baldwin half way through the semester because the other professor had left. He was very considerate of the fact that he had only taught us for half the semester and made sure his grading was fair in that way. He really cared about his students succeeding and was always available for office hours.

Provided free textbook online, which we were expected to do short readings from for every class. Attendance wasn't mandatory but it's easy to fall behind if you miss. Didn't give tests, instead gave homework assignments that we had to explain how we did in a 1 on 1 meeting. Fair grader, nice guy, and genuinely helps students wherever he can.

comment: Professor Baldwin really cares for his students and really just wants them to succeed. His grading method is a bit different then other professors but as long as you put in the effort his class is an easy A. Really recommend taking him over any other calc professor!

I really liked him. No exams and the Problem Sets are easy enough. Just make sure to GO TO THE SI SESSIONS, that guarantees an A. He does explain things using intense math, but honestly you don't need to worry about that bc it doesn't pertain to the Problem Sets which is what you are graded on.

Professor Baldwin doesn't give any tests. Instead he gives about 11 problem sets during the semester which are the only grades in the class. The problem sets are pretty fair and he always asks in the beginning of class if anyone has any questions about any set. Also, he always posts notes on canvas and the textbook is free online.

Just don't. He's too smart for his own good, and grading is based on understanding the material rather than being able to do it. For people like me who don't understand math but can get the right answer it makes getting a half decent grade near impossible. Problem sets are impossible and based on theoretical situations that complicate everything.

comment: He doesn't give tests, instead gives problem sets where you have to narrate everything you did to him. The only grades are homework sets given about once every week. You're graded by meeting with him individually and going over your homework. A lot of times the answers are given in class and posted online so it's really easy. No tests or papers. He's really good at giving students as much credit as possible.

Douglas Baldwin is a really nice guy, and really cares for his students. However he grades weekly homework's on a scale where an 8/10 is perfect work and perfect explanation. In order to get a 10 you have to solve the problems in ways he has never seen or thought of before (btw he wrote the textbook). Calc degraded my self confidence like no other
I had prof Baldwin for intd about secret codes and I believe hes the best instructor anyone can ask for. Hes really caring, love to help, give valuable feedback but hes a tough grader

Prof. Baldwin is a very caring guy. If you are ever sick or anything, he is more than willing to extend your due date. You HAVE to read the textbook pretty much every night and his grading system is stupid, and he grades you on UNDERSTANDING the material. Overall, a pretty decent professor who is too smart to teach this class.

Professor Baldwin is the single best educator I have ever had. He actually cares about teaching and his style of group note-taking and then posting the notes online for review has been exceedingly helpful. Really knows the material and likes to grade assignments one on one.

RUN THE OTHER WAY took this teacher for Calc 1. the hardest class I ever took. Didn't know how to teach the class because he was way to smart for it. Handed out crazy problem sets for homework and you had to do everything 5 times over to get at least a 6/10 on them. could never get a 10/10 unless to invited a new number basically. 0/10 don't take

Baldwin is a great teacher, although he relies heavily on the use of the textbook. If you can take a lot out of reading the text, you'll do fine. comment: First of all OPEN NOTE TESTS. Second of all, he really cares about you, after I was sick for 2 weeks he allowed to have the rest of the semester to hand in the assignments I missed. He isn't the best teacher in MATH but everything on the tests is in the notes. If you know how to get through a problem you will be all good. Definitely recommend him!

Grades based on his interpretation of how much you understand, not completeness. Can get 6/10 on hw for getting part of one question wrong. Nice, smart guy, who does explain things decently. If you like math and thinking outside of the box, then you'll enjoy this class. The only thing that made this class difficult is that Prof. Baldwin sometimes skips over details. Having a background in computer science is definitely helpful. The tests aren't too bad, he gives partial credit and they are open bookcomputer.

Baldwin is a really good professor. He always wanted to help me learn the material and was passionate about every topic we discussed. Definitely take him if you get the chance.. As long as you go to class and do the problem sets, you should get an A. Open booknotecomputer was the best thing since sliced bread.

Dr. Baldwin means well, but most of the time is pretty confusing. He doesn't answer questions very clearly, and makes other students in the class answer them. All his lecture notes and homework are online, and his tests are open book so it's not completely necessary to go to class, but his notes can be weird, so it would be easier to go to class.

I just wanted to get him to say coolwhip. Amazing guy, extremely helpful. Lots of personal attention. Labs were challenging, but in a good way. Tests are all open book/note/computer. Class was always interactive. Best class of the semester for me.

He is a really good teacher, but you will have to do a lot to keep up with the labs.  He sets aside lots of time for each student, and he's very willing to help.  His grading system is weird, but it makes you do more, and he generally curves a little in the end.  His personality seems a little fake sometimes. Overall a great teacher; take him!

Pretty decent- class was small and sometimes boring due to lack of class participation. Notes are always online so if you miss class its not too bad- but go as much as possible. Makes you come into grade labs which is annoying but class was still worth it.

Baldwin is an extremely knowledgeable professor and extremely helpful. His classes are pretty straightforward and he posts the lectures online so you really don't have to go to class. He lets you use your notes and the internet for tests which is awesome. Definitely the easiest class to fulfill the Mate Req.

What a wonderful professor. He knows soooo much, and he wants you to learn. His grading style is awkward, but it works out that even if you do something wrong, if you can probe to him you understand the concept you will get credit. Loved Csci188.

He was so helpful and readily available that I rarely got frustrated with my labs.  His teaching method was also very easy to follow, full of hands on examples.
Amazing. I knew nothing about computer science coming into his class, and he made everything so accessible and easy to understand. I write programs for fun now!
Baldwin was my favorite professor at Geneseo..  Gotta love his teaching/grading style.  Take him if you get the chance.
Very excellent prof. Knowledgable and always available for questions. Highly recommended.

Baldwin is absolutely brilliant and possibly the best professor in Geneseo.  His material is very challenging but keeps it interesting all the way through.  If he weren't in the Computer Science department I probably would've transferred out of Geneseo.

Great teacher.  Tough class though, he gave a ton of work especially at the end of the course and the assignments were hard because they were in languages most people didn't know.  I learned alot though.  If you do the work, you'll do alright.
i love baldwin

The sweetest professor ever. She's very understanding that things come up so she will let you have an extension if it is necessary. She is very sweet. May not be a good professor, but she is very knowledgeable and it can be quite easy to get an A in the class. Stacey is a sweetheart and her class is very easy - you don't really need to show up or do the readings as long as you work hard on the papers. An absolutely terrible professor. Lectures make no sense and she refuses to use an organised lectured method such as powerpoint. She instead gives lectures using a dim overhead projector.

Stacey is very smart but she is difficult to follow because I'm not sure she knows exactly where she is going either. She is the sweetest old woman, but lost my papers on multiple occasions. I would take a bullet for this woman, but I would not take another class with her.

Prof. Edgar is very sweet and really just wants everyone to pass so she's pretty accommodating. Sometimes she's not too helpful in lecture and just does practice problems so the key to pass is GO TO TA HOURS!! That's where they go over all the homework and explain anything you need.
Lectures could be better, but TA hours are helpful. READ BEFORE CLASS or you will be confused!!!!

Dr. Edgar is super nice. She brought clementines and cookies to our class every Friday. The class, although small, is entirely run by her lecturing at students. There are 33 people in my class maybe 9-10 show up each day. She just sits at the top of the class and reads from the book, doesn't actually teach, she's smart but starting to lose it a little. I got a B on both the test and the paper. I didn't even buy the books let alone read them . Humn is a lightweight just make a quizlet before each test

The sweetest woman ever!!! She's a little quiet so sit in the front of the room. She gives a ton of partial credit and acknowledges that you tried (if you actually do). comment: Such a sweet woman. However she isnt the best at explain how to do things in class and sometimes she loses her train of thought. Dr. Edgar is a nice person, but I didn't like this class. If you don't understand logic (which is hit or miss), you won't get an A unless you have a friend in class who can help you through it. Professor Edgar is an amazing professor who genuinely cares about her students. The textbook for this class is very short and explains everything you need to know thoroughly.

Stacey Edgar is extremely intelligent and a kind hearted person. She makes jokes about watching tennis, mostly. This class was extremely difficult for me and there was a ton of homework. comment: Stacey Edgar is a hot piece of potato if I have ever seen one. Her intro to logic class was informative and helped with classes later on in the philosophy department. Her TA hours are very helpful. She often shows up to class late because of the intense sport of tennis, but don't be fooled she doesn't play herself only observers at late hours.

By far the hardest class I have taken in my Geneseo career. I took it for my math credit and regret it completely. The material is very hard to understand and she barely explains in class. If you want to pass the class, you NEED to go to TA hours every week. I don't recommend this class to anyone it was brutal. But she does want you to pass.

She's very nice, but starting to lose it a little. The material shouldn't be difficult, but she doesn't explain it well. Her textbook also hasn't been updated since the Cold War, evident in problems about "The Commies". Tests count for a lot, but she drops the lowest homework grade. The TAs are more helpful than her for learning material.

This was the hardest class I've ever taken, I took it for my math credit. Thankfully Professor Edgar really does want you to pass so if you go out of your way to reach out for help, she'll put you in contact with a tutor (who you'll have to pay). You have to go to TA hours to pass the homework, but you don't have to attend class. I barely passed.

Professor Edgar is honestly one of the nicest professors I've ever met. Even if she were an absolute awful teacher, she would probably still have been my favorite of the term. The best part is that she's not awful; she's incredibly knowledgeable about the subject she teaches. Every class is incredibly informative. Papers were plentiful, but not bad

Mrs. Edgar can be confusing in her lectures.  However, she tells you exactly what is going to be on the exams and the TA's give you the answers to all the homework problems.  If you work on a lot of practice problems before the tests, then you will do well in her class.

Mrs. Edgar is a sweet woman, she stays up all night just to have our homework and tests graded for the next class. This class would be a lot easier if it was not a lecture, the material is hard and confusing and in a smaller setting, students could actually ask questions. Learning logic was like learning chinese but she gives lots of resources

This class should be a smaller lecture so people can ask questions. There are TAs available but they're not always helpful either. Professor Edgar lectures the entire time but half the time had to pause and correct herself. A lot of the material had to be essentially self-taught. A hard class but at least I didn't have to take Calc.

Easy class to skip, she's too busy talking the entire class to notice. She's nice, always brings food one day of the week and you'll watch a lot of modern movie clips. The class is dreadful in the morning, you'll want to fall asleep in it with her monotone voice. That being said, zero participation necessary and she's an easy grader on the essays.

She's a very sweet lady but very boring and rants on and on about irrelevant topics. If you can, stay away from this class because honestly you will fall asleep and become a worse writer. You do what she says and it still isnt god enough for her; take another INTD class if you can.

The concepts are difficult. I studied very hard and rarely figured out what I was doing until right before the test. But when it finally clicks, you'll feel great about yourself. As long as you can do the homework (the TAs will help) you should be fine. Save homework, because it can help you study. She writes her own text, very straightforward.
The only hard thing about Logic is trying to stay awake during lectures.

She is such a nice old lady, but the lectures are really confusing and long. She just talks for the full time and sometimes has video clips for you to watch. The tests are also long and are extremely hard. If you don't read, or go to class you probably won't do well. She grades the two essays very easy though so that can make up for the tests.

Professor Edgar is a very sweet woman. However, the way she explains things in class is extremely confusing. If you go to TA hours though, the class isn't hard at all. The TAs help you find all the answers to the homework.

Intro to Logic is a semi-difficult class made impossible by Prof. Edgar.  Sweet woman, but cannot teach this course.  Rambles.  Of little to no help.  The material is impossible to learn because of this.  Her exams are difficult, but she gives a lot of partial credit so most pass anyway, regardless of how little they know. Go to T.A. hours.

Her tests are extremely long and difficult and I did miserable on them. She grades the essays super easy and I got As on both. She will take written attendance if the class is looking small, so if you're on the verge of failing, like me, she will probably let you pass. Just talk to her - she really is the nicest woman.

Really nice lady, but the class was extremely difficult unless you thoroughly read all the books. Her tests were ridiculously hard, lots of obscure quotes that you had to identify and a ton of difficult short answer questions. She grades the 2 papers really easily so that helped bring grades up, but overall it's a really tough HUMN I class.

I am definitely biased because I did not want to take this class, but had to for a requirement. However, I thought it was ridiculous and Prof. Edgar does a horrible job walking through processes and problems.We will go over something so quickly we don't have time to write it down, and then there are questions about it on the test. I don't recommend

Professor Edgar is the most amazing woman I have ever met. Aside from her being an inspiration outside of class though, she makes class fun and easy to understand. Awesome teacher. Both the sweetest old lady you will ever meet and one of the more brilliant minds in her profession

Prof. Edgar is awesome. Such a nice person and really knows her stuff. Proofs can be tricky at first, go to office hours for extra help with the TAs, it will really help! Take this class, it's very interesting.

Logic. Material is very interesting. She makes perfect sense if you read the book (written by her, her husband, and one of their former students).
